item.title: A First Step Toward the Quantum Battery: Demonstrating 'Superabsorption' in a Microcavity
item.description: A collaboration spanning Australia and Europe used a microcavity structure, an organic dye molecule confined between mirrors, to realise superabsorption experimentally, the principle at the heart of the quantum battery. Ultrafast transient absorption measurements showed superextensive behaviour: as the concentration of molecules (their number) rose, both the charging power and the stored energy per molecule went up while the charging rise time shortened. The work finds that decoherence (dephasing) is not an obstacle but a necessary condition for holding energy stably in place, which offers a new insight for the design of practical quantum batteries. [Quantum Biology Society] In 1954 the physicist Robert Dicke predicted superradiance: when N atoms sit close together, the waves of light they emit interfere constructively, so the time for emission scales as 1/N and the peak emission power scales as N². The effect has since been confirmed broadly across quantum systems ranging from quantum dots to nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centres in diamond. The reverse process, superabsorption, has been a far harder problem. The difficulty lies in engineering the precise environment in which such behaviour can occur and in monitoring charging timescales short enough to be hard to probe at all, and until recently the effect had been seen only for small numbers of atoms. There is a further problem on the storage side: in a closed system, the same coherent effects that produce fast charging also produce fast discharging. Even so, superabsorption is the conceptual foundation of the quantum battery, a device whose charging time is inversely related to its capacity, so that a larger battery charges faster. It has long been an open goal in the field. A paper published in Science Advances in January 2022, from a team led by James Q. Quach at the University of Adelaide in Australia and Tersilla Virgili at IFN-CNR and the Politecnico di Milano in Italy, along with collaborators in the UK, demonstrated superabsorption in a microcavity built around an organic dye. ■ Dye Meets Mirrors: Demonstrating Superextensive Charging The researchers built a microcavity by inserting a 185 nm thick film containing the fluorescent dye Lumogen-F Orange (LFO), dispersed in a polystyrene matrix, between two distributed Bragg reflectors (DBRs), the dielectric mirrors that confine the light. They then ran ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy on samples with the dye concentration (and therefore the number of molecules, N) set at 0.5%, 1%, 5% and 10%. Injecting a pump pulse of under 20 fs and following the charging of energy on a femtosecond timescale, they found superextensive scaling, with the highest-concentration 10% cavity at N = 16.0 × 10¹⁰. Charging power per molecule rises: going from 1% to 10% concentration, the peak charging power per molecule (P_max) climbed steeply from 0.060 to 0.791 eV/ps. Stored energy per molecule increases: the peak stored energy per molecule (E_max) likewise grew nearly tenfold, from 0.011 to 0.108 eV. Charging rise time shortens: the rise time to reach half the maximum energy (τ) fell from 0.118 to 0.094 ps. Because E_max and P_max are per-molecule quantities, their increase with N is precisely what makes the behaviour superextensive: the whole grows faster than in proportion to its size. As the paper puts it, a single microcavity containing N molecules takes less time to charge than N single-molecule microcavities would, even if the latter were all charged at once, and it would store more energy than those N separate cavities combined. This is the core principle of the quantum battery, that gathering everything into one large battery charges faster and more efficiently than charging many small ones separately. Two qualifications are worth keeping in view. The experiment directly provides the time dependence of the signal, but the absolute scale of the energy density is difficult to estimate from first principles, so the authors extracted it by fitting to their theoretical model; the values above come from that fit. And the modelling identifies three operating regimes, with the scaling not the same across all the experiments: charging power density is superextensive in every regime, while superextensive energy density scaling and subextensive charging time show up in different regimes. ■ A Paradoxical Conclusion: Decoherence Locks the Energy In The most provocative and physically deepest conclusion in the paper concerns the way energy is stored. In a closed quantum system perfectly sealed off from its surroundings, under unitary dynamics, energy drawn in rapidly by superabsorption is superradiated straight back out at the same rate. Charging is fast, but storage is impossible. The authors identify the mechanism that resolves this as decoherence driven by environmental noise, dephasing to be precise. When dephasing occurs, energy in the optically active bright mode is transferred into inactive dark modes that cannot emit into the cavity. Absorption stays fast while decay becomes slow, so the energy is held until it can be used. In the theoretical model, the presence of these decay channels gives rise to ratchet states capable of absorbing but not emitting light, which is what allows the energy to be stored stably. Decoherence, always the thing to be overcome in quantum information science, turns out to be a working requirement for a quantum battery: the paper states that purely closed unitary dynamics is insufficient for a practical device, and that retaining energy calls for finely tuned decoherence processes. ■ Limits and Outlook The study demonstrates the charging of a prototype quantum battery convincingly, but it carries clear limits. No energy extraction: the paper demonstrates charging and trapping the energy, and no further. A practical mechanism for drawing the stored energy out into an external device, that is, discharging, was not demonstrated. The authors do point to existing approaches, such as inserting charge transport layers between the active layer and the cavity layers so that the top cavity becomes a cathode and the bottom an anode. A concentration ceiling: above roughly 10% dye concentration, quenching sets in, driven by aggregation of the dye molecules and intermolecular states such as excimers, and performance degrades. (The authors gesture at biological molecules as a possible way around this, noting that in proteins such as green fluorescent protein (GFP) the active chromophore sits inside a structural cage that suppresses exciton-exciton quenching, and suggesting such materials might open a route to higher concentrations.) In short, this work has opened a path for building superextensive absorption into the design of organic optoelectronic devices. A commercial quantum battery remains a long way off. But the fact alone that collective quantum behaviour across more than 10¹⁰ molecules was demonstrated in air at room temperature, rather than under cryogenic temperatures and ultra-high vacuum, makes this a striking milestone. As the authors put it, the idea of superextensive charging may have wide-reaching consequences for sensing and for energy capture and storage technologies. #Superabsorption #Superradiance #QuantumBattery #DickeModel #Microcavity #Polariton #Decoherence #Dephasing #RatchetStates #UltrafastSpectroscopy #OrganicDye #QuantumBiology #ScienceAdvances Source (Science Advances): https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abk3160 Theoretical precursor (Nature Communications 2014, open access): https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms5705

The authors do point to existing approaches, such as inserting charge transport layers between the active layer and the cavity layers so that the top cavity becomes a cathode and the bottom an anode. A concentration ceiling: above roughly 10% dye concentration, quenching sets in, driven by aggregation of the dye molecules and intermolecular states such as excimers, and performance degrades. (The authors gesture at biological molecules as a possible way around this, noting that in proteins such as green fluorescent protein (GFP) the active chromophore sits inside a structural cage that suppresses exciton-exciton quenching, and suggesting such materials might open a route to higher concentrations.) In short, this work has opened a path for building superextensive absorption into the design of organic optoelectronic devices. A commercial quantum battery remains a long way off. But the fact alone that collective quantum behaviour across more than 10¹⁰ molecules was demonstrated in air at room temperature, rather than under cryogenic temperatures and ultra-high vacuum, makes this a striking milestone. As the authors put it, the idea of superextensive charging may have wide-reaching consequences for sensing and for energy capture and storage technologies. #Superabsorption #Superradiance #QuantumBattery #DickeModel #Microcavity #Polariton #Decoherence #Dephasing #RatchetStates #UltrafastSpectroscopy #OrganicDye #QuantumBiology #ScienceAdvances Source (Science Advances): https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abk3160 Theoretical precursor (Nature Communications 2014, open access): https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms5705

item.title: ASSESSING THE IMPACT OF COMMERCIAL BANK LIQUIDITY ON LOAN PORTFOLIO QUALITY
item.description: The thesis analyses the theoretical and empirical relationship between the liquidity of commercial banks and the quality of their loan portfolios. Bank liquidity is interpreted as a multidimensional category that combines funding liquidity, market liquidity, deposit stability and access to central-bank facilities; loan-portfolio quality is measured by the share of non-performing loans (NPL), loan-loss provisions and the volatility of expected credit losses under IFRS-9. Drawing on the works of Diamond and Rajan, Berger and Bouwman, Acharya and Naqvi, Cornett, McNutt, Strahan and Tehranian, Beltratti and Stulz, DeYoung and Torna, and IMF and Basel Committee documents, the paper systematises two competing theoretical mechanisms — the risk-shifting channel and the buffer channel — and summarises the empirical evidence.

item.title: THEORETICAL APPROACHES TO ENSURING THE STABILITY OF THE COMMERCIAL BANK DEPOSIT BASE
item.description: This article comprehensively examines the theoretical foundations and conceptual approaches to ensuring the stability of the deposit base of commercial banks. The essence of the category of "deposit stability" is disclosed on the basis of statistical-empirical, institutional-structural and behavioural approaches, and its structural and functional aspects are identified. Particular attention is paid to the fundamental works of F. Diamond, Ph. Dybvig, J. Stiglitz, G. Akerlof, F. Mishkin, D. Kahneman, A. Tversky and R. Thaler, on the basis of which the theory of deposit behaviour, the theory of bank runs, the theory of financial intermediation, and the problems of information asymmetry and depositor confidence are analysed.

Locked constants remain unchanged. Concept DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21386124. **Abstract (Revision 4):**Cartesian handbooks record melting and expansion as 1-atm coincidences. They do not construct E_n, h_true, or ε_h. This deposit states the opposite: a unified non-Cartesian engine in which binding is the frozen ladder E_n=-13.6(1+ε_h)Z^2/n^2 eV, working action is h_true=6.626070166565175×10^-34 (not CODATA h), and dimensional jitter ε_h=2.5×10^-9 is a distinct resonator — not a second Planck constant and not a thermal shut-off. Temperature is an amplitude A on that jitter. The retired “glass jaw” (unfulfilled wedge exceeding nested overlap) is logged (glass_jaw_at_floor: true) and does not halt the physics. item.title: Braided textile tensile modulus versus braiding machine settings: dataset and analysis code (28 polyester braids, Herzog variation braider)
item.description: Dataset and analysis code accompanying the manuscript "Selecting braiding machine settings for a target tensile modulus: validated inverse prediction with calibrated uncertainty" (Department of Textile and Fibre Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology Delhi). braid_dataset.csv: the complete experimental record of 28 polyester braids (337 tex multifilament yarn) produced on a Herzog VF 1(4-32)-140 variation braiding machine in a 1 x 1 diamond pattern, covering every producible lay length at 8 and 16 carriers in bi-axial and tri-axial configuration. Columns: sample, carriers, configuration, lay length (mm), measured braid linear density (tex), specific tensile modulus at 0.2 % strain (cN/tex). Tensile testing: Instron 5982, cord capstan grips, ASTM D6775-13, 250 mm gauge length, 75 mm/min, 25 +/- 2 C and 65 +/- 5 % RH, one specimen per braid. braid_ml_analysis.py: a single Python script (numpy, pandas, scipy, scikit-learn, matplotlib) that reproduces every statistic, table and figure in the manuscript: leave-one-out comparison of seven regression models with bootstrap confidence intervals, a group-mean baseline, repeated 5-fold cross-validation, a grid-thinning check, Gaussian-process prediction-interval coverage, per-configuration trend tests, a nested F-test for parameter interactions, and a leave-one-out validation of inverse prediction of lay length from a target modulus with the search bounded to each configuration's producible window. Random seeds are fixed; results are deterministic; runtime is about one minute. results_metrics.csv and results_predictions.csv are the script's outputs: model metrics with confidence intervals, and per-braid leave-one-out predictions of every model with the Gaussian-process 95 % prediction interval. README.md documents the files and how to run the analysis.

item.title: Normative Model for SOE Procurement Contract Disclosure as a Corruption Prevention Strategy in Indonesia
item.description: Background: Procurement corruption in Indonesian state-owned enterprises (SOEs) persists through contract manipulation practices, including mark-ups, directed tendering, fictitious entities, and engineered contract addenda. Although Article 33 of the 1945 Constitution and existing laws uphold the principles of transparency and accountability, no operational regulation currently requires SOEs to proactively disclose procurement contracts, addenda, and implementation reports. Objective: This study develops a normative model for SOE procurement contract disclosure as a pre-emptive and systemic strategy for corruption prevention. Methods: This dogmatic normative legal research applies statutory, conceptual, case-based, and comparative approaches. It examines the 1945 Constitution, the SOE Law, the Anti-Corruption Law, the Public Information Disclosure Law, SOE procurement regulations, Information Commission decisions, selected corruption cases involving PLN, Merpati, Pelindo II, and Amarta Karya, as well as international open-contracting standards. The analysis maps legal norms, identifies regulatory gaps, examines fraud patterns, and constructs a model based on Fraud Diamond Theory. Results: The study identifies a gap between transparency principles and enforceable disclosure obligations, enabling contractual secrecy that increases opportunities for fraud and strengthens perpetrators’ capabilities. The proposed model requires the disclosure of principal contracts and addenda, proactive publication through standardized electronic platforms, proportionate protection of legitimate trade secrets through consequence tests, independent verification mechanisms, and graduated administrative sanctions linked to the performance of SOE organs. Conclusion: Procurement contract disclosure should be institutionalized as a binding preventive instrument to strengthen public oversight, mitigate procurement fraud risks, and realize economic democracy as mandated by Article 33 of the 1945 Constitution.

item.title: Data from manuscript entitled "High-Pressure Phase Transitions, Electrical Conductivity and Recoverability of Uranium Polyhydrides"
item.description: Resistance versus temperature data and integrated powder X-ray diffraction patterns for uranium polyhydrides under high pressures. The data are available as .txt files. Study abstract: The uranium-hydrogen system has been predicted to form numerous polyhydride compounds, exhibiting diverse physical properties. However, experiments report starkly conflicting results regarding synthesis pressures, stoichiometries, and stability, leaving their fundamental properties and even their existence uncertain. Through a series of laser-heated diamond anvil cell experiments, we systematically investigate the high-pressure phase diagram of the uranium-hydrogen system up to 99(3) GPa using synchrotron powder X-ray diffraction. Compression and laser heating of β-UH3 at pressures of 41(1) and 91(3) GPa result in the formation of hcp-UH7 and fcc-UH8, respectively. Upon decompression of hcp-UH7 below 27(1) GPa, we observe decomposition into hcp-UH5, which subsequently further dehydrogenates to U4H15 below 12(1) GPa. The U4H15 compound, analogous to the well-known Th4H15, is recoverable to ambient pressure and temperature, and slowly oxidizes over the timescale of hours. Whilst all compounds are metallic, electrical resistance measurements demonstrate an absence of superconductivity upon cooling to 3 K in U4H15, hcp-UH5, and hcp-UH7, and to 7 K in fcc-UH8.

item.title: Interface Engineering in Piezoelectric‐on‐Insulator Platforms: Coupling of Electrons, Photons, and Phonons for Multifunctional Integration
item.description: ABSTRACT The growing demand for higher speed, wider bandwidth, and enhanced power handling in electronic, photonic, and radio‐frequency systems drives the rapid advancement of monolithic heterogeneous integration. The piezoelectric‐on‐insulator (POI) architecture isolates high‐quality single‐crystal piezoelectric thin films from supporting substrates through engineered heterointerfaces, enabling simultaneous confinement of optical modes, acoustic waves, and electric fields within the active layer. This configuration provides a versatile platform for multifunctional devices targeting 5G/6G communications, high‐power electronics, and quantum photonics. This review systematically examines the physical mechanisms governing POI heterointerfaces, with a focus on interface engineering strategies across key material systems, including LiNbO 3 /Si, LiNbO 3 /SiC, LiNbO 3 /diamond and AlN/diamond heterostructures. The strategies discussed encompass atomic‐scale bonding optimization, interfacial nanostructuring, and the design of ultrathin phonon‐bridge interlayers. A notable emerging capability is voltage‐tunable thermal conductivity enabled by ferroelectric domain wall engineering. Furthermore, this review addresses current challenges in scalable synthesis, defect control, and thermomechanical stress management, while outlining future directions, such as monolithic multifunctional system integration, dynamic interface tuning, and quantum photonic integration. By repositioning the heterointerface as an actively tunable functional element, this review offers a systematic framework for the design of POI interfaces in next‐generation electronic–photonic integrated systems.

item.title: Design and development of an endoscopic robotic system and deep reinforcement learning path planning algorithm for fine-needle biopsy of liver lesions
item.description: Abstract This paper presents the design, development and evaluation of a novel robotic platform for endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle biopsy of liver lesions. The system combines a four degrees-of-freedom (DoF) two-segment tendon-driven continuum robot (TDCR) endoscope with a two DoF superelastic nickel–titanium bevel-tip steerable needle. Needle path planning is achieved using NeedleNav, a soft actor–critic (SAC) deep reinforcement learning (DRL) model that generates collision-free trajectories to deep-seated lesions. This represents one of the first integrated systems combining a TDCR, steerable needle and DRL-based navigation, and the first application of a SAC to liver lesion targeting. Evaluation of the TDCR through tip tracking of circular, diamond-shaped and arc trajectories demonstrated a mean absolute error (MAE) of 13.19 mm. NeedleNav converged to obstacle avoidance trajectories in $$\sim $$ ∼ 2500 training episodes. Needle curvature was augmented by hand-fabricating notches on its distal section. Two needles with a 3-cm and 8-cm notched section were evaluated in a gelatine liver phantom, achieving an MAE of 21.78 mm and 14.86 mm, respectively, for obstacle avoidance trajectories. The system demonstrated observable path deflection compared to obstacle-free trajectories for the same targets. Together, these findings suggest the feasibility of our proposed solution, expanding the reach of endoscopic needle interventions to deep-seated lesions in the right lobe.

item.title: Color-Center-Compatible Freestanding Diamond Directional Couplers for Quantum Photonics
item.description: Abstract Freestanding all-diamond color-center photonics is a promising platform for optical integration of spin-based quantum defects. Within this geometry, we realize a key building block for quantum-network interconnects: a directional coupler that acts as an on-chip beam splitter. We design and simulate directional couplers with triangular cross sections using eigenmode and finite-difference time-domain simulations and target near-50:50 splitting at visible wavelengths. We fabricate the devices directly from bulk single-crystal diamond by angled oxygen reactive-ion-beam etching followed by a dry postrelease hard-mask removal process. Room-temperature measurements at λ0 ≈ 637 nm yield a mean coupling ratio of Cmeas = 46(16) %. Finally, we integrate tin-vacancy (SnV–) centers into the nanophotonic structures and observe near-lifetime-limited optical line widths and coherent optical Rabi oscillations without postfabrication annealing, identifying the platform as a viable route toward integrated diamond quantum photonics.

item.title: MASLD and MASH increase fracture risk in humans and arrest new bone formation in mice
item.description: Abstract Early data suggest metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) associates with increased fractures. However, absolute risk, subpopulations at greatest risk, and risk basis are unknown. We use a two-pronged approach to address these gaps: we investigated fracture risk among humans with MASLD and mechanisms among diet-induced animal model of MASLD (DIAMOND TM ) mice. We interrogated the TriNetX US collaborative database, propensity-matching people with MASLD 10-fold with people with metabolic dysfunction alone. All-fracture and pathological-fracture risks are elevated among people >51 years of age with MASLD. DIAMOND mice with MASLD lost bone thickness, strength, and bone formation and gained increased bone resorption. MASLD associated with differential expression of key indicators of bone loss: decreased hepatic Igf1 and Cyp2r1 , increased hepatic Fgf21, Ctgf , and Anxa2 , decreased skeletal Bglap, Runx2 , and Postn , and increased skeletal Pparg . These expression changes are supported by increased serum FGF21, reported in literature to impair bone anabolism. Herein, we establish MASLD as a risk factor for fracture and propose putative mechanisms driving bone loss.

item.title: Nature of point defects in bulk hexagonal diamond
item.description: Hexagonal diamond (HD), an exotic carbon allotrope recently synthesized in bulk form, exhibits superior mechanical properties compared to cubic diamond and holds promise for advanced industrial and quantum applications. Using first-principles calculations, we systematically investigate intrinsic defects, extrinsic dopants, and defect complexes in HD. Our study shows that VC dominates intrinsic conductivity, while Ci is unstable. Among extrinsic dopants, boron acts as a benign acceptor enhancing p-type conductivity, whereas nitrogen and phosphorus serve as effective donors for n-type conductivity. Group II and Group IV dopants, however, introduce high formation energies or neutral charge states with limited impact. Furthermore, VC, MgC, and XV defect complexes display multiple spin and charge states within the HD bandgap, highlighting their potential as color centers for hosting qubits. These results not only clarify the defect physics of HD but also demonstrate its broader implications for conductivity engineering and quantum technologies.

item.title: Local hybrid exchange–correlation with contracted plane wave basis functions
item.description: Local hybrid exchange-correlation (LH XC) functionals incorporate position-dependent exact exchange but are often limited by computational cost and self-consistent field (SCF) convergence challenges. In this study, we examine the performance of a testbed LH XC functional within the contracted plane wave basis function framework, which enables the evaluation of the exact exchange energy density with minimal additional overhead. Calculations on diamond supercells show that SCF convergence is robust and that the cost of forming the non-local contributions is approximately twice that of analogous global hybrid calculations. When combined within a practical SCF optimization protocol, the results indicate that calculations using LH XC functionals incur only a modest increase in total cost relative to those using global hybrid functionals, demonstrating that this approach is computationally viable.

item.title: Competitive advantage of National Olympic Committees in a sport: from periphery to Olympic silver and bronze medal successes
item.description: This article examines a National Olympic Committee’s (NOC’s) ascent from a consistent underperformer to a contender for Olympic silver and bronze medals through a case study of artistic gymnastics in Taiwan. Porter’s national diamond model served as the theoretical framework. Qualitative data were collected from twelve senior interviewees.Taiwan’s significant progress in artistic gymnastics has been driven by the emergence of specific gymnasts, the improved coaching skills of particular male coaches, increased government financial support, and favourable rule changes introduced by the International Gymnastics Federation (FIG). However, Taiwan has been unable to win an Olympic gold medal in artistic gymnastics, constrained by limited knowledge resources and competitiveness, particularly among female gymnasts; poor gymnastics facilities; and strategic and structural issues. This article further advances four sport-specific propositions: partial diamonds can produce narrow medal advantage; chance events do not operate through external shocks alone; demand conditions require sport-specific sophistication; and NOC-level governance functions as an amplifier rather than an automatic generator of competitive advantage.

item.title: A methodological framework for intelligent management and control systems in the AEC industry based on the double diamond model
item.description: The Double Diamond model, developed by [The British Design Council. (Citation2005). The Double Diamond-Design Council. Available at: https://www.designcouncil.org.uk/our-resources/the-double-diamond (Accessed: 29 August 2024)], structures system design through two diamond-shaped phases emphasizing divergent-convergent thinking. While the Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) industry leverages Civil Engineering 4.0 technologies like BIM, IoT, and AI for robotic construction and data-driven platforms. However, the absence of a structured design theory for intelligent systems risks inefficiencies, misaligned stakeholder objectives, and solutions lacking utility or usability. This study addresses this gap by proposing a AEC-specific methodological framework adapted from the Double Diamond model, integrated with the Future Cone model and service design principles. The framework standardizes procedures for stakeholder alignment, explicit decision-making criteria for phase-specific alternative evaluation and selection, and iterative system optimization, demonstrated through a proof-of-concept case study: a smart groundwater control system for excavation dewatering in Northeast China. By integrating agile problem-framing and AI-driven convergence cycles, the model enhances adaptability in complex AEC workflows. Its contributions include a versatile decision-support oriented design framework for developing intelligent systems within Civil Engineering 4.0 and a forward-looking scaffold for emerging Civil Engineering 5.0 applications, prioritizing human-centricity alongside technical innovation. The results underscore the framework’s capacity to bridge interdisciplinary gaps and align technical solutions with practical implementation in infrastructure digitalization.

item.title: Unconventional Materials for Light Dark Matter Detection
item.description: We propose the use of several unconventional materials as detectors for dark matter with mass beneath the MeV scale. These include the transition-metal dichalcogenide TiSe 2 hosting a low-energy plasmon in the charge-density-wave phase, Sr 2 RuO 4 containing a low-energy acoustic demon mode, and hole-doped diamond with tunable optical and acoustic plasmon frequencies. We perform first-principles density functional theory computations of their loss functions at nonvanishing momenta and establish their reach into light dark matter parameter space. We show that due to intense low-energy plasmon modes—of different microscopic origin in each—the reach of detectors based on these materials could surpass existing proposals by several orders of magnitude for both dark matter scattering and absorption on electrons. The anisotropic response of these materials, which enables directional detection, renders them exceptionally strong detector candidates, motivating the design and fabrication of future devices.

item.title: Guest editorial: Mentoring and coaching as pathways to social justice in education
item.description: Guest editorial: Mentoring and coaching as pathways to social justice in educationAt this time, as our collective efforts to fix social systems face backlash and, in some cases, aggressive attacks, we must develop new strategies to sustain our work over the years and across generations.We face resistance to socially just systemic changes in our daily conversations with neighbors and other community members, in communities geographically distant from our own that nonetheless shape our daily lives, and among our political leaders who leverage their power to dismantle our collective efforts.For instance, in the United States, attacks on diversity, equity and inclusion efforts and on critical race theory specifically have shifted from commentary to legal mandates that prohibit educators in many states from addressing diversity and equity issues, such as gender, sexuality, race and ethnicity and language-based marginalization (Hoyos Ensuncho, 2025;Schultz, 2025;Woo et al., 2024).Further, both higher education and primary through secondary education are grappling with funding cuts, student health crises, rapidly changing workforce demands and ongoing social and political unrest (Berrett, 2026; Bipartisan Policy Center, 2026;Bryant et al., 2025;Kiley et al., 2026;Langreo, 2024; National Center for Education Statistics, 2024).New strategies and coalitions are needed to overcome these policy strongholds and social upheavals.We need more scholars to partner with local educators, policymakers and other reformers to continue driving socially just change in primary through secondary education.While we work to alleviate inequities for primary and secondary students, we also strive to amplify the voices of those who are least represented in higher education, both as current and future primary and secondary education leaders and as future scholars.We need to mentor and coach the next generation of social justice leaders, welcoming and supporting their innovative ideas for change.Effective mentors and coaches shepherd mentees and coachees into education spaces with the message "Come right on in.You're going to do great things here.I'll walk with you."They share with their mentees and coachees how to navigate academia, which is often a hostile space for minoritized scholars (Contreras Aguirre, 2024;Maguire et al., 2025;Sanczyk et al., 2021).They guide mentees and coachees in using their unique voices to challenge the dominant body of knowledge and increase social justice advocates' awareness of self-care practices to sustain themselves and their work.Simultaneously and importantly, mentees and coachees support their mentors' and coaches' learning and development as they walk together (Freire, 1993).Adding to the burgeoning literature on mentoring and coaching for and as and for social justice (Ekpo et al., 2025;Volpe et al., 2025;Wilkerson and James, 2026), this special issue of the International Journal of Mentoring and Coaching in Education, shepherded by the Leadership for Social Justice (LSJ) Special Interest Group (SIG) of the American Educational Research Association, aims to offer guidance for mentors, mentees, coaches and coachees as they walk their unique educational journeys together.Our SIG has been assessing the evolution of social justice theory and the presence of social justice practices in teaching, mentoring, coaching and hiring in primary through secondary schools and higher education.While the definition and inclusion of social justice have expanded dramatically in academia (e.g.Sonu et al., 2012;Theoharis, 2007), challenges persist with implementation in primary through secondary schools and school systems (Diamond and Lewis, 2019;Horsford et al., 2019) and in higher education (National Center for Faculty Development and Diversity and Collaborative on Academic Careers in Higher Education, 2025;Patton et al., 2010).The collection of articles in this special issue serves as examples of mentoring and coaching for and International

item.title: Diamond NV center electrometry under single-axis magnetic field compensation
item.description: Diamond Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) centers, as emerging solid-state quantum sensors, possess immense potential in precision electric field measurement fields such as complex environment diagnosis and high-voltage insulation monitoring, owing to their advantages of non-invasive measurement and non-distortion of the field under test. However, the magnetic field interaction (Zeeman effect) in the ground-state Hamiltonian of the NV center is typically far greater than the electric field interaction (Stark effect), causing weak electric field signals to be easily overwhelmed by background magnetic field noise. Addressing this technical bottleneck, this paper proposes and validates an electric field sensing scheme based on uniaxial magnetic field compensation. By constructing a confocal microscopy experimental system combined with a three-dimensional Helmholtz coil, the axial magnetic field component of the NV center is actively canceled, effectively suppressing the Zeeman effect under quasi-zero field conditions. The experiment clearly observed inhomogeneous broadening and mixing of energy levels under zero field using Continuous Wave Optically Detected Magnetic Resonance (CW-ODMR). Furthermore, utilizing a spin-echo pulse sequence, coherent detection of a 2 kHz AC electric field signal was successfully achieved within the decoherence time T2. This scheme effectively decouples magnetic field noise and significantly enhances the sensitivity of electric field measurements, providing an important technical means for practical weak electric field detection based on solid-state quantum systems.

item.title: Comparative evaluation of screening approaches for antiviral monoclonal antibody combinations
item.description: Monoclonal antibody (mAb) cocktails are increasingly used as antiviral therapeutics, but methods for evaluating mAb combination effects remain poorly standardized. To characterize interactions of recently isolated neutralizing mAbs targeting human cytomegalovirus glycoprotein B, we compared three screening approaches: checkerboard neutralization assays; DiaMOND, a high-throughput small-molecule interaction screening tool modified for mAb combinations; and EMERALD, a modified variable-ratio framework. As the most systematic approach, the checkerboard assay served as the baseline for subsequent comparisons. Most mAb combinations in checkerboard assays were classified as additive or antagonistic according to Loewe additivity-based analyses, regardless of whether the mAbs were competing or non-competing. Apparent synergy was observed primarily at saturating antibody concentrations. When adapted for mAb combinations, the DiaMOND framework produced interaction profiles that differed from checkerboard results under both concentration-based and dose-matched conditions. In contrast, EMERALD captured concentration-dependent interactions across variable mAb ratios and revealed asymmetric behavior, depending on which mAb was held constant. Together, these findings demonstrate that classifications of mAb interactions depend strongly on assay design, concentration range, and analytical framework. They further suggest that robust mAb synergy may be less common than often reported and highlight the need to evaluate antiviral mAb combinations across multiple experimental formats.IMPORTANCEMonoclonal antibody cocktails are gaining foothold as an important strategy for the prevention and treatment of viral infections. Synergistic antibody combinations are often reported, but whether they represent true synergy is unclear because classifications of interactions depend on the experimental design and analytical methods. Moreover, there is no broadly accepted methodology for evaluating interactions among antibody combinations. As a result, it remains unclear whether common approaches for screening antibody combinations accurately capture biologically relevant interactions. Here, we compared four approaches for evaluating antibody combinations to help define best experimental and analytical practices for studying antiviral antibody interactions. Our findings demonstrate that antibody interactions are highly dependent on assay design, choice of antibody concentrations, and timing of antibody exposure, suggesting that synergy and antagonism are not fixed properties of antibody pairs. These findings may be broadly applicable to studies of antiviral antibody combinations across diverse viral systems.

item.title: La metáfora gongorina en las Soledades desde la crítica de la razón literaria
item.description: This article examines Góngora’s use of metaphor at the opening of the Soledad primera within the theoretical framework of the Crítica de la razón literaria. It argues that the difficulty of the passage should be understood neither as irrational obscurity nor as merely ornamental artifice, but as a formal procedure through which Góngora reorganizes physical, psychological, and conceptual materials. Focusing on images such as “walls of fir,” “diamond battlements,” “crystal giants,” and “foaming coral,” the article analyzes the interplay of metaphor, hyperbaton, fiction, and poetic rationality. It draws on the categories of the genera of materiality M1, M2, and M3, together with the circular, radial, and angular anthropological axes, to account for the literary construction of the passage. On this basis, the article proposes a didactic application for advanced learners of Spanish as a foreign language, showing how textual difficulty may be transformed into an exercise in critical, reasoned, and verifiable reading.

item.title: Designing an Interactive Visual Book as a Supportive Medium for Parental Intervention in Introducing Basic Sign Language to Children
item.description: This study aims to design an interactive visual book as a supportive medium for parental intervention in introducing basic sign language to children who are newly identified as deaf and beginning to learn sign language. Most deaf children are born to hearing parents who often lack prior knowledge and experience in deafness, leading to communication barriers and language delays. To address this issue, an early intervention strategy is needed that enables parents to communicate effectively using sign language. The design process adopts the double diamond and design thinking methods, involving literature studies, observations, and experimental design. Phenomenology, the AEIOU framework, and the system usability scale (SUS) were used as references in constructing questions for depth interviews. The resulting product is a board book titled Seri Waktu Bahasa Isyarat, designed not based on chronological age, but on the child’s stage of sign language acquisition. The content is organized around daily routines and includes BISINDO signs, realistic illustrations, repetitive elements, and QR code linked videos featuring sign language interpreters. This book is expected to assist parents in the early intervention process of introducing sign language to their children.

item.title: JMMP, Vol. 10, Pages 332: Physics–AI Dual-Driven Prediction of CNC Following-Up Errors and Compensation Control in High Precision Optics Machining
item.description: Optical surface deviations in ophthalmic optics arise from fast tool servo errors, the tool footprint, freeform surface residuals, and the freeform surface curvature responses across processing stages. In this paper, a PAM-Net physics&ndash;AI dual-driven compensation control method is presented for addressing the issues in dynamically accurate positioning of a diamond cutting tool via the fast tool servo using existing methods, e.g., struggling to characterize micrometer-scale CNC following-up errors, spatial surface-form perturbations, and S/C optical quality simultaneously. PAM-Net maps Z-axis position, velocity, acceleration, jerk, and A/B-axis phases to surface-form residuals and S/C deviations through tool-lens projection and curvature-mediated optical-response operators, while jointly estimating uncertainty and safety risk for constrained NC compensation. The framework also preserves an interpretable mediation chain from servo dynamics to final optical quality. On holdout-35, removing acceleration/jerk increased RMSE from 0.512 to 5.395 &mu;m, indicating strong predictive dependence on high-order servo dynamics. Closed-loop validation increased the strict &plusmn;0.12 D pass rate from 72.5% to 87.5%, alongside reduced surface-form and curvature residuals. These results indicate that learning-based compensation control for high-precision freeform-optics manufacturing requires joint consideration of prediction accuracy, physical interpretability, executable NC write-back, and manufacturing constraints.

item.title: India–UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement 2025
item.description: The India–United Kingdom Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) 2025 marks a significant milestone in bilateral trade relations. This chapter examines the trade potential and structural alignment between the two economies using sector-level data across fifteen product categories at the two-digit HS code level. It employs the Revealed Comparative Advantage (RCA) index to assess India's export competitiveness, alongside tariff analysis to evaluate pre- and post-agreement duty structures. Additionally, the Trade Complementarity Index (TCI) and Trade Intensity Index (TII) are used to measure trade compatibility and engagement. The findings highlight India's strong advantage in diamonds, cereals, spices, and marine products, with moderate strength in pharmaceuticals and textiles. A high TCI and TII indicate strong alignment and existing trade intensity. The chapter concludes with policy recommendations to enhance export performance and leverage the agreement's full potential.

item.title: Getting on with it
item.description: Wittgenstein’s main works, the Tractatus and Philosophical Investigations , concerned themselves only in passing with a number of subjects that have traditionally been of central concern to the philosopher: ethics, religion, art, politics, culture, history, scientific method, mathematics, etc. However, the application of the philosophical approach developed in the Philosophical Investigations is not restricted to the issues discussed there. Wittgenstein’s methodological outlook has had an impact on various areas of philosophy, such as the philosophy of science (among others Thomas Kuhn), mathematics (Juliet Floyd, Hilary Putnam, Felix Mühlhölzer), the social sciences (Peter Winch), action (Elizabeth Anscombe, Charles Taylor), psychology and psychoanalysis (D. W. Hamlyn, Jacques Bouveresse, Frank Cioffi), society and politics (Rush Rhees, Winch, Hanna Pitkin, Elizabeth Wolgast), feminist philosophy (Naomi Scheman), aesthetics (Stanley Cavell, Benjamin Tilghman, Toril Moi, Stephen Mulhall) and religion (John Wisdom, O. K. Bouwsma, Norman Malcolm, Rhees, D. Z. Phillips). Ethics constitutes a special case. An early offshoot of Wittgensteinian thinking was metaethics (Charles Stevenson, R. M. Hare), later followed by an approach to ethics in which, on the one hand, the fact-value distinction was attenuated, on the other hand, the connection between ethics and moral psychology was brought to the fore (Anscombe, Philippa Foot, Winch, R.F. Holland, Raimond Gaita, Cora Diamond).
item.dc:creator: Lars Hertzberg

item.title: The Wisdom Wheel – A Pedagogical Strategy for Developing Wisdom
item.description: As teachers, we play an important role in helping students develop not only knowledge, but the capacity to think critically, reflect deeply, and grow into wise and thoughtful individuals. At St Margaret’s Berwick Grammar Junior School, our teaching is shaped by concept-based inquiry (Erickson & Lanning) and the International Baccalaureate Primary Years Programme, both of which centre on student voice, big ideas and real-world connections. This made exploring wisdom education a natural extension of our practice. With support from our Principal, Dr Annette Rome, we joined the “Wisdom Project” led by Dr Zane M. Diamond (Monash University). What began as a professional inquiry evolved into a co-construction of wisdom alongside our students. Across different year levels, we saw a common understanding emerge: wisdom is not fixed, but shaped through reflection, action, and experience. From these shared observations, the Wisdom Wheel was developed – a practical, student-informed framework supporting students to think about, practise and express wisdom in their daily lives. In this chapter, we outline our process, the questions that guided us, and the student voices that shaped this work from the ground up.
item.dc:creator: Kate Bartholomeusz
Karryn Exner
Tracey Hallam

item.title: Spirals of Wisdom
item.description: In this chapter, Zhang and Diamond engage in a dialogic, comparative exploration of their respective wisdom journeys, revealing perennial insights into how wisdom can be cultivated in schools and universities. Our dialogue highlights culturally framed memories of learning wisdom across ancestral and contemporary educational contexts, including Confucian, Catholic, and Indigenous traditions. These spirallic journeys reflect lifelong learning, self-reflection, and ethical living, which inform our pedagogical practices in teacher education – akin to learning how to “get on the wavelength.” We argue that wisdom-oriented pedagogy must be purposive, transitioning from knowledge-inquiry to wisdom-inquiry methods to help students navigate complexity and uncertainty. Through our dialogue, we identified three interconnected skill sets – ethical living, critical thinking, and life skills – that shaped our own wisdom development and should be foregrounded in student learning. These skills must be woven into the knowledge and capabilities Australian children and young people require today so they can learn to be wise. Our reflections also demonstrate how dialogic and autoethnographic methods, when combined with Indigenous practices of deep listening, can generate pedagogical models that are relational, ethical, and transformative.

item.title: Persistence and emergence of quantum defects through pressure-induced phase changes
item.description: Extreme pressures can transform materials and their properties, but probing these in-situ is made challenging by the small sample volumes and access requirements demanded by diamond anvil cells. Quantum defects offer a route to local measurements under such conditions, yet their sensing performance can be dictated by pressure-induced changes in their own host material. On the other hand, pressure may also be harnessed as a tool to engineer and stabilize new quantum defects with emergent functionalities. Here, we demonstrate both aspects within a unified platform based on optically active spin-pair defects in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). As robust quantum sensors under pressure, these spin-1/2 systems retain pressure-independent spin resonances up to 20 GPa while maintaining or even enhancing their optical emission, in stark contrast to the spin-1 boron-vacancy centre in the same material. Simultaneously, we show that compression acts as a means of quantum defect engineering: the starting hBN undergoes an irreversible transformation into wurtzite boron nitride (wBN), during which the defect landscape is reconfigured. Spin-pair sensors are seen to persist across this structural transition, however, depending on the starting material we also observe new, highly fluorescent defects in the wBN phase. These results establish spin-pair defects in boron nitride as pressure-resilient quantum sensors while highlighting high pressure itself as a versatile pathway for creating and tuning quantum emitters.

item.title: Direct Validation of Superconductivity through Contact-Free Detection of Persistent Supercurrents Using Room-Temperature Quantum Magnetometry
item.description: The accelerated emergence of new materials is driving the search for high temperature superconductors, but rapid experimental validation remains a critical bottleneck, particularly for microscopic samples under high pressure. Here, we demonstrate one-step direct superconductivity validation through room-temperature, contact-free detection of remnant supercurrents. The technique utilizes a cryogen-free optically pumped atomic magnetometer to detect the temperature-dependent magnetic field produced by supercurrents of a superconductor. The superconducting transition is directly identified by the abrupt disappearance of magnetic field from the remnant supercurrent above the transition temperature and the reversal of the supercurrent direction upon reversing the applied magnetic field. Validated on YBCO microcrystals and REBCO tape, this technique detects pico-Tesla magnetic fields from supercurrents induced by the ambient Earth's magnetic field in a millimeter-sized REBCO square disk, as well as from sub-100 micrometer YBCO microcrystals compatible with high-pressure diamond anvil cells. The use of a ferrite flux guide enables sensitive detection from centimeter-scale distances. Requiring no electrical contacts, magnetic coils, or integrated magnetic sensors, this non-invasive, room-temperature platform offers a scalable approach for high-throughput screening and validation of superconductivity.

item.title: Nonvanishing derived limits from $\clubsuit$-type principles
item.description: Combinatorial set theory provides several tools to study derived limits of certain inverse systems of abelian groups. Most known nonvanishing results for $\lim^n$ with $n>1$ depend on some guessing principles of the form $\mathrm{w}\lozenge(S)$ called weak diamonds. In this paper, we explore some applications of the guessing principle $\clubsuit(S)$ and its weakenings instead.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Casarosa

item.title: Nanoscale magnetometry via collective many-body dynamics in diamond
item.description: Many-body dynamics constitutes a promising approach for creating correlations between quantum particles which can be used for applications in sensing and metrology. However, utilizing this potential for substantial gains in practical settings is a challenging task with only a very few applications realized to date. Here, we demonstrate an approach to nanoscale magnetic sensing enabled by strongly interacting electronic spins in a room temperature solid. By coherently controlling collective many-body dynamics of a dipolar ensemble of $\sim 10^4$ nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centres in diamond with pulsed magnetic field gradients, we demonstrate practical metrological gain up to $7.9(2)\,\mathrm{dB}$ for magnetic signal detection and $8.8(3)\,\mathrm{dB}$ for magnetic noise sensing, fully accounting for experimental overheads. Finally, we combine these methods to demonstrate a momentum-space-resolved sensing modality that enables detection of spatially correlated magnetic noise at continuously tunable length scales down to 50 nanometers. These observations open the door toward practical applications of interaction-enhanced quantum sensors for nanoscale biological imaging and material characterization.

item.title: The Silence Experiment: A Multi-State Protocol for Detecting Consciousness-Dependent Decoherence in Shielded Environments
item.description: This paper specifies a controlled experimental protocol for testing the von Neumann-Wigner interpretation of quantum mechanics, the hypothesis that consciousness plays a role in quantum state reduction, against the prevailing environmental decoherence framework. It measures whether the cognitive state of a nearby conscious observer measurably affects the decoherence rate of a prepared quantum system. The platform places an experienced meditator in EEG-verified states inside a five-layer shielded chamber. A single nitrogen-vacancy centre in diamond measures coherence times across seven consciousness conditions spanning the cognitive-excitation axis, from active cognition to objectless awareness, against an empty-chamber instrumental baseline and a thermal-dummy control cell that reproduces the metabolic heat load of a seated occupant with no observer present. All seven conditions run in one randomised session, so chamber drift is common to the chain and differences out of the within-participant contrasts. Three primary tests are pre-registered at a family-wise threshold of 0.005 one-sided, Bonferroni corrected to approximately 0.00167 per test: an ordered test across the excitation axis, and two orthogonal planned contrasts specified as explicit weight vectors that sum to zero. A fourth, secondary test is the only one that can separate the protective prediction from the suppression pattern, and its non-orthogonality to the first contrast is disclosed rather than corrected away. Both the EEG classifier and the coherence-time estimation pipeline are frozen and lodged before collection, so that neither the independent nor the dependent variable carries unspecified analytic freedom. A pre-registered positive control establishes that the measurement chain is sensitive, not merely quiet, and it is a gate: without it, a null carries no information about effect size. Phase 1 runs on the same chamber with an isotopically purified sample and carries three pre-registered hypotheses of its own, including a coupling-model discriminator and a spectral-density sweep that converts the standard objection to dynamical decoupling into the measurement itself. It is not conditional on a positive Phase 0 result. The protocol is outcome-blinded and is not described as blinded in any stronger sense. Participants and the instructing experimenter cannot be blinded, because the independent variable is an instructed cognitive state, and this is stated rather than glossed. The expected outcome is a null, which is pre-registered as publishable. No calendar timeline is stated anywhere. Session burden is given as a design parameter from which a host institution computes its own schedule. The protocol is pre-registered at OSF and is not peer reviewed; no data have been collected.

item.title: Dutch Marquise: Open Geometry Specification
item.description: An open, versioned, machine-readable specification for the Dutch Marquise diamond cut and its companion the French Marquise: outline, faceting pattern, certificate nomenclature, and how to read the length-to-width ratio from a grading report, with every claim sourced. A Dutch Marquise is an elongated hexagonal cut diamond, cut for brilliance; grading laboratories describe the geometry as a hexagonal modified brilliant (IGI report, 2026). The term is a trade name, not an officially recognized gemological shape. Published by Stienhardt, New York, which controls this cut through a specialized factory relationship and hand-sets and finishes the stones in New York City, and which does not claim to have invented, named, or standardized the cut. Version 1.0.2 re-renders the PDF edition (the 1.0.1 PDF file was a blank error page); version 1.0.1 corrected the certificate term, removes an unsupported ratio range in favor of measured values, resolves the faceting description, and adds a PDF edition.

item.title: Discrete Spacetime Topological Network,DSTN.(Basic Theory And Core Derivations )/阴阳爻网络模型DSTN(基础理论与核心推导)
item.description: This study presents the "DSTN(Discrete Spacetime Topological Network)", an interdisciplinary research program that integrates Eastern wisdom with modern mathematical and physical sciences. It aims to resolve the unification problem of quantum mechanics and general relativity, and reconstruct the cognitive framework of the cosmic origin. Breaking through the traditional reductionist paradigm, the model draws inspiration from the holistic and generative perspectives in I Ching and Daoist thought, establishing five core axioms: 1. The ultimate fundamental unit is the "Yao" (±1), representing the binary states of Yin and Yang;2. The universe is a discrete dynamic network formed by the connections of Yao;3. Spacetime, matter, and interactions are all emergent phenomena of network evolution;4. The network follows the conservation of topological charge;5. The network evolves toward the minimization of energy. Based on the axiomatic system, the model naturally derives three core laws: the law of combinatorial creation, the law of closed-loop stability, and the law of threshold realization. It also proposes key geometric conjectures: the network spontaneously organizes into a dual triangular pyramid as the basic unit and a nested diamond lattice topology, giving rise to characteristic numbers such as 9, 27, 36, and 108 (where 108 = 2²×3³, the critical threshold for matter transitioning from "virtual state" to "real state"). These numbers not only correlate with key parameters in particle physics and cosmology but also align with core symbols in Eastern culture. The model constructs a complete mathematical framework and dynamic evolution path. Based on the evolutionary laws of the discrete network, it presents a derivation pathway toward the core equations of general relativity and quantum mechanics, offering a feasible approach to achieving compatibility between the continuous limit and existing theories. It also clarifies the emergent mechanism of fundamental physical constants (e.g., the speed of light c, Planck constant h, fine-structure constant α), and presents a quantitative association framework linking them to network parameters. As a testable scientific program, the model provides twelve specific physical predictions: including the cubic power distribution of dark matter mass spectrum, the large-scale attenuation and 108-fold resonance peak of cosmic microwave background radiation, the scarcity of high-redshift galaxies, and the weak dispersion effect of gravitational waves. These predictions clearly distinguish themselves from mainstream paradigms and can be verified by next-generation detectors and observation equipment. This research offers a new exploration path for quantum gravity and unified field theory. We invite scholars in mathematics, physics, computer science, and other fields to jointly advance axiom formalization, numerical simulation, and experimental verification, and decode the deep geometric and numerical order of the universe. Author Note: The author is an independent researcher, and the "Researcher" label in this record refers to a general academic identity, not a formal professional title. This section presents the foundational theoretical core of the Yin-Yang Network Cosmic Model. For extended applications of this theory and related scientific papers, please refer to the following DOIs: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18426000.DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18493628

item.title: Dickson's conjecture versus superadditivity of prime-constellation counts: explicit certificates, the exact twin-prime crossing, and a registry of incompatible conjectures
item.description: Hensley and Richards (1974) showed that the prime k-tuples conjecture contradicts the Hardy-Littlewood inequality pi(x+y) <= pi(x)+pi(y). This note records the same incompatibility for constellation counting functions (twin primes, cousins, sexy primes, two triplet patterns, quadruplets) with small explicit certificates verified by a few lines of code; for twin primes the crossing occurs already at window length 396 (22 admissible twin-pair positions of diameter 392 versus pi_2(396)=21), and each conditional statement is checked to be non-vacuous by an exhaustive scan of the actual primes. A self-contained certificate for the original Hensley-Richards incompatibility (an admissible 1699-tuple of diameter below 14500 versus pi(14500)=1698) is included, together with an explicit remote window, built by the Chinese remainder theorem, containing 1699 integers free of prime factors up to 1699. This refutes unconditionally the central claim of a recent preprint (Zenodo record 21896925) that remote intervals can never have prime capacity exceeding pi(y); that preprint's Theorem 1 is also shown to fail for every window length y from 2 to 2000. Computations, certificates and text were prepared with the assistance of an AI system (Claude, Anthropic); the author is responsible for the content. Version 4 adds the incompatibility-graph registry as supplementary data: edges.json (120 proven edges of the form 'A and B cannot both hold', each with mechanism, source and status: 33 certificate edges, 79 literature edges across number theory, fine-grained and structural complexity, harmonic analysis, arithmetic geometry and set theory, 8 trivial), nodes.json (believed/refuted statuses), registry.md (table), graph.html (interactive rendering) and build.py; plus 22 further certificate systems from an automated pipeline (constellations, Cunningham chains, arithmetic progressions, quadratic and cubic polynomials). Version 4.1: graph.html rebuilt as a standalone English page (UTF-8 declared; the previous file lacked a charset declaration and rendered garbled outside a hosting wrapper) with a corrected force layout. Version 5: the registry grows to 1096 edges (959 certificate edges from an automated pipeline over 987 systems: prime pairs {0,2k} up to k=60, all admissible even triples of diameter <= 40 and quadruples of diameter <= 30, arithmetic progressions a mod q for q <= 40, quadratic polynomials n^2+c and n^2+n+c; 124 literature edges; 13 trivial). Certificate edges compared against an initial segment with at most two occurrences are tagged 'HR-thin'. All certificate edges share one mechanism and count once as evidence; the tags allow restricting the graph to edges between independently held conjectures. Version 6: (i) the exact twin-prime crossing: the least window length at which an admissible configuration of twin-pair positions beats the initial segment is y0 = 379 (theorem, with the table of minimal diameters D(K) of admissible K-packings of twin pairs for K <= 23, program supplied, independently recomputed); (ii) ten composite incompatibilities between named statements with proofs and prior-art status (five published in substance, four folklore, one -- Chang's conjecture versus Diamond-plus -- not found stated); (iii) the registry grows to 268 edges between named conjectures (1268 edges in total), most of the new ones found by literature-search agents and confirmed by adversarial verifier agents; the full verifier log is supplied. Version 7: registry data update only; 349 edges between named conjectures (1349 in total) after three rounds of agent search and adversarial verification across ten domains; both verifier logs supplied. Version 8: 404 edges between named conjectures (1402 in total); the registry is now a signed 2-clause model (each edge excludes one of the four truth-value combinations of its pair), with a canonical-node alias map (aliases.json, 475 nodes), a pair matrix of excluded combinations, and a resolution closure that derives 88 further clauses from the recorded ones (listed in registry.md as consequences, not counted as edges). Version 9: 548 relations between named conjectures (1546 edges in total) of four kinds (incompatibility, dichotomy, implication either way), each recorded as a signed 2-clause; a pair-centric sweep over the 30 most connected statements added 63 verified relations; the resolution closure now derives 418 consequences from the 586 mapped clauses (listed in registry.md, not counted as edges). Version 10: 642 relations between named statements (1743 edges in total); 103 definitional implications between stronger and weaker forms of the same conjecture (variant_implications.json, not counted as relations); cross-field bridges found by targeted sweeps (Montgomery's large-values conjecture implies Kakeya; Vinogradov's main conjecture and l^2 decoupling; GRH and deterministic algorithms; abc and decidability); connectivity analysis: three continents (complexity, number theory with analysis, set theory) remain mutually disconnected at the hub level.

item.title: Nature of point defects in bulk hexagonal diamond
item.description: Hexagonal diamond (HD), an exotic carbon allotrope recently synthesized in bulk form, exhibits superior mechanical properties compared to cubic diamond (CD) and holds promise for advanced industrial and quantum applications. Using first-principles calculations, we systematically investigate intrinsic defects, extrinsic dopants, and defect complexes in HD. Our study shows that VC dominates intrinsic conductivity, while Ci is unstable. Among extrinsic dopants, boron acts as a benign acceptor enhancing p-type conductivity, whereas nitrogen and phosphorus serve as effective donors for n-type conductivity. Group II and Group IV dopants, however, introduce high formation energies or neutral charge states with limited impact. Furthermore, VC, MgC and XV defect complexes display multiple spin and charge states within the HD band gap, highlighting their potential as color centers for hosting qubits. These results not only clarify the defect physics of HD but also demonstrate its broader implications for conductivity engineering and quantum technologies.

item.title: Capture fishery profile of Diamondback squid Thysanoteuthis rhombus (Troschel, 1857) in Rizal, Palawan, Philippines
item.description: The diamondback squid, locally known as “dalupapa,” is a high-value marine species commonly landed in Rizal, Palawan, Philippines. However, essential fishing information remains limited. Hence, this study provides the first documentation of the Thysanoteuthis rhombus (Troschel, 1857) fishery, specifically its focused were on fishing operation, seasonality, bait types, monthly catch per unit effort, gear characteristics, and fishing grounds. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews using printed questionnaires from 16 respondents with more than five-year experiences for diamondback squid fishing. All data were processed and analyzed using MS Excel, while fishing grounds were mapped with QGIS software. Fishing operations typically begin between 0300H and 0500H and end between 1300H and 2300H, resulting in a total fishing duration of nine to 18 hours per day. These operations occur five to 10 days per month, totaling 54 to 126 hours of fishing time monthly. Commercial fishing vessels with 3.02 to 9.03 gross tonnage are equipped with 52-160 jig sets, capable of catching 35-400 individual squid. The fishing season spans from February to November, with peak activity occurring between May and September. Commonly used baits include Rastrelliger kanagurta, Exocoetus sp., and T. rhombus fins. Monthly CPUE ranges from 0.03 to 0.08 kg/js/hr. Fishing gear typically consists of two jiggers attached to a hanger, with a 545 m long mainline connected to three Styrofoam buoys. Most fishing grounds are located in the southern part of West Philippine Sea waters. Further research is recommended to deepen understanding of the diamondback squid fishery in Rizal, Palawan.

item.title: From Growth to Performance: Emerging Frontiers in Diamond Materials for High‐Performance Devices
item.description: ABSTRACT Diamond's ultra‐wide bandgap, high carrier mobility, extreme thermal conductivity, and chemical robustness make it a promising platform for next‐generation optoelectronic, electronic, photonic, and thermal technologies. This potential is increasingly unlocked by rapid advances in chemical vapor deposition, enabling precise material synthesis and integration. This review adopts a “growth‐to‐performance” perspective to evaluate emerging frontiers in diamond research. We first highlight critical progress in diamond synthesis, including large‐area single crystal and polycrystalline diamond growth, heteroepitaxy, low‐temperature deposition, and advanced doping strategies. We then examine how these upstream material advancements directly dictate downstream performance across three core technological pillars. In optoelectronics and electronics, these material breakthroughs enable diamond photodetectors, high‐voltage p – n diodes, Schottky barrier diodes, and field‐effect transistors based on both p ‐ and n ‐type diamond channels. In photonics, advances in nanofabrication and heterogeneous integration are expanding diamond's role in nonlinear optics, integrated photonics, and quantum technologies. In thermal management, diamond heat spreaders integrated with wide‐bandgap semiconductors, coupled with advances in thermal metrology and phonon‐transport modeling, enable superior heat dissipation and reliability. By connecting synthesis with emerging applications, this review outlines the critical pathways through which diamond is poised to play a transformative role in high‐performance technologies across electronics, photonics, and thermal management.

item.title: Long‐Term Bio‐Spin Readouts Enable Decoding Immune‐Imposed Stress at the Single‐Cell Level
item.description: Electronic spin dynamics represent a fundamentally important yet largely unexplored state parameter of living cells, offering stable sensitivity to intracellular paramagnetic environments associated with cellular stress responses. However, how immune-imposed intracellular stress evolves over time and relates to divergent single-cell outcomes remains unclear, owing to the lack of continuous and nonconsumptive readouts. Here, we establish a long-term bio-spin readout based on nanodiamonds hosting nitrogen-vacancy centers as inheritable intracellular spin reporters, enabling continuous spin relaxometry in living cells. By integrating population-level ROS-associated paramagnetic stress profiling with long-term single-cell tracking in Hela and A549 cancer cells during coculture with activated macrophages, we identify three characteristic oxidative-stress trajectory patterns-remote immune stress, immune evasion, and apoptosis-whose distinct temporal dynamics cannot be resolved by endpoint assays alone. Longitudinal bio-spin measurements reveal that immune pressure is encoded not only by instantaneous oxidative levels but also by the temporal accumulation and regulation of intracellular stress. An empirical bio-spin transition range provides an operational reference for distinguishing recoverable stress responses from apoptosis-associated trajectories, while characteristic completion times capture the interaction- and cell-type-dependent kinetics of stress evolution. Together, this work establishes bio-spin dynamics for resolving immune-imposed stress histories and their associations with divergent cellular outcomes in living systems.

item.title: Sub-melt nanosecond pulsed-laser induced densification and strain-field relaxation in single-crystal diamond
item.description: Dislocations and polishing-induced defect networks in synthetic diamond generate local strain fields that broaden Raman features and limit optical, thermal, and electronic performance. Sub-melt laser annealing has emerged as a route to repair near-surface defects without graphitization, yet quantitative evidence of densification, defect depletion, and property recovery remains limited. Here, we show that nanosecond pulsed-laser annealing (PLA) can relax dislocation-associated strain in single-crystal CVD diamond by compacting and reorganizing the damaged near-surface region. Single- and two-pulse PLA were applied, and structural evolution was quantified using co-registered ISO 25178 white-light interferometry, depth-resolved Raman spectroscopy, and cross-sectional STEM with geometric phase analysis (GPA). Across a 5x6 grid(n = 30), responsive regions show large reductions in local slope (Sdq 45-65%), developed area (Sdr 60-90%), height spread (Sp, Sz 30-65%), void volume (Vv 57-60%), and roughness amplitude (Sa, Sq 48-57%), consistent with densification of ~4-6.5 nm. Raman profiling reveals narrowing of the diamond line and improved spectral uniformity to depths of ~2-3 {\mu}m, indicating relaxation of dislocation-mediated strain beyond the compaction layer. STEM-GPA strain maps confirm smoother strain fields, reduced hotspots, and redistribution of localized strain concentrations after PLA. These results show that sub-melt PLA reduces dislocation-driven strain by compacting surface-connected free volume and reorganizing defect networks. The approach provides a scalable path to upgrade industrial-grade diamond including homoepitaxial, heteroepitaxial, and polycrystalline CVD to low-defect, device-ready surfaces relevant to high-power electronics, photonics, and quantum substrates.

item.title: Construction of a hierarchical h-BN/DLC composite coating on Ce-doped plasma electrolytic oxidation film for enhanced corrosion resistance of aluminum alloy
item.description: To address the inherent microporosity and inadequate long-term corrosion protection capacity of plasma electrolytic oxidation (PEO) ceramic coatings deposited on 6063 aluminum alloy substrates, a hierarchical Ce-doped PEO/h-BN/diamondlike carbon (DLC) composite coating architecture was fabricated via combined hydrothermal pore sealing and plasma enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD) post treatment routes. The microstructure, chemical composition, and corrosion behavior of the coatings were systematically characterized using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Raman spectroscopy, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), potentiodynamic polarization, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). The results demonstrated that hydrothermal treatment effectively introduced h-BN nanosheets into discharge channels and the micropores of the Ce-doped PEO coating. XPS, Raman, and FT-IR analyses confirmed the successful incorporation of h-BN while preserving its characteristic layered structure. Subsequently, a continuous DLC film containing typical sp 2 /sp 3 hybridized carbon bonds was successfully deposited by PECVD. Among all tested processing parameter combinations, the composite coating modified with 1 g·L -1 h-BN hydrothermal sealing followed by 60 min PECVD deposition delivered optimal comprehensive anticorrosion performance, featured by a minimum corrosion current density of 1.76 × 10 -9 A·cm -2 and the highest impedance response in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution. The significantly improved anticorrosion performance originates from the dual synergistic barrier effect derived from h-BN nanosheet pore plugging and the dense DLC outer capping layer. Specifically, h-BN nanosheets effectively reduced pore connectivity and prolonged the diffusion path of corrosive species, whereas the dense DLC overlayer served as additional physical barrier that suppressed electrolyte penetration and interfacial charge transfer. This study provides valuable experimental guidance and theoretical support for the design of graded ceramic-carbon composite protective coatings for aluminum alloys serving in high chloride marine environments.

item.title: Configuration of Multi-phase Interlayers for Thermal Conductivity Enhancement of Diamond/Al Composites
item.description: Interface design is critical for enhancement of interfacial bonding and thermal properties of diamond/Al composites as promising thermal management materials. Herein, we propose a new strategy combining in-situ formation of WC (W 2 C)-W coatings and gas pressure infiltration (GPI) process to construct diamond-WC (W 2 C)-W-Al 5 W interlayers to improve the interfacial bonding and thermal properties of diamond/Al composite. The microstructure of the modified coatings and their effect on interfacial bonding and thermal properties of diamond/Al composites were examined. By altering deposition time in only several minutes, the thickness of the coatings ranged from ∼100 nm to ∼400 nm was tailored. Results showed the interfacial bonding of the composites was greatly improved, while the thermal conductivity was initially increased with the thickness and decreased with a maximum thermal conductivity of 677 W/mK achieved. Besides the moderate thickness of W interlayers, the high thermal conductivity was also attributed to the interface configuration with the following characteristics: small amount of W carbides on diamond side, uniform and dense W metal interlayer in middle, as well as W-Al intermetallic sublayer on Al side. The successful configuration of diamond-WC (W 2 C)-W-Al 5 W-Al interface greatly promoted the balance of the interfacial thermal resistance and interfacial bonding to maximize the thermal conductivity of the composites, which was among the first-class team reported for diamond/metal composites modified by W-related coatings. This study offers a feasible method to prepare effective W coatings for modifying interfacial bonding and enhancing the thermal properties of diamond/Al composites.
