item.title: Characterisation of hybrid lattice structures based on triply periodic minimal surfaces and strut-based topologies
item.description: This work presents a systematic experimental campaign characterising the elastic and strength properties of a novel class of hybrid lattice structures obtained by combining triply periodic minimal surfaces (TPMS), namely Schwarz Primitive (Scp) and Gyroid (Gyr), with polyhedron-based open-cell structures (POCS), namely Diamond (Dia) and Kelvin (Kel). Hybrid configurations were generated by varying the volume fraction of each constituent under both fully-filled (FULL) and partially hybridised (HALF) infill strategies, fabricated by fused filament fabrication using polylactic acid (PLA), and tested under uniaxial quasi-static compression to characterise the compressive modulus, yield strength, plateau stress, and specific energy absorption (SEA), with mechanical responses described through Gibson–Ashby power-law scaling relations. The effective compressive stiffness is primarily governed by the TPMS parent topology, with the POCS contribution becoming appreciable only at specific volume-fraction combinations. The Scp(uc48,vf5)+Dia(uc24,vf3)–FULL configuration approached the Hashin–Shtrikman upper bound at the corresponding relative density, while Schwarz Primitive–Kelvin hybrids exhibited elevated stiffness–density exponents. For energy absorption, Kelvin-based configurations yielded systematically higher SEA than their Diamond-based counterparts, with Gyr(uc48,vf1)+Kel(uc24,vf3)–FULL recording the highest quadratic SEA coefficient ( 𝐴 = 1 3 8 . 0 J/g), while Kelvin-based Gyroid hybrids in HALF configurations achieved peak efficiencies of 𝜂 m a x = 9 1 . 5 4 % . These findings demonstrate that the mechanical response of TPMS–POCS hybrids is governed by the topological interaction between parent geometries rather than by their individual properties alone, providing a quantitative basis for the design of architected materials requiring a compromise between stiffness, energy absorption, and deformation stability.

item.title: Jet-induced recirculation and cuttings transport of a hybrid drill bit with a central conical cutter for offshore deep and ultra-deep drilling
item.description: The bottom-hole flow around hybrid drill bits with a recessed central structure involves strong interactions among impinging jets, local recirculation, and cuttings transport, which directly affect cleaning efficiency. In this study, the bottom-hole flow and particle migration of a recessed hybrid drill bit with a central conical cutter and multi-blade structure are investigated using a coupled computational fluid dynamics and discrete phase model (CFD-DPM), with validation against a published particle image velocimetry (PIV) flow-field benchmark and full-scale experimental cuttings removal results. The baseline flow field shows that nozzle jets strike the bit face and generate a strong radial sweeping flow. At the same time, recirculation develops in the recessed center and in the regions between adjacent blades. These flow structures enhance local agitation, but they also create low-velocity zones that trap particles and delay their removal. Parametric analyses are carried out to examine the effects of pump rate, concave height, and nozzle angle on cuttings transport. The results show that cleaning performance depends on the balance between jet-driven entrainment and recirculation-induced retention. Increasing pump rate improves cuttings removal at low and moderate levels. However, excessive jet strength intensifies recirculation and promotes particle trapping. Within the investigated parameter range, the most favorable cleaning performance is obtained at a pump rate of 20 L/s, a concave height of 35 mm, a polycrystalline diamond compact (PDC) nozzle angle of 25°, and a central cutter nozzle angle of 7°. These results clarify the flow features governing cuttings transport in recessed hybrid bit geometries and support hydraulic design for deep and ultra-deep drilling.

item.title: Boron-doped diamond activation of peroxymonosulfate for the safe and complete mineralization of the anticancer drug dacarbazine: role of the oxidant in controlling toxic by-products
item.description: Anticancer drugs are emerging contaminants of increasing concern, as their mutagenic and cytotoxic character poses a risk to aquatic ecosystems, and their treatment must ensure not only removal of the parent compound but also the avoidance of equally hazardous transformation by-products. Yet the electrochemical degradation of dacarbazine (DTIC), a widely administered anticancer drug, has not been previously investigated. This study evaluated the electrochemical activation of peroxymonosulfate (PMS) and peroxydisulfate (PDS) using a boron-doped diamond (BDD) anode to degrade DTIC in water, benchmarked against the electrolysis of SO 4 2- and Cl - at current densities of 5, 10, and 50 mA cm -2 . The Cl - system achieved the fastest DTIC removal and the lowest energy consumption, driven by Cl • radicals, but the progressive conversion of reactive chlorine into chlorate and perchlorate limited mineralization and generated persistent chlorinated by-products. PMS and PDS enhanced SO 4 •- production relative to SO 4 2- alone, as confirmed by quenching experiments, improving both removal and mineralization. Complete DTIC mineralization was achieved exclusively with PMS at 50 mA cm -2 , supported by the full disappearance of all transformation products and carboxylates detected by LC-MS and IC. In contrast, the SO 4 2- and PDS systems accumulated a persistent intermediate predicted to be more toxic than the parent compound. These results establish BDD-mediated PMS activation as the most effective and environmentally sound strategy for DTIC treatment in water, uniquely capable of achieving complete mineralization while avoiding the toxic chlorinated and persistent by-products generated by the other systems.

item.title: A Hybrid CFD-XGBoost Framework for Thermal-Hydraulic Performance Prediction of Perforated Pin-Fin Heat Sinks with Different Geometries
item.description: The thermal-hydraulic performance of perforated pin-fin arrays is critically influenced by fin geometry, perforation configuration, and flow conditions. This study presents an integrated computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and machine learning framework to systematically investigate and predict the heat transfer and pressure drop characteristics of circular, square, and diamond-shaped pin fins with single, double, and triple perforations. High-fidelity CFD simulations provided detailed insights into flow structures, turbulence intensity, and convective heat transfer mechanisms, revealing that fin geometry strongly governs wake development and turbulence production, while perforations effectively moderate pressure losses. The resulting CFD dataset was employed to train Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) regression models, which accurately predicted pressure drop and heat transfer coefficients, achieving coefficients of determination exceeding 0.93 and 0.99, respectively. The proposed hybrid CFD-AI methodology enables rapid and reliable performance evaluation, offering a powerful tool for the design optimization of perforated pin-fin heat sinks in advanced thermal management applications.

item.title: Removal of turning marks from aluminum alloy mirror surfaces using ion beam planarization
item.description: In theory, mirror-like optical surfaces made of aluminum alloys provide exceptional reflectivity across a wide range of wavelengths, from the deep ultraviolet to the far infrared. However, waviness resulting from single-point diamond turning tool marks and other manufacturing defects can significantly reduce actual reflectivity, particularly in the visible and ultraviolet spectra. In order to use aluminum alloy mirrors for applications requiring wavelengths below the infrared range, the machining marks on these mirrors must be removed. Ion beam planarization efficiently smooths surfaces by transferring the flat surface of a sacrificial layer into the underlying base material using ion beam etching. In this study, the ma-N2400 series photoresist was characterized as a planarization layer. The photoresist was shown to effectively embed the characteristic waviness structures originating from ultra-precise diamond turning. No surface roughening was observed on the photoresist or the rapidly solidified aluminum (RSA) 501 base substrate during ion beam etching using CF 4 process gas. Substantial reduction of the tool mark amplitude was observed for diamond-turned RSA 501 mirrors with tool mark periods ranging from 3 μ m to 6 μ m, leading to a roughness decrease from approximately 3 nm to around 1 nm rms.

item.title: Boron-doped diamond electrode as a superior tool for ultra-trace-level voltammetric determination of herbicide penoxsulam at highly positive potential
item.description: The widespread use of penoxsulam (PXN), a triazolopyrimidine sulfonamide herbicide, necessitates sensitive and reliable analytical methods for environmental monitoring due to its potential ecotoxicological impact. This study presents a novel electroanalytical method for PXN determination using a boron-doped diamond electrode (BDDE) coupled with differential pulse voltammetry (DPV). To the best of our knowledge, this is the first electrochemical study of PXN, exploiting the wide potential window of BDDE, which is particularly suited for the determination of analytes with high oxidation potentials. PXN undergoes an irreversible, pH-dependent and diffusion-controlled oxidation process on BDDE, with optimal conditions found at pH 2.0. Optimized DPV parameters yielded two distinct linear dynamic ranges (1.0 × 10-8 - 2.0 × 10-7 mol L-1 and 2.0 × 10-7 - 1.0 × 10-4 mol L-1), along with an excellent limit of detection of 1.92 × 10-9 mol L-1 and a limit of quantification of 5.80 × 10-9 mol L-1. These results were superior to those reported for chromatographic techniques. The method exhibited high selectivity toward PXN, with no significant interference from common inorganic ions, heavy metal ions, or herbicides up to an interferent-to-analyte ratio of 50:1. Successful determination in untreated, spiked river water samples (recovery 98.2%, bias -1.8%, RSD 2.4%) confirms its practical applicability. This BDDE-based DPV method offers a practical, low-cost, and environmentally friendly alternative for ultra-trace PXN analysis in water samples.

item.title: Phase Transition Selectivity of Graphite Under High Pressure
item.description: Conspectus The transformation of graphite into cubic diamond (CD) or hexagonal diamond (HD) under high pressure represents a prototypical multipathway solid-state phase transition. However, the microscopic origin of phase selectivity remains unclear, and whether HD can exist as a distinct crystalline phase has long been a subject of ongoing debate. Although conventional theoretical frameworks based on thermodynamic stability and static energy barriers provide important insights into the dominant formation of CD, they fail to adequately describe the nonequilibrium transformation kinetics under high-pressure high-temperature (HPHT) conditions and complex stress states and, thus, exhibit fundamental limitations in accounting for the formation of HD in partially transformed products. To address this critical issue, we have recently combined theoretical simulations with experimental validation to propose a new mechanism governing phase selectivity. In this framework, phase selection is governed not by final-state energetics but by the kinetics of the transformation pathway. This perspective bridges the long-standing discrepancy between theoretical predictions and experimental observations and provides a unified physical picture for the competition between CD and HD. Within this kinetic framework, phase selectivity is dictated by the evolution of stacking sequence and the amplitude of interlayer sliding in graphite. Our results show that the formation of CD involves long-range basal-plane sliding (∼1.03 Å), which reconstructs AB stacking into ABC stacking, whereas HD originates from short-range sliding (∼0.39 Å) that preserves AB stacking. Consequently, conditions that promote interlayer sliding and bending favor the formation of CD, while those that suppress sliding and maintain AB stacking favor the formation of HD. These findings provide an atomistic basis for understanding phase selectivity and highlight the critical role of transformation kinetics. Guided by this principle, we achieved the synthesis of fine nano-polycrystalline CD under conditions that promote stacking disorder and interlayer sliding (σx, σy > σz) and high-purity bulk HD under martensitic transformation conditions (σz > σx, σy). In this Account, we systematically summarize the formation mechanisms and anisotropic growth behavior of CD, as well as the formation mechanism of HD, and highlight two synthesis strategies we have developed for producing high-purity bulk HD. These approaches realize indirect and direct transformations under ultrahigh-pressure and relatively lower-pressure conditions, respectively, thereby providing evidence that HD is a distinct phase and providing practical routes for its controlled synthesis. Finally, this kinetic framework not only offers new theoretical guidance for the phase-selective synthesis of carbon allotropes but also provides broader insights into pathway selection in other pressure-induced solid-state phase transitions.

item.title: Fluorination Effects in Hexagonal XY (X, Y = C, Ge, Si, Sn; X ≠ Y) Monolayers and vdW Heterostructures: Insights from Ab Initio Calculations
item.description: Abstract By combining hybrid ab initio electronic-structure calculations that include spin–orbit coupling with phonon-spectrum calculations and molecular-dynamics simulations, we systematically investigate a family of hexagonal XY and fluorinated XYF2 monolayers (X, Y = C, Si, Ge, Sn; X ≠ Y). All compounds are confirmed to be dynamically and thermally stable, with fluorination being exothermic and further enhancing lattice robustness. Fluorination universally drives a transition from planar sp2 to buckled sp3 structures, which strongly affects the electronic structure. For instance, CSi, CGe, and CSn already display sizable gaps (3.28, 2.85, and 1.96 eV, respectively) that shift slightly upon fluorination to 3.21, 2.97, and 2.27 eV. In contrast, narrow-gap systems such as SiGe (0.19 eV) and SiSn (0.41 eV) exhibit pronounced bandgap openings to 1.43 and 1.02 eV, respectively, corresponding to relative increases of ∼653 and ∼149%. GeSn, however, remains a narrow-gap semiconductor (0.33 → 0.28 eV), showing little sensitivity to functionalization. We further investigate the corresponding van der Waals bilayers and trilayers and determine their absolute band-edge positions relative to the vacuum level to evaluate their potential for photocatalytic water splitting. For CSi+CSiF2, SiSn+SiSnF2, and GeSn+SiSnF2 heterobilayers, we identify both type-II and type-III alignments. In CSi-based trilayers, fluorination drives a systematic transformation from a graphitic sp2 lattice to a fully diamondized sp3 lattice, driving substantial hybridization changes and a pronounced reshaping of the band structure.

item.title: Electrochemical Behavior of Neratinib at a Boron-Doped Diamond Electrode: Role of Tween 20 in Interfacial Signal Enhancement
item.description: Abstract Neratinib (NER) is an irreversible tyrosine kinase inhibitor employed in the therapy of HER2-positive breast cancer. In the present research, the electrochemical oxidation of NER at a boron-doped diamond electrode (BDDE) was surveyed with particular emphasis on the act of surfactant-mediated interfacial influences. Cyclic and differential pulse voltammetry were used to characterize the oxidation behavior of NER and to establish an analytical approach for its determination. Among the explored anionic, cationic, and nonionic surfactant species, Tween 20 produced the most proper electrochemical reply, obviously augmenting the anodic peak current and improving signal stability. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) further represented that Tween 20 considerably revised the electrolyte/BDDE interface, increasing the charge-transfer resistance of the ferri/ferrocyanide redox probe from 510 to 1822 Ω. Importantly, this increment in interfacial resistance comprised concurrently with enhancement of the NER voltammetric response, indicating that Tween 20 does not act through a nonspecific acceleration of electron-transfer kinetics. Conversely, the monitored signal enhancement is consistent with affirmative NER–surfactant interplays and a modified interfacial microenvironment that assists the electrochemical accessibility of NER. Scan-rate and pH-dependent investigations defined that NER undergoes an irreversible, predominantly diffusion-controlled oxidation involving proton-coupled electron transfer. Under the optimized experimental conditions at pH 7.02 containing 100 μM Tween 20, the DPV signal was linear the NER concentration between 0.03–1.50 μM (16.7–836 ng mL–1). The limits of detection and quantification were 5.09 nM (2.84 ng mL–1) and 15.16 nM (8.44 ng mL–1), respectively. Overall, the outcomes demonstrate that the analytical enhancement of NER at BDDE originates from surfactant-mediated, analyte-specific interfacial impacts and ensure a mechanistic basis for its sensitive voltammetric determination.

item.title: Wide-Temperature-Range Near-Zero Thermal Expansion via Stuffing-Controlled Dynamics in Diamond-Like Materials
item.description: Abstract Near-zero thermal expansion (NZTE) materials are essential for emerging precision technologies, such as optical instruments and aerospace components. However, existing materials with robust performance over a broad temperature range are limited, especially if functional properties in addition to NZTE are sought. We report a data-driven materials design investigation and find that the zinc-blende structure is an excellent platform for obtaining NZTE and elucidating underlying crystal-chemical principles. Based on these, we introduced vacancy engineering and stuffed-atom incorporation, yielding a series of cubic quaternary chalcogenides AM3M′X4, where linkage ion vibrations are systematically modulated. We found that NaAg3TiS4, NaAg3TiSe4, and RbAg3TiSe4 are promising NZTE candidates with coefficients of thermal expansion below 2 × 10–6 K–1 over extended temperature windows (300–600 K). These are semiconducting materials distinct from low-thermal-expansion oxides. We explain the NZTE via the synergistic contributions of lattice softening, rigid-unit tilting, and linkage-ion transverse vibrations to the negative Grüneisen parameters. The stuffing of the zinc blende-based lattice provides a chemical way of tuning the linkage-ion transverse modes, thus controlling the thermal expansion in order to obtain NZTE.

item.title: Investigating Layered Cratonic Lithosphere in the Fennoscandian Shield
item.description: Abstract Cold, thick, and chemically depleted lithosphere with high seismic velocity and low attenuation characterizes continental cratons. However, discrepancies between xenolith‐based thermal constraints and those inferred from surface‐wave seismic models, together with the widespread observation of mid‐lithosphere discontinuities, challenge the traditional view of a simple cratonic lithospheric structure. Improving constraints on lithospheric layering is therefore essential for understanding the thermal and compositional structure of the cratonic upper mantle. In this study, we develop a three‐dimensional model of vertically polarized shear‐wave velocity (Vsv) in Fennoscandia through the joint inversion of Rayleigh wave phase velocities and S‐to‐P receiver functions, resolving both absolute velocities and strong vertical gradients. Compared to models derived from phase velocities alone, our results show that the highest velocities (>4.7 km/s) are located deeper, predominantly at ∼140–210 km depth. We compare the seismic model of the Fennoscandia craton interior with Vsv predictions based on depleted peridotite compositions along xenolith‐derived geotherms. After accounting for anelasticity and radial anisotropy, we find that the high velocities observed deeper than ∼150 km can be explained with a moderate diamond fraction (∼0.5 vol.%) combined with a colder geotherm than estimates based on standard xenolith thermometry, while remaining consistent with xenolith constraints. In the shallow lithosphere, slower‐than‐predicted shear‐wave velocities are best explained by the combined effects of radial anisotropy and the presence of carbonate and/or hydrous minerals introduced by metasomatism. The layered seismic structure revealed in this study provides new insights into the thermal and compositional architecture of cratonic lithosphere and its formation and modification.

item.title: Using X-ray free electron lasers to explore extreme states under quasi-static compression
item.description: The exceptional brilliance of X-ray free electron lasers (XFELs) combined with quasi-static compression in diamond anvil cells (DACs) has enabled novel time-resolved methods for probing extreme states of matter. Coupling serial X-ray techniques with dynamic drivers for rapidly changing pressure and temperature, these studies offer insight into phase equilibria, chemical reaction kinetics, and geophysical processes. Here, we present the current state-of-the-art XFEL techniques used for DAC research, including serial X-ray heating, pulsed laser heating, and rapid compression. Essential questions for future investigation are also highlighted, regarding the interactions of intense X-rays with samples at high pressure and associated non-equilibrium states.

item.title: The MuFusE large-volume diamond anvil cell for exploring muon-catalyzed fusion at higher pressures and temperatures
item.description: A new large-volume diamond anvil cell (DAC) has been developed for the Muon-catalyzed Fusion (μCF) Experiment (MuFusE), enabling the compression and heating of deuterium-tritium (d-t) mixtures to pressures and temperatures needed to advance μCF research. The MuFusE DAC achieves the large sample volumes necessary for high-precision fusion measurements while integrating cryogenic loading, all-metal sealing, and flexible bellows to maintain a secure environment during cell compression. Combined with remote pneumatic actuation and secondary containment, the DAC safely managed a 25 Ci tritium inventory while providing a clear optical path for in situ measurements of sample pressure and composition via laser spectroscopy. Utilizing 5 mm diameter diamond anvils oriented in the path of a high-intensity muon beam, the apparatus achieved a stable sample volume of 19.2 mm3 at liquid density, pressures up to 933 MPa and temperatures up to 400 K-benchmarks that significantly exceed previously reported limits for static d-t targets.

item.title: Development of an integrated cryogenic diamond anvil cell for photoluminescence of CrSBr
item.description: We present the design and calibration of a cryogenic adapter for a diamond anvil cell (DAC) that enables optical spectroscopy under simultaneous low temperature and high pressure conditions. What differentiates our design from prior efforts is the straightforward construction and opportunity for rapid implementation using common cryogenic hardware. The motivation for this development work arose from room temperature photoluminescence measurements of CrSBr, a chalco-halide that exhibits strong quenching of the emission intensity on approach to the pressure-induced transition near 7.6 GPa. Normalized spectra reveal reversible red and blue shifts of the broad emission band with compression and decompression, consistent with pressure-tuned changes in the inter-layer interactions. To host such measurements, the cryo-DAC adapter provides thermally stable cryogenic operation (with either liquid nitrogen or helium) while maintaining optical access and precise pressure calibration. These measurements demonstrate that compression suppresses exciton-phonon coupling in CrSBr. Construction details, required instrumentation, pressure calibration using ruby fluorescence and temperature control are described. Typical cryogen consumption is 4-5 liters per run.

item.title: A laser heating diamond anvil cell system for high-pressure nuclear resonant scattering at 3-ID, APS
item.description: Nuclear resonant scattering (NRS) provides the basis for powerful synchrotron-based techniques, including synchrotron Mössbauer spectroscopy (SMS) and nuclear resonant inelastic x-ray scattering (NRIXS), which probe the elastic, magnetic, thermodynamic, and vibrational properties of iron-bearing materials and are, therefore, well suited for studying the structure and composition of Earth's and planetary interiors. Here, we report the development and commissioning of a double-sided laser heating system for diamond anvil cell experiments at the 3-ID beamline of the Advanced Photon Source (APS). A key feature of the system is a 7° offset between the x-ray and laser-delivery paths, which positions the near-sample mirrors outside the x-ray path. This design minimizes x-ray absorption, enhances the NRS signal rate during laser heating, improves imaging quality, and significantly reduces thermal drift during extended data acquisition periods. The setup is optimized to match the reduced x-ray beam size available after the APS upgrade, making NRS measurements under extreme pressure-temperature conditions more practical. In addition, the system supports complementary online ruby fluorescence and x-ray diffraction measurements for characterizing samples before and after laser heating. We demonstrate the performance of the system through representative SMS and NRIXS measurements conducted under simultaneous high-pressure and high-temperature conditions.

item.title: Analysis and suppression of Joule heating errors in NV-center high current measurement within enclosed power equipment
item.description: Current measurements are crucial for monitoring power systems, diagnosing faults, and metering energy. The growth of ultra-high-voltage transmission, smart grids, and renewable energy integration has increased the demand for high-precision current sensors. Diamond nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers present a promising platform for these applications because of their high magnetic sensitivity. Nevertheless, most existing studies emphasize performance optimization in open environments with sufficient heat dissipation, largely neglecting the thermal interference caused by Joule heating in enclosed power equipment. This study established a coupled thermal field model to elucidate the temperature distribution and complete error transfer chain from Joule heating to NV energy level shifts, leading to equivalent current errors. To mitigate this thermal error, a dual-channel microwave differential frequency locking method was employed to decouple temperature-induced drifts from the magnetic field signals. The system achieved a sensitivity of 27 mV/A and a measurement error of 0.06%, with an RMS noise of 0.56 mA Hz−1/2 and an Allan deviation stability of 0.4 mA. Significantly, the dual-channel approach reduced the measurement error from 0.83% (single-channel) to 0.06%, demonstrating an order of magnitude improvement under a sustained thermal offset. These findings provide a practical solution for high precision online current monitoring in enclosed power equipment, where Joule heating has long posed a significant challenge to the measurement accuracy.

item.title: Progress in High-Pressure Hydride Superconductors: From Theoretical Predictions to Experimental Breakthroughs
item.description: Abstract The discovery of high-temperature superconductivity in hydrogen-rich compounds at high pressures has reshaped the landscape of condensed matter physics. This review traces the remarkable trajectory of high pressure hydride superconductors, from early conceptual proposals to recent experimental milestones. We begin with the foundational theoretical framework, including Ashcroft's chemical precompression hypothesis and the electron-phonon coupling mechanism that governs conventional superconductivity in these systems. The central experimental achievements are then examined in chronological order: the record breaking 203 K transition in H 3 S at 155 GPa, the near room temperature superconductivity at 250-260 K in clathrate structured LaH 10 , and other experimentally synthesized binary/ternary hydrides with excellent superconducting properties. We also analyze the unifying structural and electronic features responsible for high transition temperatures. Finally, we address persistent experimental challenges, from unambiguous sample characterization to the definitive detection of the Meissner effect, and outline promising strategies toward the ultimate goal of achieving higher superconducting transition temperatures under lower pressures. This review highlights the powerful synergy between first principles theory and diamond anvil cell experiments that has driven this field forward.

item.title: Rising colorectal cancer mortality among young adults in many countries
item.description: An increase in incidence among young adults (generally those under the age of 50) has been reported for multiple cancer types, with colorectal cancer being among the most prominent.1 These trends are worrying, because they could indicate the emergence of new cancer risk factors at younger ages, with important implications for prevention and early detection among populations at risk. A shift in cancer demographics is a cause for concern because it could translate into an increasing cancer incidence among older adults as the younger cohorts age. Alternative explanations for an increasing incidence in young adults must also be considered: an increase in incidence because of improved methods of detection, changing criteria of disease classification that include borderline benign cases, increased uptake in screening, or greater awareness of symptoms leading to earlier or more frequent examinations. Such changes in cancer care or diagnostic artifacts could inflate incidence at younger ages that either would have been clinically undetected or would not have been diagnosed until later in life. Crucially, these artifactual explanations would not be expected to predict a corresponding rise in mortality. It is precisely for this reason that mortality trends serve as the most robust test of whether changing incidence in young adults reflects a genuine shift in disease risk. For all of these reasons, the contribution from Sung et al.2 on mortality trends in colorectal cancer across 49 countries is of particular interest. Using World Health Organization (WHO) mortality data from 1990 to 2023, supplemented by US national mortality data, the authors examined age-standardized colorectal cancer mortality trends among adults aged 25 to 49 years and compared them with adults aged 50 to 79 years across 49 countries. Their main finding was that among adults aged 25 to 49 years, colorectal cancer mortality increased in 18 of 49 countries during the most recent decade, decreased in 15, and remained stable in the remainder. The steepest increases of an average annual percentage change of 3% or more below age 50 were observed in several South American countries, including Paraguay, Uruguay, and Chile, as well as the United Kingdom. These countries demonstrated either more modest increases in mortality above age 50 (Paraguay and Chile) or evidence of decreasing mortality (Uruguay and the UK). Other large countries including Canada, the United States, and Australia, which have recently been the focus of attention on early-onset colorectal cancer, all showed a more modest increase in mortality at ages 25 to 49 of between 1% and 2% per year, alongside decreases at older ages. This divergence of rising mortality in younger adults occurring against a backdrop of stable or declining mortality among older adults is not a statistical curiosity. It is an epidemiological signal, and one that strongly suggests younger generations are experiencing a genuine elevated and worsening risk of colorectal cancer, driven by exposures or risk factor profiles distinct from those of earlier cohorts. An immediate conclusion from these results is that the increase in incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer is unlikely to be explained as an artifact of improved registration, better detection, or changing diagnostic criteria that include more benign forms of disease.2 These phenomena would not be expected to affect disease mortality. These results therefore reinforce the conclusion that the epidemiology of colorectal cancer is changing, and that efforts must be prioritized to understand why. The results do, however, paint a heterogeneous picture of evolving mortality trends. The presence of multiple South American countries among those with the highest rates of increase at ages 25 to 49 suggests that efforts to understand the epidemiology of early-onset colorectal cancer must include a sustained research focus in these countries. In much of Latin America, rising mortality among younger adults mirrors parallel increases among older adults, which points to a systemic challenge in cancer control infrastructure rather than a cohort-specific biological phenomenon. The rapid translation of rising incidence into death in these settings likely reflects limited access to early detection and treatment, underscoring the stark inequities that persist in global cancer care. Implementation of population screening and access of young adults to screening is globally heterogenous.3 Any research focus on colorectal cancer among young adults should not, therefore, distract from primary and secondary prevention efforts at older ages, nor from the urgent need to strengthen diagnostic and treatment capacity across the full age range in resource-limited settings. The results also observed no apparent mortality increase in 31 countries, primarily from Europe and East Asia. Of these countries with a stable or decreasing annual percentage change among adults aged 25 to 49, cancer incidence data from the IARC GLOBOCAN website are available from 18 of these countries over a similar period, and the data indicate an increase in incidence for the majority of them (Figure 1). This is also not a reason for complacency, given the time lag between increases in cancer mortality and those for cancer incidence that were previously reported in a similar group of countries by the same investigators.4,5,6 Estimated annual percentage change (EAPC, solid diamond) in age-standardized incidence rates (ASR, World standard population) per 100 000 population for colorectal cancer among individuals aged 25 to 49 years in countries with reported stable or decreasing mortality. Horizontal whiskers represent 95% confidence intervals. The vertical reference line at EAPC = 0 indicates no change. Estimates with confidence intervals entirely right or left of zero indicate significant increasing or decreasing EAPC, respectively. Countries marked with an asterisk (*) represent subnational data. The figure was generated using the Global Cancer Observatory, Cancer Over Time database and visualization tool (International Agency for Research on Cancer, World Health Organization). Data accessed on June 23, 2026 at https://gco.iarc.who.int/overtime. Data version: Version 2.1. These trends in colorectal cancer mortality confirm that the increasing incidence observed in many countries is real. Increasing incidence suggests that colorectal cancer mortality at ages 25 to 49 could be expected to increase in many of these countries in the forthcoming decades. Particularly worth monitoring are those countries, including Austria, Lithuania, New Zealand, the Netherlands, France, and Czechia, where prior declines in mortality among younger adults appear to be plateauing or reversing, even as mortality among older adults continues to fall. The results do not in themselves provide clues as to the underlying etiology. The authors mention that emerging evidence implicates metabolic health-related factors; however, the current evidence does not yet allow any single etiological pathway to be elevated above others. Formal birth cohort analyses of mortality trends, which the authors call for, will be essential to characterizing when and where inflection points in risk occurred and to informing targeted preventive strategies. Future studies will need to encompass a broad range of hypotheses, employ study designs that enable accurate identification of mutagenic and promotional risk factors, and specifically include those populations, particularly in Latin America and the Caribbean, where the increases in both incidence and mortality are the most striking. The international research community should treat the findings of Sung et al. as a call to action. The clinical implications of these findings require particular emphasis. These results indicate that it is important and urgent to raise awareness of early-onset colorectal cancer (CRC) among primary care providers and that young patients presenting with persistent lower gastrointestinal symptoms are evaluated with appropriate clinical vigilance. Population screening can detect precancerous lesions and cancers earlier, potentially reducing mortality; however, as the authors rightly warn, the benefits of population screening are context-sensitive. In many resource-limited settings, expanding screening coverage is only valuable within a health-care infrastructure that can respond to its findings. The study is not without limitations. The authors acknowledge potential misclassification of CRC deaths, the inclusion of appendiceal and anal cancers deaths in some countries, underrepresentation of low-income regions (particularly Africa and sub-Saharan Asia), and imprecision of estimates in smaller populations. It was not possible to adjust for heterogeneity of stage at diagnosis, access to treatment and care, or population screening infrastructure. Subgroup analyses by CRC subsite could not be conducted without introducing additional misclassification bias, a methodologically appropriate decision. Despite these constraints, the breadth of geographic coverage and the rigor of the joinpoint regression methodology provide a robust foundation for the conclusions drawn. The rise of CRC among young adults is no longer an emerging signal—it is an established trend in a growing number of countries, and mortality data now confirm that lives are being lost. The challenge ahead is threefold: to better understand the biological and environmental drivers of early-onset disease; to ensure that health-care systems recognize and respond to it promptly; and to develop context-appropriate strategies for prevention, early diagnosis, and treatment. item.title: Vector Field Enhancement With Magnetic Flux Concentrators for NV Diamond Magnetometry
item.description: This study introduces a diamond-based vector magnetometer that leverages nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers and an advanced 3-D magnetic flux concentrator (MFC) system. The MFC system amplifies and channels external magnetic fields into the quantum NV sensor while maintaining the vector properties of the magnetic field. The design incorporates multiple orthogonal pairs of triangulars, high-permeability MFC modules hosted by a polymeric 3D-printed scaffold, enabling efficient field concentration within a compact form factor. This multiaxis MFC-pair configuration effectively resolves optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) spectral congestion, facilitating reliable detection of multiple ODMR peak pairs essential for vector-type magnetic detectors operating in the μT magnetic field range. Simulations and experimental results show that the MFCs enhances the magnetic field within the diamond interrogation volume by 144.5 with the gap between the MFC-pair of 0.42 mm. This work underscores the potential of engineered 3-D MFC systems to enhance magnetic vector sensitivity, offering practical solutions for applications, such as navigation, anomaly detection, and biomedical sensing.

item.title: Issue Information
item.description: On the cover: Our cover was designed by Indigenous Quandamooka Australian artist Amanda Diamond, of Yura Bunji Art. In Amanda's words, “The 3 yarning circles show a deepening involvement with Country. The first yarning circle is the beginning of the idea behind conservation and the subsequent yarning circles show walking in the ancestors footprints where they guide you. Guide you through the oceans, the ant mounds, the woods where you find grubs, the emus of the plains and show you which berries to eat and which berries not to. The idea is you don't show Country what's best for it, it shows you!”. Yarning circles hold deep significance for Indigenous Australians as situations in which people exchange information, learn, and share experiences through stories. Our cover reflects the role of Conservation Letters as a space in which the conservation science community comes together to share knowledge and learn respectfully from each other as we travel on our own individual paths, learning from nature and those who have gone before us.

item.title: Experimental Modeling of the Formation Conditions for Pseudo-Secondary Inclusions in Diamond
item.description: Pseudo-secondary inclusions in superdeep natural diamonds, whose formation is associated with metal–carbon melts, represent new sources of information on the mineralogy and geochemistry of the mantle. However, many aspects of their genesis remain contentious. This work presents, for the first time, the results of experimental modeling of the formation conditions of pseudo-secondary inclusions in diamonds obtained under a decreasing temperature regime in the iron–carbon system at mantle P–T parameters. A detailed study of the crystals and inclusions revealed the main factors responsible for the formation of such inclusions. It is established that the dominant stress generators in the crystals are numerous dispersed iron-bearing inclusions ranging in size from 60 to 600 nm. The heterogeneous distribution of dispersed inclusions, controlled by the surface topography of the growing crystal, creates a mosaic structure of the diamond matrix, which favors the formation of stress concentrators. Relaxation of these stresses under decreasing temperature conditions leads to brittle deformation and the formation of cracks along weakened zones. It is found that crack healing due to regeneration and overgrowth by overhanging growth layers ultimately forms pseudo-secondary inclusions. The experimentally substantiated mechanism of pseudo-secondary inclusion formation may represent one of the possible scenarios for the formation of morphologically similar inclusions in natural diamonds and other minerals.

item.title: Reconstruction of chronic Achilles tendon ruptures using a doubled peroneus longus tendon free graft and interference screw fixation: a technical note
item.description: BACKGROUND: The surgical management of chronic Achilles tendon ruptures (CATR) with significant tissue defects (Myerson Type II/III) presents a clinical challenge. Traditional reconstructive methods relying on free hamstring autografts or flexor hallucis longus transfers are often limited by donor-site morbidity, infection risks, or are unavailable in patients with a history of anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction. This technical note describes a refined, tissue-preserving surgical technique utilising a doubled free autologous peroneus longus (PL) tendon graft. METHODS: Under regional anaesthesia and thigh tourniquet control, a targeted 4 cm mini-open lateral incision is performed. The PL tendon is identified, harvested proximally using a tendon stripper, and a concomitant distal side-to-side tenodesis of the PL to the PB is performed to minimise eversion weakness. On the back table, the free PL autograft is doubled to achieve a 10 mm diameter construct. A calcaneal tunnel is drilled using progressive reaming. The free graft is routed through the proximal Achilles stump, passed subcutaneously, and drawn through the calcaneus. Final rigid stabilisation is secured with a 10 × 30 mm Bio-Interference Screw (Arthrex®) with the ankle held in maximum forced equinus to ensure optimal tensioning. Postoperatively, a 4-phase accelerated protocol begins with 3 weeks in a short-leg fibreglass cast under protected weight-bearing. RESULTS/TECHNICAL ADVANTAGES: This technique achieves reliable primary mechanical stability, allowing for early protected loading while minimising soft-tissue stripping in the hypovascular distal Achilles watershed area. The free PL autograft provides an adequate structural match, and complements the translational framework of the Soft Tissue Healing Diamond (ST-Diamond) concept. Furthermore, this approach serves as a potential alternative for middle-aged patients who have a history of prior ACL reconstruction using hamstring autografts, avoiding contralateral donor-site morbidity or the use of allografts. CONCLUSION: The described mini-open free peroneus longus autograft reconstruction with interference screw fixation represents a cautious, reproducible, and biologically sound salvage option for large chronic Achilles tendon defects, balancing mechanical stability with minimal surgical morbidity.

item.title: Prediction of Risk of Cardiovascular Events in Patients With Stable Angina Using Artificial Intelligence: A Systematic Review
item.description: Stable angina pectoris is a prevalent condition with concerning symptoms and an increased risk of myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, heart failure, and mortality. Risk stratification is important in preventive care because the severity of the condition significantly impacts prognosis. With the availability of digital data such as electrocardiogram (ECG) and clinical variables, artificial intelligence (AI) approaches, including machine learning and deep learning, can be beneficial for risk prediction of chronic diseases, such as coronary artery disease (CAD), in patients with stable angina. At the same time, traditional approaches such as Diamond–Forrester, Framingham Risk Score, and PROCAM lag because they rely on linear and population-oriented assumptions. This systematic review, guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020, evaluates AI models that have been developed to predict cardiovascular events in adults suffering from a stable angina condition. Out of 1,250 articles, only five research studies have been included because they predict the risk of cardiovascular diseases in patients suffering from stable angina. Data modalities in these studies include longitudinal electronic health record (EHR) variables, patient-reported outcomes (Seattle Angina Questionnaire), invasive angiography indices (e.g., Gensini score), and 12-lead ECG. With area under the curve (AUC) varying from moderate (about 0.78–0.83) to excellent (> 0.95) based on outcome and data richness, AI enhances discrimination for obstructive CAD and adverse outcomes across studies. This review highlights that there are a limited number of studies on this topic and a lack of clinical validity. Also, the final set of features in model development varies highly. Hence, heterogeneity, a lack of external validation, and implementation limitations exist.

item.title: Open Access Scholarly Publishing and Article Processing Charges: The Perspectives and Experiences of Researchers from Africa in Relation to their Publishing Strategies
item.description: This report presents findings from a survey of 761 researchers from across Africa examining their publishing strategies, experiences and perceptions in relation to Open Access (OA), Article Processing Charges (APCs) and Diamond Open Access. The study focuses on the demand side of scholarly publishing by exploring researchers' publication choices, the financial implications of APCs, perceptions of journal quality and prestige, and awareness and use of different Open Access publishing models. The findings show that journal publishing remains central to research dissemination and that Open Access is widely used by researchers. However, APCs present a significant challenge and may influence researchers' publishing choices, access to publication opportunities and collaboration practices. The study also highlights strong interest in alternatives to APC-based publishing, particularly Diamond Open Access, while identifying challenges relating to its visibility, sustainability, infrastructure and recognition within research evaluation systems. The report concludes that the challenge is not Open Access itself, but the ways in which Open Access publishing is financed and embedded within scholarly communication and research evaluation systems. It makes recommendations aimed at strengthening equitable and sustainable Open Access publishing in Africa, including greater support for Diamond Open Access journals and infrastructure, improved visibility and discoverability, stronger communities of practice, and appropriate recognition of high-quality Diamond Open Access publishing within research evaluation and reward systems.

item.title: J. Compos. Sci., Vol. 10, Pages 465: The Influence of Cavitation Synthesis Nanodiamonds on the Properties of Self-Compacting Concrete
item.description: This study focuses on the influence of chemically pure nanodiamonds produced by cavitation synthesis on structure formation and physical and mechanical properties of self-compacting concrete (SCC) using an analytical approach. The objective of this research was to develop a high-performance, self-compacting concrete with enhanced properties suitable for the construction sector. Chemically pure nanodiamonds produced by cavitation synthesis (KHA-HC) were added to SCC at weight percentages of 0%, 0.15%, 0.3%, 0.45%, 0.6%, and 0.75% of the binder mass. Fresh SCC modified with nanodiamonds was evaluated for density and cone spread diameter. Hardened SCC with KHA-HC was tested for density, water absorption, compressive strength, and axial compressive strength. The most effective KHA-HC content was established at 0.3%, correlating with 13.5% greater compressive strength, 15.1% higher axial compressive strength, and 19.6% lower water absorption. Incorporating KHA-HC into SCC resulted in a wider spread cone as the additive content was raised. The microstructure of SCC containing KHA-HC was found to be more homogeneous with a decrease in void content within the cement matrix. Polynomial relationships for changes in SCC properties as a function of nanodiamond content were proposed. The effectiveness of nanodiamond additives for modifying SCC was demonstrated. Highly effective self-compacting concretes with improved performance properties have been developed, which are suitable for construction.

item.title: Nanomaterials, Vol. 16, Pages 1104: Unexpected Reduction of Eu3+ Ions to Eu2+ on a Nanodiamond Surface: An XPS, NMR, EPR, and Photoluminescence Study
item.description: We present the results of a study of europium-grafted detonation nanodiamond using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR), and photoluminescence techniques. The material was prepared by mixing an aqueous solution of europium(III) nitrate hexahydrate, Eu(NO3)3&middot;6H2O, with a nanodiamond suspension, resulting in ion exchange between Eu3+ ions and protons of surface carboxyl groups and direct grafting of the nanodiamond surface with Eu3+ ions. However, after two years of storage under ambient conditions, the compound exhibits the reduction of ~13% of Eu3+ ions to the paramagnetic Eu2+ state. This unusual finding is discussed in the context of our XPS, EPR, NMR, and photoluminescence data. We propose that this effect can be associated with surface defects and sp2-hybridized graphene-like fragments that act as electron donors to Eu3+ ions. The observed spontaneous partial reduction of Eu3+ to Eu2+ during long-term storage demonstrates that the oxidation state of surface-grafted europium is not completely stable under ambient conditions. This finding is important because even a partial change in the Eu valence may modify the optical and magnetic properties of Eu-grafted nanodiamonds intended for luminescent, sensing, and quantum applications.

item.title: Nanomanufacturing, Vol. 6, Pages 24: Dual-Wavelength Analysis of Nitrogen-Vacancy Center Quantum Magnetometry Enhanced by Uniformly Coated Gold Nanoparticles
item.description: We present a dual-wavelength analysis of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center quantum magnetometry enhanced by uniformly coated gold nanoparticles (AuNPs). An ensemble-averaged model is developed to analyze the AuNP-enhanced stimulated absorption at the 532 nm excitation wavelength and the spontaneous emission at 637 nm. The resulting detected optically magnetic resonance (ODMR) signal profiles are simulated for both enhancement mechanisms. We find that the enhanced stimulated absorption at 532 nm significantly amplifies the ODMR signal intensity without broadening the linewidth, thereby improving the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) without sacrificing the magnetic field sensing resolution. Conversely, enhancing the 637 nm spontaneous emission increases the total photo emission rate but simultaneously broadens the ODMR detection linewidth due to the direct reduction in the effective spin coherence time of excited states by the enhanced spontaneous rate. The dual-wavelength analysis provides valuable design guidance for the development of low-cost spin-coated AuNP-enhanced NV-center quantum magnetometry technologies.

item.title: INVESTIGATION of PHYSICAL RISK FACTORS in NATURAL STONE QUARRIES AND ESTIMATION OF PM CONCENTRATIONS WITH M5P DECISION TREE
item.description: In this study, particulate matter (PM) concentrations (TSP, PM10, PM2.5, and PM1), as well as noise and ground vibrations, were measured and evaluated during monolamella and diamond wire cutting operations in two travertine quarries in Sivas province. PM concentrations released during the monolamella process exhibited a wider distribution compared to the diamond wire cutting method, posing a higher health risk to workers. PM measurement data did not exhibit a normal distribution, supported by the significant difference between the arithmetic mean and standard deviation. Due to the wide distribution, calculated Leq(PM) values were close to the upper limit of the data range. Therefore, the use of histogram analyses in addition to arithmetic means could yield more realistic and representative results. When PM measurement data were evaluated according to the arithmetic mean, the measured values were generally below the legislative limit values. Conventional regression methods were inadequate in estimating PM concentrations; instead, the M5P decision tree algorithm was successfully implemented, with correlation coefficients exceeding 0.88 in all tests. Ground vibration measurements conducted according to the TS ISO 2631-1 standard were below the limit values, while noise levels measured according to the TS EN ISO 9612 standard were mostly acceptable.

item.title: Why Healthcare Needs Design Thinking
item.description: Healthcare transformation initiatives systematically fail despite decades of reform and billions in investment. The $4.3 trillion US healthcare system and £200+ billion NHS continue experiencing declining outcomes, workforce burnout, and operational inefficiency. Current approaches—Lean management, change management, digital transformation, reorganisation, and leadership development—address symptoms rather than root causes because they lack understanding of how to design systems around human needs. Design thinking offers a fundamentally different paradigm. Unlike traditional approaches that begin with predetermined solutions, design thinking starts with deep empathy for stakeholders, prototypes, and tests solutions before full implementation, and iterates based on real-world feedback. The Double Diamond framework—comprising Discover, Define, Develop, and Deliver phases—provides structure for this methodology. Crucially, healthcare professionals already practise sophisticated design thinking through clinical decision-making. This chapter argues that design thinking can transform healthcare across multiple domains: reducing clinical trial costs, improving patient flow and operational efficiency, enabling world-class care for underserved populations at reduced cost, and fundamentally redesigning care delivery from hospital-centric to patient-centred systems. The methodology addresses healthcare&s;s unique constraints while providing practical frameworks for sustainable transformation.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Steenstra

item.title: Every Clinician Is Already a Design Thinker
item.description: Healthcare&s;s transformation crisis appears insurmountable: ageing populations, chronic disease burden, and workforce shortages demand change, yet billions spent on management consultants and imported methodologies yield negligible results. This chapter reveals why: we’ve been solving the wrong problem. Through detailed clinical case analysis, the author demonstrates that experienced clinicians already practise sophisticated design thinking methodology—they simply call it ‘clinical reasoning.’ The diagnostic process maps precisely onto the Double Diamond framework: divergent information gathering, convergent problem definition, divergent solution generation, and convergent implementation with continuous adaptation. This isn’t coincidence but convergent evolution: both methodologies evolved identical cognitive architecture because navigating complexity demands it. Yet healthcare systematically excludes this expertise from transformation leadership. A 1983 UK policy recommendation separated clinical work from management, creating the career bifurcation that persists today. European systems maintaining clinical leadership (50–71% of senior managers) dramatically outperform UK/US models (22–26%) that imported retail and airline management approaches. The transformation challenge reframes from ‘build new capability’ to ‘recognise existing capability.’ Healthcare doesn’t need to teach clinicians design thinking; it needs to empower them to apply their diagnostic methodology at organisational scale.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Steenstra

item.title: Redesigning Clinical Trials
item.description: Clinical trials face a crisis: $1 billion per drug, 15-year timelines, and systematic failure to recruit diverse populations. The problem isn’t effort—it&s;s design. Pharmaceutical development evolved without design thinking, spending less than 10% on understanding problems before rushing to solutions. This chapter reveals how design thinking transforms clinical trials. The Double Diamond framework addresses systematic failures: empathy-driven discovery reveals patient barriers invisible to academic medical centres, co-design with communities prevents costly protocol amendments (saving ~£500,000 each), and decentralised trials bring research to patients rather than demanding patients travel hours for participation. Real-world evidence validates the approach: trials using co-design complete enrolment 40% faster, achieve demographic diversity matching disease prevalence, and require zero major amendments. McKinsey documents 32% higher revenue growth for top design performers; the UK Design Council shows £4–20 return per £1 invested. For pharmaceutical executives facing unsustainable development costs, healthcare leaders pursuing transformation, and clinicians recognising their diagnostic expertise transferring to trial design—this chapter provides the practical roadmap from pilot to organisational transformation.

item.title: Numerical simulation of D-Wave's quantum advantage experiment with time-dependent variational Monte Carlo
item.description: Programmable quantum annealers can realize real-time dynamics of frustrated transverse-field Ising models on large, nontrivial graphs. Recent work by King et al. argued that the classical simulation of such experiments would require exponential computational resources for classical methods such as tensor networks and neural quantum states. Here, we numerically simulate the D-Wave spin-glass annealing protocol with time-dependent variational Monte Carlo (t-VMC) using a correlator state tailored to spin-glass dynamics. For the two-dimensional cylinder, three-dimensional dimer, diamond, and biclique instances considered, at annealing times of 7 and 20 ns, we show that systematically increasing the variational ansatz size enables t-VMC to approximate the final two-spin correlation errors of the quantum processing unit (QPU). We also perform an accurate large-scale simulation of a challenging biclique instance for which no other variational method is known to work, and we find close agreement with the quantum annealer. Through ablation studies, we identify poor Markov-chain mixing, high-variance local-energy estimators, and stochastic Runge-Kutta error estimates as the principal numerical failure modes. We address these numerical issues by using parallel tempering, blurred sampling and an importance-weighted differential equation solver, thereby clarifying the numerical requirements for stable, large-scale t-VMC simulations. Our results extend the frontier of classical simulation while providing a realistic assessment of the computational costs of simulating quantum dynamics at this scale.
item.dc:creator: Roeland Wiersema

item.title: A stronger upper bound on the D-chromatic index
item.description: For a graph $G$, a proper edge coloring of $G$ is called a D-coloring if every diamond subgraph of $G$ is rainbow. Let $χ'_D(G)$ be the D-chromatic index of $G$, which is the smallest integer $k$ such that $G$ admits a D-coloring with $k$ colors. Let $Δ$ be the maximum degree of $G$. The only known Brooks-type upper bound on $χ'_D(G)$ is $\frac{9}{16}Δ^2 + \frac{1}{2}Δ$, given by a greedy coloring. In this paper, using a probabilistic method, we obtain the first improvement upon this upper bound by proving that $χ'_D(G) \le (1-c)\frac{9}{16}Δ^2$ for some $c > 0$ and sufficiently large $Δ$.

item.title: The Euler Product Bifurcation Theorem: Intrinsic Multiplicative Field Horizons and the Overhaul of Continuous Transcendental Approximations for ζ(s)
item.description: Abstract: This research presents the mathematical architecture of the Euler Product Bifurcation Theorem (EPBT), demonstrating that the classical monolithic Euler product splits into two interlocking, asymmetrical field horizons governed by prime index parity: the Plus Horizon and the Minus Horizon. By treating the multiplication domain as dual expansion and compression operators rather than a single continuous sequence, this framework demonstrates that the prime spectrum intrinsically regularizes its own pole boundaries from the inside out. High-precision numerical verification across a 3,000,000-point discrete prime lattice reveals a permanent topological curvature residue against classical additive baselines, which vanishes asymptotically as the scale dimension reaches higher integer states. The simultaneous intersection of these split operators yields a stable, characteristic quadratic field polynomial free from transcendental approximations, establishing a discrete gauge field framework that uncovers a deterministic structural equilibrium within the prime landscape. Version 2.0 Change Log & Technical Revision Brief Release Date: September 1, 2026 This major version upgrade transitions the EPBT from a real-valued scalar model into a unified, cross-dimensional matrix gauge field theory. All internal mathematical systems, scripts, and tables have been structurally aligned to resolve continuous truncation errors down to an absolute bit-level precision tolerance. Integration of the Dirichlet Condition Constraint (Section 1.1): Formally integrated the structural proofs detailing how continuous-time transcendental integration forces discrete counting spaces to satisfy Dirichlet convergence criteria. This section establishes the explicit origin of continuous smoothing bias and proves that classical circular functions introduce a permanent peak truncation error by artificially clipping the natural, jagged density fluctuations of individual primes. Empirical Data Hardening (Section 5 & Appendix): Overhauled the Global Metric Dataset to replace all non-numeric text placeholders with the concrete, uncompromised real numbers computed directly across the 3,000,000-prime coordinate lattice. All numerical limits, linear trace tension chords, and characteristic polynomial coefficients are now explicitly logged to a standard decimal precision profile. The Pole Residue Discovery (Section 5.2): Secured the deterministic proofs identifying the permanent macroscopic topological residue (\(\delta_{s=1} = +0.0002847698\)) that emerges when the uncompressed field product intersection is evaluated directly against Mertens' Third Theorem (\(e^\gamma \ln p_N\)) at the singular pole. Cryptographic Precision Parameters (Section 5.3.1): Appended an engineering operational review establishing the vital role of the EPBT matrix gate as an absolute precision lock. This section details why preserving bit-level tolerances beneath \(10^{-156}\) is required to eliminate spatial misalignment and truncation drift when tracking massive primes scaling up to 155 decimal digits. Analytic Continuation & Negative Reflection Spaces (Section 5.4): Expanded the framework to withstand testing inside the negative integer domain (\(s < 0\)). At \(s = -2\), the matrix gate functions as a natural regularizer for divergent arithmetic series, mapping a discrete Casimir balance anchor before continuous smoothing acts on the space. Complex Field Overhaul & Critical Line Convergence (Section 6): Transitioned the 2D Hermitian Matrix Gate into a complex phase-rotation engine operating directly along the critical line (\(s = 1/2 + it\)). This chapter mathematically proves the preservation of the Hermitian state (guaranteeing purely real eigenvalues) and demonstrates that non-trivial zeros correspond to physical, non-commutative Phase-Lock Resonance Coordinates where the Functional Trace Scalar satisfies a localized minimum. Comprehensive Bibliography Expansion (Section 8): Added authoritative peer-reviewed references (including Hardy, Dusart, Lamzouri, Diamond & Pintz, and Lapidus) to provide full, independent scientific verification for the comparative product biases and spectral matrices introduced in this version.

item.title: Articutechnica
item.description: Articutechnica collects fifty-eight papers by Parker Emmerson (who alsopublishes as Yaohushuason) into a single continuous volume of 1,217pages, arranged in nine parts: Preface; Prerequisites; TopologyBriefings; Interactions Anterolateral; Q-Daisy Networks and MergedPipelines; The Book of Loops; Tachyons, Cauchy–Schwarz Developments,Cosmology and Extraordinary Particles; Connector Theory and ThePythagorean Operator; and Synthesis. The journey runs from point-set and non-commutative topology, throughthe anterolateral algebra of energy-tagged forms, into the self-similarworld of q-daisy networks and their operator pipelines (including theInfinity Diamond Matrices and the Diamond Matrix Method), onward tophenomenological velocity, the PV–A∞ program, Majorana and Bell–CHSHdevelopments, the loops and their fractal logical mitosis, and finallyto Connector Theory and the Operator Pythagoras Theorem that gives thecollection its subtitle. A closing gestalt synthesis reads the corpusas one construction and proves a velocity–dimension bridge: thevelocity of a split writes itself into the Hausdorff dimension of aCantor boundary. Every chapter is a complete paper, reproduced exactly as it compilesfrom its own source; papers are grouped by theme rather than by date.The accompanying archive contains the full LaTeX source of allfifty-eight papers with their figures and generating Python programs,the master file, and reproducible build and repair scripts, so that thevolume can be rebuilt from source. The edition is typeset withilluminated part pages and initials; the cover is computed from thecorpus's own exotic-loop map Z ↦ Z² − Z̄ + C. KEYWORDS anterolateral algebra; q-daisy networks; phenomenological velocity; connector theory; operator Pythagoras theorem; non-commutative topology; energy numbers; fractal logical mitosis; exotic loops; choiciotomy; Infinity Diamond Matrices; Cantor boundary; Hausdorff dimension; Bell–CHSH; Majorana fermions; PV–A∞ transform; sweeping nets; mathematical physics; formal logic; collected papers ADDITIONAL NOTES The author also publishes under the name Yaohushuason. Interior papers carry their original author lines. The volume was assembled and typeset in August–September 2026; the source archive rebuilds it with ./build.sh (TeX Live, pdflatex). The cover image is generated by build_cover.py from the corpus map.

item.title: V3 Architecture — Complete Materials Reclassification by Phase (200 Materials, Including Alloys)
item.description: This deposit presents a COMPLETE RECLASSIFICATION OF ALL MATERIALS by phase,based on the V3 Architecture. The traditional classification by type (metals, polymers, ceramics) is OBSOLETE. The V3 Architecture demonstrates that:1. ALL materials follow the same phase laws2. Classification by type is arbitrary and scientifically obsolete3. Classification by PHASE allows prediction of ALL properties4. Alloys follow the same phase laws as pure materials5. Materials can be DESIGNED ON DEMAND by controlling phase This study analyzes 200 real materials including:- Pure metals (40): Steel, Al, Ti, Cu, W, Ni, Co, Fe, Zn, Pb, Ag, Au, Pt, etc.- Alloys (40): Stainless steels, Al alloys, Ti alloys, Brass, Bronze, Inconel, Hastelloy, Superalloys, etc.- Polymers (25): PE, PP, PVC, PTFE, Nylon, PC, PEEK, Epoxy, etc.- Ceramics (25): Alumina, Zirconia, SiC, Si3N4, WC, TiC, etc.- Composites (20): Carbon fiber, Kevlar, C/Epoxy, Glass/Epoxy, etc.- Gases (20): H2, O2, N2, F2, Cl2, Br2, I2, etc.- Semiconductors (10): Si, Ge, GaAs, GaN, SiC, etc.- Exotic materials (20): Metallic glass, Aerogel, Shape memory alloys, etc. For each material, the code calculates:- Phase tension (mV) from rupture stress- V3 phase class (7 classes from UltraStable to Critical)- Predicted rupture (MPa) — without testing- Predicted melting point (K) — without testing- Predicted boiling point (K) — without testing- Deviation from empirical data (%) RESULTS:- 200 materials analyzed- 100% validation of phase classification- Average deviation for rupture: < 1 %- Average deviation for melting: < 2 %- Average deviation for boiling: < 2 %- All materials converge to the same phase laws THE NEW V3 PHASE CLASSIFICATION:┌───────────────────────┬──────────────┬──────────────────────┐│ Class │ Φ (mV) │ Examples Steel, Ti, Ni ││ Phase_Ductile │ -50 ≤ Φ < -48│ Al, Cu, Ag, Polymers ││ Phase_Soft │ -48 ≤ Φ < -45│ Pb, Sn, Zn, Bi ││ Phase_Volatile │ -45 ≤ Φ < -40│ O2, N2, Cl2 ││ Phase_Critical │ Φ ≥ -40 │ Po, At, controlling phase- Replace empirical materials science with predictive phase science- Unify metals, polymers, ceramics, and composites under ONE law IMPLEMENTATION:- Code written in Ada SPARK- 100% item.title: Exceptional Compared With What? Estimand Transfer and Background-Mortality Benchmarking in the Diamond Princess Passenger Cohort
item.description: Abstract Background The Diamond Princess became an influential early source for SARS-CoV-2 case- and infection-fatality estimates because it provided an unusually well-enumerated, older cohort. Those analyses addressed infection denominators, delay to death and age adjustment. We asked a different question: when the reported death count is interpreted at the passenger-population level, is age- and time-expected background mortality numerically negligible? Methods We conducted a descriptive benchmark analysis of 2,666 passengers. Expected all-cause deaths were calculated from official pre-pandemic life tables using passenger age structure and observation windows. The primary window was 3 February–15 April 2020 (72 days). The calculation used Japan 2019 mortality, 45% male/55% female allocation within each 10-year age band, mean single-year mortality within bands and no healthy-traveller reduction. Sex-specific annual probabilities were converted to interval risks before weighting. The reference expectation was compared with 13 passenger deaths reported in Japan as outbreak-associated/COVID-related; a sensitivity outcome added one death after Australian repatriation. Alternative start dates, national life tables, sex allocations, within-band age assumptions and healthy-traveller stress tests were examined. Results The primary calculation yielded 8.33 expected background deaths. The background-mortality benchmark ratio was 1.56 for 13 reported deaths and 1.68 for 14. With demographics fixed, four national life tables yielded 8.33–12.41 expected deaths and ratios of 1.05–1.56. Japan-only all-female and all-male structural bounds yielded 5.64 and 11.62 expected deaths. Across aligned 70-, 72- and 86-day anchors, ratios for 13 deaths ranged from 1.31 to 1.61. Conclusions Background mortality was not numerically negligible relative to the reported Diamond Princess death count. This does not reclassify deaths or estimate excess mortality. It identifies an estimand-transfer problem: the same outbreak death count can inform both infection-fatality and population-mortality questions, but these require different reference structures. 要旨 背景 ダイヤモンド・プリンセス号は、比較的高齢で、かつ人数が例外的によく把握されたコホートを提供したため、SARS-CoV-2の症例致死率および感染致死率を推定する初期の重要なデータ源となった。これらの分析は、感染者分母、死亡までの遅れ、年齢調整を扱っていた。本研究は別の問いを設定した。すなわち、報告された死亡数を乗客集団レベルの死亡として解釈するとき、年齢と観察期間から期待される背景死亡は、数値的に無視できるほど小さいのか、という問いである。 方法 乗客2,666人を対象とする記述的ベンチマーク分析を行った。公的なパンデミック前生命表を用い、乗客の年齢構成と観察期間から期待全死因死亡数を算出した。主解析期間は2020年2月3日から4月15日までの72日間とした。中心計算には日本の2019年死亡率を用い、各10歳階級内で男性45%・女性55%を割り当て、階級内の単年齢死亡率の平均を用い、健康旅行者効果による低減は行わなかった。男女別の年間死亡確率は、加重前に観察期間リスクへ変換した。参照期待値は、日本でアウトブレイク関連/COVID関連として報告された乗客死亡13人と比較し、感度分析ではオーストラリア帰国後の死亡1人を加えた14人も用いた。開始日、参照生命表、性別配分、年齢階級内の年齢仮定、健康旅行者ストレステストを変更した感度分析を行った。 結果 主解析では、期待背景死亡数は8.33人であった。背景死亡ベンチマーク比は、報告死亡13人に対して1.56、14人に対して1.68であった。人口構成を固定して4か国の生命表を用いると、期待死亡数は8.33~12.41人、比は1.05~1.56となった。日本2019生命表のみで全員女性・全員男性という構造的境界を置くと、期待死亡数はそれぞれ5.64人、11.62人であった。4月15日を同一の転帰把握終点として70日、72日、86日の開始日アンカーを用いた場合、13人死亡に対する比は1.31~1.61であった。 結論 ダイヤモンド・プリンセス号で報告された死亡数に対して、背景死亡は数値的に無視できる大きさではなかった。この結果は死亡の再分類を行うものでも、超過死亡を推定するものでもない。本研究が示すのは「推定対象の移行(estimand transfer)」の問題である。同じアウトブレイク死亡数でも、感染致死率を問う場合と集団死亡を問う場合とでは、必要な参照構造が異なる。
