Carapace rectangular, smooth; suborbital margin subovate, lined with evenly spaced small, rounded granules; stridulatory ridge with 22–24 subconical tubercles, inner half of ridge with 5–7 fungiform tubercles, last tubercle being largest, with cap of tubercle fully corneous; epistome triangular. Cheliped massive, carpus short, inner carpal spine blunt, palm broad and lower margin lined with 2 rows of granules gradually increased size towards dactylus; upper margin of dactylus granulated; P 2 – P 4 of similar length, relatively broad, merus length ca. 2.5 times width, tympanum present; carpus and propodus of P 2 and P 3 with dense patch of plumose setae in male. Female carapace rectangular, suborbital margin subovate, lined with evenly spaced small, conical granules; stridulatory ridge with 22 subconical tubercles, densely arranged, inner half ridge with 4–6 small fungiform tubercles; chelipeds small, subequal; vulvae on sternite 6, comma-shaped, vulvar cover absent. Description. Carapace (Figs 1 A, 1 C, 2 A, 7 A) transversely rectangular, smooth, ca. 1.5–1.6 times wider than long, maximum length medially; regions poorly defined; microscopically granular, with low ridges and transverse setae. Front broad, ca. one-quarter distance between external orbital angles, deflexed, lateral margins converging anteriorly, frontal margin bilobed with gently convex margins when viewed dorsally, median concavity shallow (Fig. 1 C). Gastrocardiac groove defined; cardiac region swollen, well defined by clear ridge with anterior margin deeply curved medially, straight, sloping posteriorly. Branchial regions with short transverse ridges or crests, with short stellate setae. Posterior carapace margin straight, broadly rounded laterally, with broad rim; supraorbital margin smooth, sinuous, sloping obliquely; external orbital angle forming acutely triangular, sharp tooth, separated from remainder of margin by distinct concavity; anterolateral margin minutely denticulated (Fig. 2 A, G), first anterolateral tooth low, without trace of second tooth or lobe; lateral margins slightly diverging posteriorly. Eyestalks elongated, peduncle thick, short; cornea bulbous (Figs 1, 2 C, 3 A, C, E). Male: Suborbital margin subovate, lined with evenly spaced small rounded granules; stridulatory ridge immediately below infraorbital margin long, starting outside lateral edge of orbit, appressed against margin medially, before bifurcating around median part of suborbital region (Fig. 3 A, B, D, G); outer (lower) half of main stridulatory ridge with 22–24 subconical tubercles, each with corneous tip, gradually becoming larger medially, inner half of ridge with 5–7 fungiform tubercles, last one being largest, with cap of tubercle entirely corneous (Figs 2 C, 2 E, 3 D, 3 G, 3 H); upper part of bifurcated stridulatory ridge shorter than lower ridge, extending to near base of ocular peduncle, lined with subconical tubercles without corneous tip (Fig. 3 D, G); additional short ridge of stridulatory granules below and subparallel to outer part of main stridulatory ridge, with 25 rounded tubercles, each with corneous tip, outer tubercles largest, closely packed, becoming smaller and more spaced out inwards (Fig. 3 H). Female: Similar to male, except with additional short ridge of stridulatory granules below outer part of main stridulatory ridge with 30 rounded tubercles and curving downwards along inner part (Fig. 3 A, B, D). Suborbital, subhepatic, sub-branchial and pterygostomial regions covered with evenly spaced short stellate setae (Fig. 3 A – H); external orbital tooth lined with long papposerrate (Fig. 3 I); row of long pappose setae on anterolateral tooth (Figs 2 G, 3 B, 3 G – I). Maxilliped 3 (Fig. 2 I) moderately bulging or convex, completely closing buccal cavity; merus longer than ischium, surface with evenly spaced obliquely stellate setae; antero-internal angle of ischium triangular, apically blunt, rounded, produced along edge of merus; ischium anterior margin deeply curved with line of plumose setae densely arranged, surface with few stellate setae, granules absence. Chelipeds (Fig. 4 A, C) stout, heterochelous; merus trihedral, inner and outer margins granular; carpus short, rhomboidal, armed with short inner tooth. Major chela of adult male holotype distinctly swollen, palm broader, slenderer, margin lined with granules gradually increased size towards dactylus; dactylus upper margin granulated, with broad gap when fingers closed, cutting margin with large, rounded teeth on proximal half and small evenly sized teeth on distal half; pollex cutting margin with small, evenly sized teeth along length (Fig. 5 A, B); minor chela similar in form to major chela but proportionately more slender (Figs 1 B, 4 A). Female chelipeds (Figs 5 C, 5 D, 7 C) small, subequal; carpus rounded, inner carpal spine short; palm with 1 row of rounded granules, tip of dactylus and pollex spatulate. P 2 – P 4 length subequal, relatively broad, P 5 shortest. P 2 – P 4 merus length ca. 2.5 times width, about as long as car

item.title: Addressing WoS Quality Criteria: Evidence on Publishing Volume, Continuity and Annual Publication Timeliness, Scholarly Content, Peer Review and Editorial Oversight, English-Language Accessibility, Content Availability, Persistent Identifiers and Bibliographic Traceability, 2020–2026 — L'Europe Unie / United Europe (Paris)
item.description: L’Europe Unie / United Europe (Paris): Evidence Portfolio Addressing Web of Science (WoS) Core Collection Quality Criteria on Publishing Volume and Continuity, Scholarly Content, Peer Review and Editorial Oversight, English-Language Accessibility, Content Availability, Persistent Identifiers and Bibliographic Traceability, 2020–2026 This evidence portfolio documents the publication record, scholarly content, editorial standards, international accessibility and persistent-identifier infrastructure of L’Europe Unie / United Europe (Paris) for the period 2020–2026. Founded in Paris in 2007, the journal publishes peer-reviewed research in European Studies, International Relations, Contemporary History, Political Science, European Law and Security Studies. The verified 2020–2025 corpus comprises 8 numbered issues and 111 scholarly contributions: 99 main-section articles, eight prefaces, introductions or conclusions, and four scholarly book reviews. 72 articles appeared in the 5 issues assigned to 2023–2025, demonstrating substantial recent publishing volume and continuity. All 99 main-section articles have individual records in the Central and Eastern European Online Library (CEEOL). CEEOL provides 107 individual bibliographic records for the documented corpus. According to CEEOL language metadata, 86 of the 99 articles, representing 86.9 per cent of the article corpus, are published in English. Complete issue PDFs provide access to the remaining documented contributions. The portfolio identifies 8 issue-level DOIs and 10 individual-contribution DOIs registered through Crossref for SSRN records. These persistent identifiers complement the journal’s complete issue archive, external catalogue records, issue pagination and bibliographic metadata. Together, these elements facilitate the identification, retrieval, verification and citation of the journal’s scholarly content. The journal’s publicly available editorial procedures specify editorial screening, double-blind peer review by at least two independent scholars, revision procedures, conflict-of-interest rules, authorship requirements, corrections, retractions and appeals. The same peer-review requirements apply to submissions involving members of the editorial board. The journal operates according to a Diamond Open Access model, without publication charges for authors or access charges for readers. The documented publications demonstrate a coherent scholarly focus on European integration, the external relations of the European Union, European institutions, contemporary European history, diplomacy, enlargement, neighbourhood policy, hybrid threats, disinformation, democratic resilience, European security, human rights, artificial intelligence, digital governance and European law. This evidence portfolio directly addresses relevant areas of the Web of Science Core Collection journal-evaluation framework, particularly publishing volume and continuity, scholarly content, peer review and editorial oversight, English-language accessibility, content availability, bibliographic accuracy, persistent identification and scholarly traceability. L'Europe unie does not claim that the journal has already been accepted for Web of Science Core Collection coverage. The portfolio provides direct and verifiable evidence of publication volume, continuity, annual publication timeliness and regularity, scholarly content, peer review and editorial oversight, English-language accessibility, content availability, persistent identifiers and bibliographic traceability. Complementary evidence addressing additional Web of Science Core Collection evaluation dimensions is preserved in separate DOI-bearing Zenodo records within the same dedicated community, “Indexing, Research Impact, Internationalization & Editorial Quality: L’Europe Unie / United Europe Journal (Paris).” Citation impact in Web of Science and Scopus:https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18293270 International authorship across more than 45 universities, more than 25 countries and four continents:https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18317184 High-impact authors associated with Web of Science, Scopus, Oxford University Press and L’Harmattan:https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18293237 Comprehensive international indexing, research-impact, internationalisation and editorial-quality portfolio, 2007–2026:https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22166846 Dedicated Zenodo community containing the interconnected evidence records:https://zenodo.org/communities/indexing-europe-unie/records Taken together, these interconnected and independently accessible records provide a consolidated, transparent and verifiable body of evidence relevant to the Web of Science Core Collection journal-evaluation framework. They document the journal’s sustained publishing activity, editorial standards, international authorship, citation visibility, bibliographic infrastructure, scholarly accessibility and international discoverability. item.title: The Silence Experiment: A Multi-State Protocol for Detecting Consciousness-Dependent Decoherence in Shielded Environments
item.description: This paper specifies a controlled experimental protocol for testing the von Neumann-Wigner interpretation of quantum mechanics, the hypothesis that consciousness plays a role in quantum state reduction, against the prevailing environmental decoherence framework. It measures whether the cognitive state of a nearby conscious observer measurably affects the decoherence rate of a prepared quantum system. The platform places an experienced meditator in EEG-verified states inside a five-layer shielded chamber. A single nitrogen-vacancy centre in diamond measures coherence times across seven consciousness conditions spanning the cognitive-excitation axis, from active cognition to objectless awareness, against an empty-chamber instrumental baseline and a thermal-dummy control cell that reproduces the metabolic heat load of a seated occupant with no observer present. All seven conditions run in one randomised session, so chamber drift is common to the chain and differences out of the within-participant contrasts. Three primary tests are pre-registered at a family-wise threshold of 0.005 one-sided, Bonferroni corrected to approximately 0.00167 per test: an ordered test across the excitation axis, and two orthogonal planned contrasts specified as explicit weight vectors that sum to zero. A fourth, secondary test is the only one that can separate the protective prediction from the suppression pattern, and its non-orthogonality to the first contrast is disclosed rather than corrected away. Both the EEG classifier and the coherence-time estimation pipeline are frozen and lodged before collection, so that neither the independent nor the dependent variable carries unspecified analytic freedom. A pre-registered positive control establishes that the measurement chain is sensitive, not merely quiet, and it is a gate: without it, a null carries no information about effect size. Phase 1 runs on the same chamber with an isotopically purified sample and carries three pre-registered hypotheses of its own, including a coupling-model discriminator and a spectral-density sweep that converts the standard objection to dynamical decoupling into the measurement itself. It is not conditional on a positive Phase 0 result. The protocol is outcome-blinded and is not described as blinded in any stronger sense. Participants and the instructing experimenter cannot be blinded, because the independent variable is an instructed cognitive state, and this is stated rather than glossed. The expected outcome is a null, which is pre-registered as publishable. No calendar timeline is stated anywhere. Session burden is given as a design parameter from which a host institution computes its own schedule. The protocol is pre-registered at OSF and is not peer reviewed; no data have been collected. Changes in this version. Secondary test D is corrected from weights that summed to one rather than zero. The prior weights were not centred under the null and would have been passed by any positive coherence time, and the correction is filed as a timestamped pre-data amendment with its rationale, not as a silent erratum. The transmon Phase 1 is withdrawn and replaced, with the sensitivity comparison retained in the text so the error is visible. Sessions are chained rather than one condition per session, reducing participant burden by roughly a factor of seven. The separate non-meditator resting group is removed, because it placed a between-group boundary inside the ordered test. Suppression is defined by an interval criterion rather than by an indistinguishability claim. Budget figures corrected. No repository identifiers appear in the document.

item.title: Addressing WoS Quality Criteria: Evidence on Publishing Volume, Continuity and Annual Publication Timeliness, Scholarly Content, Peer Review and Editorial Oversight, English-Language Accessibility, Content Availability, Persistent Identifiers and Bibliographic Traceability, 2020–2026 — L'Europe Unie / United Europe (Paris)
item.description: L’Europe Unie / United Europe (Paris): Evidence Portfolio Addressing Web of Science (WoS) Core Collection Quality Criteria on Publishing Volume and Continuity, Scholarly Content, Peer Review and Editorial Oversight, English-Language Accessibility, Content Availability, Persistent Identifiers and Bibliographic Traceability, 2020–2026 This evidence portfolio documents the publication record, scholarly content, editorial standards, international accessibility and persistent-identifier infrastructure of L’Europe Unie / United Europe (Paris) for the period 2020–2026. Founded in Paris in 2007, the journal publishes peer-reviewed research in European Studies, International Relations, Contemporary History, Political Science, European Law and Security Studies. The verified 2020–2025 corpus comprises 8 numbered issues and 111 scholarly contributions: 99 main-section articles, eight prefaces, introductions or conclusions, and four scholarly book reviews. 72 articles appeared in the 5 issues assigned to 2023–2025, demonstrating substantial recent publishing volume and continuity. All 99 main-section articles have individual records in the Central and Eastern European Online Library (CEEOL). CEEOL provides 107 individual bibliographic records for the documented corpus. According to CEEOL language metadata, 86 of the 99 articles, representing 86.9 per cent of the article corpus, are published in English. Complete issue PDFs provide access to the remaining documented contributions. The portfolio identifies 8 issue-level DOIs and 10 individual-contribution DOIs registered through Crossref for SSRN records. These persistent identifiers complement the journal’s complete issue archive, external catalogue records, issue pagination and bibliographic metadata. Together, these elements facilitate the identification, retrieval, verification and citation of the journal’s scholarly content. The journal’s publicly available editorial procedures specify editorial screening, double-blind peer review by at least two independent scholars, revision procedures, conflict-of-interest rules, authorship requirements, corrections, retractions and appeals. The same peer-review requirements apply to submissions involving members of the editorial board. The journal operates according to a Diamond Open Access model, without publication charges for authors or access charges for readers. The documented publications demonstrate a coherent scholarly focus on European integration, the external relations of the European Union, European institutions, contemporary European history, diplomacy, enlargement, neighbourhood policy, hybrid threats, disinformation, democratic resilience, European security, human rights, artificial intelligence, digital governance and European law. This evidence portfolio directly addresses relevant areas of the Web of Science Core Collection journal-evaluation framework, particularly publishing volume and continuity, scholarly content, peer review and editorial oversight, English-language accessibility, content availability, bibliographic accuracy, persistent identification and scholarly traceability. L'Europe unie does not claim that the journal has already been accepted for Web of Science Core Collection coverage. The portfolio provides direct and verifiable evidence of publication volume, continuity, annual publication timeliness and regularity, scholarly content, peer review and editorial oversight, English-language accessibility, content availability, persistent identifiers and bibliographic traceability. Complementary evidence addressing additional Web of Science Core Collection evaluation dimensions is preserved in separate DOI-bearing Zenodo records within the same dedicated community, “Indexing, Research Impact, Internationalization & Editorial Quality: L’Europe Unie / United Europe Journal (Paris).” Citation impact in Web of Science and Scopus:https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18293270 International authorship across more than 45 universities, more than 25 countries and four continents:https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18317184 High-impact authors associated with Web of Science, Scopus, Oxford University Press and L’Harmattan:https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18293237 Comprehensive international indexing, research-impact, internationalisation and editorial-quality portfolio, 2007–2026:https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22166846 Dedicated Zenodo community containing the interconnected evidence records:https://zenodo.org/communities/indexing-europe-unie/records Taken together, these interconnected and independently accessible records provide a consolidated, transparent and verifiable body of evidence relevant to the Web of Science Core Collection journal-evaluation framework. They document the journal’s sustained publishing activity, editorial standards, international authorship, citation visibility, bibliographic infrastructure, scholarly accessibility and international discoverability. item.title: Development of an integrated cryogenic diamond anvil cell for photoluminescence of CrSBr
item.description: We present the design and calibration of a cryogenic adapter for a diamond anvil cell (DAC) that enables optical spectroscopy under simultaneous low temperature and high pressure conditions. The motivation for developing this adapter arose from room temperature photoluminescence measurements of CrSBr, which exhibits strong quenching of the emission intensity on approach to the pressure-induced transition near 7.6 GPa. Normalized spectra revealed reversible red and blue shifts of the broad emission band with compression and decompression, consistent with pressure-tuned changes in the inter-layer interactions. To host such measurements, the Cryo-DAC adapter provides thermally stable cryogenic operation (either liquid nitrogen or helium) while maintaining optical access and precise pressure calibration. Construction details, required instrumentation, pressure calibration using ruby fluorescence, and temperature control are described. Typical cryogen consumption for a full experiment is 4 to 5 liters.

item.title: Growing CAPITOL 4 Life: A Case Study of Co-designed Material for the First 1000 Days Using a Modified Double Diamond Approach
item.description: Abstract Introduction Growing CAPITOL 4 Life is a place-based public health initiative focused on the first 1000 days (F1D), from conception to a child’s second birthday. It sought to strengthen community capacity for early-childhood health by leveraging local knowledge, assets and partnerships, while moving beyond one-way information provision towards sustained learning, empowerment and collective action. This study retrospectively examined the co-design process through the lens of the Double Diamond. Methods Parents, educators, service providers and community stakeholders across Burnie, Circular Head and Devonport, Tasmania, participated in co-design workshops. Engagement spanned government, local government, Aboriginal organizations, libraries and community services. The process was facilitated by a place-based systems-change organization and supported by the University of Tasmania. Community members contributed lived experience alongside professional and academic knowledge, with decision-making remaining largely community-led and guided by the principle of “for the community, by the community.” Results Across the four phases, communities moved from sharing experiences and identifying strengths and challenges (Discover), to refining priorities (Define), developing locally relevant resources and learning approaches (Develop), and shaping feasible delivery models (Deliver). The process centered on the F1D domains of Connection, Nutrition, Caring and Moving and resulted in community-informed Evidence Briefs, workshops and playgroup-based learning. Importantly, the Double Diamond was reflected not as a prescribed sequence, but as a recurring pattern of opening outward to explore and narrowing inward to make sense, prioritize and act. Discussions moved organically between what was working, what was missing, what an ideal future might look like and how communities could move towards it. Discussion The findings suggest that the value of the Double Diamond in public health lies less in adherence to predefined stages than in providing sufficient structure for purposeful exploration while preserving community agency. This flexible approach may support locally relevant, acceptable and trusted solutions, particularly in complex regional settings where effective public health responses must emerge from, rather than be imposed upon, communities.

item.title: Cluster-Glass Freezing with a Ferrimagnetic-like Component in KNa3Co5.74Cu1.26(PO4)6 and Antiferromagnetism in KNa3Cu7(PO4)6
item.description: Abstract The ANa3M7(PO4)6 series unites isostructural alkali A and transition metal M phosphates, arranged from diamond-like chains combined into a triperiodic metallic substructure. Two members of the family, a monoclinic, partially ordered solid solution KNa3Co5.74Cu1.26(PO4)6 and the first triclinic Cu variety KNa3Cu7(PO4)6, were obtained by spontaneous crystallization. Their morphology, chemical composition, and crystal structure were studied by means of electron microscopy, EDS analysis, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction. The symmetry lowering from monoclinic to triclinic in KNa3Cu7(PO4)6 is associated with Jahn–Teller distortion of Cu2+ polyhedra. Thermodynamic measurements have revealed that KNa3Co5.74Cu1.26(PO4)6 exhibits ferrimagnetic-like behavior below TG = 6.4 K. KNa3Cu7(PO4)6 exhibits long-range antiferromagnetic order at TN = 8 K, even though its Curie–Weiss temperature is very high in magnitude, Θ = −93 K. The analysis of the spin exchange interactions in KNa3Cu7(PO4)6 indicates that it is not caused by geometrical spin frustration, but by the fact that its spin–lattice has a layered character with weak interlayer interactions.

item.title: In Vivo Real-Time Detection of Phenylephrine in Mice Using Boron-Doped Diamond Microelectrodes with Simultaneous Video-Based Assessment of Pupil Size
item.description: Abstract Precise quantification of ocular pharmacokinetics remains a critical bottleneck in ophthalmic drug development, primarily constrained by the inability to monitor intraocular concentrations in real time. Current methods typically rely on destructive sampling, which precludes longitudinal assessment in individual subjects. Here, we report an electrochemical platform for time-resolved quantification of phenylephrine in the anterior chamber of living mice using needle-shaped boron-doped diamond microelectrodes. An optimized multistep potential protocol mitigated biofouling and enabled stable monitoring of intraocular drug dynamics while simultaneously assessing pupillary response via video. Across a range of topical doses, intraocular exposure increased with applied concentration, whereas pupil dilation showed a saturating dependence and clear pharmacokinetic–pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) hysteresis, consistent with a temporal lag between local drug availability and physiological response. This platform enables time-resolved in vivo PK/PD analysis and provides a practical framework for evaluating and optimizing ocular drug delivery strategies.

item.title: Anomalous lattice expansion of bcc Ta in helium-loaded diamond anvil cells
item.description: Anomalous lattice expansion of bcc Ta is observed in helium-loaded diamond anvil cell (DAC) experiments near 6 GPa and above 400 K, while co-loaded W, Mo, and Au exhibit normal thermal expansion. The Ta volume expansion increases with temperature, reaching ∼13% near 650 K before plateauing, and is largely retained after recovery to ambient conditions. Time-resolved measurements at 500 K reveal progressive expansion over several hours, consistent with gradual, thermally activated He incorporation. The largely retained expansion during subsequent cooling and holding at 400 K indicates that the incorporated He is predominantly kinetically trapped. The data reveal two distinct regimes: below ∼550 K, modest and spatially uniform expansion consistent with interstitial He trapping at isolated, randomly distributed vacancies; above ∼550 K, He-vacancy cluster growth producing dramatically larger expansion, peak broadening, and a core–shell microstructure revealed by micrometer-resolution x-ray diffraction mapping. These results demonstrate that He is not always a passive pressure medium in DAC experiments and reveal a previously unrecognized regime of He-mediated lattice modification in Ta, complementing conventional ion-implantation studies relevant to nuclear and fusion structural materials.

item.title: A Catalyst: What Does the Belt and Road Initiative Mean for the Next Convergence
item.description: This dissertation examines the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) through the analytical lens of a catalyst for global economic convergence. Rather than treating the BRI as a deterministic development model, this study conceptualizes it as a catalyst, a framework that is both empirically testable and methodologically pluralist, applicable not only to the BRI but also to other large scale infrastructure initiatives. As with any catalyst, three core features define its role. First, infrastructure investment is necessary but not sufficient for sustained development. Second, the ultimate developmental outcome is shaped not by the infrastructure itself but by the preexisting conditions of the recipient economies, including their human capital, institutions, industrial base, and governance, much as a catalyst facilitates but does not determine the reaction pathway. Third, the catalytic effect requires continuous input and can diminish, shift, or even produce adverse reactions when the catalyst itself is poorly deployed or, even when properly built, misaligned with local needs, in which case infrastructure investment may translate into debt rather than growth. Grounded in this framework, the dissertation investigates whether and under what conditions the BRI functions as a catalyst for economic convergence across three distinct temporal horizons, short-term, medium-term, and long-term, each corresponding to a self-contained empirical study that tests different dimensions of the catalytic logic. The short-term study evaluates the China Europe Railway Express (CR Express) on European node cities using a staggered difference in differences design combined with propensity score matching. The findings show that the CR Express has generated significant employment gains and road freight increases, particularly in the service sector, but no measurable effect on per capita gross value added, suggesting that node cities currently function primarily as redistribution hubs rather than sites of value creation. Crucially, these positive effects materialize even in the absence of direct infrastructure investment, representing marginal gains from improved logistics efficiency and connectivity alone. Given the well documented lagged effects of infrastructure on productivity and the limited time horizon of the analysis, these results indicate that the catalyst does work at the margin and suggest that the effects could be more pronounced over a longer period with complementary FDI. The medium-term analysis employs Porter's Diamond Model as an analytical framework for cross regional comparison, supplemented by a ranking based scoring method to evaluate Central Asia's competitiveness relative to Eastern Europe, ASEAN, and South Asia. The model captures six dimensions of competitive advantage: factor conditions, demand conditions, firm level performance, related and supporting industries, governance, and external chances and challenges. For the five quantifiable dimensions, a ranking based scoring system is applied, with regions scored from highest to lowest across each dimension to generate a composite competitiveness profile that reveals relative strengths and weaknesses without imposing arbitrary weights. The sixth dimension, external chances and challenges, is analyzed qualitatively to account for geopolitical shifts, trade realignments, and technological disruptions that cannot be uniformly quantified. The results reveal that Central Asia's structural weaknesses, including small markets, weak industrial diversification, limited institutional quality, and low innovation capacity, constrain its ability to translate infrastructure improvements into sustained growth, despite its resource wealth and strategic location. This finding illustrates the second feature of the catalyst framework, namely that infrastructure improvements are necessary but not sufficient for sustained economic transformation. The long-term investigation addresses a question that cannot be answered by direct observation, as the long run effects of the BRI have yet to materialize. Instead, the analysis proceeds through the logic of economic development. Historically, the East Asian flying geese paradigm established export-led growth as a well recognized pathway for developing economies to integrate rapidly into global value chains and achieve economic takeoff through participation in international division of labor. However, global merchandise trade has stagnated in recent years, while services trade has expanded at a much faster pace. A growing body of scholarship has debated whether services trade could serve as a new engine of growth for latecomer economies, potentially replacing or complementing the manufacturing-led model. This dissertation therefore investigates whether the BRI influences services trade, and if so through which channels, as a way to infer the likely trajectory of its long term catalytic impact. Applying Lewbel instrumental variables and dynamic difference in differences methods to bilateral service trade data between BRI participants and seven major economies, the results show significant positive effects on Africa's commercial service imports, driven primarily by goods related services, particularly maintenance and repair. Sensitivity analysis using an alternative BRI participant list reveals complementary findings: service exports from BRI participants to Germany increased substantially, driven by ICT outsourcing from Romania and other Central and Eastern European countries, reflecting the anticipation and spillover effects of the CR Express pilot phase. These findings demonstrate that the catalytic effect can propagate through indirect channels and may be subject to misalignment if infrastructure does not match local demand. The medium and long-term catalytic impacts discussed above, however, presuppose a sustained and reliable flow of financing. Infrastructure projects in the Global South require massive, long term capital with extended repayment horizons. Many of these countries lack prior experience of sustained economic takeoff and are constrained by weak institutional capacity and limited complementary endowments, making trial and error inevitable and some degree of waste unavoidable. The BRI alone cannot fill this financing gap. To sustain the catalytic momentum and minimize the risk that misallocated capital turns into debt rather than development, broader participation from other infrastructure initiatives and private investors is essential. The dissertation therefore examines the financial sustainability of the BRI, not to defend it against the "debt trap" narrative, but to assess whether the capital base required for medium and long-term catalytic effects can be maintained and whether the conditions for productive capital absorption can be improved. Taken together, the findings suggest that the BRI is best understood as an adaptive, open-ended development experiment rather than a fixed model. Its long-term impact will depend not on physical infrastructure alone but on whether participating regions can build the institutional, industrial, and governance capacities to convert enhanced connectivity into durable comparative advantages, and whether diverse stakeholders can move beyond zero-sum geopolitical rivalry toward inclusive, sustainable growth.

item.title: Comparative Efficacy of Hand, Piezoelectric Ultrasonic, and Diamond-Coated Ultrasonic Instruments for Subgingival Scaling and Root Planing in Periodontitis: a Protocol for Scoping Review
item.description: Purpose This scoping review aims to systematically map and compare the therapeutic effects of hand instruments, conventional piezoelectric ultrasonic instruments, and diamond-coated ultrasonic tips in subgingival scaling and root planing (SRP) for periodontitis. The review will synthesize existing evidence on clinical outcomes (e.g., probing pocket depth, clinical attachment level, bleeding on probing, etc.), root surface morphological changes (e.g., roughness, micromorphological characteristics under SEM, loss of tooth substance/cementum), and procedural parameters (e.g., operating time, patient comfort). It will also identify current knowledge gaps and methodological limitations in the literature. Anticipated Outcomes Through descriptive synthesis and qualitative analysis, this review will summarize the differences in effectiveness and safety across the various intervention modalities, clarify which instruments may offer advantages for specific outcomes, and highlight key areas where high‑quality primary research is urgently needed. The final results will be disseminated as a peer-reviewed academic paper, providing clinicians with evidence-based guidance for selecting subgingival treatment instruments and informing the design of future comparative effectiveness studies.

item.title: Mixed-paragenesis diamond inclusions form during metasomatic fluid evolution (dataset)
item.description: This dataset is related to "Mixed-paragenesis diamond inclusions form during metasomatic fluid evolution", Mikhail et al. 206, GPL. All the data used for this work are provided here. Methodology used to collect/generate the data The dataset comprises geochemical and thermodynamic modelling outputs used to investigate fluid–rock interaction and metasomatism in the mantle. Analytical data (Table S1) were generated through laboratory-based geochemical analyses of natural samples, following established protocols for sample preparation, digestion, and isotopic/elemental measurement. The model outputs (Model I, Model II, and Eclogitic Fluid datasets) were generated using thermodynamic simulations of fluid–rock interaction under high-pressure and high-temperature conditions. These simulations track the evolution of mineral assemblages, fluid compositions, and phase relations during metasomatic processes. Model parameters (e.g. pressure, temperature, bulk composition) were systematically varied to reproduce natural systems and explore reaction pathways. Type of files The dataset includes: * Tabulated geochemical data (analytical results) * Model output files from thermodynamic simulations * Compositional data for fluids, minerals, and bulk systems * Supporting datasets describing input parameters and calculated phase equilibria File formats * .xlsx – Microsoft Excel spreadsheets (e.g. Table S1) * .txt / .dat (within zipped folders) – plain text model outputs and input files * .zip – compressed folders containing grouped model datasets (Model I, Model II, Eclogitic Fluid) Software required to open, visualise and analyse files * Microsoft Excel (or equivalent such as LibreOffice Calc) for .xlsx files * Standard text editors (e.g. Notepad++, TextEdit) for .txt / .dat files * File decompression software (e.g. WinZip, 7-Zip, macOS Archive Utility) for .zip archives For advanced analysis and visualisation: * Scientific plotting and data analysis software (e.g. Python, MATLAB, R) may be used to process model outputs and generate figures * Thermodynamic modelling software (e.g. pMELTS, EQ3/6, or equivalent, depending on user preference) may be required to fully interpret or reproduce the simulations

item.title: Bulk hexagonal diamond remains elusive
item.description: Hexagonal diamond (HD) is an enigmatic polymorph of diamond whose crystal structure, diffraction properties, spectroscopic features and hardness remain controversial. [1–2] This carbon allotrope contains only hexagonal (h) stacking of puckered layers of carbon atoms and displays a complete absence of cubic (c) stacking that is found in the ‘ordinary’ cubic diamond. The use of the mineral name lonsdaleite as a synonym for HD complicates the situation further, despite several studies showing that the type material originally described as lonsdaleite does not represent a discrete phase. Obtaining pure HD would be a step change in diamond research that would resolve many long-standing controversies. A recent study claimed the bulk synthesis of 100-μm to millimeter-sized HD crystals by compressing and heating single-crystal hexagonal graphite. The authors based their identification and structural characterization on in-situ and ex-situ X-ray diffraction (XRD), transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and Raman spectroscopy. They interpreted their data in terms of ~100 nm triple-twinned HD domains. We identified problems with this interpretation and demonstrate that the material is not a highly ordered, pure HD phase, but instead stacking-disordered diamond (SDD) containing both hexagonal and cubic stacking. Our analysis also reveals a new type of intergrowth structure which provides fresh insight into the graphite – HD transition, and may help guide the future synthesis of pure HD.

item.title: Five-year bibliometric analysis of the Journal of the Foot & Ankle (2020-2025)
item.description: Objective: To characterize productivity, document-type composition, authorship, geography, and citation impact of the Journal of the Foot & Ankle (JFA) over its first five years (2020-2025) following its 2020 refoundation. Methods: All peer-reviewed articles published in JFA between January 2020 and December 2025 were retrieved from OpenAlex and cross-checked against Crossref. The 22 articles of the founding issue (V14 N1) were registered under the predecessor journal’s ISSN and recovered separately. Meeting abstracts, articles outside the study period, editorials, and one tribute were excluded. Document type was classified by manual review of each issue’s Table of Contents. Author productivity was measured by leadership appearances (first or last author), country and institution by whole counting at the article level, and citation impact by cumulative counts and the journal h-index. Analysis was performed in R. Results: A total of 334 articles were included, with a mean of 56 per year. Original articles accounted for 68.9%. Unique authors totaled 1,037, with a mean of 5.2 per article. Brazil was the predominant country in 185 articles (55.4%), followed by the United States (10.2%) and Argentina (6.0%). The most productive institution was the Universidade Federal de São Paulo (23 articles). The total accumulated 272 citations with a journal h-index of 6. César de César Netto led the leadership ranking with 15 appearances (14 as senior author). International collaboration had a mean of 10.5%. Conclusion: JFA has consolidated as the principal Ibero-American outlet for foot and ankle research, with a Brazilian-anchored yet regionally inclusive authorship, sustained Diamond Open Access, and an early but rising citation footprint. Level of Evidence IV; Bibliometric, Descriptive Observational Study.

item.title: Structural and dynamical properties of hydrous magmatic liquids at high pressure: insights from Raman spectroscopy observations during diamond anvil cell experiments
item.description: Silicate liquids play a central role in the differentiation and internal dynamics of terrestrial planets by controlling the transport of heat and matter. One of their key properties is viscosity, which can be strongly influenced by pressure. Currently, there is not enough data to develop general models of viscosity at high pressure. Besides, data on the short and medium range order structure of high-pressure silicate melts are insufficient to draw general structural laws and use them to express the effect of pressure on melt properties. Here we present a new method involving an internally-heated membrane diamond anvil cell coupled with a Raman spectrometer. This setup allowed us to acquire in situ Raman spectra of water-bearing sodium aluminosilicate glasses and melts with controlled composition, and to observe how the glass transition temperature, a parameter directly related to melt viscosity, changes with pressure. The results reveal a non-linear behavior of the glass transition temperature with pressure, with a minimum around 6 GPa and a strong increase at higher pressures. The interpretation of undercooled melt Raman spectra shows that this behavior results from a competition between structural compaction, melt polymerization and changes in the coordination of Si, Al network former cations. At pressures above 6-7 GPa, once coordination changes dominate, melts with very different chemical compositions exhibit remarkably similar positive Tg(P) slopes.

item.title: Modeling Carbon-Based Planets with MAGRATHEA
item.description: A planet’s interior structure not only influences its habitability, but it also provides information about the planet’s formation and history. In the quest to characterize the variety of planetary discoveries, the most common practice is to rely on our understanding of the Earth’s differentiated interior structure, with an iron core and silicate mantle as a starting point. However, recent work by C. J. Shakespeare et al. (2025) (https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.3847/1538-3881/adaead) shows that these assumptions may not be true for all planetary systems as the composition of the condensed material can change drastically towards a carbon mantle instead of a silicate one, once the C/O ratio of the system approaches and exceeds ∼ 0.9 . In an effort to more fully understand the range of possible planetary bodies, we added the ability to model carbon-based mantles to our open-source planetary interior solver, MAGRATHEA. The newly added carbon mantle includes three relevant allotropes of carbon: graphite, diamond, and BC8 (body centered cubic with eight atoms per cell).

item.title: Materials, Vol. 19, Pages 3709: AlSi10Mg Heat Sinks for Passive Cooling: Convective–Radiative Performance of Finned and Triply Periodic Minimal Surface Designs via Laser Powder Bed Fusion
item.description: Increasing power densities in electronic systems require efficient passive thermal-management solutions. This study numerically compares five DMLS-compatible AlSi10Mg heat-sink architectures: perforated planar-fin, curved radial-fin, Schwarz P, BCC diamond and gyroid designs. Conjugate heat-transfer simulations incorporating conduction, natural convection and surface radiation were performed under an identical 18 W thermal load. Performance was evaluated using surface temperature, thermal resistance, temperature uniformity and convective&ndash;radiative heat dissipation. The gyroid achieved the lowest average surface temperature (82.02 &deg;C) and combined thermal resistance (3.30 &deg;C W&minus;1), whereas the BCC diamond provided the greatest temperature uniformity (UI = 0.035). Radiation contributed 46&ndash;73% of total heat dissipation and was highest for the gyroid architecture. The results demonstrate that increased surface area alone does not ensure improved passive cooling; thermal performance depends on the coupled effects of topology, airflow accessibility and radiative heat exchange. Gyroid TPMS architectures therefore provide a promising DMLS-compatible approach for passive thermal management.

item.title: Metals, Vol. 16, Pages 955: Synergistic Optimization of Mechanical and Biological Properties in LPBF-Fabricated Porous Ti6Al4V Scaffolds via Structural Design and Surface Modification
item.description: Porous Ti6Al4V scaffolds with tailored architectures are promising candidates for orthopedic implants due to their potential to mitigate stress shielding and enhance osseointegration. In this study, porous Ti6Al4V scaffolds with different unit cell geometries and porosities were fabricated via laser powder bed fusion (LPBF). The effects of pore structure and porosity on mechanical and biological properties were systematically investigated. The results show that both elastic modulus and compressive strength decrease with increasing porosity, and a critical porosity of 70% is identified for uniform structures, beyond which their load-bearing capacity becomes insufficient; however, a radial gradient design can overcome this limitation. Alkali heat treatment generates a uniform sodium titanate nanowire coating, which significantly improves wear resistance and promotes apatite deposition, thereby enhancing bioactivity. Among all samples, the hexagonal diamond structure with 70% porosity exhibits the highest cell viability. To overcome the trade-off between mechanical strength and biological performance inherent in uniform porous structures, a radial gradient porous scaffold with an average porosity of 72.5% was designed. The gradient structure demonstrates improved mechanical strength while maintaining high bioactivity, indicating its potential for optimized orthopedic implant applications.

item.title: Polymers, Vol. 18, Pages 2114: A Coarse-Grained Molecular Dynamics Model for Analysis of Mesoscale Carbon Nanothread Structures
item.description: Diamond nanothreads (DNTs) represent a promising class of one-dimensional carbon nanomaterials for next-generation structural applications. However, exploring their mesoscale collective properties remains computationally prohibitive via all-atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Here, we present a physically consistent coarse-grained model tailored for both zigzag (DNT-I) and tubular (DNT-II) nanothreads. By establishing an energy equivalence framework between all-atomistic MD simulations and molecular mechanics, the bonded potentials (stretching and bending) and non-bonded Lennard-Jones parameters were derived. Moreover, a degree of coarse-graining r0 = 6 &Aring; was determined, which well preserves the interfacial cohesive energy and axial sliding behavior of all-atomistic models. Using the established coarse-grained potentials of DNTs, a high glass transition temperature (Tg = 1485 K) was predicted, and a cooperative intermolecular sliding mechanism that governs the plastic deformation of crystalline DNT aggregates under uniaxial tension was revealed.

item.title: Profilometric analysis of OptraPol®, OptraGloss®, and Sof-Lex® polishing systems on surface roughness of Endure Nano composite: An in vitro study
item.description: Abstract Aim: The aim of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of commercially available polishing systems, 3M Sof-Lex ® Diamond Polishing Spiral, Ivoclar Vivadent OptraPol ® , and Ivoclar Vivadent OptraGloss ® , on the surface roughness ( R a ) of Septodont Endure Nano composite using a profilometer. Materials and Methods: Thirty-six disc-shaped specimens (8 mm diameter and 4 mm thickness) of Endure Nano composite were fabricated using a custom-made mold and polymerized with an LED light-curing unit. All specimens were sequentially finished under running water with 400-, 600-, and 1000-grit silicon carbide abrasive papers to standardize surface texture and then stored in saline at 37°C for 24 h. The samples were randomly divided into three groups ( n = 12): Group I – Sof-Lex ® Diamond Polishing Spiral (3M ESPE, St Paul, MN, USA), Group II – OptraGloss ® (Ivoclar Vivadent AG, Schaan, Liechtenstein) Composite Kit Restoration Polisher and Group III – Optra Pól ® (Ivoclar Vivadent AG, Schaan, Liechtenstein) Composite Restoration Polisher; the polishing procedure for all three polishing systems was performed according to manufacturer instructions. Surface roughness ( R a ) was measured at three points per specimen using a profilometer, and mean values were calculated. Results: A statistically significant difference was found among the groups ( P < 0.005). OptraGloss ® ( R a = 0.2163 µm) demonstrated the lowest surface roughness, indicating the smoothest finish, followed by OptraPol ® ( R a = 0.4080 µm). In contrast, 3M Sof-Lex ® ( R a = 0.5086 µm) exhibited the highest surface roughness. Conclusions: OptraGloss ® was the most effective polishing system, producing a smoother surface compared to both OptraPol ® and 3M Sof-Lex ® .

item.title: Diamond-Shaped Strength Control Prediction Model for CSG Dam Concrete Considering the Compressive Strength and Vebe Test Results
item.description: 본 연구에서는 CSG 댐 콘크리트의 압축강도와 비비시험 결과를 동시에 고려하여, 배합 단계에서 배합 가능 여부를 사전에 판정하는 마름모꼴 강도관리 예측모델을 제시하였다. 재령 28일 강도시험 결과에 의존하는 기존의 사후적 품질관리의 한계를 보완하기 위하여, XGBoost 기반의 압축강도 예측모델과 비비시험 판별모델을 구축하고 이를 통합하였다. 압축강도 예측모델의 ±10 % 이내 정확도는 93.0 %를 나타냈으며, 비비시험 판별모델은 정확도 98.1 %를 보였다. 두 모델을 통합한 통합 판정 알고리즘은 실측 기반 검증에서 정확도 90.6 %를 나타냈다. 통합 판정 알고리즘을 골재 유형별로 적용하고 W/C를 변화시켜 목표강도와 시공성을 동시에 만족하는 배합 가능 범위를 마름모꼴 영역으로 예측･시각화함으로써, 배합 단계에서 선제적으로 품질을 관리할 수 있는 기반을 제시하였다.

item.title: Superconductivity of Tellurium Polyhydride with Tc above 90K
item.description: We report experimental diacovery of superconductivity (SC) in tellurium (Te) polyhydride. The compound was synthesized at high pressure and high temperature conditions using a diamond anvil cell combined with a laser heating system. Subsequent in situ transport measurements at high pressures, performed as a function of temperature and applied magnetic field, revealed a superconducting transition with a critical temperature Tc about 91 K at 263 GPa. The superconducting phase is assigned to TeH4 with characterized face shared TeH12 cage forming quasi molecular H2 units based on synchrotron x-ray diffraction experiments. Analysis of the SC behavior at magnetic fields yielded a Ginzburg Landau (GL) coherence length of approximately 54 angstroms. Tellurium polyhydride thus becomes another chalcogen polyhydride superconductor in addition to the landmark discovery of the first polyhydride high Tc SC SH3.

item.title: Dual-Gradient Plasmonic qBIC Metasurface for Time-Resolved In Situ Optimization of Molecular Vibrational Sensing in Water
item.description: Metaphotonic platforms based on quasi-bound states in the continuum (qBICs), harnessing strong near-field enhancement and deeply subwavelength field confinement, provide a versatile framework for surface-enhanced infrared absorption (SEIRA) spectroscopy. However, real-time molecular sensing in water using qBIC metasurfaces remains challenging. First, strong water absorption in the mid-infrared region damps qBICs and obscures weak analyte signals. Second, conventional metasurfaces rely on discrete arrays targeting individual wavelengths and coupling conditions, increasing the device footprint and fabrication effort required to match the qBIC to the molecular vibrational resonance. Here, we present a dual-gradient plasmonic qBIC metasurface with diamond-shaped resonators for in situ molecular vibrational sensing in water, where spatially encoded gradients in the scaling factor and asymmetry parameter independently control the qBIC spectral positions and radiative rates, respectively, across a 1000 um x 700 um footprint. Building on this capability, we experimentally monitor lipid vesicle dynamics in real time and resolve the carbonyl vibrational signature despite the unavoidable water absorption. We then directly identify the optimal sensing condition and track its evolution across the spatially encoded parameter space. The results establish a compact single-chip strategy that combines adsorption-kinetics monitoring, vibrational fingerprint detection, and on-chip optimization, opening opportunities for investigating biological dynamics under aqueous conditions.

item.title: Adhesive System Effect on Metal Bracket Bond Strength to Different Microhybrid Composite Brands
item.description: Aim: The aim of this in vitro study was to evaluate the shear bond strength (SBS) of orthodontic metal brackets bonded to microhybrid composite surfaces from different composite brands and to investigate the effects of composite brand and adhesive system on these values. Material and Methods: Two different brands of microhybrid composites (Charisma Smart and Herculite™ Classic) were included in this study. Surfaces received either 37% phosphoric acid etching or diamond-bur roughening. The Trulock adhesive system (Light-Activated Bonding Resin + Adhesive Paste) or the BracePaste system (MTP Primer + Adhesive) was used for bracket bonding, resulting in eight experimental groups (n = 16 per group; total n = 128). Before bond-ing, 10,000 thermal cycles were applied to the specimens; an additional 5,000 cycles preceded SBS testing. After debonding, residual adhesive was scored with the Adhesive Remnant Index (ARI). SBS values were analyzed using the Kruskal–Wallis and Mann–Whitney U tests, whereas ARI score distributions were evaluated using the Fisher–Freeman–Halton exact test with Monte Carlo estimation. Results: The highest mean SBS was obtained with the BracePaste system on bur-roughened Herculite™ Classic (HC) (8.46 ± 1.36 MPa), whereas the lowest occurred with the Trulock sys-tem on acid-etched Charisma Smart (CS) (0.55 ± 0.39 MPa). Bur roughening yielded higher SBS than acid etching for both composite brands. ARI scores differed significantly among the groups (P < 0.001). Conclusions: The composite brand and adhesive system influence bond strength. Clinically, evaluating both with the surface preparation method is critical for successful bonding.

item.title: Reposisi Rumah Sakit Umum Daerah sebagai Simpul Strategi Tempat dalam Arsitektur Cross-Border Medical Access di Indonesia: Sebuah Tinjauan Naratif
item.description: Introduction: The high number of Indonesians seeking healthcare services abroad, particularly in Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand, has led to leakage in national healthcare spending and reflects challenges to the competitiveness of domestic healthcare services. The Indonesian government has responded to this phenomenon by developing Cross-Border Medical Access (CBMA), including the establishment of Health Special Economic Zones (KEK) and strengthening the medical tourism ecosystem. However, the role of Regional General Hospitals (RSUD) in the CBMA strategy remains understudied. This article aims to analyze the position, opportunities, and repositioning strategies of Regional General Hospitals (RSUD) in the development of CBMA in Indonesia. Methods: The study employed a narrative literature review method by examining scientific publications, policy reports, and documents related to CBMA, medical tourism, and hospital development for the 2015–2026 period. The analysis was conducted thematically by integrating the concepts of place marketing, Porter’s Diamond, resource-based view, and healthcare governance. Results: The study shows that most RSUDs still play a passive role as regional referral service providers. However, several regional public hospitals (RSUD) possess geostrategic potential, excellent services, and connectivity to border areas and tourist destinations, which can be developed as cross-border medical access hubs. The analysis yields a three-tier repositioning framework: RSUD as a regional service provider, a center of excellence based on local excellence, and a strategic hub for cross-border medical access. Conclusion: RSUD have the potential to be repositioned as a strategic actor in the development of cross-border medical access. This repositioning has the potential to increase the competitiveness of regional healthcare services, reduce leakage of healthcare spending abroad, and support sustainable regional health and economic development.

item.title: The Cyclotomic Framework As A Minimal Structural Core
item.description: A minimal structural core · CC BY 4.0 · consolidated deposit 10.5281/zenodo.21836329 The Diamond One curve, one polynomial, one unit — the framework's forced lattice. PAUL WATFORD · INDEPENDENT RESEARCHER · ROYAL TUNBRIDGE WELLS, UKORCID 0009-0003-9724-7674 · hep-th (hep-ph, gr-qc) Every displayed claim is forced — a theorem or a chain of theorems — and machine-verified at machine precision. The paper is written to be attacked. 2 classical objects (curve + polynomial) 1 unit — M_Z, the only empirical input 1 premise — a stable vacuum 7 forced, interlocking facets 0 dimensionless dials to tune The one physical claim What the vacuum is Before the theorems, the statement they all serve — named in physics, not left as a convenient math object. The framework's foundational identification E : y² = x³ + 1 The vacuum of the theory is this elliptic curve — the curve of j-invariant zero, with complex multiplication by the Eisenstein integers ℤ[ω] — read at its order-3 symmetry point τ₀ = ω. This is a physical identification: a claim about what the ground state is, not a theorem of pure mathematics. Everything downstream is forced; the identification stands or falls with those forced consequences, and is falsifiable through them. What it says physically, if true to nature The ground state is a two-dimensional boundary conformal field theory at the most symmetric point of its moduli space — the order-3 fixed point, where an extra ℤ/3 automorphism acts. The one period of that vacuum, the nome |q| = e^(−π√3), fixes every mass scale: there is one scale in nature because there is one period. Time is not put in by hand — the boundary algebra is a type-III₁ factor carrying a unique intrinsic modular flow (Tomita–Takesaki, Connes), and that flow is the Lorentz boost between the two anchors; the arrow of time is the vacuum's own modular automorphism. Newton's constant is the inverse of a counting number — the four points of the curve over the field of three elements, G = 1/|E(𝔽₃)| = 1/4 — reappearing as the Chern–Simons level of the 3D bulk the boundary induces. The particles, couplings, and cosmological numbers are arithmetic invariants of this one curve. Three classical facts keep the claim from floating: the anchors ω and i are the only elliptic points of PSL(2,ℤ) and the zeros of the two generators of the modular-form ring (they cannot be post-selected); ω is independently singled out by Montgomery's minimal-theta theorem; and gravity is the curve's own point-count. Nothing enters the core the geometry does not force. The forced lattice Seven facets, each forced, each interlocking From the two objects, seven facets. They are a lattice, not a list — remove any one and the others lose their forcing. Facet Statement Tier 1 anchors The curve has j = 0 and CM by ℤ[ω]; its only elliptic points are τ₀ = ω (order 3) and τ₁ = i (order 2) — the zero loci of E₄ and E₆, the two generators of the whole ring of modular forms. They cannot be post-selected. Forced 2 nome Read at τ₀, the curve's period gives the single nome |q| = e^(−π√3) — the one transcendental, the curve's own period. Everything dimensionless is a power of |q| or a cyclotomic ratio; the framework is curve-native. Forced 3 ladder The colour count is the ramification N_c = 3. The integer ladder is the cyclotomic factors of x¹²−1 at N_c: k_H = 2, k_grav = 4, 13, 10, 7, k_GUT = N_c³−1 = 26, w = 6. Pure arithmetic. Forced 4 boost The non-torsion unit bridging the two anchors is ε = 2+√3, fundamental unit of ℚ(√3). Its trace-characters are the dynamics: Tr(M) = 4 = k_grav, Tr(M³) = 52 = 2·k_GUT. Forced 5 time On the type-III₁ boundary factor, KMS-uniqueness (Takesaki) and state-independence (Connes) make the modular flow the unique intrinsic time. By Bisognano–Wichmann it is the boost of Facet 4; signature (4,1) — de Sitter. Forced 6 Λ Λ/M_P² = [k_GUT²/(N_c^{3/2}·w)]·q^{2k_GUT} = 2.83×10⁻¹²², matching observation to 0.004 orders out of 122 with zero continuous parameters. Exponent 2k_GUT = Tr(M³) = 52. Forced 7 interlock k_grav = 4 is at once Φ₂(N_c), Tr(M), and the arrow's scale; k_GUT = 26 is N_c³−1 and ½Tr(M³); the nome is the base of Λ and the modular temperature of time. The facets share vertices. Forced New r351 The two-anchor collapse. The three modular operations the paper uses — the reciprocal S, the ladder-shift T, the rotation U — are not three inputs. The two anchor stabilisers alone generate everything: S (order 2, at i) and U (order 3, at ω) generate the whole modular group PSL(2,ℤ) = ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ/3, with T = S·U² derived. Three operations collapse to the same two points Facet 1 already forces. Peer-review hardening The referee's pushes, closed An external review named where a referee would push. Each is closed with a proof or a derivation, not deflected. 1 The axiom rests on no conjecture.ω is forced three independent proven ways: Montgomery's minimal-theta theorem (with Bernstein) — ω uniquely minimises every completely monotone pair energy; symmetry-forced stability; and gravitational arithmetic (the clean point count holds at ω's prime, fails at i's). Any one suffices. Cohn–Kumar (open in d = 2) is not load-bearing. 2 The point count is proved inline.|E(𝔽₃)| = 4 = k_grav by direct enumeration, with the dichotomy |E(𝔽_p)| = p+1 ⟺ p non-split in ℚ(ω) by the cubing-bijection character sum. Machine-checked against brute force for every p < 200. 3 The Λ prefactor is forced by the level-dictionary.Every symbol in Facet 6 is forced: the exponent 52 = Tr(M³) is boost arithmetic, the base is the period, and the prefactor k_GUT²/(N_c^{3/2}·w) is fixed by the same holographic level-dictionary that forces G. They stand or fall together. The genus-2 Mumford integral is a bonus, not load-bearing. 4 The Λ mechanism is now derived, not only forced New r351The exponent 52 is over-determined four independent ways (the boost character Tr(M³); N_c³−1 doubled; the channel count 2(c_L+2); dim F₄), and the one medium-side residual is closed on the axiom via the exact identity S = T·U, doubly-established by a worldsheet Coulomb-gas cross-check. What remains outside the forced lattice is the prefactor's genus-2 origin and the Leech/Monster specificity — neither the exponent nor the mechanism. Anti-tuning There is no continuous dial The vacuum exponent lives on the forced trace orbit. Its neighbouring exponents give 10⁻³³ and 10⁻⁴⁵⁸ — missing the observed 10⁻¹²² by ~90 and ~336 orders. Either the orbit's third trace is the vacuum exponent, or the framework is wrong; it cannot be adjusted into agreement. The input floor G = 1/k_grav is forced and is identically M_P = √k_grav = 2 in natural units, so the core carries no free dimensionless parameter — only the one overall scale that no theory derives from pure mathematics. Zero dimensionless dials, one unit. The theoretical floor for any theory of everything. What ships · how to evaluate Read it, then attack it The paper — Mathematical_Core.pdf (source Mathematical_Core.md): the self-contained Diamond, every integer forced, the point-count proved inline and the Λ prefactor forced via the level-dictionary. This revision adds the plain-prose vacuum identification and records the two-anchor collapse and the derived Λ mechanism. The verification suite — engine-free scripts (mpmath / sympy / numpy) that reproduce every displayed number at machine precision, driven by run_all_core.py (all pass). The β-programme labs run via run_beta_programme.py. The new-science register — the falsifiable predictions and structural results, each at its honest tier. Designed to be read and attacked in about an hour. The three sharpest targets are named in the paper: the point-count theorem (§5), the anchor characterisation (§2), and the vacuum identification (§0.0). Run run_all_core.py to reproduce every number from scratch. What this kernel seeds The same two objects — the cyclotomic polynomial on the CM curve at its order-3 point — go on to read the Standard Model gauge structure, gravity, and the dark and cosmological sectors in the full deposit. Representative forward, not-yet-settled predictions, ordered by when the verdict arrives: dark energy w(z) = −1 (Euclid DR1, ≈ Oct 2026); Baryonic Tully–Fisher slope = 4 (SPARC, a live 1.7σ tension); the solar angle 4/13 or 14/45 (JUNO); H₀ = 67.29 on the CMB side; δ_CP ≈ 195.6° (DUNE); and — new this cycle — graviton birefringence Δv/v = 0, a single test that falsifies the Λ mechanism if violated. Closure tiers Proved · Forced · Forced mod 1 premise · Selected · Identification · Open. The core admits only the forced tier; everything else is deferred to the full deposit at its own label. How to cite Watford, P. (2026). The Watford Framework — A Minimal Structural Core of the Cyclotomic Framework. Zenodo · CC BY 4.0. Full consolidated framework: doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21836329. An independent research framework offered for open scrutiny — results labelled by closure tier, not asserted as established physics. If a prose claim and a verifier disagree, trust the verifier.

item.title: Hamilton Cycles and Paths in the Noncrossing Partition Refinement Graph
item.description: Let NCR(n) be the cover graph of the refinement order on the noncrossing partitions of an n-element cyclically ordered set. We determine exactly when this graph has a Hamilton cycle and when it has a Hamilton path. The graph has a Hamilton cycle exactly for n in {0,1} or even n at least 4, and it has a Hamilton path exactly for n at most 3 or even n. For odd orders, block-count parity and a signed Dyck-tree recurrence give the obstruction. For every even n at least 4, an explicit Boolean-cube decomposition, refinement-diamond port assignment, and recursive square switching construction produce a Hamilton cycle. The classification and construction are accompanied by a kernel-checked Lean 4 formalization.

item.description: Newcomer documentation and archive guidance This source-only reproducibility release adds a detailed English guide for first-time users, including Python 3.11 setup, DIAMOND configuration, safe preflight, full execution, resume rules, output verification, and common troubleshooting. It also explains the distinction between the changing GitHub main branch, a tagged GitHub Release, and an immutable Zenodo version DOI, with a maintainer checklist and Zenodo metadata template. The release continues to contain source-level data, author-written code, environment specifications, workflow runners, documentation, and checksum-generation code only. It intentionally excludes precomputed models, derived result tables, figures, manuscripts, and submission materials; run python run_all.py to regenerate derived artifacts. See README.md and docs/GETTING_STARTED.md for the entry point.

item.title: Beal Conjecture — Release Guard, Genuine Frey Residual, and Typed R=T Patching — v8.4.0
item.description: Version 8.3.0 records an audited conditional milestone in Lean 4. Exact-divisibility proofs no longer live in the Wiles plan or Galois edge witnesses: the odd-prime Tate interface derives each edge from the canonical Frey model and its conductor. The terminal 2-adic exponent-one premise is explicit model-indexed data. The patching layer carries residual-representation, Hecke-attachment, deformation, comparison, finite-level action, and diamond-specialization data. The final route remains conditional on exactly three named mathematical interfaces—frey_conductor_data, tate_step2_odd_prime_external, and wiles_modularity—and two unconstructed data suppliers, TwoAdicExponentOneSupplier and EnrichedPlanSupplier. This is not an unconditional proof of the Beal Conjecture.

item.title: De Noordster als Verlovingsring en als Kruis
item.description: Teken een dorp zoals op een kerstkaart. Huisjes, een torentje, sneeuw. Daarboven één ster. Het kan maar één ster zijn, want er is er maar één die stilstaat. Dit essay toont dat de Verlovingsring een echt astronomisch asterisme is op +88°54' declinatie, met Polaris als diamant op de ring: "Polaris is the diamond on the ring." Die ring draait 360 graden om het Kruis in de hemel. De Noordster is het middenpunt van het gehele verhaal. Met het blote oog één lichtpunt, in werkelijkheid drie sterren: Polaris Aa, Polaris Ab en Polaris B. Drie ringen van licht die samen één ster vormen in het midden van alle ringen. Volgens academici Aa-Ab-B, voor de populus Ab-B-Aa = Abba. Abba is Aramees voor Vader, Papa. Paus Franciscus, Homilie Epifanie 6 januari 2022, Vaticaan: "for he is the North Star that lights up the sky of life and guides our steps towards true joy." "even in the darkest nights a star continues to shine" "The star of Jesus does not dazzle or overwhelm, but gently invites." Verder: sponsa Christi bruid van Christus draagt Polaris als diamant, Stella Maris Sterre der Zee (Franciscus 2 okt 2022), de Chinese Ziwei Paarse Ster en de Verboden Stad Zijincheng als aardse kopie van het hemelse paleis op de Noordster, titel Great Emperor of the North Star in the Purple Forbidden enclosure. En Franciscus over Lord of the Rings (26 mei 2022): "As Frodo says: The tales never end." Drie ringen om te heersen via die ene ring. En die ene ring heeft iets met onzichtbaar. Feitelijk is dat ook zo want de drie sterren vormen samen die ene Ster. Polaris Aa, Ab en B worden onzichtbaar als losse sterren, één ster blijft zichtbaar. One Ring to rule them all, One Ring to find them, One Ring to bring them all and in the darkness bind them. Precies wat Polaris doet. Conclusie: Vader, Moeder en Kind wonen in één ster. De kerstkaart klopt. The tales never end.

One Ring to rule them all, One Ring to find them, One Ring to bring them all and in the darkness bind them. Precies wat Polaris doet. Conclusie: Vader, Moeder en Kind wonen in één ster. De kerstkaart klopt. The tales never end.

item.description: The North Star as Engagement Ring and as Cross.There is only one star that stands still. The Engagement Ring is a real asterism at +88°54' with Polaris as diamond. To the naked eye one point, in reality three stars Aa, Ab, B - three rings of light forming one star in the middle of all rings. Aa-Ab-B academically, Ab-B-Aa = Abba for the populus, Aramaic for Father. Pope Francis Epiphany Jan 6 2022: "for he is the North Star that lights up the sky of life". Includes Stella Maris, Chinese Ziwei Star, Forbidden City Zijincheng, and Tolkien's One Ring invisibility parallel.

item.title: Materials Foundation for AI-Driven Atomically Precise Manufacturing: Nanofabricator Architectures, Molecular Tooling, Programmable Surfaces, Metrology, and Error Correction
item.description: This research prospectus investigates the materials foundation required for an AI-driven nanofabrication platform capable of progressing from nanometer-scale manufacturing toward reliable molecular and potentially atomically precise construction. Rather than treating atomically precise manufacturing as an extension of semiconductor fabrication, scanning-probe microscopy, additive manufacturing, or conventional nanotechnology, the work derives material requirements from the physics of the proposed machine itself. It examines dimensional stability, thermal expansion and gradients, phonons, Brownian and zero-point motion, creep, hysteresis, surface diffusion, contamination, charge noise, defects, tip deformation, mechanochemical stability, metrology, and error correction across target positional regimes from approximately 100 nm to 10 pm. The study establishes a state-of-the-art baseline spanning diamond and diamondoid systems, silicon and silicon carbide, boron nitride, graphene and other two-dimensional materials, ultrastable glasses and ceramics, refractory and high-entropy materials, MOFs and COFs, molecular machines, supramolecular systems, DNA origami, atomically precise clusters, scanning-probe tooling, functionalized tips, and surface-bound molecular chemistry. Each class is evaluated both for its enabling properties and for the limitations that prevent it from independently serving as a universal nanofabricator material. The prospectus then develops more than twenty differentiated candidate material systems and architectures, including self-metrologizing covalent frames, hard-backbone/addressable-chemistry lattices, heterogeneous 2D/3D reaction skins, reversible electronically gated construction surfaces, interchangeable molecular tooling ports, deterministic molecular inventory systems, and materials designed specifically for physical error detection and repair. Three complete nanofabricator material architectures are proposed: a conservative platform accessible to present experimental science, an aggressive architecture dependent on major AI-driven materials advances, and a longer-horizon architecture based on new but physically plausible material classes. A quantitative prioritization framework ranks candidate systems by atomic-precision potential, dimensional stability, stiffness, thermal behavior, chemical programmability, surface controllability, sensing, manufacturability, scalability, AI-designability, experimental falsifiability, and scientific upside. The report also defines a staged experimental roadmap from computational falsification through closed-loop AI-controlled fabrication and multi-chemistry nanoscale construction. A central conclusion is that the most credible path is unlikely to depend on one “perfect” material. Instead, atomically precise manufacturing is more likely to emerge from a heterogeneous metric-chemistry architecture in which structural stability, continuous self-metrology, molecular tooling, programmable reaction surfaces, feedstock control, and error correction are implemented by different optimized material systems. All major claims and proposals are explicitly distinguished according to their evidentiary status: experimentally demonstrated, demonstrated in an adjacent context, theoretically supported, plausible extrapolation, or highly speculative research hypothesis. Proposed material concepts are research directions rather than claims of scientific or patent novelty; any novelty assertion would require dedicated literature and patent analysis. The objective is to define high-leverage materials discoveries and experimental programs capable of turning atomically precise manufacturing from a speculative concept into an experimentally falsifiable engineering discipline. Keywords: atomically precise manufacturing, atomic-scale fabrication, nanofabrication, nanotechnology, molecular manufacturing, molecular nanotechnology, mechanosynthesis, AI for science, materials science, inverse materials design, molecular machines, surface science, scanning probe microscopy, AFM, STM, quantum metrology, precision engineering, programmable surfaces, molecular tooling, nanorobotics, autonomous science, computational chemistry.

item.title: Helmholtz Open Science Briefing: 72. Helmholtz Open Science Online Seminar
item.description: The 72nd Helmholtz Open Science Online Seminar ’Putting Publishing Back into the Hands of the Scientific Community – Diamond Open Access at Helmholtz and Beyond’, held on 7 May 2026, explored how science-led, open access journal publishing is practiced at Helmholtz and beyond. The event showcased concrete examples and current developments: the experience of an editor for a community-driven geoscience journal who is a Helmholtz researcher and scientific executive director, a scholar-led journal published at Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT), Germany’s national service point for diamond open access (SeDOA), and the expansion of Open Research Europe as a European publishing platform to be hosted at CERN from late 2026 on.
