item.title: The Cyclotomic Framework As A Minimal Structural Core
item.description: A minimal structural core · CC BY 4.0 · consolidated deposit 10.5281/zenodo.21836329 The Diamond One curve, one polynomial, one unit — the framework's forced lattice. PAUL WATFORD · INDEPENDENT RESEARCHER · ROYAL TUNBRIDGE WELLS, UKORCID 0009-0003-9724-7674 · hep-th (hep-ph, gr-qc) Every displayed claim is forced — a theorem or a chain of theorems — and machine-verified at machine precision. The paper is written to be attacked. 2 classical objects (curve + polynomial) 1 unit — M_Z, the only empirical input 1 premise — a stable vacuum 7 forced, interlocking facets 0 dimensionless dials to tune The one physical claim What the vacuum is Before the theorems, the statement they all serve — named in physics, not left as a convenient math object. The framework's foundational identification E : y² = x³ + 1 The vacuum of the theory is this elliptic curve — the curve of j-invariant zero, with complex multiplication by the Eisenstein integers ℤ[ω] — read at its order-3 symmetry point τ₀ = ω. This is a physical identification: a claim about what the ground state is, not a theorem of pure mathematics. Everything downstream is forced; the identification stands or falls with those forced consequences, and is falsifiable through them. What it says physically, if true to nature The ground state is a two-dimensional boundary conformal field theory at the most symmetric point of its moduli space — the order-3 fixed point, where an extra ℤ/3 automorphism acts. The one period of that vacuum, the nome |q| = e^(−π√3), fixes every mass scale: there is one scale in nature because there is one period. Time is not put in by hand — the boundary algebra is a type-III₁ factor carrying a unique intrinsic modular flow (Tomita–Takesaki, Connes), and that flow is the Lorentz boost between the two anchors; the arrow of time is the vacuum's own modular automorphism. Newton's constant is the inverse of a counting number — the four points of the curve over the field of three elements, G = 1/|E(𝔽₃)| = 1/4 — reappearing as the Chern–Simons level of the 3D bulk the boundary induces. The particles, couplings, and cosmological numbers are arithmetic invariants of this one curve. Three classical facts keep the claim from floating: the anchors ω and i are the only elliptic points of PSL(2,ℤ) and the zeros of the two generators of the modular-form ring (they cannot be post-selected); ω is independently singled out by Montgomery's minimal-theta theorem; and gravity is the curve's own point-count. Nothing enters the core the geometry does not force. The forced lattice Seven facets, each forced, each interlocking From the two objects, seven facets. They are a lattice, not a list — remove any one and the others lose their forcing. Facet Statement Tier 1 anchors The curve has j = 0 and CM by ℤ[ω]; its only elliptic points are τ₀ = ω (order 3) and τ₁ = i (order 2) — the zero loci of E₄ and E₆, the two generators of the whole ring of modular forms. They cannot be post-selected. Forced 2 nome Read at τ₀, the curve's period gives the single nome |q| = e^(−π√3) — the one transcendental, the curve's own period. Everything dimensionless is a power of |q| or a cyclotomic ratio; the framework is curve-native. Forced 3 ladder The colour count is the ramification N_c = 3. The integer ladder is the cyclotomic factors of x¹²−1 at N_c: k_H = 2, k_grav = 4, 13, 10, 7, k_GUT = N_c³−1 = 26, w = 6. Pure arithmetic. Forced 4 boost The non-torsion unit bridging the two anchors is ε = 2+√3, fundamental unit of ℚ(√3). Its trace-characters are the dynamics: Tr(M) = 4 = k_grav, Tr(M³) = 52 = 2·k_GUT. Forced 5 time On the type-III₁ boundary factor, KMS-uniqueness (Takesaki) and state-independence (Connes) make the modular flow the unique intrinsic time. By Bisognano–Wichmann it is the boost of Facet 4; signature (4,1) — de Sitter. Forced 6 Λ Λ/M_P² = [k_GUT²/(N_c^{3/2}·w)]·q^{2k_GUT} = 2.83×10⁻¹²², matching observation to 0.004 orders out of 122 with zero continuous parameters. Exponent 2k_GUT = Tr(M³) = 52. Forced 7 interlock k_grav = 4 is at once Φ₂(N_c), Tr(M), and the arrow's scale; k_GUT = 26 is N_c³−1 and ½Tr(M³); the nome is the base of Λ and the modular temperature of time. The facets share vertices. Forced New r351 The two-anchor collapse. The three modular operations the paper uses — the reciprocal S, the ladder-shift T, the rotation U — are not three inputs. The two anchor stabilisers alone generate everything: S (order 2, at i) and U (order 3, at ω) generate the whole modular group PSL(2,ℤ) = ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ/3, with T = S·U² derived. Three operations collapse to the same two points Facet 1 already forces. Peer-review hardening The referee's pushes, closed An external review named where a referee would push. Each is closed with a proof or a derivation, not deflected. 1 The axiom rests on no conjecture.ω is forced three independent proven ways: Montgomery's minimal-theta theorem (with Bernstein) — ω uniquely minimises every completely monotone pair energy; symmetry-forced stability; and gravitational arithmetic (the clean point count holds at ω's prime, fails at i's). Any one suffices. Cohn–Kumar (open in d = 2) is not load-bearing. 2 The point count is proved inline.|E(𝔽₃)| = 4 = k_grav by direct enumeration, with the dichotomy |E(𝔽_p)| = p+1 ⟺ p non-split in ℚ(ω) by the cubing-bijection character sum. Machine-checked against brute force for every p < 200. 3 The Λ prefactor is forced by the level-dictionary.Every symbol in Facet 6 is forced: the exponent 52 = Tr(M³) is boost arithmetic, the base is the period, and the prefactor k_GUT²/(N_c^{3/2}·w) is fixed by the same holographic level-dictionary that forces G. They stand or fall together. The genus-2 Mumford integral is a bonus, not load-bearing. 4 The Λ mechanism is now derived, not only forced New r351The exponent 52 is over-determined four independent ways (the boost character Tr(M³); N_c³−1 doubled; the channel count 2(c_L+2); dim F₄), and the one medium-side residual is closed on the axiom via the exact identity S = T·U, doubly-established by a worldsheet Coulomb-gas cross-check. What remains outside the forced lattice is the prefactor's genus-2 origin and the Leech/Monster specificity — neither the exponent nor the mechanism. Anti-tuning There is no continuous dial The vacuum exponent lives on the forced trace orbit. Its neighbouring exponents give 10⁻³³ and 10⁻⁴⁵⁸ — missing the observed 10⁻¹²² by ~90 and ~336 orders. Either the orbit's third trace is the vacuum exponent, or the framework is wrong; it cannot be adjusted into agreement. The input floor G = 1/k_grav is forced and is identically M_P = √k_grav = 2 in natural units, so the core carries no free dimensionless parameter — only the one overall scale that no theory derives from pure mathematics. Zero dimensionless dials, one unit. The theoretical floor for any theory of everything. What ships · how to evaluate Read it, then attack it The paper — Mathematical_Core.pdf (source Mathematical_Core.md): the self-contained Diamond, every integer forced, the point-count proved inline and the Λ prefactor forced via the level-dictionary. This revision adds the plain-prose vacuum identification and records the two-anchor collapse and the derived Λ mechanism. The verification suite — engine-free scripts (mpmath / sympy / numpy) that reproduce every displayed number at machine precision, driven by run_all_core.py (all pass). The β-programme labs run via run_beta_programme.py. The new-science register — the falsifiable predictions and structural results, each at its honest tier. Designed to be read and attacked in about an hour. The three sharpest targets are named in the paper: the point-count theorem (§5), the anchor characterisation (§2), and the vacuum identification (§0.0). Run run_all_core.py to reproduce every number from scratch. What this kernel seeds The same two objects — the cyclotomic polynomial on the CM curve at its order-3 point — go on to read the Standard Model gauge structure, gravity, and the dark and cosmological sectors in the full deposit. Representative forward, not-yet-settled predictions, ordered by when the verdict arrives: dark energy w(z) = −1 (Euclid DR1, ≈ Oct 2026); Baryonic Tully–Fisher slope = 4 (SPARC, a live 1.7σ tension); the solar angle 4/13 or 14/45 (JUNO); H₀ = 67.29 on the CMB side; δ_CP ≈ 195.6° (DUNE); and — new this cycle — graviton birefringence Δv/v = 0, a single test that falsifies the Λ mechanism if violated. Closure tiers Proved · Forced · Forced mod 1 premise · Selected · Identification · Open. The core admits only the forced tier; everything else is deferred to the full deposit at its own label. How to cite Watford, P. (2026). The Watford Framework — A Minimal Structural Core of the Cyclotomic Framework. Zenodo · CC BY 4.0. Full consolidated framework: doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21836329. An independent research framework offered for open scrutiny — results labelled by closure tier, not asserted as established physics. If a prose claim and a verifier disagree, trust the verifier.

item.title: Evolution of BT Resistance in Lepidopteran Pests: Patterns, Drivers, and IPM Strategies
item.description: Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) based transgenic crops and bioinsecticide formulations have become central tools in controlling lepidopteran pests in cotton, maize, soybean as well as various vegetable systems worldwide. Large scale utilizationhas significantly reduced insecticide use, increased crop yields and brought tremendous economic gains to the growers and society. Extensive adoption of Bt toxins has reduced pesticide use, thus making the longevity of Bt technology development defining challenge for modern pest control. Resistance has been reported in field populations of lepidopteran pests including, Corn earworm Helicoverpa zea, European corn borer Ostrinia nubilalis, Pink bollworm Pectinophora gossypiella, Cotton bollworm Helicoverpa armigera, Diamond backmoth Plutella xylostella, and Fall armyworm Spodoptera frugiperda. This review summarizes the existing information on the Bt resistance development in lepidopteran pests combining molecular, physiological, ecological, and agronomic insights. It identifies the properties and distribution patterns of Bt toxins, summarizes global resistance spread, and also discusses resistance mechanisms including modified midgut receptors and proteolytic processing and detoxication mechanisms, as well as interactions between microbiomes and the toxins. The review further explores ecological and agronomic determinants, such as refuge structure, cropping practices, landscape organization and farmer’s choice. Advances in monitoring, diagnostics and modeling of resistance evolution and emerging strategies for integrating Bt technologies into integrated pest management (IPM) frameworks for sustainable control.

item.title: Carbon Material DFT Dataset
item.description: The dataset comprises 36 data folders stored in the DeePMD-kit standard format (.npy/.raw), with a total data volume of approximately 208 MB. Among them, folders init.* (7 in total) contain the initial training set and data from early iterative expansions, while the remaining 29 folders, named with the sys.*, contain newly labeled data generated and screened during the DP-GEN active learning iterative process. All folders contain a set.000 subdirectory along with type.raw and type_map.raw files. The dataset covers four systems: bulk diamond (approximately 41.73%), diamond (001) surface (approximately 21.20%), graphite (approximately 6.35%), and amorphous carbon (approximately 30.73%), comprising a total of 163,803 DFT-calculated configurations.

item.title: Preparation and Optical Properties of Chromium Doped Diamond
item.description: Diamond combines excellent mechanical, thermal, and optical properties with good biocompatibility, making it a core candidate functional material for cutting-edge quantum devices such as quantum precision sensing and single photon light sources. The research on traditional diamond nitrogen vacancy (NV) color centers is relatively mature, but there are inherent defects such as wide central emission spectra and sensitivity to environmental disturbances, which make it difficult to meet the performance requirements of the new generation of quantum devices. Developing new quantum defect color centers for transition metal doped diamond has become a research hotspot in the field of artificial crystals. Chromium (Cr), as a transition metal element, can introduce unique defect energy levels in the bandgap after doping into diamond, which is expected to construct a new type of quantum luminescent center. Most of the existing Cr doped diamonds are synthesized using high-temperature and high-pressure methods, which are prone to introducing catalyst impurities and difficult to control doping concentration; And ion implantation doping can cause serious irradiation lattice damage. Microwave plasma chemical vapor deposition (MPCVD) can achieve in-situ doping of diamond, effectively avoiding crystal damage caused by ion implantation, and the doping concentration is controllable, resulting in excellent crystal growth quality. However, there is still insufficient systematic research on the in-situ preparation of Cr doped diamond by MPCVD, and the influence of Cr doping on the optical properties of diamond is still unclear. Based on this, this article adopts MPCVD technology and uses hexacarbonyl chromium as the chromium source to achieve in-situ Cr doping of diamond single crystals through argon gas bubbling and heating sublimation. The surface of the prepared sample is smooth, and the Cr element is evenly distributed along the film thickness direction. The optical properties of the prepared sample were systematically studied by combining optical testing. The feasibility of in-situ preparation of Cr doped diamond single crystals by MPCVD has been verified, providing experimental basis for the development of Cr doped diamond quantum functional crystals.

item.title: Feature Engineering for Virtual Currency Price Prediction in Online Games Using a Multiple Linear Regression Approach
item.description: Changes in the price of Growtopia's virtual currency can influence players' decisions when buying, selling, or storing items, while price information circulating in the community is often inconsistent. This condition confirms the need for transparent, data-driven predictions. This study aims to predict the prices of World Lock (WL), Diamond Lock (DL), and Blue Gem Lock (BGL) using multiple linear regression. The novelty of the study lies in the application of three separate models with a combination of lag features and cyclic time features, accompanied by chronological data sharing to avoid information leakage. The initial dataset contained 925 daily observations from 2024–2026, while the modeling was limited to 194 data points from 2026 that had a consistent scale. After the formation of Lag_1, Lag_2, Lag_7, Day_Sin, and Day_Cos, 187 complete lines are available, divided into 150 training data and 37 test data. The models were evaluated using MSE, RMSE, MAPE, and R². All three models yield an R² of 0.9318, a MAPE of 2.3191%, as well as a MAPE-based accuracy of 97.6809%. The RMSE is 0.1400 for WL, 14.0017 for DL, and 1,400.1705 for BGL, respectively. As of July 13, 2026, the actual and predicted differences are 0.1743 WL, 17.4286 DL, and 1,742.8648 BGL, respectively. The 123-day recursive prediction yields a final value of 2.8357 WL, 283.5670 DL, and 28,356.6979 BGL. The results show the model follows a general pattern, but its response weakens when price changes occur suddenly. The findings can be used as companion information to transactions, rather than as price certainty or investment recommendations.

item.title: Unveiling the Crystal Structures of Ice Polymorphs by using Neutron Diffraction under Pressure
item.description: Water exhibits remarkable polymorphism, with more than twenty crystalline ice phases identified to date. Understanding their crystal structures, hydrogen ordering, and pressure-induced structural transformations requires precise determination of hydrogen positions, making neutron diffraction an indispensable technique. However, the combination of neutron diffraction and high-pressure experiments has long been hindered by severe technical challenges arising from the small sample volumes required at high pressure. This article reviews our efforts to overcome these limitations through the development of advanced high-pressure neutron diffraction techniques, particularly the MITO system for individual pressure and temperature control and the integration of nano-polycrystalline diamond anvil cells with the PLANET beamline at J-PARC. These developments have enabled detailed investigations of hydrogen ordering and dynamics in high-pressure ice polymorphs. Studies on ice XV and the newly discovered ice XIX revealed the existence of partially ordered states and demonstrated that a single hydrogen-disordered phase can transform into distinct ordered phases depending on the pressure–temperature pathway. Time-resolved neutron diffraction measurements of the ice VII–VIII transition further uncovered a crossover between molecular rotational and proton translational motions that governs hydrogen-ordering kinetics. Extending neutron diffraction measurements beyond 100 GPa finally made it possible to directly observe the evolution of the hydrogen distribution toward the symmetrized hydrogen bond in ice X. These achievements illustrate how advances in experimental methodology have opened new opportunities for exploring the structural complexity of ice and hydrogen-bonded materials under extreme conditions.

item.title: Thesis from article: Effect of Distortion Profiles on the Compressive Properties of Constant-Mass Functionally Graded Lattice Structures Fabricated by Selective Laser Melting
item.description: In our research, we are investigating further opportunities for weight reduction in autonomous vehicles (and their components). We manufactured prototypes using powder-bed additive manufacturing for compressive testing of internal structures adapted to spatial requirements—functionally graded lattice structures.The novelty of this work lies in evaluating functionally graded lattice structures while maintaining a constant specimen mass (12 g). This contrasts with numerous existing studies, which also modify the mass when changing the topology. We investigated “Diamond” lattice topologies made of Ti-6Al-4V. Our experimental results demonstrate that concentrating the strut thickness toward the core (an inward-thickening gradient) results in a 7.4% increase in maximum compressive strength and a 13.1% increase in the modulus of elasticity compared to conventional, uniform lattices. In contrast, peripheral material concentration degrades mechanical performance.u

item.title: Anomalous lattice expansion of bcc Ta in helium-loaded diamond anvil cells
item.description: Anomalous lattice expansion of bcc Ta is observed in helium-loaded diamond anvil cell (DAC) experiments near 6 GPa and above 400 K, while co-loaded W, Mo, and Au exhibit normal thermal expansion. The Ta volume expansion increases with temperature, reaching ~14% near 650 K before plateauing, and is largely retained after recovery to ambient conditions. Time-resolved measurements at 500 K reveal progressive expansion over several hours, consistent with gradual, thermally activated He incorporation. The largely retained expansion during subsequent cooling and holding at 400 K indicates that the incorporated He is predominantly kinetically trapped. The data reveal two distinct regimes: below ~550 K, modest and spatially uniform expansion consistent with interstitial He trapping at isolated, randomly distributed vacancies; above ~550 K, He-vacancy cluster growth producing dramatically larger expansion, peak broadening, and a core-shell microstructure revealed by micron-resolution X-ray diffraction mapping. These results demonstrate that He is not always a passive pressure medium in DAC experiments and reveal a previously unrecognized regime of He-mediated lattice modification in Ta, complementing conventional ion-implantation studies relevant to nuclear and fusion structural materials.

item.title: Developing an Integrated University Town Framework as a Catalyst For Sustainable Tourism in Bandung
item.description: University towns function not only as centers of higher education but also as ecosystems of economic, social, cultural, creative, and tourism activity. This study aims to analyze the factors shaping university town competitiveness, identify development constraints, and formulate an integrated framework that positions university towns as catalysts for sustainable tourism in Bandung. The study applies a qualitative approach by integrating Porter’s Diamond Model with a netnographic perspective. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, observation, documentation, and digital content analysis across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Google Reviews, X, Reddit, travel blogs, and online forums. Informants were selected purposively based on their involvement in university, business, government, community, and tourism ecosystems. The data were analyzed thematically through transcription, reduction, coding, categorization, triangulation, and interpretation. The findings show that university town competitiveness is shaped by academic resources, student and visitor mobility, supporting industries, collaborative strategies, government policies, and digital transformation opportunities. Campus experiences also generate digital narratives that develop into electronic word of mouth, shape the tourist gaze, strengthen community experience, and build destination branding. This study proposes the Integrated University Town Framework for Sustainable Tourism Development, which positions universities as catalysts for knowledge-based, competitive, inclusive, authentic, and sustainable destinations with long-term socioeconomic value.

item.title: Perancangan Identitas Visual Vokasi Fest Universitas Tiga Serangkai Tahun 2026
item.description: Vokasi Fest 2026 is the inaugural event organized by the Faculty of Vocational Studies at Universitas Tiga Serangkai Surakarta, serving as a platform for showcasing and promoting student works from the Visual Communication Design, Textile Product Design, Information Technology, and Information Systems programs. The event is held over one week and features a series of activities, including a student work exhibition, photography workshop, doodle competition, and expert lecture. As an event intended to be held annually, Vokasi Fest requires a strong and consistent visual identity to establish recognition, build a distinctive image, and differentiate the event from other creative and educational events. This study aims to design a visual identity for Vokasi Fest 2026 that represents the values of creativity, innovation, collaboration, and vocational competence while supporting the promotional and publication needs of the event. The design process employs the Double Diamond approach, consisting of four stages: Discover, Define, Develop, and Deliver. The resulting visual identity system includes a logo, color palette, typography, graphic elements, and their applications across various promotional and publication media. The visual identity is expected to establish consistent, recognizable, and flexible visual communication while supporting the sustainability of Vokasi Fest as an annual event of the Faculty of Vocational Studies at Universitas Tiga Serangkai Surakarta.

item.title: Thermal and Mechanical Behaviors of Additively Manufactured Multilevel TPMS Metamaterials With Nonlinear Graded Infill
item.description: Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures offer multifunctional potential. We propose a novel temperature‐guided multilevel TPMS design by infilling Diamond cells into an IWP framework with three spatial distributions. Ti6Al4V specimens were fabricated by laser powder bed fusion. Their transient thermal responses and room‐temperature quasi‐static compressive behaviors were evaluated separately through experiments and finite element simulations. These structures reduced top‐surface temperature by up to 80 °C versus primary IWP structures. In particular, the nonlinear graded configuration produced the lowest top‐surface temperature under the prescribed 300 s heating protocol, indicating delayed through‐thickness heat transfer. The separate thermal and mechanical assessments reveal a geometry‐mediated trade‐off between transient thermal‐shielding performance and compressive response. Although the temperature‐guided morphological heterogeneity reduces the elastic modulus, yield strength, and ultimate compressive strength, it disrupts coplanar stress concentration and promotes a more progressive 45° shear deformation mode, resulting in smoother post‐yield plateau responses. Therefore, the mechanical benefit of the multilevel configurations lies in their modified deformation mode and reduced stress oscillation rather than in improved overall load‐bearing strength or mechanical robustness. This study provides a field‐guided design strategy for load‐bearing and energy‐absorbing thermal‐protection lattices requiring delayed heat penetration and stable progressive deformation.

item.title: Modeling of Diamond Trench Metal Oxide Semiconductor Barrier Schottky Rectifier Based on Dynamic Reverse Bias Simulation Framework
item.description: This work presents an electrothermal optimization study of diamond‐based trench metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) barrier Schottky (TMBS) rectifiers using mixed‐mode drift‐diffusion technology computer aided design simulations under quasi‐static and dynamic reverse‐bias conditions. The influence of drift‐layer thickness, doping concentration, oxide thickness, and trench depth is systematically investigated through electric field and charge‐sharing analysis. Under quasi‐static operation, the breakdown voltage is limited either by the electric field beneath the Schottky contact or at the trench bottom, and optimal BV is achieved when these two peak fields are balanced. Dynamic simulations including incomplete dopant ionization reveal strong modifications of the transient electric field distribution under ultra‐fast voltage ramps. Avalanche initiation is delayed, leading to significant BV enhancement compared to quasi‐static conditions, especially for shallow trench and non‐punch‐through structures. In contrast, self‐heating effects remain negligible due to the high thermal conductivity of diamond. The results demonstrate that optimal TMBS design depends strongly on the operating regime, highlighting the importance of dynamic electrothermal modeling for high‐voltage and high‐frequency diamond power devices.

item.title: Microstructural Characterization of Tungsten Heavy Alloy
item.description: In this chapter, the extensive microstructural characterization methods for tungsten heavy alloys are introduced, including optical microscopy, electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction, and chemical analysis. The basic characterization is provided by optical microscopy, which is based on the contrast of the natural reflectivity difference between darker binder phases and bright tungsten phases, with a resolution in the 0.2 µm range. Diamond abrasives are needed in sample preparation because of their different hardness, and to improve phase contrast, one may use solutions of nitric acid or ferric chloride. SEM has a better resolution (1-10 nm) and atomic number contrast between tungsten (Z= 74) and nickel/iron (Z= 28, 26), which provides high-quality phase identification at magnifications of 10x to 500,000x. Transmission electron microscopy offers the highest resolution (approximately 0.1 nm) for atomic-scale interface analysis, although specimen preparation remains challenging due to tungsten's hardness. Focused Ion Beam (FIB) methods are becoming the method of choice for preparing electron-transparent sections (less than 100 nm thick). X-ray diffraction analysis allows identification of phases conclusively: tungsten shows characteristic body-centered cubic reflections at 2θ = 40.3°, 58.3°, and 73.2°, whereas the binder phases show face-centered cubic patterns. Rietveld refinement phase analysis, which can be used to detect the presence of smaller phases, yields a detection limit of about 5-10 percent phase and provides accurate measurements of the lattice parameters (tungsten: a = 3.165 Å; binder: a = 3.52-3.65 Å). Bulk compositions (90-97 wt% W, 3-10 wt% Ni+Fe) are analyzed by chemical analysis methods (XRF and ICP), and the local composition is analyzed by local electron probe microanalysis with a spatial resolution of 1-30 µm. The tungsten L-series X-rays (8-12 keV) and nickel/iron K-series X-rays (6-7 keV) in energy-dispersive spectroscopy enable rapid phase identification and compositional mapping, which are vital for structure-property relationships.

item.title: Surface Engineering and Coatings of Tungsten Heavy Alloy
item.description: The chapter introduces a comprehensive surface engineering and coating of tungsten heavy alloys, addressing the composite microstructure, high thermal conductivity, and extremely high hardness of the tungsten and binder phases. Methods of surface modification include mechanical stress relief (shot peening, laser peening), thermal stress relief, and chemical stress relief (controlled etching, controlled passivation). Innovative methods of modification include compositional control (ion implantation), hard-phase formation (plasma-based treatments, including nitriding and carburizing), and laser surface modification to enable controlled melting, alloying, and texturing. Such methods need to account for the different responses of tungsten (chemically inert) and reactive binder phases while preserving dimensional accuracy. The problems in preparing substrates that necessitate the use of diamond abrasives due to hardness differences are solved by coating techniques, and thermal issues associated with high thermal mass and thermal expansion mismatches are addressed. Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) and Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD) enable precise control of coating thickness, whereas thermal spray and electrochemical methods produce thick, protective coatings. Nanoscale accuracy is achieved in thin-film technologies through the design of multilayer and nanocomposite structures. Heatresistant finishes are made of hard-metallic alloys, such as carbides (WC, TiC), nitrides (TiN), and ultra-hard alloys (diamond, c-BN), with hardness above 1000 HV (10 GPa). Multilayer systems are designed to provide complementary properties to achieve optimal performance, whereas tribological coatings use solid lubricants (e.g., MoS2 , DLC) to reduce friction. Corrosion protection is combined with selective attack on nickel-iron binder phases; tungsten is essentially inert, and protective measures include barrier coating, sacrificial protection, and high-temperature oxidation resistance of volatile WO3 above 600-800°C. Interface engineering increases adhesion, thermal compatibility, and stability in challenging service environments.

item.title: Enhancing Hardness and Wear Performance of Diamond-Like Carbon Films through Substrate Cooling during HiPIMS Deposition
item.description: High-power impulse magnetron sputtering (HiPIMS) is a plasma-based deposition process capable of significantly enhancing the ionization of sputtered species.The resulting ion bombardment of the substrate and the growing film during the sputtering-based process enables the synthesis of diamond-like carbon (DLC) films exhibiting both high hardness and excellent surface smoothness.However, in HiPIMS discharges the ion flux is typically dominated by Ar ions, and the associated energetic ion bombardment can cause significant substrate heating during deposition process.Such thermal effects may promote the formation of a graphite-like structure within the DLC films, thereby limiting the achievable film hardness.In this study, a substrate cooling system was implemented during HiPIMS deposition process by circulating coolants through a hollow sample holder.The effects of the substrate temperature on the surface roughness, hardness, internal film structure, and tribological properties of the DLC films were systematically investigated.The results show that substrate cooling effectively suppressed the formation of graphite domains within the films, thereby resulting in increased film hardness and improved wear resistance.These findings demonstrate that precise control of the substrate temperature is a critical factor for achieving high-hardness DLC films growth in HiPIMS deposition.

item.title: Crystals, Vol. 16, Pages 568: Orientation-Dependent Compressibility of Tin Under High Pressure
item.description: This study investigates the effect of initial microstructure on the high-pressure mechanical properties of high-purity tin (Sn). Two Sn samples from the same commercial product were measured using high-pressure X-ray diffraction in diamond anvil cells. At ambient pressure, the two samples exhibited different initial crystallographic orientations; one showed random orientation, while the other exhibited preferred orientation (i.e., texture). In the low-pressure &beta;-Sn phase, both samples exhibited the same bulk moduli with B0 = 55.0 &plusmn; 0.4 and 55.0 &plusmn; 2.3 GPa, respectively. However, their compressional behavior diverged significantly after the phase transition from &beta;-Sn to the body-centered tetragonal (BCT) phase. The measured bulk moduli for the BCT phase were 60.0 &plusmn; 0.9 GPa for the randomly oriented Sn and 91.3 &plusmn; 1.4 GPa for the textured one. These results indicate that the initial microstructure can significantly influence the compressional response of Sn under high pressure.

item.title: Freeform Mirror Design Based on Zonal Energy Mapping
item.description: In laser phase-transformation hardening and laser cladding processes, the inherent thermodynamic limitations of conventional intensity distributions severely restrict the uniformity of metallurgical reaction. Although programmable beam shaping devices offer flexibility in profile reconstruction, their transmissive structure results in a low laser-induced damage threshold (LIDT), making them unsuitable for long-term stable operation at kilowatt-level power. This study proposes a reflective freeform mirror design method based on the principle of zonal energy mapping. The method constructs energy mapping relations that correlate the irradiance distribution in every sub-region of the incident Gaussian beam with the desired M-shaped irradiance profile. Relying on such mappings, the local surface generatrices of all sub-regions are solved separately; these generatrices are subsequently assembled to yield an integrated mirror surface. Optical performance was verified through Zemax non-sequential ray tracing simulations. The mirror was precisely machined using single-point diamond turning (SPDT). The experimental results show that the measured intensity distribution on the observation screen exhibits a typical M-shaped profile, with a peak-to-valley ratio of 1.28, which is in good agreement with the design target. This method provides a technically feasible and engineering-robust solution for complex thermal flux control requirements in high-power laser material processing.

item.title: Molecules, Vol. 31, Pages 3043: Influence of the Structure of Perfluoroalkylsilanes Self-Assembled Monolayers on Tribological Properties of TiOx-Incorporated Diamond-like Carbon Coatings
item.description: This paper reports the effects of formed perfluoroalkylsilane self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) on the tribological and corrosion properties of TiOx-incorporated diamond-like carbon (TiOx-DLC) coatings deposited on a Ti6Al4V substrate. The SAMs were formed using 1H,1H,2H,2H -perfluorodecyltrichlorosilane (FDTS) and (3,3,3 -trifluoropropyl) trichlorosilane (FPTS) compounds. Their presence was confirmed using techniques such as ellipsometry, time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry, and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy. The results of the ball-on-disc test indicate the role of the structure of the created SAMs on their tribological properties. The FDTS compounds with longer alkyl chains favor the creation of a well-packed layer bonded to the TiOx-DLC coating. This hydrophobic structure allows for obtaining the lowest coefficient of friction (0.180) during tribological tests. The results of electrochemical tests indicate that the SAM modification reduces the barrier properties of TiOx-DLC and provides enhanced kinetic stability against carbon matrix oxidation at higher anodic potentials.

item.title: Numerical and Analytical Implementation of the Method for Calculating Optimal Modes of Laser Heat Treatment of Electronic Materials
item.description: A modification of the method of parametric optimization of non-stationary thermal conduction processes is proposed in relation to the problems of laser heat treatment of a wide class of materials used in electronic engineering, including semiconductors, dielectrics and superhard materials. Using the Matlab computer mathematics package, a computational algorithm has been developed for the automatic construction of the optimal heating mode according to the specified quality criterion, which makes it possible to significantly reduce the time for the experimental selection of processing parameters. The results of verification of the method are presented on the example of calculating the optimal modes of laser marking of electronic products, confirmed by comparison with known experimental data, which demonstrates the high accuracy of the proposed approach. Particular attention is paid to laser-induced graphitization of diamond, which makes it possible to form conductive structures in the volume of superhard materials, which opens up new prospects for the creation of functional elements of electronic technology based on diamond substrates.

item.title: Porter’s Diamond Model for National Competitive Advantage applied to the Italian Hydrocarbons Industry
item.description: This paper explores how Michael Porter’s Diamond Model explains Italy’s competitive edge in the hydrocarbons sector, covering natural gas and petroleum. By looking at secondary data from ENI, Shell, and academic research, it digs into the main drivers behind Italy’s performance: skill-building, advanced local demand, strong supplier networks, and lively domestic competition. Italy, despite its scarce oil and gas resources, has managed to carve out a strong competitive position through innovation and skilled labor, not sheer resource abundance. The government acts as a booster and challenger, pushing innovation without heavy-handed control.
item.dc:creator: Nabil Suleiman

item.title: Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians
item.description: This paper gives a survey of propositional modal logic in an intuitionistic setting. Mainly intended for readers already familiar with classical modal logic, we discuss why there are two prominent families of such logics, intuitionistic modal logics (IMLs) and constructive modal logics (CMLs), what motivates their study, and how they compare with each other. Moreover, we take a deeper look at the logics lying between the CML and IML traditions, including a new logic $\textbf{KI}$ for which we prove completeness, and survey various extensions and $\Diamond$/$\Box$-free fragments. We further record several observations which seem to be implicit or absent in the literature; we point out a small defect in the original semantics for $\textbf{CK}$ and prove Lyndon interpolation theorems for $\textbf{CK}$ and $\textbf{WK}$.
item.dc:creator: Y. Sato

item.title: Tribological Performance of Tetrahedral Amorphous Carbon (ta-C) Coatings on Plasma-Nitrided X153CrMoV12 Cold Work Tool Steel
item.description: Diamond-like carbon (DLC) coatings, specifically tetrahedral amorphous carbon (ta-C), provide hard, low-friction carbon films suitable for tribological applications in demanding industrial environments. In this study, we investigated diamond-like carbon (ta-C) deposited by PVD arc technology (Ionbond Tetrabond), its quality, and applicability on tool steels, X153CrMoV12. Three different surface treatments were applied: plasma nitriding (535 °C, 9 h), DLC coating, and duplex plasma nitriding combined with DLC coating. The DLCs were characterized using characterization techniques, such as Raman, XPS, SEM, and XRD. XPS analysis reveals sp3 fractions of approximately 60% (DLC-only coating) and 62% (duplex nitrided + DLC coating) which confirm the high quality of the deposited ta-C films. Wear tests were conducted under loads of 10 N and 20 N, with a speed of 0.04 m/s and a distance of 100 m. Low coating thickness (~400 nm) limited load-carrying capacity, leading to premature wear and substrate exposure, as well as increased friction under continuous loads. Compared to non-coated samples, ta-C coating exhibits improved adhesion resistance to delamination if deposited on a nitrided substrate. The duplex nitrided and DLC-coated configuration achieved the most significant reduction in wear track width of up to 78% compared to the uncoated baseline, establishing it as the optimal surface treatment strategy for industrial cold-forming applications. The coefficient of friction (CoF) for the duplex-treated sample remained the lowest throughout testing, confirming its superior tribological performance. This research paves the way to improvements in tool steels and coating technology of diamond-like carbon.

item.title: Indexing of L'Europe Unie / United Europe, 2007–2026: A Comprehensive Portfolio
item.description: L’Europe Unie / United Europe is an international, peer-reviewed academic journal founded in Paris in 2007. The journal publishes research in European Studies, International Relations, Political Science, Contemporary History, European Law, Security Studies, governance and European Union external relations. This institutional evidence portfolio documents the journal’s confirmed presence, registration, preservation or discoverability across 44 international academic databases, disciplinary indexes, university-library systems, repositories, bibliographic authorities, persistent-identifier infrastructures and scholarly discovery services. The documented services include ERIH PLUS, EBSCO Political Science Complete, DOAJ, CEEOL, ProQuest and other Clarivate academic-information services, HeinOnline, ICI Journals Master List, J-Gate, SSRN and Mendeley Data within the Elsevier scholarly ecosystem, Crossref, Zenodo, OpenAIRE, DataCite Commons, SSOAR–GESIS, Policy Commons, HAL, IDEAS/RePEc, the ISSN Portal and ROAD, WorldCat/OCLC, BnF, SUDOC/ABES, ZDB, EZB, Mir@bel, MIAR, BASE and other international discovery services. As of 29 August 2026, the documented portfolio includes 172 citations reported by Google Scholar, 225 DOI-bearing Zenodo/DataCite records and eight verified issue-level SSRN/Crossref DOI records, alongside further article-level records. The portfolio provides a transparent and verifiable account of the journal’s international academic visibility, bibliographic identity, Diamond Open Access dissemination, DOI infrastructure, digital preservation and citation discoverability. It includes only confirmed and publicly verifiable information.

item.title: There Is No Natural Boundary between a Semiconductor and an Insulator ── The Value Runs Continuously across a Span of 10^70 without One Jump ── Diamond, an "Insulator", Stands at 1000 K a Factor of 3.97x10^13 above SiC, a "Semiconductor", at Room Temperature ── [Paper 275]
item.description: Materials are divided into semiconductors and insulators. This paper asks where that boundary lies──the answer is nowhere. The intrinsic carrier concentration varies continuously as exp(-E_g/2kT), and there is not one place where it jumps. No new mathematical theorem and no new law is claimed. Scope of this paper (scope note): No new mathematical theorem and no new law is claimed──that the intrinsic carrier concentration goes as exp(-E_g/2kT), the band gaps of these materials, and the customary distinction between semiconductors and insulators are all standard. No solid-state physics is built──what is used is one exponential. Band theory is not treated──why a band gap arises is not treated at all. No absolute value is claimed──exp(-E_g/2kT) is a quantity for comparison with the prefactor dropped, and not a real carrier concentration. Neither effective masses nor their temperature dependence are included. Doping is not treated──only the intrinsic case is examined. Practical semiconductors are dominated by impurities, so the quantity here is not a real conductivity. The temperature dependence of the band gap is not included──in fact E_g shrinks with temperature. Section 4 neglects that and is therefore an estimate on the conservative side. No band gap is measured──all are cited representative values and vary between sources. No revision of the classification is urged──the custom is granted to be useful. What this paper says is only that it is a stipulation and not a discovery. Relation to earlier papers: Paper 265 treated the density of states of a crystal──this paper looks at the same crystal from the side of classification. Paper 269 wrote that what a crystal forbids is periodicity──this paper writes that the boundary of a classification is a stipulation. Both keep the same discipline of not mistaking what does the deciding. Paper 273 counted four different quantities written in the same unit──this paper writes that two names are cutting one continuous quantity. Paper 190 measured rare on a logarithmic scale──this paper writes the span of 10^70 in orders of magnitude. Paper 201 counted “complete” as four different claims──this paper is the converse, writing that two names point at one continuous quantity. What is added is computing exp(-E_g/2kT) for seven materials and obtaining a span of 10^70, observing that a line at 3 eV makes insulators of SiC and GaN, computing that diamond rises by 1.45x10^32 at 1000 K, obtaining that diamond at 1000 K exceeds SiC at 300 K by 3.97x10^13, and obtaining 1465.2 K as the temperature at which diamond reaches silicon's room-temperature value. First, set out seven materials at room temperature. Germanium gives 2.3564x10^-6 and silica 2.5312x10^-76──a span of 9.31x10^69 (Section 2). Second, this is the core of the paper. Across that span of 10^70 there is not one break──move E_g continuously and the value moves continuously (Section 2). Third, “above 3 eV is an insulator” is a stipulation. Drawing that line makes insulators of SiC (3.26 eV) and GaN (3.40 eV)──and both are called power semiconductors in practice (Section 3). Fourth, the boundary moves with temperature. Diamond gives 1.1325x10^-46 at 300 K and 1.6452x10^-14 at 1000 K──the same material rises by 1.4527x10^32 (Section 4). Fifth, the ordering is exchanged. Diamond at 1000 K, an “insulator”, stands a factor of 3.97x10^13 above SiC at 300 K, a “semiconductor”(Section 4). Sixth, the classification is not a property of the material. Diamond reaches silicon's room-temperature value at 1465.2 K──without writing down the temperature, the classification is not settled (Section 5). between a semiconductor and an insulator there was no natural boundary. At room temperature the values run from 2.3564x10^-6 for germanium to 2.5312x10^-76 for silica, a span of 10^70, and nowhere along that road is there a jump. The line “above 3 eV is an insulator” is a stipulation, and drawing it makes insulators of SiC and GaN──both of which are power semiconductors in fact. And moving the temperature moves the boundary itself. Diamond rises by 1.45x10^32 at 1000 K and stands a factor of 3.97x10^13 above SiC at 300 K──the “insulator” has overtaken the “semiconductor”. One thing separates them──writing down at what temperature one is looking. Write it down, and the property of the material separates from the line that was drawn. Do not write it down, and one reads a boundary drawn by people as one drawn by nature across a continuous span of 10^70. On the making of this work: The ideas and content of this work stem from the author's own considerations. Assistance from an AI (a large language model) was used for structuring, English translation, and checking the algebra. Any remaining errors or misinterpretations are solely the author's. Feedback and corrections are sincerely appreciated. ----- 物質は半導体と絶縁体に分けられている。本稿が問うのは、その境目はどこにあるのかである──答は、どこにも無い。真性キャリア濃度は exp(-E_g/2kT) で連続に変わり、跳ぶ場所が一つも無い。新しい数学定理も新しい法則も主張しない。 本稿の射程(射程注記):新しい数学定理も新しい法則も主張しない──真性キャリア濃度が exp(-E_g/2kT) に比例すること、各物質のバンドギャップの値、半導体と絶縁体の慣用的な区別は、いずれも標準的である。固体物理を作らない──使うのは一つの指数関数だけである。バンド理論を扱わない──バンドギャップがなぜ生じるかは一切扱わない。絶対値を主張しない──exp(-E_g/2kT) は前因子を落とした比較用の量であり、実際のキャリア濃度ではない。有効質量も温度依存も入れていない。ドーピングを扱わない──真性(不純物の無い)場合だけを見る。実務の半導体は不純物が支配するので、本稿の量は実際の伝導度ではない。バンドギャップの温度依存を入れていない──実際には E_g が温度とともに縮む。第4節はそれを無視した下限側の見積もりである。バンドギャップの値を測定しない──すべて引用の代表値であり、文献によって幅がある。分類を改めよと言わない──慣用が便利であることは認める。本稿が言うのは、それが約束であって発見ではないという一点だけである。既刊との関係:論文265 は結晶の状態密度を扱った──本稿は同じ結晶を、分類の側から見る。論文269 は結晶が禁じているのが周期性だと書いた──本稿は分類の境目が約束であることを書く。どちらも何が決めているかを取り違えないという同じ規律である。論文273 は同じ単位が四つの別の量を書いていることを数えた──本稿は一つの連続量を二つの名前で切っていることを書く。論文190 は「稀」を対数の目盛りで測った──本稿は 10^70 という開きを桁で書く。論文201 は「完備」が四つの別の主張であることを数えた──本稿は逆に、二つの名前が一つの連続量を指していることを書く。加えたのは七つの物質で exp(-E_g/2kT) を計算して 10^70 の開きを出したこと、3 eV の線が SiC と GaN を絶縁体にしてしまうと見たこと、ダイヤモンドが 1000 K で 1.45x10^32 倍上がることを計算したこと、1000 K のダイヤモンドが 300 K の SiC を 3.97x10^13 倍上回ると出したこと、ダイヤモンドがシリコンの室温値に並ぶ温度を 1465.2 K と出したことである。 第一に、室温で七つの物質を並べる。 Ge が 2.3564x10^-6、SiO_2 が 2.5312x10^-76──開きは 9.31x10^69 倍である(第2節)。 第二に、これが本稿の芯である。10^70 の開きの中に、切れ目が一つも無い──E_g を連続に動かせば、値も連続に動く(第2節)。 第三に、「3 eV 以上は絶縁体」は約束である。その線を引くと SiC(3.26 eV)と GaN(3.40 eV)が絶縁体になる──どちらも実務ではパワー半導体と呼ばれている(第3節)。 第四に、温度で境界が動く。ダイヤモンドは 300 K で 1.1325x10^-46、1000 K で 1.6452x10^-14──同じ物質が 1.45x10^32 倍上がる(第4節)。 第五に、順序が入れ替わる。1000 K のダイヤモンド(絶縁体)は、300 K の SiC(半導体)より 3.97x10^13 倍上に来る(第4節)。 第六に、分類は物質の性質ではない。ダイヤモンドは 1465.2 K でシリコンの室温値に並ぶ──何度で見るかを書かなければ、分類は決まらない(第5節)。 半導体と絶縁体のあいだに、自然の境目は無かった。室温での値は Ge の 2.3564x10^-6 から SiO_2 の 2.5312x10^-76 まで 10^70 開いているのに、その道のりのどこにも跳びが無い。「3 eV 以上は絶縁体」という線は約束であり、その線を引くと SiC と GaN が絶縁体になってしまう──どちらも実際にはパワー半導体である。そして温度を動かせば境界そのものが動く。ダイヤモンドは 1000 K で 1.45x10^32 倍上がり、300 K の SiC より 3.97x10^13 倍上に来る──「絶縁体」が「半導体」を追い越している。分けるものは一つ──何度で見ているのかを書き出すこと。書き出せば、物質の性質と、引いた線が分かれる。書き出さなければ、10^70 の連続な並びの上に、自然が引いた境目があると読んでしまう。 作成にあたって:本稿の着想と内容は、著者自身の考察に基づくものです。文章の構成整理や英訳、数式の確認には AI(大規模言語モデル)の助力を得ました。最終的な内容の解釈や誤りがあれば、それらはすべて著者の責に帰します。お気づきの点があれば、ご教示いただければ幸いです。

item.title: There Is No Natural Boundary between a Semiconductor and an Insulator ── The Value Runs Continuously across a Span of 10^70 without One Jump ── Diamond, an "Insulator", Stands at 1000 K a Factor of 3.97x10^13 above SiC, a "Semiconductor", at Room Temperature ── [Paper 275]
item.description: Materials are divided into semiconductors and insulators. This paper asks where that boundary lies──the answer is nowhere. The intrinsic carrier concentration varies continuously as exp(-E_g/2kT), and there is not one place where it jumps. No new mathematical theorem and no new law is claimed. Scope of this paper (scope note): No new mathematical theorem and no new law is claimed──that the intrinsic carrier concentration goes as exp(-E_g/2kT), the band gaps of these materials, and the customary distinction between semiconductors and insulators are all standard. No solid-state physics is built──what is used is one exponential. Band theory is not treated──why a band gap arises is not treated at all. No absolute value is claimed──exp(-E_g/2kT) is a quantity for comparison with the prefactor dropped, and not a real carrier concentration. Neither effective masses nor their temperature dependence are included. Doping is not treated──only the intrinsic case is examined. Practical semiconductors are dominated by impurities, so the quantity here is not a real conductivity. The temperature dependence of the band gap is not included──in fact E_g shrinks with temperature. Section 4 neglects that and is therefore an estimate on the conservative side. No band gap is measured──all are cited representative values and vary between sources. No revision of the classification is urged──the custom is granted to be useful. What this paper says is only that it is a stipulation and not a discovery. Relation to earlier papers: Paper 265 treated the density of states of a crystal──this paper looks at the same crystal from the side of classification. Paper 269 wrote that what a crystal forbids is periodicity──this paper writes that the boundary of a classification is a stipulation. Both keep the same discipline of not mistaking what does the deciding. Paper 273 counted four different quantities written in the same unit──this paper writes that two names are cutting one continuous quantity. Paper 190 measured rare on a logarithmic scale──this paper writes the span of 10^70 in orders of magnitude. Paper 201 counted “complete” as four different claims──this paper is the converse, writing that two names point at one continuous quantity. What is added is computing exp(-E_g/2kT) for seven materials and obtaining a span of 10^70, observing that a line at 3 eV makes insulators of SiC and GaN, computing that diamond rises by 1.45x10^32 at 1000 K, obtaining that diamond at 1000 K exceeds SiC at 300 K by 3.97x10^13, and obtaining 1465.2 K as the temperature at which diamond reaches silicon's room-temperature value. First, set out seven materials at room temperature. Germanium gives 2.3564x10^-6 and silica 2.5312x10^-76──a span of 9.31x10^69 (Section 2). Second, this is the core of the paper. Across that span of 10^70 there is not one break──move E_g continuously and the value moves continuously (Section 2). Third, “above 3 eV is an insulator” is a stipulation. Drawing that line makes insulators of SiC (3.26 eV) and GaN (3.40 eV)──and both are called power semiconductors in practice (Section 3). Fourth, the boundary moves with temperature. Diamond gives 1.1325x10^-46 at 300 K and 1.6452x10^-14 at 1000 K──the same material rises by 1.4527x10^32 (Section 4). Fifth, the ordering is exchanged. Diamond at 1000 K, an “insulator”, stands a factor of 3.97x10^13 above SiC at 300 K, a “semiconductor”(Section 4). Sixth, the classification is not a property of the material. Diamond reaches silicon's room-temperature value at 1465.2 K──without writing down the temperature, the classification is not settled (Section 5). between a semiconductor and an insulator there was no natural boundary. At room temperature the values run from 2.3564x10^-6 for germanium to 2.5312x10^-76 for silica, a span of 10^70, and nowhere along that road is there a jump. The line “above 3 eV is an insulator” is a stipulation, and drawing it makes insulators of SiC and GaN──both of which are power semiconductors in fact. And moving the temperature moves the boundary itself. Diamond rises by 1.45x10^32 at 1000 K and stands a factor of 3.97x10^13 above SiC at 300 K──the “insulator” has overtaken the “semiconductor”. One thing separates them──writing down at what temperature one is looking. Write it down, and the property of the material separates from the line that was drawn. Do not write it down, and one reads a boundary drawn by people as one drawn by nature across a continuous span of 10^70. On the making of this work: The ideas and content of this work stem from the author's own considerations. Assistance from an AI (a large language model) was used for structuring, English translation, and checking the algebra. Any remaining errors or misinterpretations are solely the author's. Feedback and corrections are sincerely appreciated. ----- 物質は半導体と絶縁体に分けられている。本稿が問うのは、その境目はどこにあるのかである──答は、どこにも無い。真性キャリア濃度は exp(-E_g/2kT) で連続に変わり、跳ぶ場所が一つも無い。新しい数学定理も新しい法則も主張しない。 本稿の射程(射程注記):新しい数学定理も新しい法則も主張しない──真性キャリア濃度が exp(-E_g/2kT) に比例すること、各物質のバンドギャップの値、半導体と絶縁体の慣用的な区別は、いずれも標準的である。固体物理を作らない──使うのは一つの指数関数だけである。バンド理論を扱わない──バンドギャップがなぜ生じるかは一切扱わない。絶対値を主張しない──exp(-E_g/2kT) item.title: INDICATORS FOR ASSESSING THE LIQUIDITY OF COMMERCIAL BANKS
item.description: The thesis systematises the modern system of indicators used to assess the liquidity of commercial banks and evaluates their analytical capabilities under the conditions of digital banking. The category of bank liquidity is treated as multidimensional, and its assessment therefore requires a combination of stock, flow, structural and market indicators. On the basis of a critical review of the works of Diamond and Dybvig, Berger and Bouwman, Brunnermeier and Pedersen, Bonner, Van Lelyveld and Zymek, Drechsler, Savov and Schnabl, Duffie, Acharya, Cornett and other scholars, and of the regulatory documents of the Basel Committee, the paper systematises three groups of indicators: traditional coefficient-based, Basel III regulatory (LCR, NSFR, LR) and modern market-based (BLC index, Amihud illiquidity, Liquidity Mismatch Index). A summary table of the indicators, their formulas and analytical purposes is presented. The paper concludes that a modern methodology for assessing the liquidity of a bank should combine indicators of all three groups within an integrated dashboard supported by real-time data analytics.

item.title: Beal Conjecture — Typed Patching and Tate-Certified Descent — v8.3.0
item.description: Version 8.3.0 records an audited conditional milestone in Lean 4. Exact-divisibility proofs no longer live in the Wiles plan or Galois edge witnesses: the odd-prime Tate interface derives each edge from the canonical Frey model and its conductor. The terminal 2-adic exponent-one premise is explicit model-indexed data. The patching layer carries residual-representation, Hecke-attachment, deformation, comparison, finite-level action, and diamond-specialization data. The final route remains conditional on exactly three named mathematical interfaces—frey_conductor_data, tate_step2_odd_prime_external, and wiles_modularity—and two unconstructed data suppliers, TwoAdicExponentOneSupplier and EnrichedPlanSupplier. This is not an unconditional proof of the Beal Conjecture.

item.title: IMPROVING THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN THE STABILITY OF THE DEPOSIT BASE AND LIQUIDITY RISK MANAGEMENT IN COMMERCIAL BANKS
item.description: Abstract: The thesis systematises the modern theoretical and empirical views on the interconnection between the stability of the deposit base and the liquidity risk management of commercial banks, and proposes directions for its improvement. Deposit stability is treated as a multidimensional category combining structural composition (retail vs corporate, insured vs uninsured, term vs demand), maturity structure and behavioural response to shocks. On the basis of the works of Diamond and Dybvig, Song and Thakor, Hanson, Shleifer, Stein and Vishny, Drechsler, Savov and Schnabl, Egan, Hortaçsu and Matvos, Koont, Santos and Zingales, the paper analyses how deposit stability enters the modern liquidity risk management framework of Basel III. A summary table of deposit categories and associated liquidity risk factors is presented. The paper concludes that deposit stability is the primary determinant of liquidity risk and that its management should combine microprudential ratios, behavioural indicators and macroprudential monitoring.

item.title: ECONOMIC ESSENCE OF COMMERCIAL BANK LIQUIDITY
item.description: Abstract: The thesis reveals the economic essence of commercial bank liquidity as a fundamental category of modern banking theory and practice. Bank liquidity is interpreted as the ability of a bank to meet its financial obligations in full and on time and, at the same time, to satisfy the borrowing needs of its clients without incurring unacceptable losses. On the basis of a critical review of the fundamental works of Diamond and Dybvig, Bryant, Allen and Gale, Freixas and Rochet, Brunnermeier, Acharya, Rochet and Vives, Drechsler, Savov and Schnabl, as well as of the documents of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, the paper systematises the evolution of theoretical views on liquidity from the classical "real bills doctrine" to the modern integrated concept combining stock, flow and market dimensions. A comparative table of the four theoretical schools of bank liquidity is presented. The thesis concludes that under the conditions of digital banking and the 2023 crisis of U.S. mid-sized banks, liquidity must be interpreted as a dynamic, multidimensional and reputation-sensitive category, and that a modern definition should synthesise the stock, cash-flow, market-liquidity and confidence-based approaches.

item.title: The Fourth Allotrope and Its Progeny: A Narrative Review of Carbon Nanomaterials Chemistry from Buckminsterfullerene to Graphene
item.description: Carbon nanomaterials chemistry---the chemistry of the closed cages, tubes, and sheets that joined diamond and graphite as carbon's allotropes---began with a mass spectrum's mysterious peak and became materials science's most decorated family. This article presents a narrative review of that arc's canonical line: Kroto, Heath, O'Brien, Curl, and Smalley's 1985 buckminsterfullerene, Kratschmer and colleagues' 1990 solid C60, Iijima's 1991 microtubules, Ebbesen and Ajayan's 1992 bulk synthesis, Bethune and colleagues' 1993 single-walled tubes, Hirsch's 1994 fullerene chemistry, Diederich and Thilgen's 1996 covalent chemistry, Kroto's 1997 Nobel lecture, Novoselov and colleagues' 2004 electric-field effect, Novoselov and colleagues' 2005 Dirac fermions, Geim and Novoselov's 2007 rise of graphene, and Hirsch's 2010 carbon allotropes. The synthesis is organized around three themes: discovery, in which cluster chemistry's forty-atom mystery became a closed cage and a new allotrope; chemistry, in which fullerenes and nanotubes acquired addition chemistry, endohedral chemistry, and bulk synthesis; and graphenics, in which the two-dimensional sheet's Dirac fermions made carbon physics extraordinary. It is concluded that carbon nanomaterials are chemistry's most improbable success story---an aesthetic cage's accidental synthesis opening three decades of nanoscience---and that their history is the proof that curiosity's chemistry funds itself.

item.title: Seeing the Invisible: A Narrative Review of Chemical Crystallography from the Braggs' Salts to Femtosecond Nanocrystals
item.description: Chemical crystallography---the art of seeing molecules by their diffraction---moved from the Braggs' first salts to the structures that wrote modern chemistry and biology: penicillin's and vitamin B12's shells solved without hydrogen, the proteins' first models, and the femtosecond nanocrystals of the free-electron era. This article presents a narrative review of that arc's canonical line: Bragg's 1913 structure of salts, the Braggs' 1913 diamond, Robertson's 1935 cholesterol, Hauptman and Karle's 1953 phase monograph, Watson and Crick's 1953 nucleic acid structure, Hodgkin and colleagues' 1956 vitamin B12, Kendrew and colleagues' 1958 myoglobin, Blake and colleagues' 1965 lysozyme, Adams and colleagues' 1969 insulin, Giacovazzo's 1992 fundamentals, Drenth's 1997 protein crystallography, and Chapman and colleagues' 2011 femtosecond nanocrystallography. The review is organized around three themes: foundations, in which the diffraction's law and the phase's problem were stated; structures, in which the molecules' shapes---from cholesterol's to insulin's---were solved and their chemistry rewritten; and methods, in which the direct methods' statistics, the protein's crystallography, and the X-ray laser's femtoseconds generalized the seeing. It is concluded that chemical crystallography is chemistry's eye---the discipline that turned the molecule from an inference into a picture---and that its pictures now anchor every structure-activity argument in the sciences.

item.title: Seeing the Invisible: A Narrative Review of Chemical Crystallography from the Braggs' Salts to Femtosecond Nanocrystals
item.description: Chemical crystallography---the art of seeing molecules by their diffraction---moved from the Braggs' first salts to the structures that wrote modern chemistry and biology: penicillin's and vitamin B12's shells solved without hydrogen, the proteins' first models, and the femtosecond nanocrystals of the free-electron era. This article presents a narrative review of that arc's canonical line: Bragg's 1913 structure of salts, the Braggs' 1913 diamond, Robertson's 1935 cholesterol, Hauptman and Karle's 1953 phase monograph, Watson and Crick's 1953 nucleic acid structure, Hodgkin and colleagues' 1956 vitamin B12, Kendrew and colleagues' 1958 myoglobin, Blake and colleagues' 1965 lysozyme, Adams and colleagues' 1969 insulin, Giacovazzo's 1992 fundamentals, Drenth's 1997 protein crystallography, and Chapman and colleagues' 2011 femtosecond nanocrystallography. The review is organized around three themes: foundations, in which the diffraction's law and the phase's problem were stated; structures, in which the molecules' shapes---from cholesterol's to insulin's---were solved and their chemistry rewritten; and methods, in which the direct methods' statistics, the protein's crystallography, and the X-ray laser's femtoseconds generalized the seeing. It is concluded that chemical crystallography is chemistry's eye---the discipline that turned the molecule from an inference into a picture---and that its pictures now anchor every structure-activity argument in the sciences.

item.title: Load-bearing capacity and vibration transmission of MSLA-printed lattices: Interplay of topology, relative density, and variability
item.description: Masked stereolithography (MSLA), a vat photopolymerization (VPP) process, offers a lightweight route to polymer lattice components with tunable mechanical and dynamic performance, yet the link between processing, load-bearing response, and broadband vibration transmission remains unclear. This study examines four strut-based polymer lattices, Simple Cubic (SC), Face-Centered Cubic (FC), Diamond (DM), and Fluorite (FL), fabricated at relative densities of 10%, 20%, and 30%. As-built density, quasi-static compression, transmissibility measurements over 10-6410 Hz, and solid-element modal analysis including the measurement assembly were used to relate topology and density to the resulting mechanical and dynamic properties. Increasing relative density shifted the first dominant resonance to higher frequencies for all topologies, but did not improve broadband isolation monotonically. The dynamic rankings refer to the tested specimen-fixture-sensor assembly. Lower-density lattices entered the isolation regime earlier, whereas denser configurations remained transmissive over a wider frequency range. Within the tested specimen set, the results indicate a static–dynamic trade-off: FL-10 behaved as the isolation-first configuration, SC-20 as the load-bearing reference, and FL-20/DM-20 as candidate compromises when first-peak load and the 500-2000 Hz descriptor are used as the two criteria. The study shows that lattice selection should be based on the intended operating band together with the minimum acceptable mechanical capacity and an allowance for process-induced variability, rather than on relative density or static stiffness alone. Because each configuration contained two or three specimens, dense-configuration results are treated as preliminary trends.

item.title: Electrochemical Degradation of PFOA Using Graphite-Sheet Electrodes: Kinetics and Mechanisms
item.description: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent, bioaccumulative, and toxic contaminants characterized by highly stable fluorinated alkyl chains. Due to their chemical resilience, PFAS are frequently detected in both influents and effluents of conventional wastewater treatment plants, where they undergo minimal to no removal. Electrooxidation offers a promising, chemical-free approach for PFAS remediation, but it typically relies on expensive, high-performance electrodes such as boron-doped diamond (BDD) or titanium-based materials, limiting scalability and practical deployment. This study establishes the use of low-cost, unmodified, flexible graphite sheet electrodes as anodes for the electrochemical degradation of perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). The degradation efficiency was assessed under varying conditions, including initial PFOA concentrations (5–1,000 μg·L–1), current densities (2.5–12.5 mA.cm–2), pH (3–9), electrolyte concentrations (0–0.05 M NaCl), and the presence of reactive radical species. Under optimized conditions (0.05 M NaCl, 10 mA.cm–2, pH ≈ 6), ∼99% PFOA degradation was achieved within 90 min at an initial concentration of 10 μg·L–1, with a corresponding energy consumption of 16.09 kWh.m–3 per order. Hydroxyl radicals and chlorine-based reactive species were identified as key contributors to the degradation mechanism. However, degradation efficiency was inhibited in the presence of a complex wastewater matrix, consistent with the known limitations of radical-mediated processes. Liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC-MS) analysis of the 90 min sample revealed the formation of intermediate degradation products, including shorter-chain perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids such as perfluoroheptanoic acid (PFHpA), perfluorohexanoic acid (PFHxA), perfluoropentanoic acid (PFPeA), and perfluorobutanoic acid (PFBA). Overall, the electrochemical oxidation approach demonstrated in this study offers a promising, economically attractive alternative for the degradation of PFAS in contaminated groundwater and wastewater.

item.title: European Hebrew Journal International Scholarly Online Zoom Conference 6–10 November 2026 · Live Online via Zoom New Discoveries and New Directions in Biblical, Hebrew, and Theological Studies
item.description: This academic conference catalogue presents the programme, speakers, research themes, and scholarly context of the European Hebrew Journal International Scholarly Online Conference, "New Discoveries and New Directions in Biblical, Hebrew, and Theological Studies," held online from 6–10 November 2026. The five-day international programme brings together more than 60 scholars and researchers across approximately 60 scholarly sessions devoted to Biblical Studies, Hebrew Bible, Biblical Hebrew, biblical archaeology, Qumran and the Dead Sea Scrolls, manuscript studies, textual criticism, Second Temple Judaism, Jewish Studies, early Christianity, theology, ancient history, Semitic languages, digital humanities, computational linguistics, artificial intelligence, multispectral imaging, and new technologies for the study of ancient texts. The catalogue provides a structured overview of the complete conference programme, confirmed speakers, institutional affiliations, presentation titles, and major areas of research represented at EHJ 2026. It also serves as a persistent scholarly reference document linking individual presentations with their dedicated conference pages and with the European Hebrew Journal, a Diamond Open Access academic journal. The conference reflects current interdisciplinary directions in the study of the Bible, Hebrew language and literature, ancient Judaism and Christianity, archaeology, manuscripts, textual transmission, and digitally assisted humanities research. Particular attention is given to new archaeological discoveries, manuscript evidence, linguistic research, historical interpretation, computational approaches, and emerging applications of artificial intelligence in the study of ancient languages and texts. This catalogue is intended for scholars, researchers, students, librarians, educators, clergy, and others working in Biblical Studies, Hebrew and Semitic Studies, archaeology, Jewish Studies, theology, manuscript studies, digital humanities, and related fields.

item.title: NAVIGATING THE CHINA PLUS ONE PARADIGM: A COMPARATIVE STUDY OF GLOBAL MANUFACTURING REALIGNMENTS AND THEORETICAL FRAMEWORKS
item.description: Systemic wage inflation, demographic shifts, strict environmental regulatory enforcement, and rising geopolitical frictions are eroding China\'s historical manufacturing cost advantages. Global multinational corporations are transitioning from hyper efficient just-in-time networks to resilient, just-in-case value chains through the China Plus One (C+1) strategy. To address this, this study systematically compares the structural readiness, competitive factor conditions, and strategic advantages of key emerging manufacturing hubs: Vietnam, Mexico, India, Indonesia, and Malaysia. The research integrates John Dunning’s Eclectic (OLI) Paradigm, Michael Porter’s Diamond Model, the Uppsala Internationalisation Model, and the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC). While China retains core Ownership (O) and Internalisation (I) advantages, declining Location (L) benefits are driving labor intensive manufacturing to lower cost alternatives. India and Vietnam lead as comprehensive friendshoring alternatives due to favorable cost to scale structures and trade architectures. However, country specific bottlenecks (e.g., Mexico\'s utility deficits, Indonesia\'s youth training gaps, and India\'s agricultural protectionism) presents critical trade-offs for corporate strategy. This paper provides an integrated theoretical roadmap for mapping global value chain (GVC) restructuring and outlines targeted policy adjustments for host countries aiming to capture foreign direct investment (FDI).
item.dc:creator: Hrishit Somani

item.title: Exceptionally high carrier mobility in hexagonal diamond
item.description: This dataset supports the theoretical investigation reported in the manuscript "Exceptionally high carrier mobility in hexagonal diamond". Based on first-principles analyses of the electronic structures, carrier mobilities, and electron-phonon coupling mechanisms in both cubic diamond and hexagonal diamond, this work demonstrates high carrier mobility in the heaxagonal phase and elucidates its physical origins. The dataset includes relevant data files for geometry optimisation, phonon dispersion, dynamical quadrupole tensors, G0W0 quasiparticle bands, and carrier mobility calculations.

item.title: Opportunities for Quantum Sensing in Epilepsy Diagnostics
item.description: Diagnosis in epilepsy depends on several distinct objectives—including interictal epileptiform discharge (IED) detection, source localisation of epileptiform activity, and seizure classification—each shaped by the underlying sensing technology. This review examines the opportunities that quantum magnetic sensing offers within this diagnostic framework, with particular emphasis on translational readiness and clinical potential. Seizure classification is included to situate the broader clinical context of epilepsy diagnostics, whereas the review of quantum sensing evidence is focused on IED detection and presurgical source localisation, the objectives for which such evidence currently exists. Magnetoencephalography (MEG) provides non-invasive source localisation that complements electroencephalography (EEG), and its clinical adoption is increasingly determined by advances in magnetic sensor technology. Optically pumped magnetometer (OPM)-based MEG represents the most clinically developed quantum sensing application, progressing from proof-of-concept in 2020 toward small-cohort clinical feasibility studies from 2022 onwards. By enabling on-scalp recordings at reduced sensor-to-brain distance, OPM-MEG improves signal amplitude and permits flexible sensor placement, with early evidence of benefit in paediatric populations and mesial temporal lobe epilepsy. However, current evidence derives from small, heterogeneous cohorts, and no prospective data yet link OPM-MEG to surgical outcomes. 4He-OPMs represent an early feasibility stage with IED detection comparable to superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID)-MEG in small case series; nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond and silicon carbide divacancy magnetometry remain preclinical, constrained by a fundamental standoff-sensitivity trade-off. We conclude that OPM-MEG is best positioned as a complementary modality within established presurgical workflows, with prospective multicentre outcome studies representing the critical next step toward clinical translation.

item.title: SIMCES: A proof-of-concept framework for command and control in emergency medical services
item.description: Objectives: Command and control in emergency medical services (EMS) responses to major incidents and mass casualty events is supported by multiple established doctrines; however, variability in their operational integration persists across EMS systems. The objective of this manuscript is to present the development of Sistema de Mando y Control en Emergencias Sanitarias (SIMCES), a proof-of-concept EMS command-and-control framework intended to integrate established incident management doctrines with selected conceptual and operational innovations.Methods: SIMCES was developed using a practice-based design-thinking methodology informed by the Double Diamond process (Discover, Define, Develop, Deliver). The Discover phase was informed by frontline operational experience, informal multidisciplinary feedback, and an exploratory narrative review of the literature related to EMS incident management and major incident response. During the Define phase, recurrent operational challenges were mapped to established functional domains using the Command, Safety, Communication, Assessment, Triage, Treatment, Transport framework. In the Develop phase, proposed framework components were iteratively refined through structured, scenario-based theoretical walkthroughs across representative incident types, including mass casualty incidents, hazardous materials incidents, structural collapses, high-threat scenarios, and preplanned major events. The Deliver phase consisted of consolidating the framework and applying it in structured, paper-based scenario walkthroughs to explore internal coherence and applicability across different levels of incident complexity.Results: SIMCES is presented as an integrated, EMS-oriented framework that combines established doctrinal elements with selected conceptual innovations. The framework includes a four-level incident classification system; a cordon-based approach to zoning and sectorization; a three-tiered EMS command structure with standardized commander and officer roles; the tactical coordination and support cell as an organizational construct for managing operational information and resource coordination; the COMMAND mnemonic to structure transfer of command; the 1-3-3 rule to guide initial actions of first-arriving units; and the introduction of a white triage category in evacuation triage to document discharged or self-evacuated casualties.Conclusions: SIMCES is proposed as a proof-of-concept framework intended to support structured thinking about EMS command and control during complex incidents. The manuscript does not evaluate performance or outcomes. External validation is planned to examine content validity, acceptability, applicability, workload, and feasibility before any conclusions regarding effectiveness can be drawn.
