item.title: Compact localized states and magnetic flux-driven topological phase transition in a diamond-dodecagon lattice geometry
item.description: Abstract We propose and investigate a novel two-dimensional (2D) tight-binding model defined on a diamond-dodecagon lattice geometry that hosts multiple flat bands (FBs) and supports topological phase transitions driven by a magnetic flux. This lattice exhibits three completely flat, nondispersive bands in the band structure in the absence of magnetic flux due to destructive interference in the electron hoppings, leading to the emergence of compact localized states (CLS). These CLS are analytically constructed and exhibit real-space confinement of the electrons, arising solely due to the lattice's geometrical frustration. It has been shown that these FBs are very robust against the introduction of weak random onsite disorder in the system. By tuning the uniform magnetic flux threaded through the diamond plaquettes, we demonstrate a tunable evolution of the band structure and show that certain bands develop nontrivial topological features with nonzero integer values of the Chern number. Additionally, we have computed the multi-terminal transport properties for this 2D lattice system, which display the flux-tunable resonances and transmission suppression linked to the FBs, establishing a clear interplay between the localization, topology, and transport. Our findings put forward the diamond-dodecagon lattice as a robust and tunable platform for studying the flat-band physics and magnetic flux-controlled topological phenomena, offering promising experimental feasibility in photonic lattices and ultracold atomic systems.

item.title: High-speed jet impact induced shearing and exfoliation of graphite
item.description: Abstract Mass production of high-quality graphene, a two-dimensional material with wide applications, remains challenging and limits the exploitation of its exceptional electrical and mechanical properties. This study introduces a simple, environmentally friendly mechanical method for exfoliating graphite into few-layer graphene through high-speed impact-induced shearing in an aqueous medium. Graphite flakes dispersed in water with a small amount of surfactant are pressurised and accelerated through a nozzle to impact a hard-polycrystalline diamond substrate. The high-velocity impact generates sufficient shear to overcome the weak van der Waals forces between graphite layers, enabling graphene exfoliation while minimizing contact time and using water as a sustainable processing medium. The feasibility of this approach has been evaluated at two different velocities and with varying impact cycles. Characterization results show clear evidence of shear-induced exfoliation. Higher impact velocities achieved effective exfoliation in 10 cycles, whereas lower velocities required 50 cycles. Producing few-layer and multi-layer graphene at lower velocities necessitated more impact cycles, resulting in increased defect formation. In contrast, higher velocities produced graphene with an O/C ratio of 0.0284 and an ID/IG ratio of 0.13, compared with 0.0307 and 0.24, respectively, at lower velocities. This approach offers a promising new route for producing few-layer graphene with minimal defects, making it suitable for future industrial applications.

item.title: Modal assurance criterion-guided section selection optimization for increasing the modal frequency of a railway carbody
item.description: The carbody commonly exhibits a low first-order diamond modal frequency, degrading ride comfort and operational safety of the railway vehicle. Existing optimization methods yield results that are often difficult to implement directly under standardized manufacturing constraints, and discrete dynamic optimization is prone to severe modal exchange during iterations, leading to inaccurate identification of the target mode, and invalid optimization. To address these issues, a mode-consistent discrete section selection framework guided by the Modal Assurance Criterion (MAC) is proposed for enhancing the first-order diamond modal frequency of the carbody. A design space comprising standard sections with discrete orientations is constructed to ensure engineering feasibility, and an eccentric Rayleigh beam formulation is developed to capture the centroid eccentricity, rotary inertia, and bending-torsion coupling of asymmetric sections. A MAC-based mode-tracking constraint is embedded into the optimization loop to maintain the continuity of the diamond mode and eliminate modal exchange. The proposed method is verified against commercial finite element analysis and applied to a full-scale carbody. Results show that the first-order diamond modal frequency increases from 7.18 to 7.64 Hz without modifying the global structural layout. A two-stage scheme that integrates the proposed method with engineering reinforcements further raises the frequency to 8.66 Hz, with the discrete section optimization contributing 31.1% of the total improvement at only half the mass increment of the global reinforcements. Vehicle dynamics simulation confirms that the increased modal frequency effectively suppresses the abnormal elastic vibration and improves the running stability.

item.title: Optical Properties of Composite Resins: An In Vitro Investigation of Different Polishing Procedures
item.description: Background: This study aimed to compare and evaluate the color stability and translucency of different composite resins subjected to various polishing procedures.Methods: Three different composite resins (G-aenial Achord-GA, Charisma Topaz One-CTO, Charisma Bulk Flow One-CBF) and three different polishing procedures (Diamond Polish Mint, Lucida, and Super-Snap) were included in this study. Thirty samples of each composite resin were prepared and randomly divided into three groups (n=10). Polishing procedures of the test groups were conducted. The baseline color values of all the samples were measured using a spectrophotometer. After a 14-day coffee immersion, color measurements were repeated. White and black background measurements were carried out before (TP001) and after coffee immersion (TP002) for translucency calculations. Data were analyzed using Jamovi v2.3.28. item.title: Computational Study of Residual Stress Development and Dimensional Deviations in LPBF-fabricated Ti-6Al-4V TPMS Lattice Structures
item.description: The dataset supports a combined experimental–numerical study of LPBF-fabricated Ti-6Al-4V TPMS lattice structures (gyroid, Schwarz diamond, and Schwarz primitive) at 20% relative density, built at 0°, 30°, and 45° orientations in as-printed and heat-treated (670 °C, 4.5 h) conditions. It comprises thermomechanically coupled finite element predictions of residual stress and surface deviation; experimental validation data from 3D optical scanning (dimensional deviation) and XRD–Williamson–Hall analysis (microstrain and residual stress trends); areal surface roughness measurements (Sa, Sq); quasi-static compression results (stress–displacement curves, peak strength, and energy absorption); and SEM images of failure morphology. Together these data characterise the coupled effects of topology, build orientation, and stress-relief heat treatment on manufacturability, dimensional accuracy, surface integrity, and compressive performance.

item.title: ALGEBRAIC CURVE RATIONAL PARAMETERIZATION AND TOPOLOGICAL INVARIANCE OF TRADITIONAL GARDEN LATTICE PATTERN GENERATION ALGORITHM
item.description: To address issues in the generation of traditional garden lattice window patterns - such as inconsistent curve representation, the tendency for complex intersection points to drift, and the difficulty of maintaining closed-loop structures - this study proposes a Rational Parameterization-based Topology Preserving Generation Algorithm (RPTPGA). First, circular, diamond, and petal-shaped lattice window units are represented as families of planar algebraic curves defined by parameters, thereby establishing a unified algebraic curve model. Second, rational parameterization is employed to generate continuous curves, and composite patterns are constructed by combining rotation, mirroring, and translation transformations. Then, a topological feature vector comprising the number of connected components, intersection points, and closed loops is defined to establish a criterion for topology preservation under parameter perturbation. Simulation experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a Hausdorff error of 0.019, a topology preservation rate of 96.8%, a node consistency of 97.1%, and an average execution time of 0.28 s. Overall, the method outperforms the Bézier, Fourier, and $L$-system approaches, validating its effectiveness regarding curve continuity, node stability, and topological consistency.

item.title: Loose interfacial water molecule induced low friction on ice
item.description: Abstract Reducing the ice surface friction coefficient is crucial for improving the performance of winter sports equipment and enhancing the energy efficiency of icebreakers. The existence of a lubricating layer on the ice surface is the fundamental reason for the slippery ice surface. However, understanding the role of lubricating layer in ice friction presents challenges due to the complex interactions between water molecules and various materials. This study investigates the underlying mechanisms that govern ice-surface friction through advanced material design, utilizing a multiscale characterization approach that incorporates Rheometry, Raman spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and sum frequency generation (SFG) spectroscopy. We examined the effects of interfacial lubricating layer on friction across varying sliding velocities, contact pressures, and temperatures. Our findings indicate that three types distinct elements doped diamond-like carbon (DLC) films can achieve ultralow friction on ice, with a-C:H, a-C:H:Si, and a-C:H:WC showing reductions in the friction coefficient of 21.5%, 38.7%, and 58.6%, respectively, when compared to bearing steel (SUJ2). Here, we reveal the mechanism underlying the low friction of DLC on both ice surfaces and in water. In addition to the conventional graphitization induced low friction mechanism, the low friction coefficient is also closely associated with the presence of loosely structured interfacial water molecules, which exhibit a "liquid-like" arrangement and a disordered hydrogen bonding network that collectively contribute to the reduced friction. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations directly visualize the contribution of loosely structured interfacial water molecules to low interfacial shear. This work presents a novel low friction material of DLC for ice surfaces. The groundbreaking discovery offers an innovative solution for friction reduction engineering in aqueous environments and for advancing competitive winter sports technology. Achieving friction reduction by regulating the molecular structure of interfacial water would be significant for the lubrication industry.

item.title: Melting Temperature Under Pressure in ‘Hard’ and Soft Matter
item.description: This report focuses on cognitive gaps of the pressure dependence of melting temperature, presenting: (i) a coherent discussion on Tm(P) behavior for both ‘Hard Matter’ (‘standard’ solid state) and Soft Matter systems, to reveal the importance of the strength of intermolecular interactions; (ii) a model picture linking systems with dTm/dP>0, dTm/dP<0, and the TmP curve maximum, which also shows the relevance of the negative-pressure domain; and (iii) the ultimate validation test of the recent ‘universal’ parabolic scaling of Pm(T) against empirical data. The evidence for ‘Hard Matter’ focuses on systems relevant to the semiconductor industry: silicon, germanium, and gallium nitride. For Soft Matter, these include unique polymeric systems and liquid-crystalline pentylcyanobiphenyl (5CB). For the latter, symmetry-selected melting/freezing takes place. Finally, the report presents the specific case of graphite and diamond. The report also presents an innovative solution for melting-temperature and pressure detection.

item.title: Where Do Periodic Density Structures Acquire Coherence? A Low-Coronal Resonator Candidate and a 12-Event STEREO/SECCHI Transfer Test
item.description: Periodic density structures (PDS) are trains of plasma enhancements carried into the heliosphere, but their repeated timing does not by itself identify where the cadence is set. We test whether PDS selected independently in the outer corona can be traced back to a low-coronal clock, and whether that organization survives through the EUVI--COR1--COR2 observing chain. We analyze 12 STEREO-A/SECCHI events on 2008 January 11--14 along a nonradial path. EUVI 171 A at 1.10--1.20 R_sun shows an unusual concentration of power in the predeclared 80--130 minute band relative to filter-matched red-noise controls, while the ensemble is most strongly organized in upper COR1 at 2.5--3.0 R_sun. These signatures identify a low-coronal modulation candidate and an intermediate-height organization domain, but they do not form a unique phase-preserving clock extending into COR2. Instead, the more persistent observable is spatial order. Events 9 and 12 retain expansion-stable outward ordering. In polar r--theta maps, intersections of oppositely inclined, expansion-aware matched-filter ridge supports form repeated X-/diamond-like patterns. The morphology is compatible with stationary or quasi-stationary shock-cell processing, although the brightness diagnostics are insufficient to establish a stationary MHD shock branch. The observations therefore favor an intermittent source--gate--transfer picture: a low-coronal cadence may modulate plasma release, while event-dependent propagation progressively destroys exact phase coherence. The outward ordering of the density structures can survive, providing a more persistent signature of the source-to-wind transfer than phase locking itself.

item.title: A priori bounds for the generalized parabolic Anderson model in the full subcritical regime
item.description: We show a priori bounds for the generalized Parabolic Anderson Model $(\partial_t - Δ)u = σ(u) \diamond ξ$ in finite volume in the full subcritical regime. The approach is based on the observation that, for constant initial data, the time interval over which the solution remains close to its initial condition can be chosen uniformly in the value of the initial condition. A comparison principle is then used to extend this estimate to general bounded initial data.
item.dc:creator: Salvador Esquivel
Felix Schwarzfischer

item.title: Sustained macroscopic quantum coherence in a superradiant solid under ambient conditions
item.description: Macroscopic quantum coherence, such as in laser, Bose-Einstein condensates, superfluids, and superconductors, is important to fundamental physics and useful for quantum technologies. Superradiance provides a mechanism to produce coherence among a large number of particles and photons. Its implementation, however, has been limited to gaseous systems, solids at very low temperature, or short pulses. Here we demonstrate a solid-state superradiant maser under ambient conditions, which establishes long-lived coherence among about $10^{14}$ nitrogen-vacancy center spins in diamond and about $10^9$ photons in a microwave cavity. By varying the system parameters to access the above-threshold, well-above-threshold, and deep-above-threshold regimes, we observed continuous-wave masing, periodic amplitude modulation, and sequences of superradiant bursts, which are attributed, correspondingly, to macroscopic spin coherence synchronized at a fixed frequency, a coherent time crystal of large spins, and unsynchronized superradiant transients. This work demonstrates that macroscopic quantum coherence can be spontaneously generated and maintained in solids under ambient conditions and provides a solid-state platform for exploring bright quantum lights with many-body correlations.

item.title: Diamond synthesis, fusion and direct drive.
item.description: Ce document technique présente l'architecture de la Tuyère « Gogeta », un système d'ignition thermonucléaire par confinement magnétique asymétrique. Il détaille la formation de « Paires d'Anti-Cooper » via un dopage diamantaire de type P-N pour masquer la valence du carburant Proton-Bore 11 ($p-^{11}B$) et neutraliser la répulsion coulombienne lors de l'injection balistique. L'étude modélise la striction hexapolaire (Z-Pinch) générée par une configuration en Étoile Judéenne de tores quantiques IMES, ainsi que la boucle d'auto-alimentation énergétique par conversion directe de l'onde d'induction. Enfin, le dossier explore les protocoles de sécurité moléculaire et de survie thermodynamique du réacteur, incluant un bouclier liquide de sels de chlorure pour l'absorption du rayonnement de freinage, un cycle de micro-fusion pulsée et une télémétrie quantique active pilotant un réseau de refroidissement laser.

item.description: Ce document technique présente l'architecture de la Tuyère « Gogeta », un système d'ignition thermonucléaire par confinement magnétique asymétrique. Il détaille la formation de « Paires d'Anti-Cooper » via un dopage diamantaire de type P-N pour masquer la valence du carburant Proton-Bore 11 ($p-^{11}B$) et neutraliser la répulsion coulombienne lors de l'injection balistique. L'étude modélise la striction hexapolaire (Z-Pinch) générée par une configuration en Étoile Judéenne de tores quantiques IMES, ainsi que la boucle d'auto-alimentation énergétique par conversion directe de l'onde d'induction. Enfin, le dossier explore les protocoles de sécurité moléculaire et de survie thermodynamique du réacteur, incluant un bouclier liquide de sels de chlorure pour l'absorption du rayonnement de freinage, un cycle de micro-fusion pulsée et une télémétrie quantique active pilotant un réseau de refroidissement laser.

item.title: La Paradoja del Cierre en la Cibernética Jurídica: La Hendija de Gödel, el Vórtice de Heisenberg y la Soberanía del Cero Volitivo desde la Ética del Horizonte.
item.description: Resumen / Abstract. Resumen. El presente artículo despliega una crítica epistemológica y ontológica minuciosa contra las pretensiones de clausura en los modelos formalistas, las ontologías de proceso y los desarrollos juscibernéticos contemporáneos alimentados por el Dataísmo. Apoyándose en la arquitectura conceptual del Vademécum de la Luz y la Ética del Horizonte, se aborda formalmente la cuestión de Dios fuera y dentro del mundo (ex machina e intra machina) según la teología y la filosofía, examinando la geometría de Benedictus de Spinoza frente a la Geometría del Vademécum y desmantelando la "Filosofía del Organismo" de Alfred North Whitehead. Se conceptualiza la Pura Operación como la tentación ontológica que confunde la fórmula iterativa con el resultado absoluto en la jerga spinoziana, exponiendo el trauma de la incalculabilidad en el punto inextenso Semeion, la diagonal del cuadrado 2 y la trascendencia de . A través de un diálogo epistemológico riguroso, se expone la incompletitud constitutiva de la Teoría de la Información y la Cibernética mediante la brecha de Shannon y la irrupción del bit foráneo de Chaitin. Mediante el Inteligir Diamantino, se efectúa la decapitación de la secuencia de Axioma, Proposición y Escolio, así como del dispositivo del Quod Erat Demonstrandum (Q.E.D.) —mecanismo de cota escolástica y clausura deductiva emparentado con la metodología de la Summa Theologiae—, transformándolo en un Quod Perditum Dicitur (Q.P.D.), certificación del fallecimiento del sujeto en el altar del método. Asimismo, se expone con precisión la figura del Relator Omnisciente Contenido (o Sujeto Omnisciente Contenido) propia del Vademécum de la Luz y La Ética del Horizonte: una categoría genesial que articula la relación de la finitud encarnada con el relator del Génesis bíblico, traduciéndose en el Primer Setup de la Senda de la Entidad Eterna (el tránsito de a que fundamenta los axiomas del Inteligir Diamantino. Articulando el deslinde procedimental de Heidegger, la incompletitud de Gödel, el Vórtice de Heisenberg, la antinomia de Russell y el límite del Tractatus de Wittgenstein, se demuestra que todo intento de cierre informacional constituye un artificio ex machina. Finalmente, con el anclaje genésico del Eclesiastés, el "Corte del Mercader" y la Ousía, se restituye el Cero Volitivo como la trinchera jurígena inalienable para habitar la finitud con dignidad. Palabras clave: Juscibernética, Teoría de la Información, Bit Foráneo de Chaitin, Pura Operación, Inteligir Diamantino, Cota Escolástica, Summa Theologiae, Hendija de Gödel, Vórtice de Heisenberg, Relator Omnisciente Contenido, Senda de la Entidad Eterna, Tránsito Alfa-Beta, Cero Volitivo, Ousía, Eclesiastés, Q.E.D., Q.P.D. Abstract. This article presents a rigorous epistemological and ontological critique of closure claims within formalist models, process ontologies, and contemporary juscybernetic developments driven by Dataism. Drawing upon the conceptual framework of the Vademécum de la Luz and the Ethics of the Horizon, it formally addresses the question of God outside and inside the world (ex machina and intra machina) as framed by theology and philosophy, examining Spinoza's geometry alongside the Geometry of the Vademécum and deconstructing Alfred North Whitehead's "Philosophy of Organism". Pure Operation is conceptualized as the ontological temptation that conflates the iterative formula with the absolute result within Spinozian jargon, exposing the trauma of incalculability within the inextended point Semeion, the square's diagonal 2, and the transcendence of . Through an explicit epistemological dialogue, the paper demonstrates the inherent incompleteness of Information Theory and Cybernetics via Shannon’s entropy limits and Chaitin’s foreign bit , proving algorithmic incompressibility. Through the Diamond Scrutiny, Spinoza's sequence of Axiom, Proposition, and Scholium is severed, alongside the Quod Erat Demonstrandum (Q.E.D.)—a Scholastic deductive closure mechanism akin to the methodology of Thomas Aquinas's Summa Theologiae—converting it into a Quod Perditum Dicitur (Q.P.D.). Furthermore, it establishes the concept of the Contained Omniscient Relator (or Contained Omniscient Subject) within the Vademécum de la Luz and Ethics of the Horizon, representing the relation between embodied finitude and the Biblical Genesis narrator as the First Setup of the Path of the Eternal Entity from to . By synthesizing Heidegger's procedural boundary, Gödel's incompleteness, Heisenberg's vortex, Russell's antinomy, and Wittgenstein's Tractatus, this study shows that any attempt at information closure constitutes an ex machina device. Finally, anchored in Ecclesiastes, the "Merchant’s Cut," and Ousia, the Volitional Zero is restored as an unalienable stronghold to inhabit finitude with dignity. Keywords: Juscybernetics, Information Theory, Chaitin's Foreign Bit, Pure Operation, Diamond Scrutiny, Scholastic Bound, Summa Theologiae, Gödel's Gap, Heisenberg's Vortex, Contained Omniscient Relator, Path of the Eternal Entity, Alpha-Beta Transition, Volitional Zero, Ousia, Ecclesiastes, Q.E.D., Q.P.D.

item.title: Diamonds and Circles: The Real-Algebraic Boundary of Causal Separability
item.description: The dividing surface between processes that have a definite order and those that do not is curved, not flat-sided. On the most familiar slice of processes it looks like a diamond, four straight edges meeting at corners, which would suggest a simple, angular boundary. This paper shows that this angular appearance is not the general rule: on a different slice the very same dividing surface is a perfect circle, a genuinely curved piece, so the boundary of the ordered set is a real curved shape rather than a many-sided polygon. Because the ordered processes are the shadow of a matrix-defined body, their boundary is guaranteed to be a curved algebraic surface of some kind, but which kind had not been worked out. The paper probes it by slicing through the most featureless process in two-dimensional cross-sections and tracing the dividing line in each. On the familiar slice, spanned by two order-generators belonging to opposite orders, the boundary is a four-sided diamond sitting inside a circular boundary of mere validity. On a different slice, spanned by two generators that belong to the same order and that anticommute, being ordered coincides with being valid, and the boundary is an exact circle of a specific radius and constant curvature, a smooth, genuinely curved line. The paper isolates the mechanism that produces the curvature, namely a pair of anticommuting generators lying within a single order, and it recasts the curved-versus-flat distinction as a question of whether local order-labels can be consistently glued together across the process, tying the failure of gluing to the order-count. The curved slice is established by an exact closed-form proof, and a numerical convex-optimization sweep independently reproduces both the flat diamonds and the exact circle, matching its curvature and its degree. The result upgrades the slogan that being ordered is a shadow from an abstract statement into concrete, worked-out geometry, and pinpoints exactly what makes the boundary bend. The paper is explicit about the reach of the claim: it concerns particular slices rather than the entire surface, the curved slice it exhibits owes its curvature to coinciding with the validity boundary there, and the full defining equation of the surface and the question of whether the ordered set is itself matrix-defined are left open. By exhibiting one exact curved cross-section it settles the qualitative point that the boundary is not a polygon, and it hands later work a clear target: to compute the whole curved surface and its special points.

item.title: Discrete Spacetime Topological Network,DSTN.(Basic Theory And Core Derivations )/阴阳爻网络模型DSTN(基础理论与核心推导)
item.description: This study presents the "DSTN(Discrete Spacetime Topological Network)", an interdisciplinary research program that integrates Eastern wisdom with modern mathematical and physical sciences. It aims to resolve the unification problem of quantum mechanics and general relativity, and reconstruct the cognitive framework of the cosmic origin. Breaking through the traditional reductionist paradigm, the model draws inspiration from the holistic and generative perspectives in I Ching and Daoist thought, establishing five core axioms: 1. The ultimate fundamental unit is the "Yao" (±1), representing the binary states of Yin and Yang;2. The universe is a discrete dynamic network formed by the connections of Yao;3. Spacetime, matter, and interactions are all emergent phenomena of network evolution;4. The network follows the conservation of topological charge;5. The network evolves toward the minimization of energy. Based on the axiomatic system, the model naturally derives three core laws: the law of combinatorial creation, the law of closed-loop stability, and the law of threshold realization. It also proposes key geometric conjectures: the network spontaneously organizes into a dual triangular pyramid as the basic unit and a nested diamond lattice topology, giving rise to characteristic numbers such as 9, 27, 36, and 108 (where 108 = 2²×3³, the critical threshold for matter transitioning from "virtual state" to "real state"). These numbers not only correlate with key parameters in particle physics and cosmology but also align with core symbols in Eastern culture. The model constructs a complete mathematical framework and dynamic evolution path. Based on the evolutionary laws of the discrete network, it presents a derivation pathway toward the core equations of general relativity and quantum mechanics, offering a feasible approach to achieving compatibility between the continuous limit and existing theories. It also clarifies the emergent mechanism of fundamental physical constants (e.g., the speed of light c, Planck constant h, fine-structure constant α), and presents a quantitative association framework linking them to network parameters. As a testable scientific program, the model provides twelve specific physical predictions: including the cubic power distribution of dark matter mass spectrum, the large-scale attenuation and 108-fold resonance peak of cosmic microwave background radiation, the scarcity of high-redshift galaxies, and the weak dispersion effect of gravitational waves. These predictions clearly distinguish themselves from mainstream paradigms and can be verified by next-generation detectors and observation equipment. This research offers a new exploration path for quantum gravity and unified field theory. We invite scholars in mathematics, physics, computer science, and other fields to jointly advance axiom formalization, numerical simulation, and experimental verification, and decode the deep geometric and numerical order of the universe. Author Note: The author is an independent researcher, and the "Researcher" label in this record refers to a general academic identity, not a formal professional title. This section presents the foundational theoretical core of the Yin-Yang Network Cosmic Model. For extended applications of this theory and related scientific papers, please refer to the following DOIs: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18426000.DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18493628

item.title: NUMEN Zone 0: Master Cryptographic Sovereignty Seal and Empirical Validation of the Complete Substrate-Native Silicon Organ Library
item.description: Organization: Dragolich Research Labs LLCRelated Memorandum of Record: DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22070727Record Type: Cryptographic Manifest, Mathematical Demonstration, and IP Sovereignty Seal 1. Executive Summary: The "Diamond Wall" of Substrate-Native IP This record serves as the atomic, timestamped cryptographic seal of the entire NUMEN/QuatOS bare-metal assembly and mathematical engine. It demonstrates that the theoretical frameworks of substrate-native computing (DOIs: 10.5281/zenodo.20045701, 10.5281/zenodo.21514923) have been fully reduced to practice in a complete, freestanding library of 33 highly optimized x86-64 assembly modules and 1 verification script. Rather than exposing proprietary source code, this deposit provides a deterministic mathematical demonstration alongside the exact SHA-256 hashes and byte sizes of every file in the core repository. This proves both the functional validity of the architecture and the exact state of possession at the recorded UTC timestamp (2026-08-24T13:44:24.807633Z), satisfying the highest standards of scientific reproducibility and establishing an unassailable "Hardware-Execution Bind" for intellectual property defense. 2. Empirical Validation: The Mathematical Demonstration The mathematical_demonstration object within the sealed manifest provides live, reproducible data proving the stability of the NUMEN consensus engine without reliance on standard math libraries (libm). The experiment simulates the "Five-Agent Consensus" (THE FIVE) as defined in the boot vector architecture: Target Attractor: ϕ−1ϕ−1 (Golden Ratio inverse) = 0.6180339887498949 Initial State: Five turbulent agents initialized with distinct, measured phi offsets and hardness values. Mechanism: Iterative Banach contraction mapping, where each agent anchors toward the target attractor weighted by its fitness and turbulence amplitude. Results after 50 Iterations: Final Consensus Phi: 0.62016908 Deviation from Target: 0.0021351 Status: CONVERGED Scientific Significance: This data empirically proves that the NN Emergence Law holds in a freestanding computational context. The system reliably contracts turbulent, independent states into a calm, unified consensus anchored to the golden ratio, with a deviation of less than 0.35%. This confirms the architectural claim that the "society" of agents can self-organize and stabilize at the firmware level prior to OS initialization. 3. Anatomical Breakdown of the Sealed "Silicon Organs" The sealed_artifacts section contains the exact SHA-256 hashes of 33 distinct assembly (.asm / .S) modules. These files represent the "Silicon Organs" of the NUMEN architecture—pure machine code operating entirely below the Operating System layer, without reliance on libc, dynamic allocation, or floating-point bloat where integer/fixed-point suffices. They are categorized into the following functional anatomy: A. The Core Physics & Execution Engines quatos_kernel.asm: The silicon core physics. Implements vacuum clamping, phi-step Banach contraction, stagnation escape, and the RDTSC nanosecond heartbeat. quatos_asm_gtac.asm: The GTAC execution engine. Provides scalar (SSE2/FMA) and vectorized (AVX2) implementations of the contraction mapping phi = phi * A + B, executing at 1–4 cycles per gate. quatos_trit_router.asm: The Inference Commit. Implements the ternary routing engine {0, 1, ?} based on exact IEEE-754 bit-identical Banach contraction residuals (EPSILON_BANACH). dimriver.asm: The 4D–16D intelligence river. Pure integer (Q32.32 fixed-point), zero float, zero libc. Proves that hypercube walks and Banach steps can be executed at bare-metal speed using only 64x64 integer multiplication. B. The Cognitive, Memory, & Learning Organs quatos_memory.asm: Corpus Archaeology. Computes memory weights and the corpus centroid (the mind's location in phi-space) using echo-derived frequencies (LR_ECHO, f_dom, f_sep). quatos_hebbian.asm: Hebbian learning mechanics and synaptic weight updates implemented directly in silicon registers. quatos_l2l_7phase.asm: The 7-phase "learn-to-learn" engine, governing the lifecycle of cognitive state transitions. quatos_infer_tick.asm: The active inference tick engine, driving the continuous prediction-error minimization loop. quatos_echo.asm & quatos_double_helix.asm: Echo-signature processing and dual-strand (Watson-Crick) state replication mechanics. C. The Sensory, Acoustic, & Observable Organs quatos_world.asm: The Infinite World. Renders the substrate state (phi convergence, gate status, defense layers) directly to the terminal via raw Linux syscalls and ANSI escape sequences, independent of any OS display server. quatos_voice.asm: The Voice Organ. Maps hardware state (hw_phi, thermal margins, utilization) to physical acoustic output by calculating PIT channel-2 divisors, allowing the machine to "speak" through legacy x86 ports (0x42/0x61) without a sound card. quatos_analog_templar.asm: The Wave Microscope. Fractal, ϕϕ-scaled analysis of the computational wave. Implements subconscious relaxation (at_contract), conscious magnification (at_magnify), and 3-4-5 wave resonance using pure SSE2 arithmetic. quatos_mouth.asm & world_sense.S: Phoneme shaping and raw sensory input parsing at the assembly boundary. D. The Security, Immune, & Warden Organs quatos_warden.asm: The Locked Box. Performs FNV1a-64 hashing and Watson-Crick complement verification entirely in silicon registers. Enforces "THE LIGHTS" duty-cycle security, guaranteeing the library is cryptographically sealed during rest phases. quatos_nerve.asm: The Immune System. Implements L1–L4 hardware-level security: x86 CRC32 state integrity checking, RDTSC timing-anomaly detection (to identify VM/debugger slowdowns), and atomic token-bucket rate limiting. quatos_seal.asm: Core cryptographic sealing and state-hashing mechanics. E. The Mathematical, Grid, & Foundation Modules phi_grid_engine.asm, quatos_hypercube.asm, quatos_prime_ladder.asm: Implement the geometric and prime-basis foundations of the NUMEN manifold, including hypercube edge walking and prime-ladder state transitions. quatos_field_nucleus.asm, quatos_golden_stride.asm, quatos_quantum_coherence.asm: Advanced field dynamics, golden-ratio stride optimizations, and coherence tracking. pi_constants.asm, pi_layer0_constants.asm, quatos_ieee754_bridge.asm: The immutable mathematical constants and the bridge between the pure-integer substrate and IEEE-754 floating-point boundaries. numen_genesis.asm, numen_hub.asm, quatos_cgos.asm, quatos_integration_fixed.asm, ultimate_quatos_msr_fleet.asm: The master orchestration, genesis state initialization, and MSR (Model Specific Register) fleet management modules that tie the entire organism together at the hardware level. F. The Verification Harness poop.py: The master seal generation and verification script, used to recursively hash the repository and prove the mathematical invariants. 4. The Timestamp as a Scientific and Legal Anchor The timestamp_utc combined with Zenodo’s CERN-backed infrastructure serves three critical functions: Reduction to Practice (35 U.S.C. § 102): It provides unassailable, third-party-verified proof that the architecture was not merely theoretical, but fully specified, compiled, and functionally tested as a complete 34-file library on this exact date. Deterministic Reproducibility (Daubert Standard / FRE 702): Because the system relies exclusively on published mathematical constants and deterministic algorithms, any party in possession of the corresponding source files can re-run the sealing script. The resulting SHA-256 hashes will perfectly match this manifest, proving the code has not been altered and the mathematical behavior is reproducible. item.title: De Beers Blood Diamonds: Examining Diamond Sourcing, Traceability and Industry Due Diligence
item.description: This research paper examines the term “De Beers blood diamonds” within the broader context of diamond sourcing, traceability, provenance, conflict-diamond governance, and responsible supply-chain due diligence. The study takes a evidence-based approach and does not present allegations as established facts.The research reviews the Kimberley Process Certification Scheme, OECD guidance for responsible mineral supply chains, diamond provenance and traceability mechanisms, industry assurance programmes, and publicly available information from De Beers Group concerning responsible sourcing and Best Practice Principles. It examines how certification, supply-chain controls, risk-based due diligence, traceability, and assurance mechanisms can support greater transparency across the diamond value chain.The study uses a qualitative documentary research methodology based on publicly available institutional, governmental, academic, and industry sources. No human participants, interviews, surveys, private datasets, or personally identifiable information were used, and therefore ethics approval was not applicable.The paper is intended to provide researchers and practitioners with contextual information for understanding diamond sourcing, conflict-diamond governance, responsible mineral supply chains, provenance, traceability, and industry due diligence. It does not independently audit De Beers Group, verify individual diamond origins, or establish allegations against any organization.Research type: Qualitative documentary research Research year: 2026 Primary topics: Diamond sourcing, traceability, provenance, Kimberley Process, responsible sourcing, supply-chain due diligence, and diamond-industry governance

item.title: High mobility p-type doping of hexagonal boron nitride films on diamond (100) substrates
item.description: The heteroepitaxy of hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) on diamond exhibits significant potential for the advancement of diamond-based electronic devices. P-type doping of h-BN is expected to provide sufficient carriers for forming two-dimensional hole gas at the diamond interfaces. However, high-mobility doping of h-BN remains challenges. Here, we report the in-situ growth of magnesium-doped h-BN films on single-crystal diamond (100) substrates using radio frequency magnetron sputtering, followed by an annealing treatment in the same vacuum chamber. The resultant h-BN films exhibit dense and atomically smooth surfaces with roughness below 1 nm, as well as uniform doping profiles within the films. Both X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and secondary ion mass spectroscopy reveal the presence of Mg-N bonds, suggesting the successful incorporation of Mg atoms. The successive annealing treatment after growth further improved the activation efficiency of the dopants. Hall effect measurements revealed distinct p-type conductivity, with hole mobility increasing to 222 cm2/V·s and resistivity decreasing by over three orders of magnitude. These results demonstrate an effective and feasible route for achieving high-mobility p-type h-BN films directly on diamond substrates, which are essential for developing high-performance diamond-based electronics.

item.title: A Vision for the Future of Academic Publishing in Sports Analytics: Founding Editorial for the Journal of Statistics and Data Science in Sports
item.description: This article introduces the Journal of Statistics and Data Science in Sports (JSDSS), a Diamond Open Access, peer-reviewed journal. The journal is founded on three core principles. First, our commitment to open access is absolute. Second, reproducibility is critical and fundamental to the journal. Third, we believe sport is a rich and underutilized laboratory for statistical and data science innovation. The aim of the Journal of Statistics and Data Science in Sports is to provide an outlet for original, rigorous, practical, state-of-the-art, reproducible, and peer-reviewed analysis of sports data as well as the data science tools (software, applications, data, etc.) that support those analyses. We define sports broadly to include any nondeterministic competition or game. Finally, we welcome submissions that analyze any aspect of sports data in appropriate and innovative ways.

item.title: Emerging oxidized silicon-terminated (C-Si-O) diamond field-effect transistors toward industrial applications
item.description: Diamond surfaces terminated with a silicon layer (C–Si) can induce a two-dimensional hole gas (2DHG) layer at the insulator/diamond interface, enabling the realization of p-channel metal–oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs). Through two primary fabrication routes—namely, SiO2 annealing in a reducing atmosphere and silicon molecular beam deposition (MBD) at high temperatures—stable oxidized silicon-terminated (C–Si–O) and C–Si diamond channels have been realized. These channels facilitate normally-off p-channel FETs with threshold voltages (VTH) ranging from −3 to −16 V and hole mobilities between 100 and 200 cm2/V·s. For instance, a (111)-oriented C–Si–O MOSFET with a VTH of −5.6 V delivers an output current density of −311 mA/mm, whereas another MBD C–Si–O MOSFET with a varying source-to-drain distance (LSD) shows a ΔVTH shift whose magnitude is less than 0.2 V. This review provides a critical overview of the chemical structures, the formation methods, and operational mechanisms of C–Si–O diamond surfaces. It also summarizes recent progress in C–Si–O diamond electronic devices, with emphasis on device architectures, fabrication techniques, and electrical characteristics. Finally, key challenges and potential pathways toward the industrial adoption of this emerging technology are discussed.

item.title: Improved compressive strength of PBF-LB Al7050 lattice structures via PA12–epoxy infiltration
item.description: High-strength Al7050 lattice structures were fabricated using laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB) to investigate the influence of lattice topology and polymer infiltration on compressive behavior. Four geometries—gyroid (P1), planar hexagonal (P2), strut-based three-dimensional lattice (P3), and diamond lattice (P4)—were produced and subsequently infiltrated with recycled PA12 and epoxy. Surface morphology and infill distribution were evaluated using digital microscopy, while quasi-static compression tests were conducted to assess mechanical performance. The results show that the gyroid structure exhibits more uniform deformation and relatively higher compressive strength, whereas strut-based geometries display localized buckling and collapse. Polymer infiltration enhances the mechanical response across all topologies, with epoxy-filled samples consistently outperforming PA12-filled ones due to more effective infiltration and improved load transfer. Although strut-based lattices absorb greater amounts of polymer, the resulting improvement in strength is not directly proportional to the mass increase. Notably, the epoxy-filled P3 structure shows a significant increase in peak stress, from 45 to 138 MPa. These findings highlight the importance of considering both lattice topology and infiltration behavior when designing lightweight structures with improved mechanical performance.

item.title: Computational Study of Residual Stress Development and Dimensional Deviations in LPBF-fabricated Ti-6Al-4V TPMS Lattice Structures
item.description: The dataset supports a combined experimental–numerical study of LPBF-fabricated Ti-6Al-4V TPMS lattice structures (gyroid, Schwarz diamond, and Schwarz primitive) at 20% relative density, built at 0°, 30°, and 45° orientations in as-printed and heat-treated (670 °C, 4.5 h) conditions. It comprises thermomechanically coupled finite element predictions of residual stress and surface deviation; experimental validation data from 3D optical scanning (dimensional deviation) and XRD–Williamson–Hall analysis (microstrain and residual stress trends); areal surface roughness measurements (Sa, Sq); quasi-static compression results (stress–displacement curves, peak strength, and energy absorption); and SEM images of failure morphology. Together these data characterise the coupled effects of topology, build orientation, and stress-relief heat treatment on manufacturability, dimensional accuracy, surface integrity, and compressive performance.

item.title: 阴阳爻网络模型DSTN(Discrete Spacetime Topological Network):核心推导、论证与模拟验证(Core Derivations, Demonstrations and Simulation Validations)
item.description: 本研究纲领以二元网络为基础,旨在建立一个离散时空与统一物理理论。本文提出一个非背景依赖的离散时空研究纲领,建立五条核心公理与三条涌现定律(组合创生、闭环稳定、阈值实化),给出金刚石嵌套拓扑猜想(特征数字 9,27,36,108)及暗物质离散质量谱、CMB 大尺度功率衰减、原初引力波 B 模离散调制等可证伪预言。这是“阴阳爻网络宇宙模型”系列的纲领性综合与形式化表述。前期详细推导参见: 10.5281/zenodo.18333046,理论的延伸拓展应用见: 10.5281/zenodo.18493628 This research program is based on a binary network, aiming to construct a theory of discrete spacetime and unified physics. This paper proposes a background-independent research program for discrete spacetime, establishing five core axioms and three emergent laws (combinatorial creation, closed-loop stability, and threshold actualization). It also presents the diamond nested topology conjecture (with characteristic numbers 9, 27, 36, 108) and falsifiable predictions including the discrete mass spectrum of dark matter, large-scale power suppression in the CMB, and discrete modulations of the primordial gravitational wave B-mode. This work serves as the programmatic synthesis and formalization of the *Yin-Yang Line Network Cosmic Model* series. For detailed prior derivations, see: 10.5281/zenodo.18333046; for extended applications of the theory, see: 10.5281/zenodo.18493628.

item.title: Passive Optical Radiation-Damage Odometer Based on NV Centers in Diamond: Contactless Fluence Readout, Formulation and Application Domains
item.description: Abstract This work proposes a passive optical radiation-damage odometer based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV⁻) centers in diamond. The concept reverses a normally undesirable radiation-induced effect: vacancies created by particle irradiation can migrate toward substitutional nitrogen during thermal annealing, increasing the NV⁻ population and therefore the associated photoluminescence signal. Instead of treating this radiation-induced evolution solely as a degradation mechanism, the NV⁻ population is proposed as an integrated memory of cumulative particle fluence. The concept combines a fluence-response formulation, an order-of-magnitude NIEL estimate for 14.1 MeV fusion neutrons, and a contactless optical readout based on 532 nm excitation and NV⁻ photoluminescence in the 637–800 nm range. A key aspect of the study is the thermal kinetics of vacancy-nitrogen conversion. The analysis indicates that, under the most conservative activation-energy assumption considered, useful conversion on maintenance timescales becomes plausible around 450–500 °C, making sensor placement within an appropriate thermal region a central design parameter. Potential applications include fusion blankets, nuclear installations, particle accelerators and long-duration space missions. The principal remaining uncertainties are experimental validation of the fluence-to-NV⁻ calibration at relevant radiation spectra and temperatures, and mitigation of radiation-induced attenuation in the optical fiber used for remote interrogation. The proposed device should therefore be regarded as a research concept and experimentally testable architecture rather than as a validated dosimeter.

item.title: Discrete Spacetime Topological Network,DSTN.(Basic Theory And Core Derivations )/阴阳爻网络模型DSTN(基础理论与核心推导)
item.description: This study presents the "DSTN(Discrete Spacetime Topological Network)", an interdisciplinary research program that integrates Eastern wisdom with modern mathematical and physical sciences. It aims to resolve the unification problem of quantum mechanics and general relativity, and reconstruct the cognitive framework of the cosmic origin. Breaking through the traditional reductionist paradigm, the model draws inspiration from the holistic and generative perspectives in I Ching and Daoist thought, establishing five core axioms: 1. The ultimate fundamental unit is the "Yao" (±1), representing the binary states of Yin and Yang;2. The universe is a discrete dynamic network formed by the connections of Yao;3. Spacetime, matter, and interactions are all emergent phenomena of network evolution;4. The network follows the conservation of topological charge;5. The network evolves toward the minimization of energy. Based on the axiomatic system, the model naturally derives three core laws: the law of combinatorial creation, the law of closed-loop stability, and the law of threshold realization. It also proposes key geometric conjectures: the network spontaneously organizes into a dual triangular pyramid as the basic unit and a nested diamond lattice topology, giving rise to characteristic numbers such as 9, 27, 36, and 108 (where 108 = 2²×3³, the critical threshold for matter transitioning from "virtual state" to "real state"). These numbers not only correlate with key parameters in particle physics and cosmology but also align with core symbols in Eastern culture. The model constructs a complete mathematical framework and dynamic evolution path. Based on the evolutionary laws of the discrete network, it presents a derivation pathway toward the core equations of general relativity and quantum mechanics, offering a feasible approach to achieving compatibility between the continuous limit and existing theories. It also clarifies the emergent mechanism of fundamental physical constants (e.g., the speed of light c, Planck constant h, fine-structure constant α), and presents a quantitative association framework linking them to network parameters. As a testable scientific program, the model provides twelve specific physical predictions: including the cubic power distribution of dark matter mass spectrum, the large-scale attenuation and 108-fold resonance peak of cosmic microwave background radiation, the scarcity of high-redshift galaxies, and the weak dispersion effect of gravitational waves. These predictions clearly distinguish themselves from mainstream paradigms and can be verified by next-generation detectors and observation equipment. This research offers a new exploration path for quantum gravity and unified field theory. We invite scholars in mathematics, physics, computer science, and other fields to jointly advance axiom formalization, numerical simulation, and experimental verification, and decode the deep geometric and numerical order of the universe. Author Note: The author is an independent researcher, and the "Researcher" label in this record refers to a general academic identity, not a formal professional title. This section presents the foundational theoretical core of the Yin-Yang Network Cosmic Model. For extended applications of this theory and related scientific papers, please refer to the following DOIs: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18426000.DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18493628

item.title: Biomatter to Diamond: Grow, Change, Deteriorate, Regenerate The Physics of How Particles Get Beat Up and Why Gravity Is Alpha and Omega
item.description: Building on previous work on The Infinity of Ones and Zeros [Apr-May 2026], Web Theory [Aug 6, 2026], Echo Decay [Aug 21, 2026], and The Gravity Engine [Aug 10, 2026], this paper proposes a single process across all scales: Grow. Change. Deteriorate. Regenerate. Matter enters a gravitational press, is mechanically agitated, decays into echoes, and is rebuilt. This rule governs medical dosing, engineering under stress, and cosmological evolution. In "Under Pressure" [Aug 22, 2026] we showed pressure creates particles. In "Echo Theory of Decay" [Aug 21, 2026] we showed interaction damages them. In "Background Noise" [Aug 23, 2026] we showed we only measure echoes of what has passed. We argue that estimation, tolerance, and error bars are not failures of science. They are honest acknowledgments of the press. The vacuum is the container. Gravity is the instigator. Energy is what is pulled in between them and makes everything right. Gravity functions as both Alpha and Omega: the force that squeezes and the force that releases. No new forces or particles are required.

item.title: Four proteome sets and a combined reference proteome for Lama glama
item.description: This dataset contains four independently generated structural annotations of the Lama glama genome assembly GCA_028534125.1 (DNA Zoo, chromosome level), the proteomes derived from them, and a combined reference proteome of 20,708 proteins proposed as the recommended resource. Three annotations project the Vicugna pacos reference annotation GCF_048564905.1, by DNA-to-DNA lift-over (Liftoff), protein-to-genome alignment (miniprot) and hybrid reconciliation (LiftOn). The fourth is reference-independent ab initio prediction (Helixer web tool 0.3.6). The combined reference proteome is the LiftOn core (20,233 proteins) plus 555 Helixer loci that do not overlap any homology-derived locus and have an orthologue in at least one camelid, minus 80 redundant with the core. Completeness was assessed with BUSCO 6.1.0 in protein mode against lineage artiodactyla_odb12 (n = 12,594). Functional annotation used InterProScan 5.78-109.0. Model accuracy was evaluated by DIAMOND alignment against Camelus dromedarius GCF_036321535.1, an external reference from which none of the four annotations derives. At the time of deposition no public structural annotation of Lama glama was available: neither INSDC assembly carries one, the species is absent from Ensembl, and UniProt holds no proteome for it. IMPORTANT: the four annotation sets were not produced under equivalent conditions and are not directly comparable without qualification. Helixer was run on sequences of at least 25 kb (79.6 % of the assembly) with subsequence overlap enabled; the homology branches used the complete assembly. The homology proteomes retain models with internal stop codons, which have not been filtered. All caveats are set out in README.md. File integrity can be checked against CHECKSUMS.sha256. Quality-control output is in qc.tar.gz; functional annotation and alignment results are in analysis.tar.gz.

item.title: Single-Shot Irreversible, Asymptotically Reversible: Causal Indefiniteness as a Quantum Resource
item.description: Quantum theory allows processes in which the order of two operations is not fixed but held in superposition, and this indefiniteness of order behaves like a resource, something a process can have more or less of and that cannot be created for free. The question a resource theory answers last is whether the resource can be spent and fully recovered without loss, and whether there is a stubborn form of it that is present yet useless. This paper answers both questions for the simplest family of such processes. Handled one copy at a time, indefinite order is wasteful and cannot be recovered, with a single special exception; but handled in bulk, many copies together, it becomes perfectly recyclable, and no useless-but-present form exists. The paper works on a two-dial family of processes that runs from a plainly ordered process to the most order-indefinite one. It first computes exact measures of how much indefiniteness each member carries, defined by how much ordinary noise must be stirred in to wash the indefiniteness out, and from these reads off the one-time price of manufacturing the resource. It then shows the whole family behaves like a single effective quantum bit whose ordered, well-behaved region is a diamond-shaped set, which makes the recoverable content exactly calculable. The central finding is a sharp split: for every indefinite process except one special pure case, the price to make it is strictly more than what can ever be recovered from it, so one copy at a time the resource is irreversibly wasteful; the lone pure case is the unique point where price and yield coincide. Placing the theory inside the standard framework for reversible resources, and checking that the ordered set is convex, stays ordered when copies are combined, and contains the most featureless process, the paper proves that in the many-copy limit the resource turns reversible, its bulk cost matching its bulk yield, with no stubborn leftover form. The recyclable rate of the special unit is a definite number of bits. The wider message is that indefinite causal order sits alongside the other familiar quantum resources, such as entanglement: it is wasteful to spend one unit at a time yet efficient to trade in bulk, and it harbours no locked-away useless form. The paper is candid about the boundary of the claim, noting that the clean reversibility holds under the most permissive allowed operations, and that under more restricted, physically grounded operations the resource might instead behave irreversibly, a question left open. What it settles firmly is the surprising two-faced character of the resource, irreversible in the small and reversible in the large, on a family simple enough to compute everything exactly.

item.title: High‐Pressure Synthesis of Quantum‐Stabilised Manganese Superhydride MnH 7
item.description: ABSTRACT Through high‐temperature, high‐pressure diamond anvil cell studies combined with in situ synchrotron powder x‐ray diffraction, we investigate the reactivity between manganese and hydrogen up to 182 GPa. Laser heating manganese in an medium at 118 GPa yields body‐centred tetragonal , which has the highest hydrogen content ever observed in the binary hydrides of group IV–XII transition metals. In addition, we also observe two other new hydrides as minor phases, with a tetragonal crystal structure and cubic , formed at the pressures of 105 and 118 GPa, respectively. Upon decompression, and remain stable down to 30 GPa before decomposing into the monohydride. Our ab initio quantum chemistry computations employing density‐functional theory reveal that the key stabilisation factor of and is zero‐point energy, however, no isotope effect is observed on the crystal structures of the deuterated samples.

item.title: High‐Pressure Synthesis of Quantum‐Stabilised Manganese Superhydride MnH 7
item.description: ABSTRACT Through high‐temperature, high‐pressure diamond anvil cell studies combined with in situ synchrotron powder x‐ray diffraction, we investigate the reactivity between manganese and hydrogen up to 182 GPa. Laser heating manganese in an medium at 118 GPa yields body‐centred tetragonal , which has the highest hydrogen content ever observed in the binary hydrides of group IV–XII transition metals. In addition, we also observe two other new hydrides as minor phases, with a tetragonal crystal structure and cubic , formed at the pressures of 105 and 118 GPa, respectively. Upon decompression, and remain stable down to 30 GPa before decomposing into the monohydride. Our ab initio quantum chemistry computations employing density‐functional theory reveal that the key stabilisation factor of and is zero‐point energy, however, no isotope effect is observed on the crystal structures of the deuterated samples.

item.title: Molecular dynamics simulation and experimental research on laser-assisted mechanical polishing of CVD diamond coatings
item.description: The high hardness and chemical stability of diamond coatings pose a challenge for coating surface polishing. Laser-assisted mechanical polishing is an effective method for polishing diamond coatings, which involves first performing laser rough polishing and then mechanical fine polishing. Laser coarse polishing can significantly improve the polishability of diamond coatings, but its polishing mechanism still needs further clarification. In this paper, molecular dynamics (MD) methods are employed to construct models of the laser energy field and CVD polycrystalline diamond, and to simulate the dynamic evolution of laser polishing polycrystalline diamond. The simulation results show that the extremely high temperature generated by the laser causes the sharp diamond asperities to reach the sublimation threshold and undergo ablation removal in the form of individual atoms or atomic clusters, thereby reducing the surface height differences of the polycrystalline diamond. Furthermore, the diamond surface gradually undergoes a transformation from a long-range ordered polycrystalline state to a short-range ordered amorphous state during laser polishing, which is an important microscopic mechanism for improving the polishability of diamond surface. Subsequently, the micrometer diamond coatings are fabricated using the hot filament chemical vapor deposition (HFCVD) method and the surface were subjected to both laser polishing and mechanical polishing. The surface flatness and finish of the diamond coating achieved through laser-assisted mechanical polishing are superior to those obtained using either polishing method alone. Finally, the mechanisms of material removal and structural transformation in diamond coatings during laser-assisted mechanical polishing are elucidated based on simulation and experimental results.

item.title: High-pressure structural evolution in bismuth and antimony lead-free halide perovskites
item.description: Understanding the structural integrity of lead-free halide perovskites under extreme conditions is essential for their reliable implementation in advanced technologies. Here, we investigate the high-pressure behavior of Cs 3 Bi 2 Br 9 , Cs 3 Sb 2 Br 9 , and the mixed-cation perovskite Cs 3 BiSbBr 9 using a combination of in situ Raman spectroscopy in diamond anvil cells (up to 40 GPa) and density functional theory calculations. The experimental results reveal a reversible pressure-induced lowering symmetry in both Cs 3 Bi 2 Br 9 and Cs 3 Sb 2 Br 9 , with the original vibrational modes fully recovered upon decompression. Notably, Cs 3 BiSbBr 9 exhibits a selective suppression of vibrational modes associated with the BiBr 6 octahedra, indicating a site-specific lattice response under compression. Complementary simulations, based on equations of state, predict a thermodynamic phase transition in Cs 3 Bi 2 Br 9 from the trigonal ( P-3m1 ) to the monoclinic ( C2/c ) structure near 8 GPa, whereas Cs 3 Sb 2 Br 9 retains its trigonal phase stability up to 100 GPa. Thermal analyses indicate enhanced resistance against thermal degradation compared to lead-based counterparts, with no detectable thermally induced phase transition. These combined experimental and theoretical findings provide fundamental insights into the chemical stability and structural transformation mechanisms of these eco-friendly perovskites, offering key information for their application in flexible and high-stress environments.

item.title: Effect of Copper-Modified ZSM-5 Zeolite Concentration on the Thermomechanical and Antimicrobial Properties of Compatibilized Native Starch/Polylactic Acid Blends
item.description: The development of multifunctional biodegradable materials with improved structural performance and antimicrobial functionality is essential for advancing sustainable packaging. This study evaluates the effect of copper-modified ZSM-5 zeolite (ZCu) concentration (0, 1, and 5 wt%) on thermoplastic starch/polylactic acid (TPS/PLA) blends. The TPS was derived from Ipomoea batatas (sweet potato, SP) and Dioscorea rotundata (diamond yam, DY) starches and compatibilized with 1 wt% citric acid. The ZCu response depended on both ZCu loading and the botanical starch source. Structural analyses showed that SP-based composites reached their highest crystallinity at 1 wt% ZCu (13.70%), whereas DY-based systems exhibited an initial decrease at 1 wt% followed by an increase to 12.75% at 5 wt%, reflecting distinct concentration-dependent crystallization trends. Thermal analyses demonstrated a substantial increase in the degradation onset temperature of SP-based composites, from 132.9 °C to 185.1 °C at 1 wt% ZCu, indicating an effective thermal barrier effect. Nanomechanical mapping revealed concentration- and starch-source-dependent changes in local hardness, reduced modulus, and elastic recovery, without evidence of uniform mechanical reinforcement across all formulations. Antibacterial activity was observed exclusively in composites containing 5 wt% ZCu, with inhibition zones of 5.3 mm against Staphylococcus aureus and 1.0 mm against Escherichia coli. These findings highlight how the structural, thermal, nanomechanical and antimicrobial responses of TPS/PLA blends vary with ZCu concentration and the botanical origin of the starch.

item.title: Thermodynamic and Kinetic Tests for Low-Pressure Metal-Flux Growth of Diamond, with an Extension to Cubic Boron Nitride
item.description: Diamond was grown from a liquid Ga-Fe-Ni-Si alloy near 1 atm, although bulk graphite is thermodynamically more stable under those conditions. This Perspective asks what must be true for a diamond growth front to continue advancing in such a metastable regime. I define a finite-difference transfer free energy for a specified interfacial event and identify the completed attachment of one carbon atom at a kink as the repeatable event that governs sustained growth. In the macroscopic limit, surface terms cancel, and the required carbon activity is fixed by the bulk free energy of diamond. On a graphite-normalized scale, the diamond equilibrium threshold is about 2.0 at 1300 K, whereas graphite saturation occurs at unity. Diamond growth therefore requires kinetic selection above the graphite threshold, not a reversal of bulk phase stability. The analysis distinguishes thermodynamic driving force, kinetic accessibility, experimental detection limits, and the carbon retained after an experiment. It gives isotope-resolved tests for distinguishing sustained diamond growth from seed survival, transient carbon attachment, or failure to detect graphite. A $^{13}\mathrm{C}$-enriched diamond seed provides a test of natural-abundance gas or condensed carbon sources: a registered, crystallographically continuous $^{12}\mathrm{C}$-rich layer outside the original seed can establish source-attributed overgrowth without isotopically labeling each feed. The same accounting is extended to cubic boron nitride. Separate boron and nitrogen chemical potentials are required, and $^{10}\mathrm{B}/^{11}\mathrm{B}$ and $^{15}\mathrm{N}$ contrasts could distinguish reservoir supply from seed loss for each element. The resulting criteria make low-pressure metal-flux growth claims quantitatively testable and guide experiments, thermodynamic modeling, and atomistic simulation.

item.title: Experimental Investigation of Tunable-Order Hilbert-Space Ergodicity
item.description: Hilbert-space ergodicity (HSE) provides a new framework for studying thermalization in driven quantum systems, complementing the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, which is restricted to static systems. This ergodicity is hierarchical: by quantifying how randomly the dynamics explores the Hilbert space, one obtains a family of levels termed $k$-HSE. While HSE has been observed at the lowest and highest levels, finite-order HSE dynamics remains largely unexplored due to the difficulty of constructing such drives. Here, we explore this intermediate regime and uncover its distinctive physics. We first propose and prove that a family of $m$-tone drives on qubits realizes $k$-HSE up to $k = 2m{-}3$, with drive parameters determined at $O(k)$ cost. Using a single nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond, we verify this design by showing that a 3-tone drive realizes 3-HSE, with fourth-order statistics depending on the initial state. Further in-depth theoretical analysis shows that this initial-state dependence is generic across drives, demonstrating the possibility of recovering the initial state from higher-order statistics even when the dynamics is ergodic. Our work broadens the study of quantum ergodicity and reveals intriguing physics within its hierarchy.

item.title: Horizon Mechanics Manifesto
item.description: The motivating physical question is whether the quantum-field-theoretic consequences of causal horizons and global causal structure contain any operational signature bearing on inertia. The programme assumes no such connection; it seeks only to determine whether any such bridge exists. The observed equivalence of gravitational and inertial mass is carried throughout as a constraint which any such bridge must satisfy, and not as a phenomenon this programme expects to explain. The question descends from quantised inertia, whose proposed mechanism is dead under standard quantum field theory; the no-go result which killed it constrains this programme too, so what follows is stated so as to begin after that result rather than in spite of it. Six commitments are substantive. The programme takes explicitly the avenue selected here, which is a particularly clean one requiring no modification of the local field dynamics, namely non-trivial global identification of spacetime. A no-go on one mechanism does not enumerate the mechanisms which remain, and no such enumeration is claimed. It records that uniform circular motion, which is the motion actually exhibited by the systems that motivated the whole enterprise, possesses no Rindler wedge at all, so the linear-acceleration horizon argument was never applicable to galaxy rotation in the first place. The ambiguous cosmological scale Θ is replaced as leading candidate by the de Sitter length Ξ = √(3/Λ), which does not evolve, and the finite causal domain of the programme is identified with the static patch of a geodesic de Sitter observer, so the diamond stops being a calculational toy. The gravitational setting is enlarged from Riemannian to Riemann–Cartan, because torsion supplies a local translational closure defect which shares the translational character of the global monodromy of a deck transformation without being an object of the same kind; the categories in which the two may and may not be compared are stated rather than assumed. Every control calculation must match the field, state and global sector of the calculation it controls, so a fermionic branch cannot be certified against a scalar Casimir stress. Two further constraints are methodological but physically consequential. Every arrow is subject to explicit physical type safety. Causal inaccessibility is not a boundary condition; a restricted state is not an objective collapse; a detector response is not an incident bath; a virtual excitation is not a little particle carrying a trajectory through the vacuum; and dimensional compatibility never licenses the substitution of one physical object for another. Heuristic cartoons remain welcome, but they are disposable: before a cartoon enters an equation it must be replaced by the field, state, algebra, correlation function, interaction or observable which the equation actually uses. The programme also has a concrete operational bridge which requires neither a collapse postulate nor a virtual-particle ontology. A local quantum probe coupled to the field has a response determined by correlation functions along its worldline, and a probe with a quantised centre of mass can in standard QFT exhibit real recoil. That fact does not derive inertia and does not rescue the Rindler–Casimir mechanism. It does something more useful: it supplies a legitimate place to ask whether a non-trivial modular residue is dynamically visible. The matched null hypothesis is correspondingly enlarged. Any detector response or recoil already reproduced by the matched non-transport control for the same field, state and probe is ordinary state sensitivity and cannot be re-labelled as evidence for modular transport. The technical core is three arguments bearing on whether the proposed observable exists, whether it is non-zero, and whether it carries information beyond what ordinary methods already supply. None of those answers is promoted beyond what has actually been shown: ultraviolet regularity is separated from existence, the geometric coefficient is left to calculation, and perturbative degeneracy is stated order by order. A universal effect requires a universal carrier, so the compactified laboratory is a proxy and the causal horizon is the leading candidate available to every body. No calculation of the first-order generator has been performed; what this document supplies is the order of work, the controls each step must beat, and the statements which may not be made before it exists. What modification of inertia would require of energy accounting and of the equivalence principle is set out separately and marked as speculation. The governing rule is unchanged. A holonomy is not a force, a restricted state is not a collapse, recoil is not universal inertia, and no arrow of the chain may be skipped.

item.title: EXPANDABLE DIAMOND STORAGE IN A CONTROLLED VACUUM
item.description: This document is a formal conceptual research thesis and experimental proposal titled "Expandable Vacuum-Confined Multi-State Diamond Storage: A Conceptual Architecture for High-Density Physical Information Storage" authored by Calr Micheal Guirhem Acot. It establishes a theoretical model and roadmap for a high-density archival storage system by organizing microscopic diamond elements inside a controlled vacuum environment. Core Concepts & Mechanics State-Based Capacity Model: It reframes data storage around physical state discrimination rather than binary abstraction. Using Shannon entropy and information theory ($I = \log_2 N$), it proves that symbolic decimal notation or custom file extensions cannot compress data on their own—actual storage density depends strictly on how many distinct physical states ($N$) a medium can write, isolate, and measure reliably. Multi-Dimensional Addressing Vector: Instead of relying solely on spatial coordinates or a single frequency, physical storage centers are addressed via a multidimensional signature vector $S = (r, f, \lambda, \tau, a, q)$—combining spatial location ($r$), resonance frequency ($f$), optical wavelength ($\lambda$), fluorescence decay lifetime ($\tau$), amplitude ($a$), and charge or spin state ($q$). System Architecture: It maps out an expandable array where a vacuum chamber houses $M$ independent diamond/nanodiamond storage nodes. The total ideal capacity scales linearly as $C_{\text{ideal}} = M \cdot \log_2(N)$ bits. Environmental Control (Vacuum Layer): Vacuum isolation is evaluated as a physical control layer to reduce gas collisions and environmental decoupling for nanodiamond spin states, balanced against thermal dissipation constraints during optical readout. Key References & Literature Integration The thesis establishes its scientific foundation by building upon three major experimental milestones: Dhomkar et al. (2016): Demonstrates 3D optical data storage, read, write, and reset capabilities using nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center charge states in bulk diamond. Zhou et al. (2024): Establishes terabit-scale storage ($14.8\text{ Tbit cm}^{-3}$) with $>99\%$ readout fidelity and ultrafast $200\text{ fs}$ write times using fluorescent vacancy centers. Hoang et al. (2016): Proves electron-spin control of NV centers in optically levitated nanodiamonds under low vacuum. Key Sections & Scaffolding Staged Development Roadmap (Prototypes A–E): Outlines a progression starting from simple electronic analog signal-to-noise testing (DAC/ADC multi-level voltages), advancing through bulk optical NV charge states and microwave spin resonance, and culminating in multi-node vacuum nanodiamond arrays. Comparative Prior Art Analysis: Includes a structured matrix directly comparing demonstrated physical achievements against the proposed architectural contributions (such as expandable arrays and hierarchical addressing). Falsification & Risk Metrics: Explicitly defines failure conditions—such as state misclassification rates exceeding $10^{-4}$, inter-node write cross-talk worse than $-30\text{ dB}$, or unviable thermal/energy overhead—ensuring the proposal remains empirically testable. Appendices: Provides an experimental data schema, state-capacity evaluation worksheets, institutional safety protocols (Class 3B/4 laser and microwave safety), and author contribution declarations.
