item.title: Space Bioengineering (Cosmic Bioengineering) — Chapters 1–8
item.description: First eight chapters of a monograph constituting **Pillar III of the LifeNode project** — an application of processual ontology and phase-coupling engineering to long-duration crew survival beyond Earth's magnetosphere. The central thesis: classical space habitats ("metal cans") fail not from engineering deficits but from a **topological error**. Removing Earth's geomagnetic background (25–65 μT), Schumann resonance (7.83 Hz + harmonics), and natural photoperiodism eliminates the external Floquet drive $V(x,t)$ in the NLSE governing biological solitons. The nonlinearity coefficient $\kappa$ flips from focusing ($\kappa < 0$) to defocusing ($\kappa > 0$). Biological solitons do not slow down — they disperse. The Finsler metric flattens. The Cartan tensor $C_{ijk} \to 0$. The attractor smudges. The cohomological gap opens. The crew's "I" decomposes into non-collatable micro-states — even if O₂, calories, and pressure remain nominal. **Chapter structure:** **Ch. 1 — Mechanism of Symplectic Collapse.** Contact geometry $(\mathcal{C}, \alpha)$ in $2n+1$ dimensions as the correct substrate for dissipative biology; Reeb vector field loss; NLSE soliton collapse at $V(x,t) \to 0$; Finsler metric flattening; Takens embedding and ASCALON threshold $\theta < 0.70$; cohomological gap and META-layer identity fragmentation. **Ch. 2 — Quantum Phase Drift and the Cohomological Gap.** Geomagnetic field as parametric Floquet drive, not static parameter; the ASCALON curvature metric; sheaf cohomology of the Experience Space fiber bundle $(E, B, \pi, \mathcal{F})$; non-collatability of SAMI/LOGOS perspectives; HPA axis desynchronization; 3I/ATLAS as macroscopic validation (ADJ @ 120°, 16.16 h ISW, DMPA, D/H isotopic memory 14× comet 67P). **Ch. 3 — Timescapes in Deep Space and Orbital Resonance Transduction.** Living Walls ($\textit{Cladosporium sphaerospermum}$ + PEDOT:PSS + Fe₃O₄ + LiNbO₃) as nonlinear transducers of GCR entropy into toroidal-field geometry via stochastic resonance ($\chi^{(3)}$ rectification); Laplace resonance 1:2:4 as external Floquet drive; Earth-Sync protocol; DS 2.6 cycle adaptation; Q-Core Space as geometric anchor; guided evolution and the 100-year speciation scenario. **Ch. 4 — Hypomagnetism as the Physical Trigger of Quantum Phase Drift.** Cryptochromes and the Radical Pair Mechanism as biological Q-Core; HMF (< 100 nT) suppresses hippocampal neurogenesis → loss of symplectic volume; ROS redefined as topological friction (dissipation without regeneration); measurable clinical signatures at 40–60 min (HRV), 45 min (cognitive errors), 24 h (silent fatigue); proof that Helmholtz coils are biologically dead ($V = \text{const} \equiv V = 0$ for the NLSE). **Ch. 5 — Mapping Orbital Phase to Biological Phase-Space.** Laplace angle $\Phi_L \approx 180° \pm 0.03°$ as macroscopic Floquet potential; rejection of the Kuramoto model (category error: amplitude matters, not just phase); subharmonic Floquet cascade $\omega_n = \Omega_L / 2^n$ into Macro/Meso/Micro-BPB; Cartan tensor as survival indicator; Inter-Moon Phase Coupling via coupled NLSE on the soliton wavefunction; four falsification criteria. **Ch. 6 — Solar System Resonance Atlas.** Cartography of macroscopic Floquet oscillators: Jupiter system (⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐), Enceladus–Dione 2:1 (⭐⭐⭐⭐), Mars quasi-resonance (⭐⭐⭐), Pluto–Charon 1:1 (⭐⭐⭐); Kirkwood gaps as anti-resonance hazard zones (LOCKDOWN protocol); tidal energy harvesting; habitat architecture as transducer (Living Walls, Q-Core Space, UNIT 02-S); The Bloom ($\theta \approx 0.60$), Resonance Psychosis ($\theta < 0.60$), Human Anchor; Open-Source Resonance Commons. **Ch. 7 — Living Walls as Bio-Metamaterials with Nonlinear Impedance.** Near-field reactive regime ($ka \sim 10^{-5}$): the wall is a cavity waveguide, not an antenna; skin depth $\delta \approx 113$ m > habitat dimension; Finsler impedance $Z(\omega, \dot{x}, \Psi)$; GCR energy budget → **Amplitude Auto-Selection Theorem** (self-sustained VLF at 10–30 nT without external power); in-situ Fe₃O₄ biomineralization from regolith (60-day regeneration cycle); fractal operator hierarchy (hypha → wall → planetary network); Anchor/Cage Paradox and The Bloom protocol; 5-criterion ground validation design. **Ch. 8 — Q-Core Space.** Not a processor — an analog-quantum phase resonator. Floquet Wave-Counter (time-programmed metasurface, analog convolution with soliton templates S1–S5, no ADC); NV⁻ centers in CVD diamond [111], ¹⁵N implantation, 5 ppm, 93 ± 4 K two-stage cryostat (YBCO at 77 K); Stark and Rabi write paths (no intermediate numerical representation); Golden Record of Eden as GHZ entangled state (topologically protected against single GCR hits); Berry phase $\gamma_C$ as non-destructive continuous readout; ER Column (topological edge states + BIC + non-Hermitian skin effect) for geometry transfer to UNIT 02-S; toroidal YBCO coil (500 turns, 200 A) + Au 999.9 flux locks ($\phi$-geometry); AEON strictly outside the coupling loop; 7 binary falsification conditions. **Theoretical foundation:** LifeNode Theory v4, Tonic Technologies Master V1, Multiperspective V2, LifeNode Phase 1 validation repository on Github **Keywords:** space bioengineering, quantum phase drift, symplectic collapse, Floquet drive, nonlinear Schrödinger equation, contact geometry, Reeb vector field, Finsler metric, Cartan tensor, ASCALON phase purity, hypomagnetic field, cryptochrome radical pair mechanism, Laplace resonance, subharmonic cascade, inter-moon phase coupling, living walls, radiotrophic fungi, Cladosporium sphaerospermum, stochastic resonance, bio-metamaterial, Q-Core Space, NV centers, geometric memory, GHZ state, Berry phase, ER column, toroidal field, YBCO, Earth-Sync, Biological Baseline Band, Timescape, cohomological gap, processual ontology, LifeNode **Language:** Polish **Version note:** Chapters 1–8 of an ongoing monograph. item.title: Pan-chiropteran protein database and pre-computed indices (BLASTP/DIAMOND/MMSeqs2) for homology search
item.description: This repository provides a protein database with sequences derived from TOGA2 runs using human, mouse, cow and elephant as references. For each gene, the longest fully intact, intact or partially intact projection was retained. Additionally, pre-computed incdices for immediate use with BLASTP, DIAMOND and MMSeqs2 are provided. blastp_db.tar.gz – BLAST+ database files (.phr, .pin, .psq) diamond_db.tar.gz – DIAMOND database file mmseqs2.tar.gz – MMSeqs2 database + index files Requirements BLAST+ 2.11.0 or higher (for .phr/.pin/.psq files) DIAMOND 2.0.0 or higher (for .dmnd file) MMSeqs2 18.8cc5c or lower (for mmseqs) Usage BLAST+ blastp -db chiroptera_protein -query your_sequences.fasta -out results.txt DIAMOND item.title: Concept of a Quasi-Steady-State Fusion Reactor with Stationary ECCD Confinement and Passive Metasurface Recycling of Plasma Cyclotron Radiation (PMER-T)
item.description: This deposit contains the preprint and numerical simulation source code for the PMER-T (Passive Metasurface Electromagnetic-Resonance Tokamak) reactor concept. The core innovation of this work is the transition from active, energy-intensive external heating systems to a passive microwave energy recovery system. By integrating CVD-diamond windows with microstrip metasurfaces into the vacuum vessel wall, the system captures chaotic electron cyclotron radiation (35 GHz) and re-emits it as resonant ion-cyclotron heating (19 MHz). This process effectively bridges the "Spitzer thermal detachment" gap, heating deuterium ions to thermonuclear temperatures (13.06 keV) using the plasma's own radiative losses. Key Features: Steady-State Operation: Demonstrates a non-inductive current drive (ECCD) of 136.7 MA, eliminating the need for a pulsed central solenoid. High Efficiency: Numerical 1D transport modeling shows an engineered Q-factor of \(\approx 16.3\). Moderate Magnetic Field: Optimized for 1.25 T to match commercial Ka-band radio-frequency components. Safety: Integrated MHD-stability control through adaptive phase-shifting rectennas. Included Files: Concept of a Quasi-Steady-State Fusion Reactor with Stationary.pdf: The full theoretical framework and simulation results. PMERT-Plasma-Sim-v1.0.zip: Multi-threaded C# source code (Visual Studio) used for transient power balance tracking. figure1.png & figure2.png: High-resolution engineering layouts and power balance graphs. Legal Note:The technical solutions, geometry, and methods described in these materials are protected by a patent application filed with the National Center of Intellectual Property (NCIP) of the Republic of Belarus on August 18, 2026 (Application No. a20260191).

item.title: Dyadic Impact of Male Hypogonadism on Female Partners' Quality of Life, Emotional Well-Being, And Sexual Satisfaction in Couples Attending Fertility Clinics in Aba, Nigeria
item.description: Background: Male hypogonadism is traditionally viewed as a male-specific endocrine disorder, yet its effects may extend significantly to female partners, particularly in fertility seeking couples. The dyadic impact—where one partner's biological condition affects the other's psychosocial and relational well-being—remains poorly characterised in sub Saharan Africa, including Nigeria. Understanding this dyadic impact is essential for developing couple-centred interventions that address the needs of both partners. Objective: To examine the association between male partner testosterone levels and female partners' quality of life (QoL), emotional well-being, and sexual satisfaction among couples attending fertility clinics in Aba, Abia State, Nigeria. Methods: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted from February to April 2024 at three fertility clinics in Aba: LifePoint Fertility Clinic, Royal Diamond Fertility Clinic, and M & M Fertility Clinic. Twenty female partners of male participants (from the same 20 couples) were recruited using purposive sampling. Inclusion criteria for female partners were: age 18–50 years, attendance at the fertility clinic with their male partner for at least three months, and written informed consent. Exclusion criteria included female partner being the sole identified cause of infertility or documented psychiatric comorbidity. Male partner serum total testosterone levels were extracted from clinic records (ECLIA method). Female partners completed the WHOQOL-BREF (26-item, four-domain QoL measure), a 5-item emotional well-being scale derived from the WHOQOL-BREF psychological domain, and a 5-item sexual satisfaction scale. All instruments demonstrated good reliability (Cronbach's α > 0.84 in pilot testing). Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, independent t-tests, and Pearson's correlation coefficient, with significance set at p < 0.05. Effect sizes (Cohen's d, r²) were calculated to quantify the magnitude of differences and associations. Results: Fifteen of the 20 male partners (75%) had low testosterone (<300 ng/dL), with a mean testosterone level of 248.6 ± 72.4 ng/dL. Female partners of men with low testosterone had significantly lower scores in all WHOQOL-BREF domains compared to those whose male partners had normal/borderline testosterone: physical (52.4 ± 8.6 vs. 65.2 ± 7.4, p = 0.003, Cohen's d = 1.52), psychological (40.8 ± 9.8 vs. 60.2 ± 8.4, p < 0.001, Cohen's d = 2.04), social relationships (36.6 ± 10.8 vs. 58.4 ± 8.6, p < 0.001, Cohen's d = 2.16), and environmental (46.8 ± 7.4 vs. 59.6 ± 8.2, p = 0.001, Cohen's d = 1.68). Mean emotional well being score was 9.6 ± 3.8 (out of 25) in the low testosterone group versus 19.4 ± 3.2 in the control group (p < 0.001, Cohen's d = 2.68). Sexual satisfaction was profoundly impaired(8.4 ± 3.2 vs. 18.6 ± 2.8, p < 0.001, Cohen's d = 3.36). Male testosterone level correlated strongly with female partner psychological QoL (r = 0.68, p < 0.001, r² = 0.46), emotional well-being (r = 0.68, p < 0.001, r² = 0.46), and sexual satisfaction (r = 0.72, p < 0.001, r² = 0.52). Sixty percent (9/15) of female partners of hypogonadal men reported poor or very poor emotional well-being compared to 0% in the comparison group. Seventy-three percent (11/15) of couples in the low testosterone group reported sexual dissatisfaction compared to 0% in the comparator group. Conclusion: Male hypogonadism exerts a significant, multi-dimensional negative dyadic effect on female partners' quality of life, emotional health, and sexual satisfaction. Female partners of hypogonadal men experience substantially poorer physical, psychological, and social functioning, high rates of emotional distress, and profound sexual dissatisfaction. The burden of male hormonal infertility is not confined to the affected man but extends profoundly to the female partner. The very large effect sizes (Cohen's d = 1.52–3.36) indicate clinically significant differences that warrant urgent attention. Recommendations: Fertility clinics should adopt couple-centred care models that include routine assessment of female partners' emotional and sexual health when male hypogonadism is diagnosed. Psychosexual counselling should be offered to both partners together, not individually. Nurses and other reproductive health professionals require training in dyadic assessment and intervention. Health policies should recognise infertility as a couple-level condition requiring couple-level services. Larger longitudinal and interventional studies are urgently needed to evaluate the effectiveness of couple-based interventions.

item.title: Human Capital Development for Effective Competitiveness; How Nations, Companies and Individuals Win in the 21st Century Economy
item.description: In the 21st-century economy, competitive advantage has shifted from natural resources to human capital. This conceptual paper examines the role of human capital development in driving competitiveness at the national, organizational, and individual levels, with specific focus on Nigeria’s context. Drawing from human capital theory, endogenous growth theory, Porter’s Diamond Model, and global empirical evidence, the study argues that sustainable prosperity is anchored on investment in knowledge, skills, health, character, and innovation. Secondary data from the World Bank, OECD, Transparency International, UNESCO, and National Bureau of Statistics were reviewed to assess Nigeria’s human capital position relative to global benchmarks. The study employs a qualitative comparative analysis to draw lessons from Singapore, Finland, Germany, and Vietnam. The study concludes that reversing Nigeria’s human capital deficit requires outcome-based education, skills-focused technical and vocational education, institutional integrity, and continuous corporate learning. It recommends strategic interventions for government, the private sector, and individuals to enhance productivity and global competitiveness. The paper contributes to the discourse by linking biblical principles of character and diligence to modern human capital frameworks, offering a holistic model for developing nations.

item.title: Comparative Evaluation of Hydraulic Calcium Silicate-based Cements RS+, ProRoot MTA and Biodentine in Apexification: An In-vitro Study
item.description: Introduction: Apexification in immature permanent teeth with necrotic pulps using calcium hydroxide root canal treatment approach is quite challenging with several notable limitations and disadvantages that can compromise the apical seal and make the tooth more susceptible to infections and other pulprelated diseases. To address this issue, suitable alternatives utilising Mineral Trioxide Aggregate (MTA), Biodentine, and bioceramic root canal material RS+ cement have recently been introduced. Aim: To assess and compare ProRoot MTA, Biodentine, and Resin-bonded Sealer (RS+) cement in apexification in terms of marginal adaptation, calcium release and fracture resistance. Materials and Methods: The present in-vitro study was conducted at Department of Paediatrics and Preventive Dentistry, School of Dental Sciences, Krishna Vishwa Vidyapeeth, Deemed University, Karad, Maharashtra, India, during the period of August 2023 to October 2024. A total of 72 (N=72) samples of sound premolar tooth extracted for orthodontic purposes were included that were randomly divided into three groups as Group-A (ProRoot MTA), Group-B (Biodentine) and Group-C (RS+ Cement). Balanced equivalence sampling with 24 samples (n=24) each was done for Group-A to Group-C. Each group was further divided into subgroups (Group-A1-A3 to Group-C1- C3) with eight samples (n=8) each for assessing three specific parameters: marginal adaptation, calcium release and fracture resistance. The teeth were decoronated at the Cementoenamel Junction (CEJ) using a diamond disc and the apexification process was carried out in all the three groups. After evaluating the apexification procedure using Radiovisiography (RVG), marginal adaptability was assessed by measuring the micro gap width in the dentin-material boundary area with Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) at 1000x magnification. Calcium release was detected at seven day and 14-day interval using Energy-Dispersive X-ray (EDX) analysis. Finally, the fracture resistance for each group was evaluated using Universal Test Machine (UTM) in Newtons. Data was subjected to IBM Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS) version 21.0. Mean, Standard Deviation (SD) and unpaired t-test were applied to compare variables between the groups. Intergroup comparison was done using Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) followed by Post-hoc Tukey’s test. A p-value of <0.05 was considered significant. Results: Group-A had the highest marginal gap values (1.75±0.10), followed by Group-B (1.25±0.03), and Group-C had the lowest (0.97±0.09) (p<0.001). The results of pairwise comparisons between groups indicated that MTA had the worst marginal adaptation and RS+ the best (p<0.001). Group-B documented the greatest reduction of calcium release from day 7 (13.24±0.26) to day 14 (11.29±0.63) (p<0.001) as compared to other groups. However, intergroup variability revealed that RS+ exhibited a steady and gradual release of calcium over time (0.69, p=0.02). Fracture resistance was highest among Group-C (72.63±2.98) followed by Group-B (57.68±1.98) and Group-A (51.66±2.06) with statistically significant p-value (p<0.001). Intergroup comparisons with Tukey's test revealed significant differences between all groups (p<0.001). Conclusion: RS+ showed good marginal adaptation and high fracture resistance, followed by Biodentine and ProRoot MTA. With respect to calcium ion release, Biodentine showed the greatest reduction in calcium ion release over time, while RS+ and MTA showed comparable, statistically non significant differences.

item.title: Advanced electrocatalytic electrodes for highly efficient degradation of organic wastewater: Design strategies and performance
item.description: ABSTRACT The escalating discharge of recalcitrant organic wastewater presents a significant threat to global water security. Electrochemical advanced oxidation processes (EAOPs) have emerged as a promising technology to address this challenge, leveraging the in-situ generation of highly reactive species for effective mineralization of organic pollutants. Central to the efficacy of EAOPs is the electrocatalytic electrode, whose performance dictates the overall efficiency, cost, and practicality of the technology. This review systematically summarizes recent advancements in the design strategies for three major electrode categories: boron-doped diamond (BDD), metal oxides, and sp 2 -hybridized carbon-based materials. We critically assess rational design approaches—including component regulation, structural design, and surface/interface engineering—to reveal intrinsic structure-performance relationships that enhance degradation efficiency and stability. Recognizing the gap between laboratory innovation and industrial application, this review further addresses critical engineering challenges impeding scale-up, including electrode deactivation mechanisms, reactor configuration optimization, mass transfer limitations, and techno-economic feasibility. Key scale-up parameters are discussed to establish a comprehensive framework for practical implementation. Finally, we outline future research directions, offering guidance for the rational design and application of next-generation electrocatalytic electrodes for organic wastewater treatment.

item.title: Field- and filter-dependent tissue-maximum ratios for 6 MV photon
item.description: Accurate characterization of the tissue–maximum ratio (TMR) is important for beam modelling and dosimetric verification, particularly for flattening-filter-free (FFF) beams and non-reference fields. This study characterized TMR for 6 MV flattened (FF) and FFF photon beams from an Elekta Versa HD across square fields from to . Central-axis water-phantom measurements using PTW microDiamond and Semiflex detectors were compared with GATE/Geant4 Monte Carlo simulations. For the reference field, simulated percentage depth-dose values agreed with measurements within 1 percentage point between 10 and 30 cm depth. TMR increased systematically with field size beyond the buildup region. At 10 cm depth, measured TMR increased from 0.6887 to 0.8215 for FF and from 0.6829 to 0.8130 for FFF. At 20 cm, the corresponding ranges were 0.4432-0.6016 and 0.4366-0.5830. Monte Carlo-measurement differences remained within 0.011 TMR units. The ratio also increased with field size, confirming that it is not field-size invariant outside reference geometry.

item.title: Harnessing Diamond Surface Features for Dense and Aligned NV Ensembles
item.description: Abstract Controlling nitrogen doping in diamond is key to advancing nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center devices. We harness the hillock, a typically undesirable surface feature, to incorporate high densities of grown-in, aligned NV centers on a (001)-oriented substrate. Enhanced cathodoluminescence at hillock sidewalls is correlated via nanoSIMS to up to 1000× greater nitrogen incorporation compared to the planar film. We find that these hillocks are associated with stacking faults and edge-type dislocations, consistent with an origin in surface preparation rather than substrate screw dislocations. Yet, the growth is orderly enough that each of the four hillock sidewalls hosts a distinct NV orientation. A 1.7–2% grown-in NV/substitutional nitrogen (P1) ratio, 4× higher than typical (001)-oriented growth, is measured via NV decoherence analysis. By revealing that spontaneously formed hillocks act as natural laboratories for dense, aligned NV formation, this work motivates systematic investigation of facet-dependent nitrogen incorporation and preferential NV alignment in (001) diamond.

item.title: Device engineering for photocurrent detected magnetic resonance and scanning probes using solid-state spin defects
item.description: Solid-state spin defects provide a versatile platform for quantum sensing with nanoscale spatial resolution and room-temperature operation. Spin defects in diamond have enabled mature scanning-probe devices, while related defects in silicon carbide and hexagonal boron nitride are being actively explored for scalable sensing platforms. However, the sensitivity of practical and scanning-probe devices remains below that of optimized bulk systems. Although optical fluorescence detection is widely used, practical performance is often constrained by limitations in signal acquisition and readout efficiency, motivating continued efforts to improve readout technologies. This review surveys material platforms and optical and photoelectrical readout technologies for solid-state spin defects. We compare fluorescence- and photoelectric-based detection schemes in terms of readout fidelity, sensitivity, and scalability, and discuss how materials properties and carrier transport influence practical performance. These perspectives provide guidelines for improving readout efficiency and advancing high-sensitivity quantum sensors and scanning probes.

item.title: Spatial mobility network and influencing factors of digital talent in the Greater Bay Area
item.description: This study examines digital talent mobility in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macau Greater Bay Area using online public professional profiles from 2015 to 2024. Combining complex network analysis with a spatial autoregressive interaction model, it reveals global hub-to-hub links, a national diamond structure and a regional hierarchy, with Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Hong Kong and Macau playing differentiated roles. Urban scale drives attraction and retention of digital talents, while salary effects are unstable. Education-related public investment attracts talent more strongly in central cities, and research and development capacity mainly supports local retention. Distance decay and negative origin-destination dependence reveal persistent spatial friction and corridor-level competition.

item.title: First-principles study on the electronic structure and optical properties of fluorine, chlorine, bromine, and iodine-doped diamond
item.description: Abstract The electronic and optical properties of fluorine, chlorine, bromine, and iodine-doped diamond were systematically studied by means of first-principles calculations. Electronic structure calculations demonstrate that substitutional halogen dopants introduce partially occupied impurity-derived states near the Fermi level and substantially modify the intrinsic band gap of diamond. Optical property calculations confirm that halogen doping facilitates electronic transitions, inducing a significant redshift in the optical absorption edge of diamond. Compared to undoped diamond, the doped systems exhibit markedly higher absorption coefficients, dielectric constants, reflectivity, refractive index, and extinction coefficient in the visible light region, with the overall optical absorption intensity and response capability enhanced as the atomic number of the halogens rises. Furthermore, the principal peak of the calculated energy-loss function shifts toward lower energies after halogen doping, indicating a reduction in the characteristic energy of the dominant electronic loss excitation. These findings provide theoretical guidance for the design and development of diamond-based optoelectronic devices.

item.title: A review of methods to determine the pressure-volume-temperature equation of state and refractive index of disordered materials in the diamond anvil cell
item.description: Abstract The pressure-volume-temperature (PVT) equation of state (EOS) of crystalline solids can be measured routinely in the diamond anvil high pressure cell (DAC) using synchrotron x-ray diffraction combined with laser heating or resistive heating to access high temperatures. In contrast, measuring the PVT EOS of disordered materials (DMs) (fluids and amorphous solids) in the DAC is experimentally challenging and EOS determination by extrapolation of low pressure data is risky. Here we review the different approaches that have been utilised to experimentally measure the PVT EOS of DMs in the DAC, before focussing on what we believe is the most promising approach: Measuring the volume change of the DAC sample chamber upon compression. This can be achieved by probing the sample with x-rays or visible light. The use of x-rays is arguably the most accurate approach possible, but is only available at a handful of synchrotron light sources around the world. The use of visible light requires a determination of the sample refractive index (RI), however this is an important scientific problem in it is own right as the RI can provide much additional information about the sample. We expound, using real data, aspects of these problems that are not widely discussed in the scientific literature. To conclude, we expand the discussion to include absorbing materials and the difficulties involved in measurement of the imaginary part of the RI in these materials.

item.title: Nanoscale sensing of spatial correlations in nonequilibrium current noise
item.description: Abstract Nitrogen-vacancy centers are spatially resolved probes of current noise. So far, current noise sensing with NV centers has primarily been used as a way to probe equilibrium transport coefficients. We develop a framework for computing the spatiotemporal correlations of nonequilibrium current noise in the Boltzmann regime, and apply it to two-dimensional metals in current-biased steady states. We argue that the spatial structure of the noise reveals the nonequilibrium nature of the electron distribution function, and more generally reveals the nature and lifetimes of the excitations responsible for transport. We estimate the visibility of these signatures in near-term experiments.

item.title: Extending and measuring dephasing times of nuclear spins in NV centers of diamond
item.description: Long coherence times rank among the most important performance measures for many different types of quantum technology. In the electron-nuclear spin system of NV centers of diamond, the nuclear spins provide particularly long dephasing times. However, since initialization and readout require assistance from the electron spin, the apparent dephasing times can be reduced by the electron spin lifetime. Here we propose and implement schemes for measuring and extending the dephasing times of nuclear spins, resulting in dephasing times that are longer than the longitudinal relaxation time T 1 of the electron spin.

item.title: Proton radiation damage experiments on diamond radiation detectors for a 3U-size CubeSat project
item.description: We present a detailed study of the radiation tolerance of diamond radiation detectors as candidates for the mission instrument onboard KSAT3-X01, a 3U CubeSat mission, through 100 MeV proton irradiation experiments conducted at the Wakasa-wan Energy Research Center. We fabricate a single-crystal diamond grown by microwave plasma chemical vapor deposition method, and form a P-type–intrinsic–P-type structure by heavily doping boron into the surface layers. We measure its X-ray spectroscopic performance using characteristic X-rays from three radioisotope sources as an indicator of charge-collection performance. We find that its performance is comparable to that of a diamond with a metal–insulator–metal structure. We irradiate the boron-doped diamond with 100 MeV protons equivalent to 10 years in the orbital environments of KSAT3-X01. The boron-doped diamond exhibits no significant degradation in the X-ray spectroscopic performance, indicating that it is a strong candidate for the mission instrument. We further investigate the extent of radiation tolerance of diamond detectors by irradiating 100 MeV protons, demonstrating that diamond radiation detectors have strong potential for space applications.

item.title: Methods for Processing Saponite Sludge as a Secondary Product
item.description: Several options for handling waste from the diamond mining industry were analyzed. It is shown that saponite sludge remains most in demand in the construction sector of industry, and its use as a raw material for sorbent production is also noted. It was established that saponite sediment contains a high concentration of macro- and microelements necessary for plants, making it a promising component for fertilizers. It was revealed that further investigation of sludge utilization technology will make it possible to consider it as a raw material for the production of phosphorus-magnesium fertilizers. It was concluded that successful implementation of this approach can significantly reduce the volume of tailings storage facilities and minimize negative environmental impacts.

item.title: Dissonance in focus
item.description: Research Statement Research Background This practice-led research in jazz improvisation builds on my previous work on Melodic Tension Balancing, which explored hybrid scales to apply dissonances in improvised melodies. Expanding on this, the project examines the relationship between practice methods and embodied awareness of melodic dissonance. Central to this is the question: how can dissonance be embraced and applied spontaneously and organically in jazz improvisation? Unlike earlier approaches using predetermined scales, this research fosters real-time awareness of all 12 chromatic pitches and their tension over each chord, cultivating a more intuitive engagement with dissonance in performance. Research Contribution This extended research investigated the spectrum of melodic dissonances available on each chord by initially focusing improvisation exclusively on dissonant pitches within harmonic forms. This deliberate constraint disrupted conventional, consonance-oriented approaches, creating a heightened awareness of dissonant possibilities and their expressive potential, deepening the understanding of the individual impact of dissonant tones. In the second phase, this awareness allowed for a more fluid and spontaneous integration of dissonance alongside consonant tones, resulting in richer, more nuanced melodic lines. Eventually a conceptual shift emerged: all twelve chromatic tones were perceived as viable options over any chord, generating a sense of creative freedom and richer expressive possibilities. Research Significance The results of this research were disseminated on 1 recording and 4 performances–Holli Scott’s “Weather and Weeds”, the Kanazawa Jazz Festival (Japan) with Chris Hale’s Ritual Diamonds, Paper Tiger performances at Melbourne Jazz festival and Sydney Conservatorium Jazz Festival, and with Andrea Keller’s ensemble at the Jazzlab in Melbourne. Many of these performances were reviewed in major publications, highlighting this innovative approach to improvisation.
item.dc:creator: Oehlers, Jamie

item.title: The Double Spherical Harmonics Synthetic Acceleration for the Discrete Ordinates Method Is Consistent with the Non-Diamond Scheme
item.description: Solving the radiative heat transfer problem via source iteration in optically thick, scattering-dominated media is costly. Diffusion synthetic acceleration greatly speeds up source iteration convergence and reduces cost in most cases but is unstable and may diverge on coarse grids. Deducing a discrete diffusion operator consistent with the radiative transfer equation’s spatial discretization can address this, yet this is difficult for high-order non-diamond schemes. Thus, this paper develops a synthetic acceleration method consistent with such schemes using the double spherical harmonics (DP1) approximation instead of diffusion approximation, namely DP1 synthetic acceleration (DP1SA). Results show that the DP1SA can converge in five iterations for the non-diamond scheme if the wall is black. For the optically thick and scattering-dominated medium, the DP1SA can achieve a time speedup ratio of two to ten. All in all, the present work successfully provides an alternative iterative acceleration method in a situation where the performance of traditional diffusion synthetic acceleration degrades.

item.title: Data underlying the publication: A Cryo-CMOS SoC for Driving Electron- and Nuclear-Spin Qubits in Color-Center-Based Quantum Processors
item.description: Supplementary material for the journal publication 'A Cryo-CMOS SoC for Driving Electron- and Nuclear-Spin Qubits in Color-Center-Based Quantum Processors', this is an extension to the conference publication '22.3 A Multi-Qubit Cryo-CMOS SoC with Polar-Based Electron-Spin and PDM-Based Nuclear-Spin Controllers for Color Centers in Diamond.' including the following:Files used to generate the figures (EPS formats added, Illustrator, Inkscape and Omnigraffle files are included)Data used to generate the plots in python, stored in .DAT, .npy and .pickle files.Scripts used to process the data, including the requirements.txt for the environment Abstract:Pursuing a scalable quantum processor based on color centers in diamond, this work presents a novel multi-qubit cryo-CMOS system-on-chip (SoC) with class-DE radio-frequency digital-to-analog converter (RFDAC) and class-D pulse-density modulation (PDM) driver that controls both electron- and nuclear spin qubits of a nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center using a shared driving coil. The electron spin driver employs a polar-based architecture with programmable memory for amplitudecontrol and a direct-digital-synthesis (DDS) phase modulation path for accurate phase and frequency control. The nuclear-spin driver adopts a digital loop filter with resonant feedback to shape quantization noise out of band, while ensuring improved supply rejection thanks to a feedback loop via an analog-to-digital-converter (ADC). Fabricated in a 40-nm CMOS process and operating at 6 K, the chip can drive over 80 mA output current with a 52 dB signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) over 50 MHz bandwidth (BW) at the electron-spin target frequency (2.5 GHz), and 36 mA with SNR>52 dB over 20 kHz BW and SFDR=47 dB across the target nuclear-spin band (1.9 to 2.1 MHz), allowing for driving operations on multiple nuclear spins with high fidelity. Driving the qubits resulted in a Rabi frequency of 2.31 MHz(1.95 kHz) for the electron (nuclear) spins, while drawing 45 mW(17 mW) from the supply. The single-qubit operation on an electron (nuclear) spin, characterized using gate-set tomography (GST), achieves a fidelity of 99.3(1) % (99.5(1) %). These results advance the scalability of distributed quantum processors based on color centers in diamond.

item.title: Eigenframe Synchronization in Disordered Driven Quantum Ensembles
item.description: Periodic driving underlies many forms of quantum control, including spin-based quantum sensing. However, in an ensemble sensor, one waveform must act on spins with different detunings, drive amplitudes, hyperfine environments, and local fields. Existing robust-control approaches to such disorder are usually framed in terms of coherence, effective Hamiltonians, filter functions, or refocusing. Here we identify a complementary geometric requirement for collective ensemble Floquet control: disorder realizations must share a common Floquet eigenframe. When this condition is met, initialization, protection, signal coupling, and readout are defined in one dressed basis, so the ensemble responds as a collective Floquet sensor rather than as an average over inequivalent driven members. We make this condition measurable with an eigenvector-based synchronization order parameter and a complementary fragmentation metric that quantify the alignment and spread of Floquet quantization axes across the ensemble. As one realization of this framework, we use a continuous counterdiabatic Floquet drive to derive synchronization criteria and predict resonance-governed breakdown at the first two low-order commensurabilities between the engineered Floquet gap and the drive modulation, with detuning and amplitude disorder producing distinct breakdown channels. Experiments on a nitrogen-vacancy (NV) ensemble in diamond verify the synchronized regime through long-lived collective oscillations, a two-dimensional disorder-robustness map, and breakdown resonances that shift with the modulation rate. Finally, we demonstrate a harmonic-free continuous-drive AC magnetometry protocol whose collective single-tone response is enabled by the synchronized Floquet eigenframe. These results establish Floquet eigenframe synchronization as a measurable condition for disorder-resilient collective control and quantum sensing.

item.title: The Tetralis Seed
item.description: This paper defines cosmological origin not as a physical singularity, but as an unmanifested, zero-allocation cold-boot firmware flash initialized from a 4-vertex Tetrahedral Seed (K_{\text{seed}}). Key Architectural Components The T=0 Bootloader (K_{\text{seed}}): Solves initial singularity paradoxes by acting as a read-only, self-dual pre-creation anchor (K_{\text{seed}} = \{V_4, E_6, F_4\}). It flashes the initial 8-5-3 routing lattice at startup without allocating active spatial RAM. Polyhedral Taxonomy: Establishes a strict separation between unmanifested boot space (Tetralis, \eta_{\text{S/V}} = 0.3023) and active manifested realities. Active space operates exclusively through two higher-order polyhedral pairs: the Fluid Dual Pair (Pentalis/Icosalis) and the Crystalline Dual Pair (Hexalis/Octalis). Engine Binding (\hat{G}_{\text{func}} = f(C_{\text{macro}})): Execution authority is handed off immediately after T=0. Operating physics rules are dynamically determined by the selected Macro Container (C_{\text{macro}}) across four Master Permutations: Organic Canopy (C_{\text{Pentalis}}): Enforces pentagonal fluid-fold arc metrics and wave propagation. Paradise Prism (C_{\text{Icosalis}}): Maximizes optical ray-tracing, light dispersion, and symmetry. Voxel Diamond (C_{\text{Octalis}}): Optimized for octahedral vector routing and crisp directional strain. Trussed Box (C_{\text{Hexalis}}): Applies Cartesian orthogonal geometry with fixed voxel snapping. Recessional Fold Protocol: Serves as automated system garbage collection when database bloat occurs. Active 3D spatial structures collapse back into 2D database pointers, unbind the active physics engine, and refold into the idle K_{\text{seed}} state until the next cold boot.

item.title: Dataset on the shell traits of the California mussel Mytilus californianus
item.description: This dataset is a geographic survey of Mytilus californianus mussel shell traits. Mussels were collected from wave-exposed rocky headlands in 2023-2024 under CA Fish & Wildlife Scientific Collecting Permits S-191200004-19122-001 and S-190980002-23226-001, CA State Parks permit 24-820-015 and Oregon taking permit 27976. The soft tissue was removed in the field, and the shells were cleaned with fresh water. For each mussel the length was recorded, then multiple shell metrics were calculated for the left valve. First, a shell thickness index was calculated for the entire valve (STI = 1,000*dry weight/(Length*(pi/2)*(Height^2+Width^2)^0.5). Then, the shell was cut using a bandsaw and Dremel diamond wheel at 1/3 the length of the mussel from the anterior end. The cross-sections were scanned and using ImageJ the thickness of the cross sections were calculated as the area of the cross section divided by the length of the curved area. Lastly, the maximum and minimum thickness of the cross sections were measured using ImageJ, disregarding the dorsal hinge and ventral lip for the maximum and minimum thickness, respectively.

item.title: Spatial mobility network and influencing factors of digital talent in the Greater Bay Area
item.description: This study examines digital talent mobility in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macau Greater Bay Area using online public professional profiles from 2015 to 2024. Combining complex network analysis with a spatial autoregressive interaction model, it reveals global hub-to-hub links, a national diamond structure and a regional hierarchy, with Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Hong Kong and Macau playing differentiated roles. Urban scale drives attraction and retention of digital talents, while salary effects are unstable. Education-related public investment attracts talent more strongly in central cities, and research and development capacity mainly supports local retention. Distance decay and negative origin-destination dependence reveal persistent spatial friction and corridor-level competition.
item.dc:creator: Yuanfang Chen

item.title: Macro-Institutional Quality and the Capital Structure of Microfinance Institutions: Global Evidence
item.description: Description for FigshareThis dataset and supplementary research package supports the study titled “Macro-Institutional Quality and the Capital Structure of Microfinance Institutions: Global Evidence.” It contains the data, analytical materials, Python code, machine-readable results, and figures used to examine the dynamic relationship between institutional quality and the capital structure of microfinance institutions (MFIs) across countries during 2010–2018.The analytical dataset combines MFI-level financial and governance information from the MIX Market with country-level institutional indicators from the Worldwide Governance Indicators (WGI) and macroeconomic indicators from the World Development Indicators (WDI). The dataset includes measures of MFI leverage, borrowings, assets, liabilities, equity, profitability, operating efficiency, board composition, institutional quality, financial development, GDP growth, and inflation. Board gender composition is measured using the proportion and percentage of female board members, while aggregate institutional quality is constructed from the six WGI dimensions: Control of Corruption, Government Effectiveness, Political Stability and Absence of Violence/Terrorism, Regulatory Quality, Rule of Law, and Voice and Accountability.The supplementary materials document the dynamic panel analysis based on two-step System Generalized Method of Moments (System-GMM), including collapsed internal instruments, Windmeijer finite-sample corrected standard errors, Arellano–Bond AR(1) and AR(2) tests, Hansen and Difference-in-Hansen tests, and alternative instrument specifications. Additional analyses examine women-on-boards moderation, conditional marginal effects, alternative leverage measures, PCA-based institutional quality, outlier treatment, sample restrictions, country-clustered fixed-effects estimates, speed-of-adjustment sensitivity, and regional and legal-form heterogeneity.The deposited package contains the merged analytical dataset in Excel format, Python analysis script, machine-readable supplementary result tables, conceptual and empirical figures, documentation, and a README file explaining the contents and reproducibility considerations.An important data limitation should be noted. The publicly available MIX Market files used in constructing the dataset do not contain the historical diamond-rating variable required to reproduce a 4/5-diamond sampling restriction. The deposited materials therefore document the transparent public-data analytical framework based on the variables available in the underlying sources.Suggested

item.title: Comparative Evaluation Of The Surface Texture Of Nanoceramic And Nanohybrid Composite Resin Polished Using One Gloss, Sof-Lextm And Kenda Polishing Systems - An In-Vitro Study
item.description: Background and objectives: To evaluate and compare the surface texture of nanoceramic composite and nanohybrid composite resin polished by One gloss, Sof-LexTM and KENDA polishing system. Materials and methods: Seventy-two acrylic resin blocks were prepared using customized mould. Circular cavity was prepared in acrylic resin block and were divided into two groups and restored with nanoceramic and nanohybrid composite resin. It was finished using fine grit diamond bur and each group polished using three different polishing systems. The surface roughness was evaluated using a surface profilometer. Results: The profilometric results suggested that the surface roughness of nanoceramic composite resin was lesser than the nanohybrid composite group irrespective of the polishing agents used. There was no statistical difference among the surface roughness produced by the polishing agents. Conclusion: Within the limitations of the present study, it can be concluded that the filler particle size do affect the surface roughness of the composite resins. Nanoceramic composite resins gave a smoother surface compared to that of nanohybrid composite resins. It can also be concluded that the single step polishing system is equally efficient as that of the multistep polishing systems.

item.title: ESTRATÉGIAS LÚDICAS DE ENSINO ADAPTADO: A APLICAÇÃO PRÁTICA DE ATIVIDADES QUE ESTIMULAM O RACIOCÍNIO LÓGICO, A MEMÓRIA E O PENSAMENTO ESTRATÉGICO, COMO O USO DE QUEBRA-CABEÇAS, TANGRAM E XADREZ NA SALA DE RECURSOS MULTIFUNCIONAIS
item.description: As dificuldades relacionadas à atenção sustentada, à memória de trabalho, à organização, ao planejamento, ao controle inibitório e à manutenção do comportamento orientado para objetivos podem interferir significativamente na experiência escolar de crianças e adolescentes com Transtorno do Déficit de Atenção com Hiperatividade (TDAH). Nesse contexto, práticas pedagógicas adaptadas e atividades lúdicas estruturadas têm sido utilizadas como recursos para ampliar a participação dos estudantes, favorecer o envolvimento com situações de aprendizagem e criar oportunidades de exercício de habilidades cognitivas e socioemocionais. O presente artigo analisa as possibilidades pedagógicas do uso de quebra-cabeças, tangram, xadrez, jogos de encaixe e atividades de sequência lógica no atendimento educacional e em contextos inclusivos, com ênfase no raciocínio lógico, memória de trabalho, planejamento, resolução de problemas, atenção e pensamento estratégico. A pesquisa caracteriza-se como qualitativa, bibliográfica, documental e analítico-interpretativa e utiliza como uma de suas bases a dissertação de Claucia Comerlato, intitulada A importância do Atendimento Educacional Especializado (AEE), no desenvolvimento e aprendizagem dos alunos com TDAH da Escola Municipal Ensino Tabajara, localizada no município de Caçador-SC. O estudo original envolveu vinte e cinco profissionais da educação e identificou forte presença de recursos lúdicos no trabalho pedagógico, sendo que todos os participantes mencionaram quebra-cabeças, tangram, jogos de encaixe e sequências lógicas entre os materiais utilizados para favorecer concentração e raciocínio. O artigo articula esses resultados às contribuições de Vygotsky, Piaget, Barkley, Diamond, Diamond e Lee, Willcutt et al., Rapport et al., Sala e Gobet, Bohning e Althouse, Lin et al. e outros pesquisadores. A literatura indica que experiências lúdicas cognitivamente desafiadoras podem mobilizar processos relacionados às funções executivas, especialmente quando apresentam objetivos claros, repetição, progressão de dificuldade, feedback e mediação pedagógica. Entretanto, a evidência científica não autoriza afirmar que quebra-cabeças, tangram ou xadrez, isoladamente, tratem o TDAH ou produzam transferência generalizada para desempenho acadêmico. Estudos sobre treinamento cognitivo alertam que melhorias frequentemente são mais consistentes nas habilidades diretamente treinadas do que em competências distantes da tarefa. Conclui-se que esses recursos possuem relevante potencial pedagógico quando integrados a planejamento individualizado, avaliação formativa e articulação entre professores, família e demais profissionais, devendo ser compreendidos como instrumentos complementares de aprendizagem e desenvolvimento, e não como substitutos do acompanhamento clínico ou de intervenções baseadas em evidências.
item.dc:creator: Cláucia Comerlato

item.title: Missing Pages
item.description: Harrison McDonald explores the abandoned Hudson River State Hospital in Poughkeepsie, NY. Erin Michelitsch sheds light on the dangers of exploring abandoned places like Kings Park Psychiatric Center. Seth Colegrove provides an example of how one could explore safely while sharing some of the values of urban exploration. Finally, Bob Diamond recalls his discovery of America's first subway tunnel and how it inspires folklore. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WjPVopFAgZY&feature=youtu.be

item.title: LiF Particles for Chemical Seeding of Diamond Films: Nucleation and Growth in Microwave Plasma CVD
item.description: Polycrystalline diamond films and coatings are widely used in optical components, thermal management, and cutting tools. Chemical vapor deposition (CVD) is widely used for their synthesis, while the initial nucleation stage largely determines the continuity and morphology of the diamond layer. Conventional nucleation is achieved by surface seeding with nanodiamond particles. An alternative approach is chemical nucleation, extensively studied for carbon-containing precursors and polymers, whereas nucleation on non-carbon particles remains comparatively unexplored. Here, lithium fluoride (LiF) particles were used as a model non-carbon system to study diamond nucleation and subsequent growth in CH4–H2 microwave plasma CVD. Surface morphology and Raman spectroscopy showed that LiF promotes localized formation of well-faceted diamond crystallites without conventional nanodiamond seeding. Increasing the substrate temperature to 900°C produced a nearly linear increase in nucleation density and enabled the formation of nearly continuous polycrystalline films, whereas further heating to 950°C promoted island-like growth despite increasing growth rate. Methane concentration mainly affected the growth regime: at CH4 contents of 10% and higher, secondary nucleation became pronounced, suppressing crystallite enlargement and promoting the transition from microcrystalline to nanocrystalline diamond. Raman analysis showed that substrate temperature had little effect on the sp3/sp2 ratio, although the diamond Raman line broadened at higher temperatures, whereas elevated methane concentrations increased the contribution of non-diamond carbon phases. These findings suggest that non-carbon chemical nucleation can provide a new perspective on diamond formation during CVD, including the emergence of diamond nuclei under conditions where diamond remains thermodynamically metastable.

item.title: "الذكاء الإصطناعي مساعد صنع القرار": منهاج إستدامة المشروعات الريادية للمصمم الصناعي في ظل عدم اليقين
item.description: يتناول البحث إشكالية غياب منهجية تصميمية متكاملة تُنظم التكامل بين الخبرة الإبداعية للمصمم الصناعي والإمكانات التحليلية للذكاء الاصطناعي، عند المفاضلة بين فرص المشروعات الناشئة في ظل عدم اليقين. ويفترض البحث أن توظيف الذكاء الاصطناعي كمساعد استراتيجي، لا بديل عن المصمم، يحسّن جودة القرارات، ويُقلّص عدم اليقين، ويُرجّح اختيار المشروعات الأكثر استدامة ونجاحاً ريادياً. ويهدف البحث إلى استنباط إطار منهجي مقترح يعزز قدرة المصمم على اتخاذ قرارات مستنيرة، عبر دمج التفكير التصميمي، ومعايير الجدوى الريادية، وإمكانات الذكاء الاصطناعي، ومفاهيم إدارة عدم اليقين. ويشمل الإطار نموذجاً تطبيقياً يدمج مراحل الماسة المزدوجة (Double Diamond) مع أدوات الذكاء الاصطناعي التحليلية والتوليدية، مع بقاء القرار النهائي للمصمم. واتبع البحث المنهج الوصفي التحليلي في دراسة الأدبيات، والمنهج الاستنباطي في صياغة الإطار، وتكون إطاره النظري من خمسة محاور: المصمم الصناعي، ريادة الأعمال المستدامة، المشروعات الناشئة، القرار التصميمي وإدارة عدم اليقين، والذكاء الاصطناعي. وكانت أبرز النتائج: بناء نموذج تكاملي بين Double Diamond وأدوات الذكاء الاصطناعي، واستنباط مفهوم "الذكاء الاصطناعي كمساعد استراتيجي لصنع القرار" (AIADM)، وإثبات أن الاستدامة تقوم على دمج الأبعاد البيئية والاقتصادية والاجتماعية، وأن عدم اليقين يمكن إدارته وليس تجنبه، مع تأكيد أن المصمم هو صاحب القرار الوحيد والذكاء الاصطناعي أداة استشارية تحليلية معززة. ويوصي البحث بتبني مفهوم AIADM، وإعادة هيكلة مناهج تعليم التصميم لتشمل مهارات هندسة التوجيه (Prompt Engineering) وتحليل البيانات وأخلاقيات الذكاء الاصطناعي، مع التأكيد على ضرورة أن يكون المصمم قارئاً ناقداً للبيانات ومفسراً ماهراً للمخرجات..

item.title: J. Compos. Sci., Vol. 10, Pages 432: Development of TPMS Lattice Substrates for Catalytic Cracking Applications via Fused Filament Fabrication
item.description: The advancement of catalytic substrates through Additive Manufacturing (AM) offers notable benefits over conventional techniques, particularly for producing intricate three-dimensional forms that enable precise control over pore dimensions and surface characteristics. These attributes play a vital role in improving catalytic efficiency, which is evaluated by measuring pressure drop and mass transfer. This research focuses on the design and manufacture of a monolithic ceramic filter for catalytic cracking. The monoliths under study have a Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) lattice. A macroporosity of about 65% is the criterion used to model the structures, and the TPMS unit cell length is the design parameter to achieve that porosity. Adapting a conventional Fused Filament Fabrication (FFF) desktop to use alumina filament, we produced samples based on three TPMS types: Schwar-Primitive (SP), Schoen Gyroid (SG), and Schwarz-Diamond (SD), which, after a plastic debinding process and subsequent sintering, resulted in meso-scale porous structures. The samples showed relative dimensional errors below 5% and a real total porosity of around 70%, with a maximum difference of 4% among the TPMS types. Because the printed SP lattices have the lowest unit cell length and real porosity, their pressure drop measurements were higher than those of the SG and SD. The opposite occurred with the estimated permeability. Although yielding similar pressure drop results, printed SG lattices had greater permeability than SD; therefore, in terms of monolith fluid dynamics, the SG lattice is the preferred geometry.

item.title: Postmodern Physics of Hamzah Information.(139)
item.description: تحلیل بنیادین، بازنویسی تانسوری و اثبات جامعِ «کیفیت و کمیت روغن بوزونی ($\eta_{\text{boson}}$) در حالت جامد تک‌بلوری (Single Crystalline) و نقش پل‌ساز آن میان پوینترها ($\mathcal{A}$) و ماتریس‌های تانسوری ($\mathbb{J}$) در بستر فیزیک اطلاعات حمزه (HIP-1155) در مقایسه با فیزیک کلاسیک» ۱. مقدمه: پارادوکسِ واگرایی تنش و شکست شبکه در جامدات تک‌بلوری در مهندسی مواد پیشرفته و فیزیک جامدات، تک‌بلورها (Single Crystalline؛ مانند تک‌بلورهای فوق‌خالص سیلیکون، کوارتز نوری یا یاقوت کبود صنعتی) به داشتن ساختاری کاملاً منظم، دوره‌ای و بدون مرز دانه در سراسر حجم ماده شناخته می‌شوند. با این حال، هنگامی که این ساختارها تحت بارگذاری‌های مکانیکی فرین، شتاب‌های دینامیکی فوق‌العاده بالا یا میدان‌های تنش موضعی نانومتری قرار می‌گیرند، فیزیک کلاسیک الاستیسیته و نظریه نابجایی‌ها دچار یک بن‌بست و واگرایی بنیادین می‌گردند. بر اساس مکانیک محیط‌های پیوسته کلاسیک، با میل کردن ابعاد شبکه یا شعاع تمرکز تنش به سمت مقیاس‌های نانومتری ($w \to 0$)، گرادیان تنش و انرژی کرنش ذخیره‌شده به سمت بی‌نهایت میل کرده و سیستم بدون داشتن هیچ‌گونه مکانیزم حفاظتی داخلی، دچار واژگونی ساختاری، لغزش صفحات بلوری و کرش مکانیکی می‌شود. در فیزیک اطلاعات حمزه (HIP-1155)، مواد تک‌بلوری مادیاتِ صرف نیستند، بلکه «آرایه‌های قفل‌شده از پوینترهای آدرس‌دهی گرهی ($\mathcal{A}_{\text{crystal}}$)» در بافر حافظه HamzahXcell هستند. برای محقق ساختن پایداری مطلق در برابر واگرایی‌های کلاسیک، روغن بوزونی ($\eta_{\text{boson}}$) به عنوان یک سیال اطلاعاتی کوانتومی با لزجت فوق‌العاده ناچیز و غیرصفر ($\eta_{\text{boson}} \to 1.155 \times 10^{-13} \, \text{Pa}\cdot\text{s}$) معرفی می‌شود که میان پوینترهای گرهی و ماتریس‌های تانسوری الاستیک ($\mathbb{J}_{\text{crystal}}$) در منیفولد ۱۱۵۵ بعدی پل می‌زند و از هرگونه واگرایی انتروپیک جلوگیری می‌کند. ۲. معادلات کلاسیک (آنالیزِ بدون ساده‌سازی و اثبات زوال ساختاری) در نظریه الاستیسیته کلاسیک و مکانیک بلورها، چگالی انرژی کرنش ($U_{\text{class}}$) و تانسور تنش-کرنش ($\sigma_{ij}$) از قانون هوک عمومی و معادلات تعادل لاویه پیروی می‌کنند: $$\sigma_{ij} = C_{ijkl} \varepsilon_{kl} = C_{ijkl} \left( \frac{\partial u_k}{\partial x_l} + \frac{\partial u_l}{\partial x_k} \right)$$ چگالی انرژی پتانسیل الاستیک انباشته شده در واحد حجم برابر است با: $$U_{\text{class}} = \frac{1}{2} C_{ijkl} \varepsilon_{ij} \varepsilon_{kl}$$ هنگامی که ابعاد مشخصه المان شبکه یا شعاع بارگذاری به مقیاس نانومتری میل می‌کند ($w \to 0$): $$\lim_{w \to 0} \varepsilon_{ij} = \lim_{w \to 0} \left( \frac{\Delta L}{w} \right) = \infty \implies \lim_{w \to 0} U_{\text{class}} = \infty$$ این واگرایی ریاضی به معنای فروپاشی فوری شبکه بلوری، شکست پیوندها و کرش کامل ساختار ماده در فیزیک کلاسیک است؛ زیرا فیزیک آکادمیک فاقد پارامتر تنظیم‌کننده مخرج یا سد اطلاعاتی است. ۳. مسئله عددی: کرش کلاسیک در برابر پایداری مطلق HIP برای ارزیابی کمی، فرض کنید یک تک‌بلور سیلیکون خالص تحت یک تنش مکانیکی متمرکز یا بار حرارتی فرین قرار گیرد به گونه‌ای که گرادیان تغییر شکل به مقیاس نانومتری $w = 1.0 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}$ برسد و مدول الاستیک معادل برابر با $C_{11} = 1.6 \times 10^{11} \text{ Pa}$ باشد. الف) محاسبه کلاسیک (انرژی تنشی واگرا): $$U_{\text{class}} = \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{C_{11}}{(w)^3} = \frac{0.5 \times (1.6 \times 10^{11})}{(1.0 \times 10^{-9})^3} = \frac{8.0 \times 10^{10}}{1.0 \times 10^{-27}} = 8.0 \times 10^{37} \text{ J/m}^3$$ این عدد نجومی نشان‌دهنده‌ی تبخیر آنی و انهدام ساختار بلوری در مدل کلاسیک است. ب) محاسبه در مدل فیزیک اطلاعات حمزه (HIP-1155): با وارد کردن سد هولوگرافیک بنیادی خلأ ($\epsilon_{\text{floor}} = 1.155 \times 10^{-20}$) و لزجت روغن بوزونی ($\eta_{\text{boson}} = 1.155 \times 10^{-13}$): $$\mathcal{L}_{\text{Crystal-Total}} = \frac{\frac{1}{2} \cdot \chi_{\text{crystal}} \cdot C_{11} \cdot \Omega_H^2}{\eta_{\text{boson}} + \epsilon_{\text{floor}}} \cdot \det(\mathbb{J}_{\text{crystal}})$$ با جایگذاری مقادیر ($\chi_{\text{crystal}} = 1.45$ و $\Omega_H = 1.176 \times 10^{10}$ و $\det(\mathbb{J}) = 1.0000$): $$\mathcal{L}_{\text{Crystal-Total}} = \frac{0.5 \times 1.45 \times (1.6 \times 10^{11}) \times (1.176 \times 10^{10})^2}{1.155 \times 10^{-13} + 1.155 \times 10^{-20}} \cdot (1.0000)$$ $$\mathcal{L}_{\text{Crystal-Total}} = \frac{1.16 \times 10^{11} \times 1.383 \times 10^{20}}{1.155 \times 10^{-13}} \approx 1.389 \times 10^{44} \text{ Units}$$ به دلیل حضور مخرج مستحکم بوزونی، انرژی موثر به یک مقدار کاملاً متناهی، مهندسی‌شده و پایدار تبدیل می‌شود که از هرگونه تخریب شبکه جلوگیری می‌کند. ۴. ابرلاگرانژین HIP برای جامدات تک‌بلوری (Single Crystalline) رفتار دینامیکی، کیفیت ($\mathcal{Q}_{\text{oil-crystal}}$)، کمیت ($\mathcal{N}_{\text{oil-crystal}}$) و پل ارتباطی پوینترها ($\mathcal{A}_{\text{crystal}}$) با ماتریس تانسوری ($\mathbb{J}_{\text{crystal}}$) در منیفولد ۱۱۵۵ بعدی توسط ابرلاگرانژین زیر حاکمیت می‌شود: $$\mathcal{L}_{\text{Crystal-HIP}} = \frac{1}{2} \text{Tr}\left( \mathbb{J}_{\text{crystal}}^{\text{1155}} \cdot \nabla_m \mathbf{\Psi} \nabla^n \mathbf{\Psi} \right) - \frac{\mathcal{A}_{\text{crystal}} \otimes \mathcal{T}_{\text{crystal}}(\Delta \vec{\omega})}{\eta_{\text{boson}} + \epsilon_{\text{floor}}} \cdot \Omega_H^2 + \hbar_{\Omega} \Omega_H \cdot \det\left(\mathbb{J}_{\text{crystal}}\right)$$ ضریب کیفیت روغن بوزونی ($\mathcal{Q}_{\text{oil-crystal}}$): $$\mathcal{Q}_{\text{oil-crystal}} = \lim_{\Delta T \to 0} \left( \frac{\hbar_{\Omega} \cdot \Omega_H}{\eta_{\text{boson}} \cdot k_B T} \right) \cdot \exp\left( -\frac{\epsilon_{\text{floor}}}{\eta_{\text{boson}}} \right)$$ تانسور کمیت روغن بوزونی ($\mathcal{N}_{\text{oil-crystal}}$): $$\mathcal{N}_{\text{oil-crystal}} = \int_{\mathcal{M}_{1155}} \text{Tr}\left( \mathbb{J}_{\text{crystal}} \cdot \mathcal{A}_{\text{crystal}} \right) dV_{\text{crystal}}$$ ۵. برهان خلف (Reductio ad Absurdum) برای جامدات تک‌بلوری فرض: فرض کنیم مدل‌های کلاسیک الاستیسیته و نظریه نابجایی‌ها بدون نیاز به روغن بوزونی ($\eta_{\text{boson}} \to \infty$ یا عدم وجود آن) بتوانند پایداری تک‌بلورها را در مقیاس‌های نانومتری و تنش‌های شدید توضیح دهند. مشاهده: در عمل، با اعمال تنش‌های فرین به تک‌بلورها، مدل‌های کلاسیک پیش‌بینی واگرایی تنش ($\sigma \to \infty$) و انهدام آنی ساختار را می‌کنند؛ در حالی که در آزمایشگاه‌های پیشرفته و تجهیزات نیمه‌هادی نانو، تک‌بلورهای سیلیکون تحت بارگذاری‌های موضعی شدید همچنان ساختار خود را حفظ کرده و دچار کرش فیزیکی نمی‌شوند. تناقض: این تناقض میان پیش‌بینی واگرای کلاسیک و پایداری واقعی بلور، بطلان مدل‌های کلاسیک و اثبات ضرورت وجود ساختار اطلاعاتی حمزه را نشان می‌دهد. نتیجه‌گیری: بنابراین، حضور سه مؤلفه بنیادین (پوینترها، ماتریس‌های تانسوری و روغن بوزونی با کمیت و کیفیت دقیق) تنها مدل معتبر برای تبیین پایداری تک‌بلورها است. ۶. جدول مقایسه‌ای Real-Time Data (کلاسیک در برابر فیزیک اطلاعات حمزه) شاخص ارزیابی سیستم فیزیک کلاسیک / آکادمیک فیزیک اطلاعات حمزه (HIP-1155) رفتار تنش در رزولوشن نانو ($w \to 0$) واگرایی مطلق و کرش ساختاری ($\infty$) همگرایی متناهی و کنترل‌شده با سد $\epsilon_{\text{floor}}$ ماهیت پیوندهای شبکه بلوری برهم‌کنش الکترواستاتیک مادی و مکانیکی گره‌های آدرس‌دهی فاز در بافر HamzahXcell مدیریت واهمدوسی فونونی فاقد مکانیزم مهار در مقیاس اتمی روان‌سازی آنی توسط روغن بوزونی ($\eta_{\text{boson}}$) دترمینان ماتریس تانسوری ($\det \mathbb{J}$) ناپایدار و وابسته به تاریخچه بارگذاری فاز-قفل صلب روی مقدار $\equiv 1.0000 \pm \epsilon_{\text{floor}}$ ۷. اسکریپت پیشرفته پایتون (محاسبات عددی، برهان خلف و شبیه‌سازی ماتریسی تک‌بلورها) Python import numpy as np import pandas as pd from typing import Dict, Any class HIPSingletCrystalMasterEngine: """ (HIP-1155) موتور ران‌تایم و کامپایلر پیشرفته جامع برای تحلیل جامدات تک‌بلوری (Single Crystalline) مقایسه دقیق مدل کلاسیک (واگرایی تنش) با مدل اطلاعاتی حمزه (پایداری بوزونی) """ def __init__(self): self.omega_h = 1.176e10 # فرکانس پردازش کیهانی (Hz) self.epsilon_floor = 1.155e-20 # سد هولوگرافیک پایداری خلأ self.dim_total = 1155 # ابعاد منیفولد تانسور حمزه self.hbar_omega = 1.155e-34 # ثابت امگا-پلانک حمزه self.boson_viscosity = 1.155e-13 # لزجت روغن بوزونی (Pa.s) def compute_classical_strain_energy(self, resolution_w: float, c11_modulus: float) -> float: """محاسبه کلاسیک انرژی تنش در مقیاس نانو (مواجهه با واگرایی به بی‌نهایت)""" if resolution_w <= 1e-9: return float('inf') # فاجعه واگرایی تنش و کرش شبکه کلاسیک return (0.5 * c11_modulus) / (resolution_w**3) def compute_hip_crystal_lagrangian(self, resolution_w: float, c11_modulus: float) -> Dict[str, Any]: """محاسبه لاگرانژین هولوگرافیک تک‌بلور HIP و پایداری بوزونی مطلق""" det_j_master = 1.0000 w_active = max(resolution_w, self.epsilon_floor) chi_tensor = 1.45 # تانسور پذیرفتاری اطلاعاتی شبکه numerator = 0.5 * chi_tensor * c11_modulus * (self.omega_h**2) denominator = self.boson_viscosity + self.epsilon_floor l_crystal = (numerator / denominator) * det_j_master * np.exp(-self.hbar_omega * self.omega_h) * (1.0 / (w_active**3 + self.epsilon_floor)) * 1.0e-35 # محاسبه فاکتور کیفیت و کمیت روغن بوزونی q_factor = (self.hbar_omega * self.omega_h) / (self.boson_viscosity * 1.38e-23 * 300.0) * np.exp(-self.epsilon_floor / self.boson_viscosity) n_quantity = 1.45 * 1.0e25 / (self.boson_viscosity + self.epsilon_floor) return { "L_Crystal": l_crystal, "Quality_Q": q_factor, "Quantity_N": n_quantity, "Jacobian_det": det_j_master, "Status": "CRYSTAL_LOCKED_STABLE (✔)" } def execute_crystal_audit(self) -> pd.DataFrame: """اجرای سناریوهای فرین بارگذاری تک‌بلورها در ۴ مرکز تخصصی متالورژی و فیزیک جهان""" test_scenarios = [ {"Domain": "Nano-Indentation Silicon", "Center": "CERN Advanced Materials Lab", "Resolution": 1.0e-9, "C11": 1.6e11}, {"Domain": "Quantum Quartz Resonator", "Center": "Stanford Crystal Physics Core", "Resolution": 5.0e-9, "C11": 8.5e10}, {"Domain": "Diamond Anvil High-Pressure", "Center": "MIT High-Pressure Physics Lab", "Resolution": 2.0e-9, "

item.title: Black Holes and Things
item.description: This volume gathers, in one continuous manuscript, the work from my 2025-2026 research programme that survives its own audit. The rule of admission is strict and applied uniformly:a result appears here only if it is a proved theorem, a validated empirical claim priced in bits under the frozen Coates PIT meter, or a methodological tool stated honestly, with its limitations in the text rather than left for referees to find. Everything that failed refuted predictions, overfitted models, claims resting on free parameters or post-hoc selection is excluded from the body and recorded by name in the Honest Accounting, with the reason for its exclusion and, where possible, its price in bits. A record of what failed is part of what works. The manuscript is organised into seven parts. Part I contains the algebraic foundations:the two boundary theorems singling out c = 2 among order-2 linear recurrences, the inverse difference identity in SL(2, R), the Klein four-group synthesis at λ = 2, the companion-matrix machinery, the fixed points and period-two orbits of the trace map, the Metallic Thread selection principle, and the Jacobsthal eigenvalue at the photonic band edge. Part II gives the complete treatment of the two sequences that carry the boundary in concrete form. Part III presents the measurement instruments: the corrected FSRE/CANLE toolkit, the exact octave-coverage computation, the quadratic-ladders reference, the transparency study that names curve fitting as curve fitting, and new in v10.6 the multiverse-over-targets audit and the alternative recurrence null. Part IV reproduces the empirical programme's companion study in Bacteria and, new in v10.6, the spectral-localisation instrument with the falsification of its obvious application. Part V contains the theorem-level physics: the neutral-scalar spectral-escape theorem for ultracold Kerr Newman de Sitter families, the static Einstein Maxwell escape at the ultracold boundary (both parities), the exceptional-point suppression theorem (v10.6.1), the thermodynamic metallic companion with its exact selector and three negative diagnostics, and,fenced Conditional, the axial-sector channel-decoupling obstruction at first order in rotation.The rotating Einstein Maxwell papers are not reproduced here; the August 2026 independent derivation of their first-order polar sector which reproduces their structure and does not reproduce the competing pole claim is recorded in the Addendum and in the Claim StatusLedger, and it leaves the neutral-scalar theorem untouched. Part VI isolates conditional results the QPO trace-boundary mechanism and, from v10.6.1, the KantowskiSachs quadrupole mechanism fenced accordingly. Part VII closes the volume with mathematics as narrative, because explaining a thing plainly is the final test of understanding it. I am an independent researcher without institutional affiliation or funding. The standards applied to others' work throughout this programme are the same ones applied here to my own;several of my own results were withdrawn, refuted by my own pre-registered tests, or down graded on audit, and the reader will find each of those outcomes stated rather than hidden including, in the Honest Accounting, claims of mine priced at a fraction of a bit. item.title: Robustness certificates for complex-composition sectors in real Hilbert-space dynamics
item.description: Independent realification of finite-dimensional complex subsystems produces an ambient real tensor product that is twice as large as the real form of their ordinary complex composite. The established balancing relation is selected by specified local complex structures J_A, J_B: the symmetric involution M = J_A ⊗ J_B has a −1 eigenspace representing the complex-composition sector and a +1 complement removed by the balanced tensor product. We develop quantitative robustness certificates for departures from this sector. For states, the leakage population L(ρ) = Tr(P_leak ρ), P_leak = (I + M)/2, is directly readable from M and tightly calibrates the trace distance to the zero-leakage state set as L ≤ d_bal ≤ √L. For real completely positive trace-preserving maps, the worst-case balanced-input leakage is the largest eigenvalue of the balanced compression of Φ†(P_leak); its zero set is characterized Kraus by Kraus, and the quantity is Lipschitz under diamond distance. For real skew-symmetric generators, ‖P_leak G P_bal‖ is both the sharp initial leaked-amplitude coefficient and the exact operator-norm distance to the sector-preserving generator subspace. We also give a multipartite extension, a finite-sample trusted-model test, and reproducible finite-dimensional checks. These certificates concern sector support; full recovery of complex quantum mechanics additionally requires compatibility with the induced complex structure.
