item.title: How Journal Editors are Addressing Challenges with No-fee Open Access
item.description: No-fee or “diamond” open access (OA) embodies the principles of the UNESCO Recommendation on Open Science, particularly openness, inclusivity, and collaboration (2023). This model of publishing strengthens equitable access to knowledge, promotes multilingualism, and democratizes science. Importantly, no-fee OA eliminates both article processing charges (APCs) and subscription fees, making it completely free for both authors and readers. The no-fee model is often supported by academic institutions, governments, or non-profit organizations, focusing on equity, inclusivity, and accessibility. To investigate the efficacy of this model, the presenters administered a survey of North American no-fee journal editors. This paper will share an overview of the survey data, focusing on the main challenges facing no-fee journals, the strategies journal editors are using to overcome those challenges, and the issues around equity and sustainability. In an effort to center the voices of those editing and managing no-fee OA journals, we will also share anonymized comments from the survey respondents to provide more insight into the spectrum of their perspectives.
item.dc:creator: Colleen Lyon
Christopher Hollister
item.dc:source: Journal of Open Educational Resources in Higher Education

item.title: Design, Kinematic Control, and Implementation of a LEGO-Based Drawing Robot for Lissajous Curve Generation
item.description: Lissajous figures are frequently studied and widely used objects in engineering and physics. Although these patterns are usually analysed using computer simulations or oscilloscopes, such tools may limit their educational value by covering the core physical processes that generate the curves. In order to address these problems, the design, kinematic validation, and prototyping of a dual-axis drawing robot were carried out on the LEGO Education SPIKE Prime platform. The hardware implementation centres on a LEGO-based dual Scotch yoke mechanism, which supports precise transformation of uniform circular motion into simple harmonic motion. This setup implements the superposition of two independent simple harmonic oscillations by simultaneously moving the paper tray along the x-axis and the pen along the y-axis. High-fidelity trajectories are achieved through a 40:1 worm gear reduction, which enables precise control of the parameter configuration. The phase shift can be manually set by adjustment levers. The robot’s geometry supports discrete amplitude settings of 8, 16, and 24 mm by adjusting the crankpin position. System control is managed by Python code that synchronises motor speeds and angular displacements according to frequency ratios. The research methodology used the Double Diamond design thinking framework, structuring development into four phases: identifying historical mechanical solutions, defining pedagogical and technical classroom requirements, iteratively developing the LEGO prototype, and testing the system through representative drawing experiments. Results show that the robot can reproduce a broad range of periodic Lissajous curves with high repeatability, and that its physical outputs show strong visual and mathematical correspondence to ideal trajectories simulated in the Desmos graphing calculator. The final prototype satisfies classroom constraints, providing a transparent, low-cost, modular STEAM tool that bridges the distance between abstract parametric equations and complex mechanical implementations.
item.dc:creator: Attila Körei

item.title: NanoPrism: A Taxonomy-Guided Pipeline for Rapid Functional Profiling of Oxford Nanopore Long-Read Metagenomes
item.description: Background/Objectives: Oxford Nanopore sequencing produces long reads quickly, but most functional profiling tools were developed for short reads or rely on assembly pipelines that are computationally costly and sensitive to long-read error rates. We present NanoPrism, a taxonomy-guided pipeline for rapid functional profiling of long-read metagenomes. Methods: NanoPrism (i) identifies sample composition with Kraken2, (ii) constructs compact species-specific coding sequence (CDS)–KEGG ortholog databases, and (iii) estimates ortholog abundances by direct minimap2 alignment of nanopore reads with single-copy marker normalization. We evaluated NanoPrism on simulated Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 and PA14 reads and on ZymoBIOMICS mock-community datasets sequenced on GridION and PromethION platforms. Results: On the Zymo long-read datasets, NanoPrism achieved Pearson correlations of 0.917–0.922 against independent expected ortholog profiles under unit-sum normalization. On matched one-million-read subsets, NanoPrism achieved higher correlations and lower Jensen–Shannon distances and mean absolute errors than the evaluated DIAMOND-based MEGAN-LR workflow. Experiments that omitted one species at a time from the reference database showed that omission of low-abundance community members had limited effects on the aggregate KO profile, whereas omission of the dominant Listeria monocytogenes reference from the Log community reduced Pearson correlation from approximately 0.92 to 0.29. Conclusions: NanoPrism offers a computationally efficient option for taxonomy-guided functional profiling of bacterial isolates and defined microbial communities. Validation on complex clinical and environmental metagenomes, broader forms of taxonomic-classification error, and dedicated fungal benchmarks remain necessary.

item.title: The Effect of Socio-Economic and Energy-Related Factors on Environmental Degradation in South Africa: An Autoregressive Distributed Lag Model Approach
item.description: Over the past two decades, the world has experienced significant and relentless increase in environmental degradation, measured through carbon emissions (CO2). These emissions have been one of the persistent global concerns. South Africa boosts abundance of natural resources and some of the world’s most substantial mineral deposits endowment in the form of precious metals, diamonds and gold. The paper aims to examine impact of socio-economic and energy-related factors on environmental degradation from South African perspective. Using multivariate annual data spanning from 1991 to 2022, Autoregressive Distributed Lag Model (ADRL) was employed to determine both short-run and long-run impact of financial development (FD), renewable energy(RE), non-renewable energy (NRE), unemployment rate (UNE), economic growth (GDPPC), and population growth (PoPG) on CO2 emission. The results show that FD, RE, GDPPC, and PoPG promote environmental quality in the long run while NRE has opposite impact. The study thus calls for actions by relevant policymakers to stimulate economic growth and promote access to climate change finance, thereby encouraging investment in green energy technologies and consumption, to enhance and promote environmental quality in South Africa.
item.dc:creator: Lehlohonolo Godfrey Mafeta
Amahle Madiba
Robert Nicky Tjano

item.title: Linear response across interaction regimes in two-dimensional ferromagnets
item.description: Recent discoveries of two-dimensional (2D) ferromagnets have stimulated intense interest in understanding and controlling their spin transport properties. A central microscopic feature of these systems is that exchange-driven magnon--magnon interactions are strongly momentum dependent: low-momentum magnons interact weakly, while high-momentum ones can scatter strongly and exhibit collective hydrodynamic behavior. Understanding transport in such systems therefore requires a microscopic description capable of capturing ballistic and hydrodynamic regimes on equal footing. The natural framework is the quantum Boltzmann equation (QBE), whose solution is notoriously difficult because of the multidimensional collision integrals. Here, we develop a method based on an efficient representation of distribution functions as sums of Gaussians, which renders the collision integrals tractable. This approach enables accurate solution of the linearized QBE and computation of momentum- and frequency-resolved linear response in 2D ferromagnets across a broad range of temperatures and magnetic fields. In particular, we resolve a temperature-driven crossover from a ballistic regime dominated by weakly interacting low-momentum magnons to a collective hydrodynamic regime governed by strongly interacting high-momentum modes. Applying this method to monolayer CrCl$_3$, we obtain good agreement with recent nitrogen-vacancy-center dephasing experiments that reported anomalous magnetic noise consistent with magnon sound. More broadly, our work establishes a general framework for computing momentum- and frequency-resolved linear response in interacting 2D quantum systems describable within quantum Boltzmann kinetics.

Pavel E. Dolgirev
Oleksii Malyshev
Eugene Demler

item.title: Color Matching Ability Among Single-Shade Resin Composites: Instrumental and Visual Evaluation
item.description: Background: This study aimed to evaluate the color-matching ability of 4 single-shade resin composites (RCs), using 2 different evaluation methods. Methods: One hundred and twelve specimens (8 × 2 mm) were fabricated in disc shape using 4 single-shade RCs (Omnichroma (OM), Essentia Universal (EU), Zenchroma (ZC), and Charisma Diamond One (CDO)) (n = 28). The specimens were randomly divided into 4 subgroups (na = 7), and cylindrical cavities (4 × 1 mm) were prepared in the center of each specimen. The cavities were then restored with either the same material or one of the other single-shade RCs. Color matching was measured instrumentally using a spectrophotometer and visually using a 0-4 scoring scale. Data were recorded and statistically analyzed (P < .05). Results: When instrumental analysis results were evaluated, ΔE00 values above the clinically acceptable threshold were observed in all groups except the control groups. The highest ΔE00 value was seen in the OM-EU group (P < .05); OM showed the worst color matching. The best color matching was observed in CDO. When visual analysis results were examined, the highest visual scores were seen in the EU-OM and ZC-OM groups (P < .05), whereas CDO presented the lowest visual scores. Conclusion: Color-matching ability of single-shade RCs varies depending on the material composition. Single-shade RCs with higher translucency after polymerization and enhanced optical design may provide better color matching. Some color differences detected instrumentally may not always be visually perceptible under clinical conditions.
item.dc:creator: Seda Gömleksiz

item.title: MetaPointFinder: Detection of Antimicrobial Resistance-Conferring Point Mutations (ARMs) from Metagenomic Reads
item.description: This download contains the scripts, metadata and files to generate the data for figures and tables in the MetaPointFinder manuscript, first revision. Read the file "readme.txt" in the zip file on how to generate all data files. Warning. you need at least 10 tb of disk space and several week of computing time. Abstract Background: Many clinically important antimicrobial resistance (AMR) phenotypes such as fluoroquinolones and rifamycins are driven by antimicrobial resistance-conferring mutations (ARMs) in conserved chromosomal loci (e.g., gyrA, parC, rpoB). Resistome profiling by metagenomics sequencing is a promising AMR surveillance tool as it is organism-agnostic, but currently, existing metagenomic AMR surveillance pipelines are only able to identify acquired AMR genes but not point mutations associated with AMR. This is a serious gap in metagenomics-based AMR surveillance, as the true extent of AMR may be underestimated. Methods: We developed MetaPointFinder (v1), a read-based method that can process both long and short metagenomic reads. The tool identifies resistance determining region carrying reads using DIAMOND (translated protein) or KMA (nucleotide) mapping against complete reference gene sequences from AMRFinderPlus, followed by classifying resistant, wild-type and unknown variants by inspecting individual pairwise sequence alignments for known resistance conferring mutations in each read per antibiotic class. The tool outputs ARMs per read, per gene and per antibiotic class. Results: We benchmark our tool using simulated reads with different lengths and error rates from complete gene and complete reverse-translated protein references, and with mixtures of real reads from 42 isolates with known resistance mutations. We show that MetaPointFinder outperforms MuMaMe for detection of ARMs in these simulated read data, genomic mixtures and real metagenomics data. In proof-of-concept analyses, MetaPointFinder identified known AMR-associated mutations and quantified resistant/susceptible read counts and ratios from metagenomic samples. Conclusion: MetaPointFinder complements gene-centric resistome profiling by capturing chromosomal mutation-based AMR directly from metagenomes.

item.title: Open-Access-Publizieren
item.description: Die Präsentation "Open-Access-Publizieren. Ein kurzer Überblick über die verschiedenen Möglichkeiten und Fallstricke bei Open Access" bietet eine praxisorientierte Kurzeinführung in das wissenschaftliche Open-Access-Publizieren. Sie richtet sich insbesondere an Forschende und Promovierende oder dient zur Nachnutzung durch Bibliotheken oder andere wissenschaftsunterstützende Einrichtungen. Mit Blick auf den Nachnutzungsaspekt wurden institutionsspezifische Lösungen, Fonds, Lizenzen bzw. Verträge und weitere Unterstützungsangebote möglichst vermieden. Die Datei liegt als pdf, pptx und odp vor. Zu Beginn werden die grundlegenden Prinzipien von Open Access anhand der Berliner Erklärung zu Open Access erläutert, gefolgt von einem Exkurs zu Creative-Commons-Lizenzen. Ein Schwerpunkt liegt anschließend auf der Darstellung der unterschiedlichen Open-Access-Wege („Farben des Open Access“). Behandelt werden: Gold Open Access mit Erstveröffentlichung in Open-Access-Zeitschriften und möglicher Finanzierung über Article Processing Charges (APCs), Diamond Open Access als APC-kostenfreies Publikationsmodell für Autor:innen und Leser:innen, Hybrid Open Access einschließlich Transformationsverträgen, Subscribe to Open (S2O) als bibliotheksfinanziertes Transformationsmodell sowie Grüner Open Access über Repositorien und Zweitveröffentlichungen. Darüber hinaus werden praktische Hilfsmittel und Informationsquellen benannt, darunter das Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ), Think. Check. Submit., B!SON und oa.finder, der Diamond Discovery Hub, der Open Policy Finder, und weitere Dienste zur Recherche geeigneter Publikationsorte sowie zur Prüfung von Qualität, Kosten und Zweitveröffentlichungsrechten. Ein weiterer Schwerpunkt der Präsentation ist die Sensibilisierung für häufige Herausforderungen bzw. "Fallstricke" im Publikationsprozess, primär der Kostenaspekt, z. B. Unterscheidung Open-Access-Zeitschriften und Abonnementzeitschriften (und hierbei ggfs. Open-Access-Optionen), hierzu Nutzung der Elektronischen Zeitschriftenbibliothek (EZB) und dortiger Hinweise, z. B. auf das DOAJ oder zu DEAL-Verträgen, Recherche der Kosten zum Beispiel auf den Verlags- und Zeitschriftenseiten und wie man über das DOAJ schnell dorthin springt und der DEAL-Kosten, falls z. B. die eigene Einrichtung DEAL-Kostenweitergaben betreibt, und wie man, z. B. mit Journal Suggester Tools, geeignete Open-Access-Zeitschriften findet und Raubverleger meidet.

item.title: Recommendations for Revising the Open Access Classification System in OpenAlex
item.description: The open access (OA) color classification system used by Unpaywall (i.e., Gold, Green, Hybrid, Bronze, and closed) was introduced in 2018 and has since become widely used across the ecosystem, including by Scopus, Web of Science, Dimensions, and numerous funders and institutions worldwide. However, the scholarly communication landscape has changed significantly since these categories were defined and the limits of this system are proving problematic. In particular, the current system struggles with research outputs that are not journal publications, relies too heavily on journal-level policies rather than work-level attributes, conflates business models with access status, and is difficult to accurately operationalize in an environment where journals regularly change the OA status of publications en masse. The OpenAlex Colors Working Group was convened by the OpenAlex Community Advisory Board in January 2026 to evaluate these limitations and recommend a revised framework. After consultation and analysis, the Working Group recommends replacing the color-based system with a three-dimensional classification framework based on: Access — whether a work is freely accessible to read or is closed Location — whether a work is available at the publisher or on another platform (repository, preprint server, etc.) License — whether a work carries an open license, a closed/restrictive license, or has no clearly identifiable license This framework enables descriptive, work-level labels (such as Publisher Open, Platform Public, or Closed) that can accommodate articles, preprints, datasets, dissertations, books, and other scholarly output types, while avoiding the confusion that comes with the previous classification. Under the proposed system, venue-level classifications are left to the user, but can be derived from observed aggregate behavior, or left up to a separate classification system (see recommendations). Importantly, this proposal focuses on access, location, and license but does not address the business models of publishing venues (e.g., those funded with Article Processing Charges, Hybrid, diamond, subscribe-to-open, transformative agreements). One of the key complications of the existing color system is that it blends access status (a property of an article) with business models (a property of a venue)—distinct dimensions that cannot be easily reconciled. The Working Group recognizes that business model classification is an important and distinct need, and recommends that a separate initiative be established to develop a complementary venue business model taxonomy. This report is intended to capture the discussion of the Working Group. In recognition that any eventual implementation in OpenAlex will impact the broader community, the Working Group invites feedback from funders, institutions, publishers, librarians, database providers, and researchers ahead of making their final recommendations for consideration for implementation by OpenAlex.

item.title: Material type conditions the importance of model-paradigm choice in predicting surface roughness during vacuum-brazed diamond milling of marble — reproducibility package
item.description: Reproducibility package for the manuscript "Material type conditions the importance of model-paradigm choice in predicting surface roughness during vacuum-brazed diamond milling of marble", submitted to the Journal of Manufacturing Processes. The package contains the complete pipeline as eight Google Colab notebooks, the two experimental datasets (2,640 observations each for Afyon White and Afyon Grey marble, six process inputs and Ra), and every archived run artefact behind the published tables and figures. Sixteen machine-learning models across four modelling paradigms (classical, tabular foundation, deep and Bayesian, additional learners) are evaluated as 18 prediction series per material under a leakage-safe within-block chronological expanding-window cross-validation, with a pre-specified conjunctive ceiling test (Wilcoxon, Diebold-Mariano and permutation, Holm-corrected), a paired block bootstrap over the 16 parameter blocks and a studentised sign-flip test. Two audit files make the archive checkable without running anything: MANIFEST.csv gives the SHA-256, role and run state of every deposited file, and NUMBER_MAP.csv maps every table and figure in the manuscript and supplementary material to the artefact, notebook and cell that produced it, with a verification status. Notebooks 02 and 02b require a personal TabPFN token from Prior Labs; no token is included in this archive. All TabPFN results are deposited, so every reported value can be audited without one.

item.title: rosetta_stone_air_substrate.m
item.description: ## Abstract We present a scalar field-theoretic reinterpretation of the Bird Song Notation System (BSNS), an AI-driven transcription framework that achieves 93.7% accuracy in decoding avian vocalizations across 40 species. Rather than treating bird song as mere acoustic signal, we model it as **scalar field excitation** — coherent density modulations propagating through the atmospheric substrate. The BSNS elements (diamond, square, triangle, circle notes; microtonal arrows; syllable brackets; amplitude envelopes; repertoire superscripts) are mapped to scalar operations: coherence peaks, decoherence events, harmonic stacks, neutral carriers, inflection vectors, phrase-level closure, density modulation, and identity signatures. Cross-species resynthesis experiments — wherein a Chickadee song structure is rendered through Cardinal acoustic parameters while retaining recognizable semantic architecture — demonstrate that the **scalar topology of meaning is substrate-independent**. This mirrors the scalar cosmological principle that birth modality (imprint) varies while underlying field topology remains invariant. We propose a four-stage pipeline — **Capture → Transcribe → Scalar Decode → Movement Narrative** — that translates avian vocalization into field-theoretic language, establishing bird song as the first fully decoded scalar dialect of non-human intelligence. The implications extend from biomimetic quantum communication protocols to a unified theory of coherent expression across all resonant cavities. **Keywords:** scalar field theory, avian bioacoustics, Bird Song Notation System, coherence topology, cross-species translation, atmospheric substrate, density differential, harmonic language

item.title: The Work That Works
item.description: This volume gathers, in one continuous manuscript, the work from my 2025–2026 research programme that survives its own audit. The rule of admission is strict and applied uniformly: a result appears here only if it is a proved theorem, a validated empirical claim priced in bits under the frozen Coates PIT meter, or a methodological tool stated honestly, with its limitations in the text rather than left for referees to find. Everything that failed — refuted predictions, overfitted models, claims resting on free parameters or post-hoc selection — is excluded from the body and recorded by name in the Honest Accounting, with the reason for its exclusion. A record of what failed is part of what works. The manuscript is organised into five parts. Part I contains the algebraic foundations: the two boundary theorems singling out c = 2 among order-2 linear recurrences, the inverse-difference identity in SL(2,ℝ), the Klein four-group synthesis at λ = 2, and the companion-matrix, trace-map, and classification machinery built on them. Everything in this part stands on proof alone. Part II gives the complete pedagogical treatment of the two sequences that carry the boundary in concrete form — the Lichtenberg sequence and its Diamond Lattice geometry, and the Jacobsthal sequence developed from first principles through structure and application. Part III presents the measurement tools, FSRE and CANLE, in their corrected form: two distinct instruments sharing an Aitken acceleration step, described as what they are. Part IV contains the physics: the neutral-scalar spectral-escape theorem for ultracold Kerr–Newman–de Sitter families, organised by a multi-horizon synchronization obstruction, together with a trace-boundary mechanism for the 3:2 QPO resonance, retained with an explicit caveat about an unpriced selector. Part V closes the volume with mathematics as narrative, because explaining a thing plainly is the final test of understanding it. I am an independent researcher without institutional affiliation or funding. The standards applied to others' work throughout this programme are the same ones applied here to my own; several of my own results were withdrawn, refuted by my own pre-registered tests, or downgraded on audit, and the reader will find each of those outcomes stated rather than hidden. What remains is smaller than the corpus that produced it, and that is the point. This work is dedicated to the memory of Shirley. ---

item.title: Cross-Element Validation of the Bond-Energy–Phonon Framework: SiC and Phosphorus — Effective Domain, Failure Modes, and Diagnostic Value of a Zero-Parameter Model Beyond Carbon
item.description: Abstract: We previously established a zero-parameter framework for carbon that links gas-phase molecular bond dissociation energies (BDE) to solid-state vibrational frequencies via a single Badger-type ladder parameter A and one solid-state clamping factor η ≈ 1.50. The framework reproduces the diamond F₂g mode (1332 cm⁻¹), the graphite G peak (1580 cm⁻¹), and the carbon nanotube radial breathing mode (RBM) without any fitting to solid-state data. Here we push this framework unchanged into two systems beyond carbon—silicon carbide (SiC) and phosphorus (P)—using a triple-test protocol (molecular ladder + solid-state phonon + spectroscopic referee) to determine its effective domain. Main results: (1) For SiC, the gas-phase ladder degenerates into a two-point platform because the triple-bond/double-bond bond-length difference collapses to <0.01 Å, yielding a diatomic force constant deviation of −86%. However, η-calibrated reverse validation from the solid-state anchor reveals a systematic sp³→triple-bond deviation of −16% ± 2%, falling on the same universal band as carbon and BN. (2) Phosphorus delivers the most important positive result of this work—the P₄ breathing mode (A₁, 600.5 cm⁻¹) is a pure stretching mode, yielding a solid-state stiffness kᵣ = 164.5 N/m. The ratio to the molecular ladder value (109.9 N/m) gives η_P = 1.50, coinciding with carbon's η = 1.5125 to within 1%. This provides the first carbon-external evidence that "η ≈ 1.5 is a cross-element universal calibration constant." (3) Full-spectrum validation on black phosphorus shows that the zero-parameter model (M1) fails (χ² = 86566), but the two-parameter model (M2)—with ladder force constants pinned and only two angle parameters fitted—hits all three Raman fingerprint peaks at χ² = 9133 with errors of +0.6%, +4.6%, and −0.7%; 7 of 8 experimental modes fall within ±12%. The sole outlier, the infrared mode B₂ᵤ (+23.6%), together with the overestimated silent mode Aᵤ, localizes the pathology in the z (out-of-plane) sector of the Davydov pair. (4) We demonstrate a negative example: a three-parameter fit to three peaks achieves "perfect" agreement (±0.4%) but is a false positive—the remaining six optical modes are pushed to 607–886 cm⁻¹ (nature ≤ 470 cm⁻¹), and the fitted bond-strength ratio kᵣ₂/kᵣ₁ = 1.8 contradicts the 1/R³ prediction. These results together yield four methodological laws that delimit the model's applicability boundary: the ladder survival condition is "homolytic covalent + bond-order variation"; forward error is a π-bond strength meter; the reverse sp³→triple-bond deviation is universally −16% ± 2% across systems; and η ≈ 1.5 is a candidate universal constant. All code and data are released with the manuscript. ORCID: 0009-0007-1999-0293 Email: 1352533302@qq.com phone:+86 18278275520(china)

item.title: Dutch Marquise: Open Geometry Specification
item.description: An open, versioned, machine-readable specification for the Dutch Marquise diamond cut and its companion the French Marquise: outline, faceting pattern, certificate nomenclature, and how to read the length-to-width ratio from a grading report, with every claim sourced. A Dutch Marquise is an elongated hexagonal cut diamond, cut for brilliance; grading laboratories describe the geometry as a hexagonal modified brilliant (IGI report, 2026). The term is a trade name, not an officially recognized gemological shape. Published by Stienhardt, New York, which controls this cut through a specialized factory relationship and hand-sets and finishes the stones in New York City, and which does not claim to have invented, named, or standardized the cut. Version 1.0.1 corrects the certificate term, removes an unsupported ratio range in favor of measured values, resolves the faceting description, and adds a PDF edition.

item.title: Comparative analysis of lattice-based scaffold architectures: geometrical, mechanical, and manufacturing considerations for tissue engineering applications
item.description: This study explores how scaffold geometry affects structural and mechanical performance in tissue engineering. Lattice-based designs ̶ including cross, diamond, honeycomb, octet, grid, vintiles, and X-type ̶ were modeled within a standardized 1728 mm3 volume. High-porosity structures (X, diamond) promoted cell adhesion and nutrient transport, while honeycomb architectures exhibited low porosity and high relative density, enhancing mechanical stability. Mechanical performance was evaluated via mesh analysis and finite element simulations, and manufacturing feasibility was assessed using FDM and SLA, with SLA showing superior fidelity for complex microstructures. Scaffold behavior is governed by the interplay of geometry, material properties, and fabrication constraints.

item.title: Beyond Porterian Positioning: A Resource-Based View of Tourism Destination Competitiveness in China
item.description: HRMARS - Michael Porter’s competitive positioning view (CPV) and Diamond Model have long shaped urban tourism competitiveness research in China. However, applying market-centric logic to China’s state-driven development model, which relies heavily on political promotion targets and centralized capital allocation, creates major governance problems, including destination homogenization, growing fiscal burdens, and declining community well-being. To address this institutional mismatch, this conceptual paper examines why Porterian logic falls short in Chinese urban tourism and proposes a shift toward Jay Barney’s resource-based view (RBV). Using the valuable, rare, inimitable, and non-substitutable (VRIN) criteria, the study redefines destination competitiveness around four internal capabilities: authentic core assets, memorable tourism experiences, holistic sustainability, and resident well-being. The proposed framework reorients destination strategy away from capital-intensive, superficial expansion and toward the cultivation of internal, non-replicable governance capabilities. It therefore offers a theoretically grounded perspective for tourism researchers and practical guidance for destination management organizations seeking sustainable competitive advantage in emerging Asian economies.

item.title: Heterogeneously Integrated Diamond-on-Lithium Niobate Quantum Photonic Platform
item.description: Diamond photonics has enabled efficient interfaces for quantum memories and is predicted to be a critical component of quantum networks. However, scalable network architectures require spatial, temporal, and spectral control of photons, which relies on nonlinear and electro-optic functionalities that diamond alone cannot provide. Here, we demonstrate heterogeneous integration of a thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) platform, which has strong chi-2 nonlinearity and electro-optic effects, with thin diamond films. We demonstrate high-Q diamond photonic crystal cavities (Q factors exceeding 5x10^4 at 735 nm) that are lithographically aligned with TFLN photonic backbone and critically coupled to it. This allows us to realize low-loss diamond-TFLN "escalators" (loss ~1 dB/coupler) that support efficient light transfer between them. At cryogenic temperatures (5K), we can collect photons emitted from silicon vacancies (SiVs) embedded within the diamond structure via the TFLN photonic circuit. This approach establishes a scalable route toward integrated photonic circuits for practical quantum networking and other technologies.

item.title: Video-Based Tutorials and the Academic Performance of Grade 10 Students in TLE Cookery at Sto. Domingo National High School
item.description: This study examined the utilization of video-based tutorials and its relationship with the academic performance of Grade 10 students enrolled in TLE Cookery at Sto. Domingo National High School during School Year 2025–2026. A quantitative descriptive-correlational design was employed with 102 purposively selected learners from Grade 10 Diamond, Sapphire, and Pearl. Data were gathered through a researcher-made questionnaire and the respondents’ third-quarter Cookery grades and analyzed using frequency, percentage, weighted mean, independent-samples t-test, one-way analysis of variance, and Pearson product-moment correlation. Most respondents were 15–16 years old, female, had previous cookery experience, had limited technology access, and viewed video tutorials occasionally. Utilization was high to very high across food preparation skills, proper use of tools and equipment, and food presentation, while academic performance was generally high, with 53.92% rated Outstanding and 28.43% Very Satisfactory. Selected demographic variables were associated with differences in tutorial utilization, particularly age for food presentation, viewing frequency for food preparation skills, and application of content across all three utilization domains. Academic performance differed significantly according to previous cookery experience or training but not according to the other examined demographic factors. Video-tutorial utilization showed statistically significant positive relationships with academic performance in food preparation skills (r = .199, p = .045), proper use of tools and equipment (r = .261, p = .008), and food presentation (r = .228, p = .021). The study supports the use of carefully designed video tutorials as supplementary learning resources and proposes an action plan integrating accessible video materials, guided practice, safety routines, and performance-based activities in TLE Cookery.

item.title: Determinasi Perilaku Kecurangan Akademik Mahasiswa di Era Artificial Intelligence: Peran Penggunaan AI Generatif, Self-Efficacy, dan Moral
item.description: The development of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed learning processes in higher education while raising concerns about the increasing prevalence of academic dishonesty among university students. This study aims to examine the effects of generative AI use, self-efficacy, and morality on academic dishonesty among students at Universitas Nusa Cendana. A quantitative approach with a cross-sectional survey design was employed. The study involved 120 social science students who used generative AI in their academic activities and were selected using purposive sampling. Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using multiple linear regression, including t-tests, F-tests, and the coefficient of determination. The results indicate that generative AI use has a positive but insignificant effect on academic dishonesty, while self-efficacy has a negative but insignificant effect. In contrast, morality has a positive and significant effect on academic dishonesty. Simultaneously, the three variables have a significant effect on students' academic dishonesty. The findings indicate that academic dishonesty is shaped by the interaction of technological, psychological, and moral factors, with morality emerging as the primary determinant of students' tendency to engage in academic dishonesty. Furthermore, this study extends the application of the Fraud Diamond Theory by demonstrating that a sound understanding of moral values does not necessarily translate into consistent ethical behavior and, therefore, may not always prevent academic dishonesty.

item.title: A New Record of Pseudopyrenula (Lichenized Ascomycota) From India
item.description: ABSTRACT The present study reports Pseudopyrenula endoxanthoides Vain. in India for the first time. The species is characterized by a hamathecium densely inspersed with yellow oil droplets, K+ pale pink to purplish, and 3‐septate ascospores with diamond‐shaped lumina. A detailed description and illustrations are provided to facilitate its identification.

item.title: DPASV detection of metribuzin using the cathodic pretreated boron-doped diamond electrode
item.description: Abstract The widespread use of the triazinone herbicide metribuzin (MTZ) demands reliable, rapid, and cost-effective analytical methods for environmental monitoring. In this work, we report, for the first time, the electroanalytical determination of MTZ based on its anodic behavior at a boron-doped diamond (BDD) electrode. The method exploits a differential pulse anodic stripping voltammetry (DPASV) approach, in which MTZ undergoes a preconcentration step via electrochemical reduction, followed by oxidation of the generated intermediate. The influence of surface pretreatment was systematically evaluated, demonstrating that cathodically pretreated BDD (BDD-CTP) significantly enhances electron-transfer kinetics and analytical sensitivity due to hydrogen-terminated surfaces characteristics. The electrochemical oxidation process was found to be irreversible, diffusion-controlled, and governed by a two-electron/two-proton mechanism, with a heterogeneous rate constant of 1.5 s ‒1 . Under optimized conditions ( E ac = ‒0.60 V, t ac = 60 s, pH 2.0), the method exhibited a linear response in the concentration range of 1.31 – 12.4 µmol L ‒1 ( R 2 = 0.9994), with a limit of detection ( LOD ) of 0.17 µmol L ‒1 . The sensor demonstrated excellent repeatability (RSD ≤ 2.7%) and good selectivity in the presence of common inorganic interferents. The applicability of the method was successfully demonstrated in environmental water samples (tap and river water), yielding satisfactory recoveries (100–106%) Compared to conventional reductive approaches, the proposed anodic strategy provides complementary mechanistic insight while avoiding limitations associated with electrode fouling and narrow potential windows. These findings highlight the potential of BDD electrodes as robust and versatile platforms for herbicide MTZ in environmental matrices. item.title: Carbon nanostructures in a carbon-rich mineral: evidence for formation under extreme conditions
item.description:
We report a carbon-rich mineral from San Luis Potosí, México, characterized by an unusual morphology and a complex carbonaceous composition. Spectroscopic and electron microscopy characterization reveals diverse carbon nanostructures within the mineral, including graphene-like lamellae, nanotube-like structures, carbon nano-onions, and nanodiamond-like domains. The coexistence of sp2- and sp3-bonded carbon phases and their structural heterogeneity are consistent with formation or transformation under extreme, nonequilibrium conditions rather than conventional crustal processes. The occurrence of these carbon nanostructures is associated with the presence of iron (Fe) particles in the mineral, suggesting Fe-mediated catalytic processes that may operate via vapor–solid–solid (VSS)-type mechanisms at elevated temperatures. Beyond their formation pathways, the identification and characterization of natural sources of carbon nanostructures carry important environmental implications. Elucidating the mechanisms governing their natural genesis, independent of synthetic routes, is therefore essential for evaluating their potential abundance, mobility, and impact in environmental systems. These findings provide insight into carbon organization and transformation pathways within a geological framework, bridging concepts from materials science, nanoscience, mineralogy, and geology.

item.title: Effects of crystal anisotropy on nanoindentation deformation in single-crystal 4H-SiC
item.description: : Single-crystal 4H-SiC is widely used in semiconductor devices and precision optical systems owing to its outstanding properties. However, its high hardness, brittleness, and strong covalent bonding pose challenges for low-damage machining. In this study, nanoindentation tests were carried out on C, M and A planes using a Berkovich diamond indenter. Load-displacement responses, hardness, apparent indentation modulus and indentation morphologies were analyzed under different loads. A stress field model was then used to resolve the indentation stress onto representative slip systems. Schmid factors for the three Berkovich contact faces were also calculated. The results show that the indentation response exhibits significant crystal orientation dependence. At room temperature, C plane exhibits the largest indentation depth and the greatest decrease in apparent indentation modulus as the load increases from 50 to 400 mN, whereas M and A planes show relatively higher indentation resistance. Cracks become more pronounced at higher loads, and their propagation paths depend on the crystallographic orientation. Under the present indentation geometry and loading conditions, the stress distribution and Schmid factor analyses indicate that basal slip dominates plastic deformation on C plane, whereas prismatic slip is more readily activated on M and A planes. These results clarify the coupling among indentation response, stress distribution and slip-system activity, and provide a theoretical basis for understanding crystallographic-orientation effects during the ultra-precision and low-damage machining of single-crystal 4H-SiC.

item.title: Beyond certifications: Questioning the design and economic effects of the canadian ethical diamond policy
item.description: This paper investigates the design, signaling effectiveness, and economic impacts of the Government of the Northwest Territories’ ethical diamond certification. Employing a sequential exploratory mixed-methods approach, the study combines a longitudinal institutional analysis with a macro-panel econometric evaluation of value-chain upgrading across key diamond-producing and processing countries. Qualitative evidence shows that compliance burdens, rigid chain-of-custody protocols, and subsequent policy relaxations undermined both the industrial feasibility and the credibility of the territorial signal. Quantitative findings indicate that the certification is linked to a significant negative effect on downstream value retention. By contextualizing the Canadian case within broader debates on resource-based industrialization, global value-chain governance, and credence-goods signaling, the paper reveals how ethical certifications can inadvertently reinforce structural constraints instead of promoting upgrading. These results underscore the need for certification architectures that balance credibility with operational feasibility in globally fragmented and cost-sensitive industries.

item.title: Temporal Decoupling Enables Allylic C–H Hydroxylation with Effectively Suppressed Overoxidation by Pulsed Electrolysis
item.description: The selective oxidation of allylic C-H bonds to alcohols without overoxidation to carbonyl compounds remains a long-standing challenge due to the high reactivity of hydroxylated intermediates under anodic conditions. Herein, we report a programmable pulsed electrolysis strategy that effectively suppresses overoxidation to achieve allylic hydroxylation by temporally decoupling oxidative activation from product desorption. Using N-hydroxyphthalimide (NHPI) as a hydrogen-atom-transfer mediator and water-derived reactive oxygen species (ROS) as the oxidant, pulsed operation on a boron-doped diamond (BDD) anode enables kinetic control over intermediate residence at the electrode interface. As a result, α,β-unsaturated alcohols are selectively obtained under transition-metal-free conditions. This work highlights temporal waveform control as an effective strategy for directing selectivity in complex anodic oxidation pathways.

item.title: Generation of Small Droplets for Molten Salt Reactor Fluoride Fuel Salt Sampling
item.description: The analysis of molten salt samples benefits significantly from using small, uniform samples. One such analysis technique that requires these samples is the diamond-based microfluidic alpha spectrometer (DiMAS), which relies on depositing very small quantities of molten fluoride salts on its surface to enable high-resolution alpha spectrometry. To facilitate this, a pneumatic droplet generator for molten fluoride salt has been developed. The system employs a fast-acting solenoid to pulse argon gas through a heated vessel, allowing it to dispense droplets through a diamond orifice. A parameter study was performed to identify the optimal settings for producing small, consistent droplets. The results indicate that the system can reliably produce salt droplets around 1 mm in diameter. Further analysis of the findings was undertaken to explore design changes and operating conditions that could further improve performance for future implementation with DiMAS and other analysis techniques.

item.title: White ants and mining: reading degrowth in South Africa
item.description: South Africa has an abandoned mines problem. These mines pose serious risks to lives and the environment and raise questions of what degrowth may look like in parts of the Global South that are confronting legacies of racial and migrant labour exploitation while also facing post-extractivist futures. Any attempt at a just transition to degrowth in South Africa will not only have to grapple with the economy’s continued dependence on the mining sector, but also address the deep injustices caused by this sector and the informal/illegal economy of precarious labourers that shadows it. Given the centrality of mines, their undergrounds, and their racialised labour systems to the modern South African nation and its literary cultures, this article turns to the nation’s literature to investigate the relationship between social and environmental justice and degrowth. Taking a transhistorical approach, the article explores the way artisanal, informal, illegal, and migrant labour marks the various forms and genres of South African mining literature, from the late nineteenth-century diamond rush compound novels to the speculative fiction of a ‘Rainbow Nation’ encountering economic precarity and environmental collapse in the twenty-first century.

item.title: Micromagnetic Tomography: Insights from a single Hawaiian basalt
item.description: Paleomagnetism is the art of retrieving the direction and intensity of the Earth Magnetic Field from rock samples of varying ages and locations. This data can be used for a wide variety of Earth Scientific purposes, from reconstructing plate tectonics to modeling the geodynamo. Classic paleomagnetic experiments generally consist of replacing the natural remanent magnetization (NRM) of a bulk (1 inch3) sample with a lab-induced remanent magnetization. These experiments sometimes give puzzling, inconsistent, or no results at all, which can be frustrating when samples are physically scarce, or unique in age or location. Misbehavior of bulk samples is often attributed to large magnetic grainsizes, or rocks with complicated geological histories. Bulk protocols do not give insight why certain bulk samples misbehave. Micromagnetic Tomography (MMT) is a newly developed technique to retrieve the magnetic signal from individual magnetic grains using a Quantum Diamond Microscope (QDM). In bulk measurements, grains with good recording properties can be obscured by grains with bad recording properties. Retrieving paleomagnetic data from individual magnetic grains, or from sets of magnetic grains, is the next step in retrieving paleomagnetic data from samples that do not give results in bulk protocols. Furthermore, examining individual magnetic grains can give insight why a sample misbehaved in bulk experiments. Also, the samples required for MMT are much smaller, so more experiments can be done on less sample material, which is paramount if material is scarce. Micromagnetic tomography is a developing field of research. In this thesis I advance the method by applying it to a Hawaiian basaltic sample that has previously been studied both chemically, mineralogically and paleomagnetically. The sample is a 3 mm wide microcore that was drilled out of a 30 µm thin section. This thesis can be used as a reference and inspiration for designing MMT experiments for a research question. It contains an extensive explanation of the physics that lead to MMT results to advance the understanding of choices in the measurement process, which influence data quality, data size and speed of measurement. It also contains details of all the methods applied in this thesis, to be able to repeat the experiments in the future in order to compare and contrast. Lastly I apply a classical paleomagnetic experiment to this MMT sample and study how the results at grain level compare to bulk measurements. Over the course of 5 years I have done close to 100 MMT scans of this single 3 mm microcore. Most of those results did not make it into this thesis. It is amazing how much insight we have gained from this single tiny sample.

item.title: Load Reduction and Fragmentation Behavior of Ultrasonic-Assisted Pick Cutting: A Calibrated EDEM–Experimental Study
item.description: Cantilever roadheaders are widely used in medium-soft rock tunneling. However, conventional pick cutters suffer from high rock-breaking load, excessive energy consumption, and severe abrasion, which restrict the performance of roadheader vehicle-end intelligent control systems. Existing ultrasonic rock-breaking studies mainly focus on drilling and polycrystalline diamond compact (PDC) cutters, while calibrated EDEM simulation and experimental studies of synchronous ultrasonic-vibration-assisted pick cutter cutting remain limited. This study investigates the rock-breaking behavior of synchronous ultrasonic vibration coupled with pick cutter cutting using 21 MPa artificial rock-like specimens. A calibrated EDEM simulation model was developed based on the Hertz–Mindlin with Bonding contact model and validated by uniaxial compression and Brazilian splitting tests. Meta-particle technology was applied to analyze fragmentation characteristics. The effects of ultrasonic frequency, cutting angle, and cone angle on rock-breaking load, debris production, and specific energy consumption were investigated through simulations and experiments. An ultrasonic-assisted cutting test system equipped with force sensors was established for validation. Results show that 30 kHz ultrasonic vibration effectively reduces rock-breaking load under the investigated operating conditions. A relatively favorable parameter combination obtained from the numerical simulations consists of an ultrasonic frequency of 30 kHz, a cutting angle of 40°, and a cone angle of 60°. Compared with conventional cutting, the optimized scheme reduces average cutting load by 74.69%, increases debris yield by 54.71%, and decreases mass-specific mechanical cutting energy consumption by 83.63%. This study provides quantitative data support for roadheader vehicle-end intelligent control systems.

item.title: Bayesian optimization and topographic exploration of drag-reducing dimples for aerodynamic surfaces
item.description: Dimples offer a promising route to reducing drag on aerodynamic surfaces. However, whether such shallow concavities yield a net benefit depends sensitively on their topography, which demands systematic mapping and exploration of their comprehensive design space. In this study, dimple design is examined as a mixed-variable optimization over four design variables: dimple type, depth, in-plane scale, and streamwise stretch. The design space is explored using MixMOBO, a Bayesian optimizer, coupled with immersed-boundary large eddy simulations of channel flows at a constant flow rate corresponding to a flat channel at a friction Reynolds number of 180. The optimal solution, a relatively deep, fully packed, streamwise-elongated diamond dimple, attains a 13.2% drag reduction, notably above previously reported values. A Gaussian process metamodel sensitivity analysis identifies dimple topology as the dominant factor, with coverage and elongation acting mainly through interactions, and depth itself carrying no universal sign. A near-wall flow analysis links the leading designs to fully attached, groove-like flow, whereas poorer designs tend to produce local flow separation that incurs adverse form drag. From these findings, key design insights for drag-reducing dimples are provided.

item.title: Synthesis of Entropy-Locked Bio-Organic Hybrid Macro-Cables via Magnetohydrodynamic Plasma Forging and Cyclic Abyss-Quenching OPEN Design Concept
item.description: This technical report is an open design concept that provides a comprehensive overview of the design framework, manufacturing workflow, and physical characteristics of the Entropy-Locked Hybrid Macro-Cable. Developed for the CERN Conceptual Design Review (CDR) phase, the paper outlines a revolutionary "space-to-trench" manufacturing loop that allows engineers to combine the extreme tensile strength of diamond into the highly flexible matrix of silicon rubber. The report details how a 10-mile orbital plasma forge, multi-spectrum acoustic alignment, and extreme high-pressure ocean tempering remove all atomic irregularities. This process brings the material to its absolute lowest energy state—the Entropy Point of Perfection. Additionally, it breaks down the cable's smart defense layers, featuring a drag-reducing dimpled ceramic skin and a self-healing liquid gallium "nervous system." The document serves as a foundational blueprint for planetary-scale engineering projects, including space elevators, deep-sea power grids, and indestructible hull designs. item.title: ARTICLE I: THE AVICENNA PROTOCOL DECRYPTING THE VIRAL CONNECTOME, SOCIOVIROLOGY, AND THE BILLION-ALPHABET CRYPTOGRAPHY
item.description: Classical epidemiology traditionally models viral pathogenesis as a stochastic, mechanical process driven by inert, solitary particles relying purely on mathematical probability to replicate. This manuscript introduces a comprehensive epistemological rupture from this orthodox paradigm, hypothesizing that pathogenic infections operate instead as highly coordinated, decentralized cyber-biological deployments. By integrating principles from sociovirology, network neuroscience, proteomics, and biosemiotics, this framework re-evaluates the viral swarm as an advanced, integrated macro-intelligence. We propose that viruses actively hijack host cellular hardware—modulating ion channels, mitochondrial thermodynamics, and protein conformations—to construct active bio-quantum transmitters. When scaled across a biological host, these interconnected cellular nodes form a "Viral Connectome" arranged in a topological Diamond Lattice, capable of distributed memory, environmental adaptation, and systemic computation. Furthermore, this framework posits that pathogenic swarms communicate via a "Billion-Alphabet Cryptography," an ancient, multidimensional biochemical syntax optimized over billions of years of planetary evolution. The teleological aim of this theoretical proposition is absolute protective foresight: by shifting the diagnostic focus from the physical eradication of isolated biological particles to the decryption of a systemic communication network, medical science can mathematically jam pathogenic signaling and seamlessly command the infection to deactivate from within.

item.title: The Author Who Stood Outside the Frame: A Reflection on Inherited Ground, Outsider Vision, and the Geometry of Becoming
item.description: This piece is me looking back at the ground I started on and the person who got built from it. I didn’t come into this world choosing my foundation — it was already there, shaped by the existence that came before me. The project didn’t change who I am; it just showed me the corners I was already built to walk around. I stayed the same North Wales human being I’ve always been, just with a clearer view of the shapes I’ve been navigating in quiet. I talk about climbing trees I was never meant to climb, about being pushed out of learning and finding my way back in solitude, about coal under pressure and diamonds buried too long. I write about how original thought only exists at birth, and everything after that is entropy from the labels we inherit. I write about giving people the benefit of the doubt because I know how much of my own path wasn’t chosen — just absorbed. Gödel shows up, because he always does when you’re talking about the inside trying to map itself. I realised the vantage point I was forced into — the outside angle — was exactly where I needed to stand to see what the inside couldn’t. And from that angle, I don’t see lost souls; I see people walking different flavours of the same geometry I had to walk. item.description: This dataset contains the data for the paper entitled "Imaging the Meissner effect in lanthanum hydride using diamond quantum sensors" (to be published in PNAS). All data were collected using a home-built optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) system at the Institute of Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences (IOP, CAS). The experiments were conducted from 2025-05-27 to 2026-04-20. The experimental procedure and data analysis are described in the article and supplementary materials. The data are organized as they are presented in the article, e.g. the file “Fig. 1B.txt” contains the data of Fig. 1B of the article. These files can be opened with a text editor. item.title: Coherent control of solid-state defect spins via patterned boron-doped diamond circuit
item.description: We demonstrate the coherent control of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) spins using an electronic circuit integrated within diamond: a patterned, conductive boron-doped diamond (BDD) microwave waveguide. First, we validated the high-frequency performance of the circuit by characterizing its impedance up to the microwave range, confirming its capability for efficient microwave transmission. Then, using this diamond-compatible microwave circuit platform, BDD--NV hybrid system, we perform optically detected magnetic resonance and observe noticeable Rabi oscillations driven by the heavily-doped BDD circuit. Importantly, we verify that the BDD antenna has a minimal detrimental impact on the NV spins; microwave-induced heating is negligible under both pulsed and continuous driving, and the spin relaxation time (T1) remains unperturbed. These results indicate the potential of BDD circuits for on-chip microwave delivery in NV-based quantum devices.

item.title: FuncSeek: Multi-PLM contrastive learning for protein functional similarity search
item.description: Abstract Below 30% pairwise sequence identity, alignment-based methods struggle to reliably distinguish true homologs from chance, and enzyme function prediction degrades accordingly: on proteins in this regime, even advanced methods (CLEAN) achieves only 55.1% accuracy at full EC specificity on the CARE benchmark. To this end Protein Language Models (PLMs) have gained favor as alternatives. However, PLMs often encode only a subset of the biology, whereas the understanding of enzyme function requires among other things a combination of sequence, structure and functional-context simultaneously. In this work, we describe FuncSeek, a contrastive learning model which utilizes three diverse, complementary PLMs: ESM2 (to model evolutionary co-variation), ProstT5 (for bilingual sequence and structure embeddings), and ProteinBERT (for functional semantic similarities). Using SwissProt data, these 2816-D embeddings are labelled with Enzyme Commission numbers (EC) and are trained through a supervised contrastive head into a 256-D space. FuncSeek attains 64.6% nearest-neighbour EC4 accuracy on the CARE out-of-distribution benchmark set ( ood30 ; proteins below 30% identity to training set), outperforming CLEAN (55.1%) and Diamond BLASTp (51.4%), and obtains 93.7% nearest-neighbour EC4 accuracy on the promiscuous, multi-functional enzymes benchmark (CLEAN, 69.4%). We also show that the learned representations transfer without retraining to the TrEMBL database, achieving 97.3% nearest-neighbour EC4 accuracy on an 8,031 BRENDA-validated enzyme set, never seen during training. Because only projected embeddings are stored in the target index, and function is inferred from an annotated reference set, we propose this paradigm for rapidly searching extremely large metagenomic databases, bypassing costly sequence alignment and annotation pipelines. Author Summary Enzymes are the molecular machines that carry out the chemistry of life, and knowing which reaction an enzyme performs is essential for medicine, biotechnology, and understanding how organisms work. Yet new protein sequences are being discovered far faster than we can study them in the laboratory, and the most common computational shortcut, comparing a new sequence to well-studied ones, breaks down when the sequences are only distantly related. We asked whether recent artificial intelligence models that learn the “language” of proteins could close this gap. Rather than rely on a single model, we combined three that each capture a different aspect of protein biology: evolutionary patterns, three-dimensional shape, and functional context. We then trained a system, which we call FuncSeek, to arrange enzymes so that those performing the same reaction sit close together. FuncSeek predicted enzyme function more accurately than the leading existing tools, especially for distantly related and multi-functional enzymes, and this accuracy carried over to proteins it had never seen. Because it represents each protein as a compact numerical fingerprint, it can search enormous, unexplored collections of sequences quickly.

item.title: Expanding the Application of Boron-Doped Modified Diamond Electrodes in the Treatment of Recalcitrant Organic Pollutants
item.description: Wastewater from textile, leather, pharmaceutical, and chemical industries contains high concentrations of recalcitrant organic pollutants, which are difficult to mineralize completely using conventional biological or chemical processes and pose persistent ecological risks. Boron-doped diamond (BDD) electrodes, with a wide electrochemical potential window, high oxygen evolution overpotential, strong hydroxyl radical generation ability, and excellent chemical stability, provide an effective electric-field-driven route for advanced oxidation treatment. This paper systematically reviews the preparation processes, structural optimization, and electrochemical performance of BDD electrodes, and analyzes the roles of boron doping, substrate selection, surface termination, and functional modification in regulating conductivity, interfacial activity, and long-term stability. The degradation mechanism of recalcitrant organics is discussed from the perspectives of quasi-free hydroxyl radical oxidation, direct electron transfer, adsorption-controlled interfacial reactions, and mineralization pathways. Potential applications in textile dyeing wastewater, pharmaceutical wastewater, emerging pollutant degradation, and wastewater reuse are further examined. In addition, the synergistic coupling of BDD electrochemical oxidation with biological treatment, membrane separation, photocatalysis, and ultrasonic enhancement is evaluated for improving mass transfer, energy efficiency, and process stability. The analysis shows that BDD electrodes have strong engineering potential for high-COD and chromatic industrial wastewater treatment, while future scale-up requires lower-cost electrode fabrication, optimized flow-field design, and intelligent control of electrochemical parameters.

item.title: Effect of solution conductivity on the anodic oxidation of diuron in secondary effluent
item.description: Supporting electrolytes are commonly added in matrices in anodic oxidation (AO) electrolyses to increase the solution conductivity and reduce energy consumption, albeit this approach increases chemical demand and may not reflect real wastewater conditions. The present study investigated the feasibility and applicability of AO in the degradation of diuron, a model micropollutant, using a boron-doped diamond (BDD) anode under conductivity conditions representative of secondary effluents. The influence of current density, pH, diuron concentration, and solution conductivity was systematically evaluated. Reactive species were identified through scavenger experiments and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) analyses, and hydroxyl radicals were confirmed as the primary oxidizing species responsible for diuron degradation. Among the inorganic species investigated, chloride was found to enhance diuron degradation via the formation of reactive chlorine species, bicarbonate inhibited oxidation through radical scavenging, and nitrate and ammonium caused very minor effects. Complete diuron removal was achieved in a simulated secondary effluent with a solution conductivity of 1750 μS cm −1 absent adjustment. The influence of natural organic matter in diuron mineralization was thoroughly evaluated using humic acid, and dissolved organic carbon measurements indicated that the background organic matrix was only partially mineralized. In addition, 11 transformation products were identified and used to propose pathways for diuron degradation. ECOSAR predictions indicated that most transformation products exhibited lower predicted aquatic toxicity than the parent compound. Overall, the results demonstrate that AO is effective for diuron degradation in simulated secondary effluent under low-conductivity conditions without supplemental supporting electrolyte. These findings provide mechanistic insights and establish a basis for future validation using real secondary effluents.

item.title: Material-extrusion additive manufacturing of biodegradable, mechanics-driven reinforcement topologies on cellulose and fungal mycelium membranes
item.description: Abstract This study explores the material effects of mechanics-driven reinforcement topologies on fully compostable membranes made from fungal mycelium or recycled cellulose tissue using material extrusion. Biodegradable poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyhexanoate) (PHBH) was additively printed as defined diamond and re-entrant lattice structures onto compliant substrates. The systematic Make–Break–Simulate approach combines fabrication, tensile testing, simplified mechanical modelling and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA). Additive reinforcement significantly increased ultimate tensile strength and Young’s modulus in all configurations. Cellulose-based hybrids showed higher stiffness and ultimate tensile load than mycelium systems, indicating more efficient stress transfer due to substrate homogeneity. Diamond lattices exhibited stretching-dominated behavior with axial load amplification, whereas re-entrant lattices produced geometry-induced stiffening and progressive fracture. The re-entrant topology consistently achieved the highest stiffness values and enabled distributed fracture behaviour through geometric stress redistribution. The screening-level LCA further showed that the mechanical gains of re-entrant reinforcement exceeded the corresponding increase in global warming potential (GWP). The findings demonstrate that mechanical properties of bio-based membranes can be tuned through geometric pattern design without altering the biological substrate. Topology-controlled additive reinforcement thus offers a scalable strategy to enhance structural reliability while preserving full compostability and material circularity. The presented approach further highlights the potential of geometry-controlled reinforcement as a design strategy for lightweight biodesign and membrane-based applications.

item.title: Dimension-Tunable Medium-to-High-Entropy All-Inorganic Perovskites for Methanol Oxidation and Oxygen Evolution Reactions
item.description: Abstract Halide and organic linker-free, all-inorganic cubic (ABO3) and Ruddlesden–Popper perovskites (RPPs) with the general formula An+1BnO3n+1 are less explored in the field of alcohol fuel cells. Subsequently, the impact of variation in the synthesis approach leading to phase transformation with the change of nanoarchitecture is also not known, especially for compositional high-entropy-based Ruddlesden–Popper perovskites (HERPPs). At the same time, the literature is very silent with regard to the application of 2D and 3D phases of such perovskites for the methanol oxidation reaction (MOR) in an alkaline medium and the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). The present manuscript thus brings into light the influence of the transformation of RP perovskites from 2D layered to 3D cubic perovskite (ABO3) phases, along with the change of compositional entropy and how structural dimensionality governs the balance between active site density and intrinsic activity of the perovskites in electrocatalytic oxidation of methanol. The structural information on these synthesized materials was analyzed through synchrotron XRD, and other parameters were evaluated through various other analytical tools. During the MOR study, at a scan rate of 100 mV s–1, the 2D RPPs exhibited an onset potential of 1.59 V vs RHE with a maximum current density of 79.06 mA cm–2 and an overpotential of 310 mV. In contrast, at the same scan rate, the 3D cubic perovskite phase displayed a maximum current density of 168.79 mA cm–2 at a lower onset potential of 1.32 V vs RHE and an overpotential of 110 mV. OER showed a similar trend with improved kinetics. The Tafel slope also showed a decrease in value from 197 to 22 mV dec–1 in MOR and from 361 to 217 mV dec–1 in OER. The compositional high-entropy-based 3D cubic perovskite (ABO3) phase having minor impurity of the “n” = 4 RP phase with a diamond-like morphology showed the highest MOR and OER activity compared to medium-entropy-based RPPs with “n” = 1, 2 and “n” = 1, 3. The MOR activity of the materials was found to be the same until 18 h under alkaline conditions. Further, from the theoretical analysis, it was evident that the compositional high-entropy-based perovskites showed metallic and semimetallic nature on phase transformation.

item.title: Acoustic Control of Spin States in Diamond Nitrogen-Vacancy Centres
item.description: Abstract We report acoustic control of spin resonance in nitrogen-vacancy (NV–) centers in diamond using low-frequency free-space sound waves. Acoustic excitation redistributes spin populations between the |+1⟩ and |−1⟩ states, producing an asymmetric, tunable double-dip ODMR spectrum without shifting resonance frequencies. This contrasts with conventional magnetic-field-induced splitting and reveals a previously unobserved mechanism for spin manipulation via strain-mediated acoustic coupling. Analytical modeling captures the essential features of the amplitude flipping and elucidates the underlying spin-strain interaction. Our findings establish a new degree of freedom for selective multimodal quantum sensing and open avenues for hybrid spin-mechanical quantum devices.

item.title: Toward Precision in Biomarker Analysis: A Novel Malondialdehyde Detection Method Based on Molecularly Imprinted Polymers
item.description: Abstract Malondialdehyde (MDA) is a critical biomarker of oxidative stress, playing a significant role in diagnosing and monitoring conditions associated with oxidative damage, including cardiovascular diseases, neurodegenerative disorders, and cancer. This study reports the synthesis and application of a molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP)-based electrochemical sensor for MDA detection using a dual biopolymer chitosan/κ-carrageenan matrix integrated with Fe3O4 nanoparticles on a boron-doped diamond (BDD) electrode. Differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) was employed to evaluate analyte recognition, while FTIR, DLS, SEM, EIS, and cyclic voltammetry were used for sensor characterization. Under optimized conditions (75% chitosan, 25% κ-carrageenan, and 10 mg Fe3O4 nanoparticles), the sensor exhibited high sensitivity (687.35 μA/μM), a low detection limit (0.005 μM), and a linear detection range of 0.026–0.26 μM. The developed platform also demonstrated good reproducibility, repeatability, and selectivity toward MDA in the presence of common interfering compounds. Analytical performance was further validated in spiked water and artificial serum samples, showing satisfactory recovery values. The proposed sensor outperformed several previously reported MDA sensing platforms, highlighting its potential as a sensitive and reliable tool for oxidative stress biomarker detection and future clinical applications.

item.title: Room-temperature alignment-free magnetometry with boron vacancies in hot-pressed hexagonal boron nitride
item.description: Abstract Magnetic-field sensing is essential for applications ranging from communication and environmental monitoring to biomedical diagnostics. Quantum sensors based on solid-state spin defects, such as nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond and boron vacancies (V B - ) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN), typically require precise alignment between the external magnetic field and the defect spin quantization axis, limiting their practical deployment. Here, we demonstrate room-temperature optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) from negatively charged boron vacancies in commercially available hot-pressed polycrystalline hBN. The random orientation of crystallites gives rise to an ensemble of defect quantization axes, enabling magnetic-field detection without the need for precise sensor alignment. The resulting orientation-averaged ODMR response exhibits broadened linewidths and reduced contrast compared with single-crystal hBN, while retaining clear magnetic-field-dependent signatures. Numerical simulations incorporating hyperfine interactions, anisotropic broadening, and preferential defect alignment accurately reproduce the experimental ODMR spectra across different magnetic-field strengths and orientations. Although the ensemble response does not permit unambiguous reconstruction of the magnetic-field vector, it enables robust alignment-free (scalar) magnetometry under ambient conditions. These results establish hot-pressed polycrystalline hBN as a scalable platform for room-temperature quantum magnetic-field sensing and highlight the potential of disordered spin ensembles for practical quantum sensing applications.

item.title: Mass Spectrometry-Based Characterization of Electrolytic Decomposition Products of Carbamazepine and Aripiprazole Under Different Electrode Conditions
item.description: Background: Carbamazepine (CBZ) and aripiprazole (ARI), frequently detected in medical facility effluents, are resistant to conventional wastewater treatment. However, a systematic comparison of their electrolytic degradation product profiles under different electrode conditions using an identical operating platform has not been previously reported. Methods: CBZ and ARI in NaCl solutions were subjected to electrolytic oxidation using the Eleca® system with either a boron-doped diamond (BDD) or a metal electrode. Residual drugs were quantified by LC-MS/MS and pseudo-first-order degradation kinetics were calculated. Transformation products were characterized by LC/PDA/HRMS/MS based on accurate mass measurements, MS/MS fragmentation, chromatographic behavior, and UV absorption. Radical scavenger experiments using methanol and tert-butanol were conducted to investigate reactive species’ contributions to degradation. Results: Both drugs were rapidly degraded under all conditions, with the metal electrode consistently exhibiting higher apparent pseudo-first-order rate constants than the BDD electrode. The metal electrode generated hydrophobic intermediates apparently retaining aromatic skeletons (consistent with partial oxidation), whereas the BDD electrode yielded more polar, low-molecular-weight products consistent with more extensive skeletal fragmentation (deep oxidation). Scavenger experiments suggested a greater relative contribution of hydroxyl radicals (•OH) under BDD electrode conditions. Transformation products were transiently detected but eliminated by prolonged electrolysis. Conclusions: Electrode material critically determines the degradation pathway, reactive species distribution, and product profile. Structural analysis of the tentatively identified transformation products suggests loss of pharmacophore integrity in several intermediates; however, residual pharmacological risk has not been experimentally validated and requires biological sassays for confirmation. Furthermore, the observed disappearance of the parent compounds does not demonstrate complete mineralization, detoxification, or environmental safety, as total organic carbon measurements and ecotoxicological assays were not performed. This study provides the first comparative characterization of transformation products of recalcitrant psychotropic drugs under metal vs. BDD electrode electrolysis, offering mechanistic insights for pharmaceutical wastewater treatment optimization.

item.title: Experimental Modeling of Mantle Metasomatic Processes Involving Carbon- and Sulfur-Bearing Agents in an Olivine–Siderite–Sulfur System at Early-Subduction Mantle Conditions
item.description: During Precambrian subduction, banded iron formations (BIFs) may have represented an early significant input of carbonates and atmospheric sulfur into the lithospheric mantle, initiated the formation of carbonatite melts and probably triggered mantle metasomatic processes. Experimental modeling of the interaction of BIF-related metasomatic agents with upper mantle rocks, under Archean subduction geotherm, was performed in the simplified olivine–siderite–sulfur system. Experiments were carried out at 6.3 GPa, temperature range of 1150–1450 °C and durations of 20–60 h, using a multi-anvil high-pressure apparatus of a “split-sphere” type. Interaction of Fe,Ni–olivine and siderite with sulfur melt leads to the formation of pyrrhotite + orthopyroxene + ferromagnesite ± magnetite assemblage (1150–1250 °C, 40–60 h), as well as generation of sulfide (1350–1450 °C) and carbonate–silicate melts (1450 °C, 20 h); in all experiments, dissolution of diamond seed crystals is observed. Redox conditions are estimated to approximately correspond to ƒO2 ~ CCO + 0.5 log. units. We demonstrated that during experiments, sulfidation of Fe,Ni–olivine and siderite and redox dissociation of siderite took place. It was shown that indicators of these processes are (1) polycrystalline orthopyroxene + pyrrhotite and pyrrhotite + ferromagnesite aggregates, inheriting shape of olivine and siderite crystals, respectively; (2) orthopyroxene zoned crystals with pyrrhotite inclusions; (3) pyrrhotite with ferromagnesite inclusions and ferromagnesite with magnetite + pyrrhotite inclusions. The obtained results with certain limitations can be used to constrain processes of metasomatic alteration of upper mantle rocks by agents enriched in iron, sulfur, and carbon under relatively oxidizing conditions (ƒO2 ~ CCO + 0.5 log. units).
