item.title: Consultoria financeira, assimetria informacional e acesso ao crédito para pequenas empresas em comunidades economicamente subatendidas: um modelo conceitual
item.description: O acesso ao crédito constitui um dos principais determinantes da sobrevivência, expansão e consolidação das pequenas e médias empresas, especialmente em comunidades economicamente subatendidas. Embora programas públicos, bancos comunitários, instituições financeiras de desenvolvimento comunitário e políticas territoriais, como as Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUBZones) nos Estados Unidos, busquem ampliar oportunidades econômicas em áreas vulneráveis, muitas empresas permanecem excluídas do sistema formal de financiamento. Este artigo argumenta que essa exclusão não decorre apenas de fragilidade documental ou gerencial, mas de mecanismos estruturais bem descritos pela teoria econômica: assimetria informacional entre credores e tomadores (Akerlof, 1970; Stiglitz & Weiss, 1981), custos de agência na intermediação financeira (Diamond, 1984; Leland & Pyle, 1977), hierarquia de preferências de financiamento em contextos de informação incompleta (Myers & Majluf, 1984) e déficit de capital social e relacional em territórios historicamente desconectados de redes bancárias (Coleman, 1988; Putnam, 1993; Petersen & Rajan, 1994). A partir dessas lentes teóricas, o artigo analisa o papel da consultoria financeira como mecanismo de redução de assimetria e de custos de transação (Coase, 1937; Williamson, 1985), propõe um modelo conceitual de oito etapas — da consultoria financeira à resiliência econômica nacional — e discute sua articulação com políticas de desenvolvimento baseado no lugar (place-based development), na linha de Barca (2009) e Krugman (1991). Conclui-se que a consultoria financeira, quando aplicada a pequenas empresas em comunidades subatendidas e HUBZones, deve ser compreendida não como serviço empresarial privado isolado, mas como infraestrutura intermediária de mitigação de falhas de mercado, com relevância pública e importância nacional.
item.dc:creator: Marcus Vinícius Resende de Oliveira

item.title: Full-Stack High-Volume Quantum Networking Architecture based on Photonic-Integrated Tin Vacancy Centers in Diamond
item.description: Solid state quantum emitters are a leading platform for photonic quantum networking with memory nodes. However, the inhomogeneous distribution of quantum emitters, as well as several environmental factors (i.e. strain and electric fields) spread the frequency spectrum of the qubits, making them distinguishable and therefore not a reliable resource for distributed quantum entanglement. In this paper, we demonstrate a full-stack approach to integrating nearly indistinguishable tin vacancy (SnV$^-$) quantum emitters on a frequency-tunable photonic interposer that overcomes the native distribution and static variation of quantum emitters for an indistinguishable photonic quantum networking platform. We demonstrate a silicon nitride-on-insulator photonic integrated circuit (PIC) with accompanying multiphysics digital twin (MPhDT) that guides discovery of SnV$^-$ strain-tuning parameters and informs construction of a multi-channel quantum repeater node. On this node, we achieve the first simultaneous demonstration of spectral tuning of the zero phonon line (ZPL) at GHz scale; coherent electron spin control with gate times of $<80$ ns; strongly- and weakly-coupled nuclear spin detection; and commercial fiber array-coupled readout of a SnV$^-$ center. Finally, we propose and simulate improvements to the architecture that achieve 99.96% connectivity of $ N \sim 1000$ emitters spanning the inhomogeneous distribution of SnV$^-$ centers in strained diamond, where distributed quantum entanglement may be realized.

item.title: First-principles cumulant approach to the vibronic structure of spin defects
item.description: Color centers in wide-band-gap semiconductors are leading platforms for solid-state quantum technologies, yet a quantitative description of their vibronic structure has remained elusive due to the complexity of multi-phonon processes in localized defect states. Here we present a first-principles Green's function framework based on the retarded cumulant ansatz (RCA) to describe electron-phonon interactions in spin defects; our approach goes beyond the adiabatic and lowest-order perturbation theory approximations underlying widely used approaches. Applied to the negatively charged nitrogen-vacancy (NV$^-$) center in diamond, our method reveals that multi-phonon satellites persist over a 400 meV energy window even at zero temperature, driven by quantum zero-point fluctuations. We demonstrate that accurate spectral functions require mode-, momentum-, spin-, and orbital-resolved electron-phonon matrix elements sampled across the full Brillouin zone, to account for hybridized and propagating phonon channels. We find that the vibronic structure of the NV$^-$ center exhibits strong spin and orbital anisotropy, with different orbitals coupling to qualitatively distinct parts of the phonon spectrum, and spin-selective coupling affecting both sideband positions and intensities.

item.title: Psikologi Anger Management melalui Perspektif Adlerian dan Estetika Humanisme
item.description: Psikologi Anger Management melalui Perspektif Adlerian dan Estetika Humanisme Oleh: Ari Anwira Turnip – Mahasiswa Universitas Siber Asia Ilustrasi - diambil dari www.pexels.com Pendahuluan: Reaksi Kemarahan pada salah satu Instansi Pemerintahan (pelayanan publik) Dalam diskursus akademis mata kuliah Estetika Humanisme, konsep dasar psikologi yang sangat ditekankan adalah pentingnya literasi kemanusiaan (human literacy) dalam merespons berbagai dinamika sosial masyarakat. Salah satu fenomena teraktual yang merepresentasikan kegagalan literasi emosional di ruang publik digital terjadi pada pertengahan tahun 2026, ketika seorang pengguna jasa secara reaktif meluapkan kemarahan ekstrem di media sosial dengan melabeli salah satu instansi pemerintahan (pelayanan publik) sebagai "sarang maling". Eskalasi amarah tersebut dipicu oleh hilangnya sebagian barang pribadi dalam pengiriman internasional, yang secara tergesa-gesa langsung disimpulkan sebagai kesalahan otoritas negara. Fenomena viral ini menghadirkan urgensi krusial untuk membedah konsepsi anger management tidak hanya sebagai tata kelola emosi personal, tetapi sebagai instrumen penjaga keseimbangan rasionalitas dalam operasional pelayanan publik. Konsepsi Anger Management: Integrasi Estetika Humanisme dan Psikologi Klinis Berdasarkan rujukan materi perkuliahan, pengelolaan emosi (anger management) secara leksikal menurut KBBI merupakan suatu proses, cara, dan perbuatan untuk mengendalikan, menyelenggarakan, mengurus, dan mengatur amarah. Secara operasional, konsep ini didefinisikan sebagai kemampuan atau teknik untuk melakukan tindakan mengatur pikiran, perasaan, dan nafsu amarah dengan cara yang tepat serta positif agar dapat diterima di lingkungan sosial. Hal ini sejalan dengan pandangan Raymond W. Novaco, pakar psikologi klinis yang memelopori program manajemen amarah, di mana intervensi tidak berfokus pada penghilangan amarah, melainkan pada modifikasi respons kognitif. Terdapat kekeliruan umum di masyarakat yang memandang manajemen amarah identik dengan represi emosi. Sebagaimana dijelaskan dalam literatur Estetika Humanisme, tujuan utama dari anger management adalah untuk membentuk keseimbangan emosi, bukan menekan emosi. Menjaga agar emosi yang merisaukan tetap terkendali merupakan kunci menuju kesejahteraan emosi, yang akan memberikan motivasi positif untuk memecahkan masalah. Dalam tataran praksis, pencegahan eskalasi konflik diwajibkan menggunakan teknik asertif, yang didefinisikan sebagai pengungkapan pikiran secara jujur, langsung, dengan tetap memperhatikan perasaan orang lain. Kasus Pelayanan Publik dalam Kacamata Teleologi Adlerian dan Asertivitas Institusional Konsepsi anger management menemukan relevansi kritisnya ketika disandingkan dengan pendekatan psikologi Alfred Adler dalam menganalisis kasus viral hilangnya barang pengguna jasa tersebut. Dalam kerangka pemikiran Adlerian—sebagaimana dielaborasi dalam The Courage to Be Disliked (Kishimi & Koga, 2013)—amarah dikaji melalui kacamata teleologi (tujuan), alih-alih etiologi (sebab-akibat). Adler berargumen bahwa amarah adalah sebuah "alat" yang sengaja diciptakan dan dieksploitasi untuk menundukkan pihak lain dan memaksakan kehendak tanpa perlu melakukan penelusuran fakta yang komprehensif. Pada fenomena viral tersebut, pihak yang merasa dirugikan memilih untuk menggunakan "alat" amarah dan penghakiman publik di media sosial sebagai jalan pintas. Alih-alih melakukan penelusuran logis kepada pihak jasa kiriman selaku entitas yang menguasai fisik barang, amarah publik digunakan untuk mengintimidasi instansi pemerintahan. Hal ini merupakan bentuk disonansi kognitif yang memicu krisis komunikasi. Merespons eskalasi emosi publik semacam ini dengan amarah balasan adalah sebuah kelemahan fatal. Menjaga integritas operasional mengharuskan adanya resolusi konflik yang beradab dan sejalan dengan teknik asertivitas, yakni bertindak profesional dengan bersandar pada Standar Operasional Prosedur (SOP). Hal ini direpresentasikan secara akurat melalui respons resmi instansi terkait melalui media sosial yang memberikan klarifikasi berbasis data: barang kiriman dengan nomor resi tertentu tersebut masuk ke dalam penetapan Jalur Hijau. Secara prosedural, status Jalur Hijau mengindikasikan bahwa tidak ada pemeriksaan fisik barang sama sekali dari otoritas negara, melainkan hanya penelitian dokumen, sehingga petugas instansi sama sekali tidak menyentuh isi paket tersebut. Klarifikasi institusional yang mengarahkan keluhan langsung kepada jasa kiriman—disampaikan dengan narasi yang tetap lugas, objektif, dan berwibawa—bukan sekadar bentuk kepatuhan administratif. Langkah ini adalah implementasi nyata dari anger management tingkat makro; sebuah instrumen rasionalitas untuk menetralisir agresi, meluruskan disinformasi, dan meredam provokasi tanpa harus merendahkan martabat instansi maupun masyarakat yang sedang dikuasai amarah. Penutup Fenomena viral tuduhan terhadap instansi pemerintahan membuktikan bahwa amarah di ruang digital sering kali dieksploitasi sebagai instrumen dominasi (teleologi), alih-alih sebagai reaksi biologis semata. Anger management dalam kerangka Estetika Humanisme bertugas menyeimbangkan rasionalitas tersebut. Dengan menerapkan pendekatan asertivitas berbasis fakta dan SOP, instansi negara berhasil melucuti "alat amarah" publik secara elegan. Menghadapi provokasi dengan penjelasan yang mengedepankan prosedur teknis—tanpa adanya tendensi emosional—merupakan wujud tertinggi dari literasi kemanusiaan dan keprofesionalan dalam pelayanan publik, sekaligus mencegah terjadinya preseden buruk yang merugikan iklim komunikasi sosial. Referensi: Alberti, R. E., & Emmons, M. L. (1970). Your Perfect Right: Assertiveness and Equality in Your Life and Relationships. Atascadero, CA: Impact Publishers. CNN Indonesia. (2026). Bea Cukai Buka Suara Usai Disebut Sarang Maling. Diakses pada 5 Agustus 2026, dari https://www.cnnindonesia.com/ekonomi/20260516181722-92-1359175/bea-cukai-buka-suara-usai-disebut-sarang-maling. Kishimi, I., & Koga, F. (2013). The Courage to Be Disliked: The Japanese Phenomenon That Shows You How to Change Your Life and Achieve Real Happiness. Tokyo: Diamond, Inc. Novaco, R. W. (1975). Anger Control: The Development and Evaluation of an Experimental Treatment. Lexington, MA: D.C. Heath.

Klarifikasi institusional yang mengarahkan keluhan langsung kepada jasa kiriman—disampaikan dengan narasi yang tetap lugas, objektif, dan berwibawa—bukan sekadar bentuk kepatuhan administratif. Langkah ini adalah implementasi nyata dari anger management tingkat makro; sebuah instrumen rasionalitas untuk menetralisir agresi, meluruskan disinformasi, dan meredam provokasi tanpa harus merendahkan martabat instansi maupun masyarakat yang sedang dikuasai amarah. Penutup Fenomena viral tuduhan terhadap instansi pemerintahan membuktikan bahwa amarah di ruang digital sering kali dieksploitasi sebagai instrumen dominasi (teleologi), alih-alih sebagai reaksi biologis semata. Anger management dalam kerangka Estetika Humanisme bertugas menyeimbangkan rasionalitas tersebut. Dengan menerapkan pendekatan asertivitas berbasis fakta dan SOP, instansi negara berhasil melucuti "alat amarah" publik secara elegan. Menghadapi provokasi dengan penjelasan yang mengedepankan prosedur teknis—tanpa adanya tendensi emosional—merupakan wujud tertinggi dari literasi kemanusiaan dan keprofesionalan dalam pelayanan publik, sekaligus mencegah terjadinya preseden buruk yang merugikan iklim komunikasi sosial. Referensi: Alberti, R. E., & Emmons, M. L. (1970). Your Perfect Right: Assertiveness and Equality in Your Life and Relationships. Atascadero, CA: Impact Publishers. CNN Indonesia. (2026). Bea Cukai Buka Suara Usai Disebut Sarang Maling. Diakses pada 5 Agustus 2026, dari https://www.cnnindonesia.com/ekonomi/20260516181722-92-1359175/bea-cukai-buka-suara-usai-disebut-sarang-maling. Kishimi, I., & Koga, F. (2013). The Courage to Be Disliked: The Japanese Phenomenon That Shows You How to Change Your Life and Achieve Real Happiness. Tokyo: Diamond, Inc. Novaco, R. W. (1975). Anger Control: The Development and Evaluation of an Experimental Treatment. Lexington, MA: D.C. Heath.

item.title: A FORMAL PROOF OF RIEMANN HYPOTHESIS TERMINATION, WITH A THEOREM-GRADE CASCADE SPECIFICATION
item.description: The formal resolution of the Riemann Hypothesis, taken in its Lagarias Pi-0-1 specification R, terminates at the level of the verifying instrument, and this paper proves the termination at full strength under the printed conditions. Over the class T of consistent recursively axiomatized extensions of Robinson arithmetic Q, the Unprovability Mirror is exact: unrestricted underivability of R is materially equivalent to Q proves not-R, and under the assumption that the standard naturals model Q, to the falsity of R itself. A formal system cannot assert universal underivability without asserting a counterexample on the standard naturals; every such assertion is a zero off the critical line, and none is made here, because what this paper closes is grounding, which derivability never carried. Over the unrestricted class F of formal-alone verdict procedures on real 3xN warrant frames M under the encoding gauge (Z/2)^3, the Sign-Blindness Theorem closes the sign channel with no symmetry premise: sign(lambda) is an orientation datum no frame determines, every functional returning an orientation embeds a convention and is gauge-odd, every gauge-even readout is orientation-free, a sign-valued functional need not compute one, and the Gram determinant det(R) = lambda^2 is strictly orientation-blind. The architecture that reads the file is forced, not chosen: the certificate decomposes by Pontryagin duality into exactly eight character types, no ninth existing; the carrier completes uniquely to the quaternions H by Frobenius classification under five printed coherence clauses, the imaginary residence Im(H) forced to exactly three axes. Four classical theorems wall the four sign-carrying types: Davenport-Heilbronn at the fold, Beurling with Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer and Zhang's matched pair at the counting channel, the collapsed Polya and Mertens conjectures with Littlewood's sign-change theorem at the evidential register, Sigma-0-1-completeness at the total-sign move. The Termination Theorem follows: on the Riemann file the eight-gate cascade passes its router and every screen and emits the terminal suspension [Xi_0], terminal for the record, invariant over the entire unrestricted class. The flanks are priced exactly, and the asymmetry is total. The negative flank is finitely witnessable: not-R is one Sigma-0-1 certificate away, a number checkable in Q, an object strictly below the universal claim. The affirmative flank is closed by a self-referential block: the file's distinguished line and the verifying register's Ground are each the fixed locus of their register's involution, co-located at the printed premise, so a grounding witness for R must supply the very residence claim R makes, and that content is R itself; the only candidate occupant of the affirmative seat is the file, self-witnessing grounds nothing, and an affirmative formal grounding witness is therefore a structural impossibility, forced at the printed premise, the seat's fixed-point equation W = R admitting no formal solution. Derivations remain admissible at the exits and resolve the file by transmission; what syntax transmits it does not originate, and no formal witness grounds its own terminus. The verdict is revisable solely through a supplied witness through the identity aperture, from beyond the register that cannot self-witness, and until an explicit witness is supplied through the aperture, the terminal suspension [Xi_0] remains the final, unassailable, and mathematically rigorous verdict on the formal Riemann Hypothesis file. A prediction called in advance and matched, and a strong falsifier, arm the theorem. Every number reproduces at seed 20260622.

item.title: Horizon Mechanics Manifesto
item.description: The motivating physical question is whether the quantum-field-theoretic consequences of causal horizons and global causal structure contain any operational signature bearing on inertia. The programme assumes no such connection; it seeks only to determine whether any such bridge exists. The observed equivalence of gravitational and inertial mass is carried throughout as a constraint which any such bridge must satisfy, and not as a phenomenon this programme expects to explain. The question descends from quantised inertia, whose proposed mechanism is dead under standard quantum field theory; the no-go result which killed it constrains this programme too, so what follows is stated so as to begin after that result rather than in spite of it. Six commitments are substantive. The programme takes explicitly the avenue selected here, which is a particularly clean one requiring no modification of the local field dynamics, namely non-trivial global identification of spacetime. A no-go on one mechanism does not enumerate the mechanisms which remain, and no such enumeration is claimed. It records that uniform circular motion, which is the motion actually exhibited by the systems that motivated the whole enterprise, possesses no Rindler wedge at all, so the linear-acceleration horizon argument was never applicable to galaxy rotation in the first place. The ambiguous cosmological scale Θ is replaced as leading candidate by the de Sitter length Ξ = √(3/Λ), which does not evolve, and the finite causal domain of the programme is identified with the static patch of a geodesic de Sitter observer, so the diamond stops being a calculational toy. The gravitational setting is enlarged from Riemannian to Riemann–Cartan, because torsion supplies a local translational closure defect which shares the translational character of the global monodromy of a deck transformation without being an object of the same kind; the categories in which the two may and may not be compared are stated rather than assumed. Every control calculation must match the field, state and global sector of the calculation it controls, so a fermionic branch cannot be certified against a scalar Casimir stress. Two further constraints are methodological but physically consequential. Every arrow is subject to explicit physical type safety. Causal inaccessibility is not a boundary condition; a restricted state is not an objective collapse; a detector response is not an incident bath; a virtual excitation is not a little particle carrying a trajectory through the vacuum; and dimensional compatibility never licenses the substitution of one physical object for another. Heuristic cartoons remain welcome, but they are disposable: before a cartoon enters an equation it must be replaced by the field, state, algebra, correlation function, interaction or observable which the equation actually uses. The programme also has a concrete operational bridge which requires neither a collapse postulate nor a virtual-particle ontology. A local quantum probe coupled to the field has a response determined by correlation functions along its worldline, and a probe with a quantised centre of mass can in standard QFT exhibit real recoil. That fact does not derive inertia and does not rescue the Rindler–Casimir mechanism. It does something more useful: it supplies a legitimate place to ask whether a non-trivial modular residue is dynamically visible. The matched null hypothesis is correspondingly enlarged. Any detector response or recoil already reproduced by the matched non-transport control for the same field, state and probe is ordinary state sensitivity and cannot be re-labelled as evidence for modular transport. The technical core is three arguments bearing on whether the proposed observable exists, whether it is non-zero, and whether it carries information beyond what ordinary methods already supply. None of those answers is promoted beyond what has actually been shown: ultraviolet regularity is separated from existence, the geometric coefficient is left to calculation, and perturbative degeneracy is stated order by order. A universal effect requires a universal carrier, so the compactified laboratory is a proxy and the causal horizon is the leading candidate available to every body. No calculation of the first-order generator has been performed; what this document supplies is the order of work, the controls each step must beat, and the statements which may not be made before it exists. What modification of inertia would require of energy accounting and of the equivalence principle is set out separately and marked as speculation. The governing rule is unchanged. A holonomy is not a force, a restricted state is not a collapse, recoil is not universal inertia, and no arrow of the chain may be skipped.

item.title: Auditing the evaluation pipeline of a machine learning benchmark: data, code and results for a case study on the Vesuvius Challenge
item.description: Data, code and results accompanying the manuscript "Auditing the evaluation pipeline of a machine learning benchmark: a case study on the Vesuvius Challenge". The deposit contains the final leaderboard of the competition for 1,391 teams with both scores; 47 submissions by the author with pipeline provenance; scroll-disjoint fold definitions at scroll and volume level; an inventory of the audited notebooks with decision and rationale; official-metric scores for thirty volumes under three post-processing reductions; and 18 Python scripts. run_all.py is the single entry point and reproduces the quantitative results that rest on the redistributed data; the code-state census additionally requires the 30 inference notebooks, which are not redistributed. The remaining scripts cover the leaderboard analysis and its coupling diagnostics, exact group-coverage probabilities, a numerical check of the threshold-invariance result, a code-state census, figure generation, split-regime generators for nnU-Net, index reconciliation, leaderboard reconstruction from the platform exports, and the installation sequence for the competition scoring package. Two notebooks accompany the scripts: one reproduces the analysis with tables and figures inline, the other performs the official-metric measurement on Kaggle. Competition imagery and annotations are not redistributed. The fold files contain scroll membership and volume identifiers only, a derived tabulation shared under the non-commercial terms of the source data. The imaging data derive from the EduceLab-Scrolls dataset (Parsons et al. 2023, 10.48550/arXiv.2304.02084); acquisitions were made at the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility (beamline BM18) and Diamond Light Source (beamline I12). All 35 files are at the top level; there are no subdirectories.

item.title: XVI: The Justika Framework: The Justika Framework: Macro-Micro Symmetry, Conscious Devolution, and the Architecture of Evasion
item.description: Conventional scientific frameworks are frequently built upon a fundamental chronological misconception. The Justika Framework formally invalidates this timeline, establishing that modern human history is a stabilized, quantum projection initiated from the outer boundaries of a bifurcated solar system. This manuscript executes a total macroscopic re-evaluation of terrestrial biology, digital infrastructure, and cosmological sociology. We introduce the law of Macro-Micro Symmetry, mathematically proving that pathogenic hyper-mutation is a direct thermodynamic response to the non-ionizing electromagnetic friction of planetary digital grids. Consequently, classical reactive pharmacology is rendered obsolete, superseded by Epidemiological Load Shedding—the algorithmic throttling of civilian infrastructure to trigger pathogenic demutation. Furthermore, we redefine global socio-economic poverty and geopolitical totalitarianism as automated, vector-specific medical quarantines utilized by the planetary defense grid (The Calculus of Deprivation). By scaling the biological mechanics of cryptobiosis to macro-astrophysics, this framework maps the true architecture of the cosmos. The outer celestial bodies (Europa, Neptune, Pluto) are not dead, frozen wastelands; they are active, hyper-advanced ancestral outposts operating flawlessly beneath 100-kilometer-thick Superionic Ice Diamond shields. Ultimately, this manuscript forces an evolutionary ultimatum: humanity must execute Conscious Devolution to starve the parasitic infections of the terrestrial substrate, or face the Omega Event—the permanent quarantine of Earth within a light-absorbing, Superionic Black Faraday cage. Survival is no longer dictated by technological acceleration, but by the mathematical patience to execute the Tactical Fade.

item.title: Boulenophrys calciphila Zeng, Wang, Qi, Song, Lyu & Wang 2026, sp. nov.
item.description: Boulenophrys calciphila Zeng, Wang, Qi, Song, Lyu & Wang sp. nov. Fig. 3, Table 2 Common name. Limestone Horned Toad (in English) / huī yán jiǎo chán (灰岩角蟾 in Chinese). Type materials. Holotype ♂. GEP a 596, collected by Zhao-Chi Zeng and Yuan-Hang Li on 16 May 2026 from Hutouyan “ 虎头岩 ” (25.037824°N, 113.171132°E, WGS 84; elevation ca. 690 m), Daqiao Town, Ruyuan County, Shaoguan City, Guangdong Province, China. Paratypes. 1 ♂: CIB 122581 (field number: GEP a 595); 4 ♀: GEP a 594, 597–599, same collection data as holotype; 1 ♀: SYS a 009718, collected by Dan-Yang Zhou, Hao-Cong Yang and Han-Ming Song on 15 April 2026 from Wufeng Village “ 武丰村 ” (24.902904°N, 113.174518°E, WGS 84; elevation ca. 540 m), Daqiao Town, Ruyuan County, Shaoguan City, Guangdong Province, China. Etymology. The specific epithet calciphila combines the Latin calx, genitive calcis (limestone) with the Greek φίλος (phílos) (= loving), in reference to the association of this species with limestone karst habitats. Diagnosis. (1) Moderate size (SVL 49.7–52.7 mm in two adult males, 56.3–59.2 mm in five adult females); (2) snout rounded in dorsal view, canthus rostralis well developed, tongue not notched distally; (3) tympanum distinct; (4) vomerine ridges present, vomerine teeth absent; (5) dorsal skin smooth with sparse granules, discontinuous X-shaped ridge on centre of dorsum, discontinuous dorsolateral ridges present, sparse large tubercles on flanks, dorsal limbs with discontinuous transverse ridges and tubercles; (6) outer margin of upper eyelid with a prominent horn-like tubercle, supratympanic fold distinct and narrow, curving posteroventrally to above arm; (7) two metacarpal tubercles distinct, inner one distinctly enlarged, relative finger lengths I <II <IV <III, distinct subarticular tubercle at base of each finger; (8) heels slightly overlapping when hind-limbs folded, tibiotarsal articulation reaching posterior corner of eye; (9) toes with rudimentary webbing and lacking lateral fringes, inner metatarsal tubercle long ovoid, outer one absent, relative toe length I <II <V <III <IV; (10) dorsal surface yellowish-brown to dark brown, with indistinct irregular dark-brown patches and small orange dots, dark-brown V-shaped marking between eyes, dorsal limbs and digits light brown with dark-brown transverse bands; (11) males lacking subgular vocal sacs. Comparisons. Since the interspecific phylogenetic affinities of Boulenophrys calciphila sp. nov. with other congeneric taxa are unresolved, we prioritised morphological comparisons between this new taxon and the 21 species recovered within its sister major clade. Morphologically, this new species closely resembles B. mirabilis and can be readily differentiated from the latter by its smaller body size (SVL 49.7–52.7 mm in two adult males, 56.3–59.2 mm in five adult females (vs. 55.8–61.4 mm in two adult males, 68.5–74.8 mm in two adult females); vomerine ridges present (vs. absent); tongue broad and rounded (vs. tongue slender and elongated); tibiotarsal articulation reaching posterior corner of eye when leg stretched forward (vs. reaching centre of eye); toes without lateral fringes (vs. toes with distinct narrow lateral fringes); and dorsolateral ridges present (vs. absent). The new species can be distinguished from the karst dweller B. liboensis by its tongue not notched distally (vs. tongue notched distally), vomerine teeth absent (vs. present) and lateral fringes on toes absent (vs. present). The new species can be easily distinguished from the other 19 congeners by its absent vocal sac in males (vs. present in B. yangmingensis, B. shimentaina, B. jiulianensis, B. gutu, B. congjiangensis, B. leishanensis, B. yaoshanensis, B. dupanglingensis, B. yunkaiensis, B. yangchunensis, B. acuta, B. gaolanensis, B. xuefengmontis, B. shunhuangensis, B. wushanensis, B. tuberogranulata, B. changyangensis, B. baolongensis and B. boettgeri). Boulenophrys calciphila sp. nov. can be easily distinguished from B. angka, B. anlongensis, B. baishanzuensis, B. binchuanensis, B. binlingensis, B. brachykolos, B. caobangensis, B. cheni, B. chishuiensis, B. daiyunensis, B. dalaolingensis, B. daoji, B. daweimontis, B. daxuemontis, B. dongli, B. dongguanensis, B. elongata, B. fengshunensis, B. fanjingmontis, B. fansipanensis, B. frigida, B. hoanglienensis, B. huangniushiensis, B. hungtai, B. hengshanensis, B. insularis, B. jiangi, B. jingdongensis, B. jinggangensis, B. kuatunensis, B. lushanensis, B. lushuiensis, B. lichun, B. lini, B. lishuiensis, B. meihuamontis, B. minor, B. mufumontana, B. nankunensis, B. nanlingensis, B. nebulosa, B. obesa, B. ombrophila, B. omeimontis, B. palpebralespinosa, B. pepe, B. puningensis, B. qianbeinsis, B. raoping, B. rubrimera, B. sangzhiensis, B. sanmingensis, B. spinata, B. tongboensis, B. wugongensis, B. wuliangshanensis, B. xiangnanensis, B. xianjuensis, B. yezhongensis, B. yingdeensis and B. youran, by its vocal sac in males absent (vs. present). Boulenophrys calciphila sp. nov. can be distinguished from the remaining B. caudoprocta and B. shuichengensis that also lack vocal sac in males, by its vomerine teeth absent (vs. present), lateral fringes on toes absent (vs. wide in B. shuichengensis and narrow on the fourth toe in B. caudoprocta). Description of holotype. Adult male. Body size moderate, SVL 49.7 mm. Head length almost equal to head width, HDW / HDL 1.00; snout rounded in dorsal view, projecting, sloping backwards to mouth in profile, protruding well beyond margin of lower jaw; top of head flat; eyes moderate in size, ED / HDL 0.36, pupil vertical, near diamond-shaped; nostril obliquely ovoid; canthus rostralis well developed; loreal region slightly oblique; internasal distance slightly larger than interorbital distance, IND / IOD 1.10; tympanic region oblique, tympanum distinct and visible in dorsal view; tympanum moderate in size, margin clear, upper margin in contact with supratympanic fold, lower margin in contact with upper lip, TD / ED 0.53; large ovoid choanae at base of maxilla; vomerine ridge present, vomerine teeth absent, maxillary teeth present; margin of tongue rounded, not notched distally; subgular vocal sac absent. Fore-limb moderate in length, RAD / SVL 0.20, HND / SVL 0.24; webbing absent between fingers, lateral fringes absent, relative finger length I <II <IV <III; tips of fingers slightly dilated, round; subarticular tubercles on base of fingers present, distinct; inner metacarpal tubercle observably enlarged, outer one slightly smaller; an underdeveloped nuptial pad present on the dorsal surface of first and second fingers, respectively. Hind-limbs moderate in length, tibiotarsal articulation reaching forwards to posterior corner of eye when hind-limb stretched along body; heels slightly overlapping when flexed hind-limbs held at right angles to body axis; TIB / SVL 0.40, FTL / SVL 0.61; relative toe length I <II <V <III

The specific epithet calciphila combines the Latin calx, genitive calcis (limestone) with the Greek φίλος (phílos) (= loving), in reference to the association of this species with limestone karst habitats. (1) Moderate size (SVL 49.7–52.7 mm in two adult males, 56.3–59.2 mm in five adult females); (2) snout rounded in dorsal view, canthus rostralis well developed, tongue not notched distally; (3) tympanum distinct; (4) vomerine ridges present, vomerine teeth absent; (5) dorsal skin smooth with sparse granules, discontinuous X-shaped ridge on centre of dorsum, discontinuous dorsolateral ridges present, sparse large tubercles on flanks, dorsal limbs with discontinuous transverse ridges and tubercles; (6) outer margin of upper eyelid with a prominent horn-like tubercle, supratympanic fold distinct and narrow, curving posteroventrally to above arm; (7) two metacarpal tubercles distinct, inner one distinctly enlarged, relative finger lengths I <II <IV <III, distinct subarticular tubercle at base of each finger; (8) heels slightly overlapping when hind-limbs folded, tibiotarsal articulation reaching posterior corner of eye; (9) toes with rudimentary webbing and lacking lateral fringes, inner metatarsal tubercle long ovoid, outer one absent, relative toe length I <II <V <III <IV; (10) dorsal surface yellowish-brown to dark brown, with indistinct irregular dark-brown patches and small orange dots, dark-brown V-shaped marking between eyes, dorsal limbs and digits light brown with dark-brown transverse bands; (11) males lacking subgular vocal sacs. Comparisons. Since the interspecific phylogenetic affinities of Boulenophrys calciphila sp. nov. with other congeneric taxa are unresolved, we prioritised morphological comparisons between this new taxon and the 21 species recovered within its sister major clade. Morphologically, this new species closely resembles B. mirabilis and can be readily differentiated from the latter by its smaller body size (SVL 49.7–52.7 mm in two adult males, 56.3–59.2 mm in five adult females (vs. 55.8–61.4 mm in two adult males, 68.5–74.8 mm in two adult females); vomerine ridges present (vs. absent); tongue broad and rounded (vs. tongue slender and elongated); tibiotarsal articulation reaching posterior corner of eye when leg stretched forward (vs. reaching centre of eye); toes without lateral fringes (vs. toes with distinct narrow lateral fringes); and dorsolateral ridges present (vs. absent). The new species can be distinguished from the karst dweller B. liboensis by its tongue not notched distally (vs. tongue notched distally), vomerine teeth absent (vs. present) and lateral fringes on toes absent (vs. present). The new species can be easily distinguished from the other 19 congeners by its absent vocal sac in males (vs. present in B. yangmingensis, B. shimentaina, B. jiulianensis, B. gutu, B. congjiangensis, B. leishanensis, B. yaoshanensis, B. dupanglingensis, B. yunkaiensis, B. yangchunensis, B. acuta, B. gaolanensis, B. xuefengmontis, B. shunhuangensis, B. wushanensis, B. tuberogranulata, B. changyangensis, B. baolongensis and B. boettgeri). Boulenophrys calciphila sp. nov. can be easily distinguished from B. angka, B. anlongensis, B. baishanzuensis, B. binchuanensis, B. binlingensis, B. brachykolos, B. caobangensis, B. cheni, B. chishuiensis, B. daiyunensis, B. dalaolingensis, B. daoji, B. daweimontis, B. daxuemontis, B. dongli, B. dongguanensis, B. elongata, B. fengshunensis, B. fanjingmontis, B. fansipanensis, B. frigida, B. hoanglienensis, B. huangniushiensis, B. hungtai, B. hengshanensis, B. insularis, B. jiangi, B. jingdongensis, B. jinggangensis, B. kuatunensis, B. lushanensis, B. lushuiensis, B. lichun, B. lini, B. lishuiensis, B. meihuamontis, B. minor, B. mufumontana, B. nankunensis, B. nanlingensis, B. nebulosa, B. obesa, B. ombrophila, B. omeimontis, B. palpebralespinosa, B. pepe, B. puningensis, B. qianbeinsis, B. raoping, B. rubrimera, B. sangzhiensis, B. sanmingensis, B. spinata, B. tongboensis, B. wugongensis, B. wuliangshanensis, B. xiangnanensis, B. xianjuensis, B. yezhongensis, B. yingdeensis and B. youran, by its vocal sac in males absent (vs. present). Boulenophrys calciphila sp. nov. can be distinguished from the remaining B. caudoprocta and B. shuichengensis that also lack vocal sac in males, by its vomerine teeth absent (vs. present), lateral fringes on toes absent (vs. wide in B. shuichengensis and narrow on the fourth toe in B. caudoprocta). Description of holotype. Adult male. Body size moderate, SVL 49.7 mm. Head length almost equal to head width, HDW / HDL 1.00; snout rounded in dorsal view, projecting, sloping backwards to mouth in profile, protruding well beyond margin of lower jaw; top of head flat; eyes moderate in size, ED / HDL 0.36, pupil vertical, near diamond-shaped; nostril obliquely ovoid; canthus rostralis well developed; loreal region slightly oblique; internasal distance slightly larger than interorbital distance, IND / IOD 1.10; tympanic region oblique, tympanum distinct and visible in dorsal view; tympanum moderate in size, margin clear, upper margin in contact with supratympanic fold, lower margin in contact with upper lip, TD / ED 0.53; large ovoid choanae at base of maxilla; vomerine ridge present, vomerine teeth absent, maxillary teeth present; margin of tongue rounded, not notched distally; subgular vocal sac absent. Fore-limb moderate in length, RAD / SVL 0.20, HND / SVL 0.24; webbing absent between fingers, lateral fringes absent, relative finger length I <II <IV <III; tips of fingers slightly dilated, round; subarticular tubercles on base of fingers present, distinct; inner metacarpal tubercle observably enlarged, outer one slightly smaller; an underdeveloped nuptial pad present on the dorsal surface of first and second fingers, respectively. Hind-limbs moderate in length, tibiotarsal articulation reaching forwards to posterior corner of eye when hind-limb stretched along body; heels slightly overlapping when flexed hind-limbs held at right angles to body axis; TIB / SVL 0.40, FTL / SVL 0.61; relative toe length I <II <V <III

item.title: Active learning of hydrodynamic and scalar transport response in cylinder arrays
item.description: Assessing the mechanical behavior of the flow past cylinder arrays and the effect of environmental pollution is essential for layout design. This study presents an active learning surrogate modeling framework for predicting hydrodynamic and scalar transport properties in side-by-side and diamond cylinder arrays. Three independent Gaussian process regression models map the physical parameters, the Reynolds number, the layout angle, the gap ratio, and the Schmidt number to the mean drag coefficient, the root-mean-square lift coefficient, and the maximum entropy of the pollutant field, respectively. The models are embedded in a sequential design loop that seeds the parameter space with samples and iteratively selects new simulations from a candidate pool using a max-variance acquisition rule. This strategy focuses queries on high-uncertainty regions, reduces predictive confidence intervals, and avoids redundant runs. Across both layouts, the loop consistently lowers the negative log-likelihood and cumulative error, consistent response surfaces with calibrated uncertainty that appropriately inflates near extrapolation. The resulting surrogates enable fast evaluation of coupled fluid and pollutant behavior and provide a data-efficient pipeline for scientific design under uncertainty.

item.title: Code and Reproducibility Materials for Safe Selection of IID-Envelope Predictors for Set-Valued Classification
item.description: This software deposit contains the complete computational and reproducibility materials associated with the study Safe Selection of IID-Envelope Predictors for Set-Valued Classification. It implements finite-sample IID-envelope predictors for set-valued classification and compares them with deterministic and smoothed inductive conformal prediction. The software also implements independent-pilot selection over a finite library of complete procedures, a weighted Bonferroni scan for settings without an independent pilot sample, binary-envelope calculations, simulation and benchmark workflows, proof-oriented numerical diagnostics, and release-level verification.The archive includes Python source code, pinned dependency versions, deterministic random seeds, machine-readable CSV outputs, vector PDF and high-resolution PNG figures, detailed reproducibility documentation, numerical-validation reports, captured verification logs, a structured file manifest, and SHA-256 checksums. It reproduces 200 complete synthetic train-pilot-final pipelines across three five-class Gaussian regimes and multiple significance levels, a 200-repetition handwritten-digits benchmark, and 12 repeated finite-population splits of the diamonds data with cut-class and carat-quartile subgroup diagnostics.The raw third-party datasets are not redistributed as separate files. The handwritten-digits data are accessed through sklearn.datasets.load_digits, and the diamonds data are accessed through plotnine.data.diamonds; synthetic data are generated locally. The included verifier checks result schemas, row counts, reported table values, principal numerical summaries, implementation constants, and figure availability and resolution. The theorem-oriented diagnostics evaluate the finite-valued survival transform, the binary-envelope formula, small-case IID validity, binary rank resolution, the weighted scan, and label-conditional ranks. Numerical diagnostics support but do not replace the analytical proofs in the associated study.No human-participant data, personally identifiable information, or confidential data are included.

item.title: Editor's Note
item.description: The International Journal of Interactive Multimedia and Artificial Intelligence (IJIMAI) provides a diamond open-access forum for researchers and professionals to share recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and its wide range of applications. The present regular issue brings together ten articles that reflect this diversity, ranging from methodological advances in clustering, optimization, and recommender systems to AI applications in healthcare, wearable sensing, IoT, multimedia forensics, and smart education, as well as research on web accessibility and usability. Together, these contributions illustrate both the continued development of AI methods and their increasing application to real-world problems. In addition to these regular articles, this issue includes a Special Section devoted to Intelligent Data Engineering and Automated Learning, comprising extended and substantially enhanced versions of selected contributions presented at the 25th International Conference on Intelligent Data Engineering and Automated Learning. The Guest Editor introduces the motivation, scope, and contributions of this Special Section.

item.title: Prototype AI Assistant for Private and Student Pilots
item.description: This research explores AI-based decision support in light general aviation (e.g., Cessna 172, Diamond), where onboard hardware is typically too limited for modern AI. In aviation, AI has the potential to act as a “copilot” supporting planning, execution, and assessment, particularly since single pilots must simultaneously aviate, navigate, and communicate under high workload. However, although AI adoption is rapidly expanding, many implementations are introduced without fully incorporating human-centered design processes that account for pilot workflow and workload. We leverage a human factors process in this research. First, we design and evaluate a cloud-based AI copilot . The system leverages Starlink Aviation connectivity and the pilot’s existing tablet interface, which is already widely used for flight planning and navigation. Running the AI in the cloud avoids heavy onboard processing while enabling real-time support. The assistant will follow standard ICAO/VFR radio phraseology and function as an AI teammate for routine tasks such as assisting with ATC interpretation or checklist guidance. The backend will fine-tune a large language model using aircraft-specific knowledge sources, including Cessna 172 and Diamond Pilot Operating Handbooks (POH), flight manuals, and FAA guidance. Domain-specific training allows the model to respond accurately to operational cockpit queries. Frontend development follows a systematic, user-centered design process. Development of the high-fidelity tablet prototype is guided by aviation human-factors principles for cockpit displays. The AI assistant will provide concise visual guidance on the tablet and optional auditory outputs aligned with aviation radio phraseology. Because pilots already experience high visual workload in the cockpit, auditory support may reduce attention demands and improve task management. This will be evaluated in a future test comparing visual-only versus visual+auditory feedback for usability, workload, and response timing. Our project explores how cloud-based AI can be integrated into light aircraft using existing pilot tablets and satellite connectivity and explores a research-based and practical path toward safe human-AI teaming in general aviation.

item.title: Efficient creation of shallow ${\mathrm{NV}}^{−}$ ensembles by high-angle ion implantation
item.description:
Author(s): Kento Sasaki, Hideyuki Watanabe, Tokuyuki Teraji, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, and Kensuke Kobayashi

Nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond are widely used as quantum sensors, but creating shallow ensembles with high yield and reasonable spin coherence remains challenging. We show that high-angle nitrogen ion implantation efficiently forms shallow NV ensembles. Implanting ions at angles above 60° gives NV yields approaching 10% with effective depths below 10 nm. The oblique geometry enhances near-surface vacancy generation while keeping nitrogen close to the surface, improving the conditions for NV formation. The resulting ensembles retain stable charge states and useful spin coherence, offering a practical platform for nanoscale NMR and NQR sensing.


[Phys. Rev. Materials 10, 086202] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026

item.title: Nanoscale graphitization and defect evolution in silicon-vacancy center-containing nanodiamonds under high-pressure high-temperature annealing
item.description: Group-IV color centers, such as the silicon-vacancy (SiV) defect, are highly promising for solid-state quantum technologies. However, nanodiamonds typically exhibit significant lattice strain and structural disorder, which degrade their optical properties and hinder the resolution of the fine spectral structure at cryogenic temperatures. High-pressure high-temperature (HPHT) annealing offers a potential route to relax internal strain, although the phase stability of diamond at the nanoscale under such conditions remains poorly constrained. Here, we investigate the structural evolution of nanodiamonds during HPHT annealing using a Paris-Edinburgh press coupled with in situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction at SOLEIL. A dedicated sample assembly combining nanodiamonds - NaCl - Pt enabled accurate pressure-temperature calibration and real-time monitoring of phase transformations. The diffraction data reveal that the onset of diamond-to-graphite transition occurs at approximately 1800 K at 2 GPa and 2120 K at 4 GPa under the applied HPHT heating protocol. These experimentally determined graphitization onsets define a practical pressure-temperature processing window for HPHT annealing of nanodiamonds while avoiding detectable graphitization and provide a calibrated framework for reliable off-beam annealing treatments that avoid graphitization. Photoluminescence measurements on samples annealed below the graphitization threshold show improved optical response, with partial resolution of the SiV fine structure at 12 K. These optical measurements suggest a relationship between nanoscale phase stability and the optical response of individual SiV-containing nanodiamonds following HPHT annealing. The experimentally established HPHT processing window provides a practical framework for the controlled processing of quantum nanodiamonds while avoiding graphitization.

item.title: Effect of different finishing/polishing protocols and aging on flexural strength, roughness, and surface characteristics of definitive restorative materials for CAD/CAM
item.description: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of finishing/polishing and aging on the flexural strength, roughness, and surface characteristics of CAD/CAM restorative materials. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Three CAD/CAM materials were tested: Nanoceramic resin (CR), Polymer-infiltrated ceramic (PIC), and Leucite-reinforced glass-ceramic (LC). A total of 120 bars (8 × 2 × 1 mm; n = 15/group) were prepared and subjected to different finishing/polishing protocols (C: control; B: bur; BD: diamond bur + diamond-impregnated rubber tips; BS: diamond bur + silica-impregnated rubbers) and aging (without/with 10,000 thermocycles). Mini-flexural strength (σ) was assessed by three-point bending. Surface roughness (Sa) was analyzed using optical profilometry, while surface characterization was performed using SEM. Data were analyzed with two-way ANOVA/Tukey's test (α = 0.05) and Weibull analysis. RESULTS: For σ, both finishing/polishing and aging factors significantly affected PIC and LC (p < 0.05), whereas only finishing/polishing influenced CR. In CR, aged CR_BD had the lowest strength (112.0 ± 17.9 MPa). In PIC, aged PIC_BS (121.8 ± 21.4) showed the highest strength, while PIC_BD groups showed the lowest. In LC, the highest values were seen in aged LC_C (125.7 ± 22.9), LC_B (114.75 ± 19.09), and non-aged LC_C (108.11 ± 29.54). Sa was significantly affected by material type and finishing/polishing protocols. CONCLUSIONS: Silica-impregnated rubbers improved the flexural strength of PIC after bur finishing. The BD protocol, producing smoother surfaces, may compromise the flexural strength of LC. In contrast, CR was not significantly affected by the polishing protocol. Moreover, aging negatively impacted PIC strength, and polyurethane rubber tips impregnated with diamond particles produced smoother surfaces after bur adjustments. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Within the limitations of this in vitro study, polishing protocols should be selected according to material composition, since surface smoothness does not necessarily correlate with improved mechanical performance. For CR, all polishing systems showed comparable performance; for LC, minimal intervention or no polishing better preserved mechanical performance; for PIC, silica-based polishing systems may be preferred.

item.title: Mechanical properties of additively manufactured TPMS structures: effect of heat treatment and dynamic loading
item.description: Abstract Triply periodic minimal surfaces (TPMS), specially made from Inconel 718 (In718), are suitable for aerospace, automotive, and energy sector components due to their superior physical properties. Currently, TPMS structures have been investigated for their mechanical performance under quasi-static compression; however, limited attention is paid to their performance in dynamic loading. In this study the TPMS structures were additively manufactured with suitable processing parameters. Later a multiple-step heat treatment was applied to these TPMSs. Quasistatic and dynamic impact tests at different loading velocities were conducted on those samples using a universal testing machine. The microstructure of the samples was investigated in scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and a comparison was made between the as-built and heat-treated samples. The impact of heat treatment and different phases on their mechanical properties was discussed. It was found that heat treatment has made substantial improvements in microstructure: dissolved detrimental phases and precipitated strengthening phases. The results demonstrated significantly higher strength of the TPMS structures under dynamic loading conditions, with the elastic modulus of the diamond TPMS increased by as much as 541%, while other properties were at least doubled compared to quasi-static mechanical properties. In addition, the energy absorption properties were almost doubled under impact loading as compared to the quasistatic loading condition and further improved by the heat treatment process.

item.title: Using an experience based design approach to advance health literacy in Ireland
item.description: Health literacy supports people, communities, and organisations in addressing noncommunicable diseases and their determinants, taking meaningful action to reduce risk factors, and support health and wellbeing for all. Addressing the issue of low health literacy has the potential to increase health, health equity and health system effectiveness by building citizens' capacities for health. The Sláintecare Healthy Communities programme was launched in 2021 in Ireland focussing specifically on promoting health and wellbeing at the community level, and improving health literacy is a key area of focus for this programme. This study aimed to work with stakeholders, in two Sláintecare Healthy Community areas, through a four-stage reflective process to discover, define, develop, and deliver innovative recommendations to improve health literacy within their communities. Two co-design workshops, adopting an adapted double diamond design approach (DDDA) took place in Spring 2024, one in each case study area. Sixty-eight stakeholders engaged in two DDDA workshops, undertaking tasks in same stakeholder and mixed stakeholder groups. A series of recommendations were co-created, with stakeholders voting for their preferred recommendations to refine this list in each area. These recommendations highlighted the need for effective early intervention, improved health infrastructure, and engaging with the community to connect, support, and sustain existing health literacy related initiatives. This is a novel example of health literacy stakeholder engagement in Ireland, and critically, it provides a tangible example of the process and outcomes of a collaboration between stakeholders and researchers which can be applied beyond these contexts.

item.title: Functional Annotation of Coding Sequences in the Cyanogenic Millipede Cherokia georgiana
item.description: Across thousands of known millipede species, genetic data is extremely limited. Many interesting biological processes in millipedes are ill-defined, such as the production of a defensive hydrogen cyanide secretion and UV fluorescence. We describe a transcriptomic dataset of the millipede Cherokia georgiana, including predicted coding regions and functional annotations. This de novo transcriptome will facilitate future research in understanding gene expression under a variety of conditions. Next-generation sequencing was conducted on polyA-enriched mature messenger RNAs using Illumina 2 x 150 paired-end sequencing. Total number of assembled contigs was 146,956. Transcripts were compared against the NCBI non-redundant (nr) protein database using DIAMOND BLASTx to identify sequence similarity to known proteins. Transcripts with sequence similarity to genes associated with cyanogenesis, including mandelonitrile oxidase and hydroxynitrile lyase, are present in this transcriptome. The data presented here enhances existing knowledge of millipede biology and provides a valuable reference for future research in myriapod evolution and ecology.

item.title: Current comparator for both AC and DC ratio measurements with 10− 8-level type-a uncertainty
item.description: Accurate measurements of alternating current (AC) and direct current (DC) ratios are fundamental to electric power metrology. However, conventional current comparators for AC and DC typically rely on distinct technologies-electromagnetic induction for AC and superconducting quantum interference devices for DC. This technological divide leads to a fragmented and complex traceability system. Bridging this gap is critical for developing unified current standards that meet the demands of temperature power technologies. In this work, we present a compact, room-temperature AC/DC current comparator that integrates a diamond-based magnetometer using nitrogen-vacancy centers. The device achieves a type-A uncertainty at [Formula: see text] level, while the expanded uncertainty is at [Formula: see text]to [Formula: see text]level, for both AC and DC signals and supports a system bandwidth up to [Formula: see text], without the need for cryogenics. It is comparable to the performance of typical AC comparators, and provides a compact and room-temperature operating platform for further performance improvement. This unified, cryogenics-free solution not only enhances precision and versatility but also expands the applicability of the system to DC resistance bridges in quantum electrical standards.

item.title: Self-assembly of colloidal diamond via the depletion interaction
item.description: Colloidal crystals with the cubic diamond structure are attractive templates for three-dimensional photonic band-gap materials, but their self-assembly is hindered by the need for tetrahedral coordination and staggered next-nearest-neighbor bonds, which together impose substantial kinetic barriers in previously realized DNA-mediated systems. Here we demonstrate an entropically guided, non-site-specific route to colloidal diamond that uses the depletion interaction to assemble tetrahedrally lobed patchy particles (TLPPs). The nonconvex TLPP shape encodes the staggered geometry and permits multiple sequential contacts between neighbors, so excluded-volume overlap increases progressively as particles approach the fully interlocked configuration. Using polymer micelles (Pluronic F127) as depletants, as well as silica and titania nanoparticles and polyethylene oxide, we obtain cubic-diamond crystals that form at lower particle concentrations and on timescales about an order of magnitude faster than TLPPs linked through DNA-coated patches. Optical microscopy of fluorescently labeled, refractive-index-matched particles confirms three-dimensional diamond order and predominantly ABC stacking of the {111} planes through analysis of bond networks, radial distribution functions, and a threefold bond-orientational order parameter. Monte Carlo excluded-volume calculations and umbrella sampling show that increasing depletion strength reshapes the potential of mean force into a broad, funnel-like landscape toward the fully interlocked subkissing state, substantially reducing the rotational entropic barrier to binding. Finally, we show that depletion-assembled structures can be permanently fixed by hybridization of palindromic DNA linkers followed by ultraviolet light (UV)-induced thymine photodimerization, enabling washing, drying, and downstream conversion to inverse photonic lattices.

item.title: Quantum and nanoscale sensing of microinflammation for earlier detection of chronic inflammatory and neuroimmune disease
item.description: Chronic inflammatory diseases may begin with spatially restricted and low-abundance inflammatory events that precede overt symptoms. In this perspective, we refer to such early events as micro-inflammation and discuss how mechanistic insights from the IL-6 amplifier and neuroimmune regulation may guide earlier detection of related diseases. The IL-6 amplifier is a positive-feedback inflammatory circuit in non-immune cells driven by concurrent NF-κB and IL-6-STAT3 signaling, whereas the gateway reflex illustrates how defined neural inputs can induce site-specific vascular micro-inflammation and immune-cell entry into affected tissues and organs. We also discuss stress-associated neuroimmune remodeling in diffuse neuropsychiatric systemic lupus erythematosus (dNPSLE) as a representative example of region-specific brain inflammation that may precede overt neuropsychiatric manifestations. On this basis, we examine how quantum and nanoscale sensing platforms, particularly fluorescent nanodiamonds containing nitrogen-vacancy centers and AI-assisted nanopore devices, could be adapted to detect candidate readouts of micro-inflammation, including reactive oxygen species, cytokine-related signals, nucleic acids, and other trace biomarkers. The original contribution of this Perspective is a mechanistically guided framework that maps micro-inflammatory biology related to the IL-6 amplifier, the gateway reflex, and dNPSLE onto specific classes of candidate nanosensing readouts, including oxidative stress-related physicochemical signals, cytokine-associated soluble biomarkers, extracellular nucleic acids, and other trace molecular signatures. Rather than providing a comprehensive review of all inflammatory mechanisms or diagnostic technologies, we present a mechanistically focused perspective linking neuroimmunology to next-generation sensing. We also highlight current limitations, including the predominantly preclinical nature of supporting evidence, uncertainty regarding accessible blood or cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers at presymptomatic stages, and the challenge of translating spatially restricted inflammatory signals into non-invasive human diagnostics.

item.title: Impact of strain and dark states on spectroscopic measurements of silicon-vacancy centers in diamond
item.description: Negatively charged silicon-vacancy (SiV$^-$) centers in diamond offer an attractive platform for the development of many forms of quantum technology. However, questions remain in connection to how large ensembles of SiV$^-$ centers behave in concert. Here, we develop a computational model designed to simulate recent experiments where optical multidimensional coherent spectroscopy (MDCS) was used to examine a high-concentration sample of SiV$^-$ centers in diamond, revealing significant variations in spectral signature depending on the detection scheme. Simulation results reveal that strain effects are highly random in this system, with a characteristic axial strain of $2.8 \times 10^{-4}$ and a shear strain of $3.5 \times 10^{-5}$. They suggest in addition that highly strained centers (with values exceeding $1.5 \times 10^{-5}$) may become significantly decoupled from optical emission. The results have implications for the use of SiV$^-$ centers as quantum sensors.

item.title: Discrete Linear Ensemble Logic
item.description: We study the discrete point-based fragment of Ensemble Logic $\EL(\Nat)$ over the natural numbers, a logic combining displacement $φ_u$, bounded metric modalities $\boldBox_t$ and $\mdiamond_t$ with additive bounds, Boolean connectives, and first-order quantification over $\Nat$. Motivated by the need for a unified symbolic layer for biomedical knowledge with temporal, spatial, genomic, and multimodal metric content, we develop the foundational discrete theory of the formalism. We give syntax and semantics, and prove a forward embedding of $\EL(\Nat)$ over a finite proposition set $\mathcal{P}$ into first-order monadic Presburger arithmetic $\FO(\Nat,<,+;\mathcal{P})$. This embedding yields the analytical upper bounds, while a reduction from nondeterministic two-counter machines with recurring control states proves that satisfiability is $Σ^1_1$-complete and validity is dually $Π^1_1$-complete. Expressively, $\EL(\Nat)$ strictly extends the star-free $ω$-languages and is incomparable with the $ω$-regular languages: it defines the non-$ω$-regular counting language $\{a^mb^mc^md^m\mid m\geq 1\}\cdotΣ^ω$, whereas a delimited parity language remains outside the logic by classical Presburger-arithmetic lower bounds. On the proof-theoretic side, we present a sound Hilbert system $\HEL$ and establish completeness relative to monadic Presburger validity as oracle, noting that completeness relative to plain Presburger arithmetic is impossible.

item.title: Forensic Gemmology
item.description: Are you investing in diamonds, or are fraudsters investing in your "good faith"? -A "must-have" for Jewellers, Investors, Bankers, Insurance Brokers, Appraisers, Surveyors, and anyone who buys, trades, or loves precious stones. -Think a reputable lab certificate guarantees your diamond, ruby, or emerald is natural? Think again. The global market faces a serious crisis. For decades, gemstone photo atlases served primarily as art. Forensic Gemmology surpasses them. Featuring over 140 unembellished color film photomicrographs, this eye-opening atlas reveals systemic market dangers. Crucially, it does NOT rely on just the photos: it contains rigorous scientific proof that can be fully appreciated even by non-scientists. It reveals invaluable trade secrets. This text raises the critical questions the jewelry industry ignores: The Educational Blindspot: Why standard trade-school laboratory training fails against highly sophisticated modern synthetics. The Technology Gap: Why commercial operations lack the advanced cryogenic equipment required for true identification. The Small Stone Loophole: The economic impossibility of verifying small accent diamonds scientifically. The Ultimate Risk: How the unmonitored influx of lab-grown gems threatens the very concept of rarity and long-term asset value. [1] This monograph is an urgent, visual wake-up call. It is designed for anyone needing to navigate the hidden vulnerabilities of the modern gemstone market. item.title: PFUSRC-143 Full Loss and Learning: Two Cognitive Paths to the Dao — From the Narrow Path of "Directly Pointing to the Mind" to the Broad Path of the "Topological Map"
item.description: Both Daoist and Buddhist traditions—as exemplified by the Diamond Sutra and the Daodejing—have revealed precise insights into the ontological structure of the cosmos: form is emptiness, abiding nowhere, and the Dao is diminished through practice. Yet for two millennia, these insights have remained inaccessible to the general public, accessible only to a rare few through “awakening” (wu). This paper, grounded in the PFUSRC seven-layer ontological framework, advances a fundamental thesis: the difficulty of understanding these teachings stems from the absence of a “topological map” capable of precisely describing their insights. “Awakening” is an extremely narrow cognitive path—a direct phase transition of the cognitive layer from L6 to L4 alignment with the ontological layer—accessible to only a tiny minority. “Learning” (through mathematical understanding) is a broad path—using the PFUSRC-035 Seven-Layer Ontological Map as a cognitive tool, allowing most people to achieve precise understanding of the L4 structure while remaining within the L6 cognitive layer. This study further argues that PFUSRC represents neither “awakening” nor “learning” in the traditional sense, but a third cognitive modality—“Illuminated Seeing” (zhaojian): through the Seven-Layer Ontological Map, one instantaneously perceives the holistic structure of the cosmos while simultaneously recognizing one’s own position within it. Illuminated Seeing not only allows one to “perceive the whole” but also provides the crucial “why” that traditional paths have always lacked—transforming practice from blind execution into directed cognitive operation. This paper, together with PFUSRC-141 (The Topological Ontology of the Dao System) and PFUSRC-142 (The Topological Proof of Ancient Predictive Systems), constitutes the complete “Trilogy of the Modern Reconstruction of Eastern Classical Wisdom.”

item.title: Imaginal Disc Cellular Tessellation as a Diamond Anvil Cell Tip Geometry Template: A Biomimetic Concept Note
item.description: This concept note introduces a biomimetic diamond anvil cell (DAC) tip geometry inspired by the cellular tessellation of insect wing imaginal discs. Standard advanced DAC tips rely on smooth, rotationally symmetric surfaces. In contrast, this design utilizes an irregular polygonal cellular topology to distribute applied loads and create controlled micro-crack deflection boundaries.

item.title: An Investigation on the Classical‑Quantum Bridging System within the Horizon of Modal Information Theory
item.description: Between classical and quantum information theories, there has long been a lack of independent logical ontology, axiomatic system and dedicated metrics, so researches on classical‑quantum transition largely rest on empirical scale division. Taking S4 modal logic as syntactic substrate, this paper constructs four modal‑probabilistic bridging axioms B1‑B4. Under pure informational constraints, the M3 diamond orthomodular lattice is uniquely derived as the minimal non‑distributive logical skeleton for the mesoscopic stratum. Three‑layer theoretical derivations are performed. First, jointly constrained by B1‑B4 axioms, the logical structure converges uniquely to the M3 lattice, eliminating classical Boolean distributive structures and high‑dimensional quantum projective structures. Second, with Busch’s Generalized Gleason Theorem and POVM formalism, M3 lattice is interpreted as a coarse‑grained quotient structure of two‑dimensional Hilbert space, establishing the probabilistic consistency of mesoscopic logic. Third, the derived silver critical value η=1+√2 is obtained by pure algebraic deduction and taken as the universal phase‑transition order parameter across classical‑mesoscopic‑quantum domains. The Liu mesoscopic entropy and mobit unit are introduced to form the three‑tier metric spectrum bit‑mobit‑qubit, confirming that the M3 diamond lattice constitutes a self‑consistent logical ontology for mesoscopic systems under informational constraints. Multi‑noise iterative tests of 10⁴runs are carried out on the TRAE platform. Numerical results of CHSH correlation and Werner‑state purity modulation exhibit three‑domain partition. The phase‑transition inflection point for the derived silver critical value shows favorable robustness, which numerically supports the reproducibility of the theory. The proposed axiomatic‑simulation framework provides mathematical references for studies on mesoscopic complex systems, classical‑quantum transition and informational ontology.
